items.description: Synology DSM contains an improper encoding or escaping of output vulnerability in the system plugin daemon in Synology BeeStation OS (BSM) that could allow a remote attacker to execute arbitrary code via unspecified vectors.

pREST (PostgreSQL REST) is an API that delivers an application on top of a Postgres database. Prior to 2.4.0, the vulnerable parameter is _groupby, handled by GroupByClause in adapters/postgres/postgres.go. adapters/postgres/postgres.go uses the weaker isSafeSQLExpression check for this function-expression branch instead of the stricter single-field validator used for _select. That check validates only the outer function name against a 13-function allowlist and permits nested subqueries, trailing UNION syntax, and inner pg_ functions. controllers/crud.go concatenates the GROUP BY expression while parameterizing only WHERE values, allowing attacker-controlled SQL structure into the clause. Default configuration permits unauthenticated access; a restricted installation may require a low-privilege table reader. UNION-based extraction requires compatible column counts and types and was not verified end to end, but a delay-producing function can cause denial of service without that alignment. This issue is fixed in 2.4.0.

In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

ocfs2: fix chunk number of the first chunk in a local quota file

Mounting a crafted OCFS2 image can corrupt kernel memory.  When the
local quota file header of such an image claims zero chunks, the first
quota entry allocated during the mount gets a chunk number taken from a
kernel pointer, and releasing that entry clears a bit far outside the
chunk bitmap.

The write will corrupt the data stored at that address, and the
corruption may lead to a system crash or damage unrelated data. 
Mounting requires CAP_SYS_ADMIN, so it takes an untrusted image, such
as removable media or a loop mount of a file from elsewhere.

Since the chunk number comes from a kernel pointer, the address of the
bit that gets cleared differs from boot to boot, and the issue has been
reported under several titles:

- BUG: unable to handle kernel paging request in ocfs2_local_release_dquot
- KASAN: use-after-free Write in ocfs2_local_release_dquot
- KASAN: slab-out-of-bounds Write in ocfs2_local_release_dquot
- KASAN: slab-use-after-free Write in ocfs2_local_release_dquot
- KFENCE: use-after-free write in ocfs2_local_release_dquot

Note that none of these is a use-after-free in the quota code: the
chunk and its buffer head are alive.  The bit that gets cleared lies
far outside the bitmap.  KASAN and KFENCE name each report based on the
object occupying that address, which explains why the same issue is
reported under so many different titles.  In the report I sent, the
address fell in a free page, which KASAN labels use-after-free.

There are known reproducers.  Both a syzkaller and a C reproducer are
available from the Google Drive link [1] in my report thread.  The
issue was found by our modified syzkaller, not a theoretical thing
found by an LLM.  I have not seen it outside fuzzing, so it is not
affecting me in the real world.

The local quota file in OCFS2 is divided into chunks, and each chunk
begins with a header block holding a bitmap of the quota entries that
chunk has handed out.  Chunks are numbered from zero, and that number is
used to convert the file offset of an entry back into a bit position in
the bitmap.  ocfs2_local_quota_add_chunk() appends a new chunk to the
in-memory list and numbers it one past the chunk that was last:

	list_add_tail(&chunk->qc_chunk, &oinfo->dqi_chunk);
	chunk->qc_num = list_entry(chunk->qc_chunk.prev,
				   struct ocfs2_quota_chunk,
				   qc_chunk)->qc_num + 1;

The predecessor is looked up after the new chunk is added to the list, so
if the list was empty, the prev pointer is the list head itself.  The head
is the dqi_chunk member of struct ocfs2_mem_dqinfo and is not a chunk, so
reading qc_num through it lands 16 bytes past the start of the head, on
the dqi_gqinode pointer that follows it.  The first chunk of the file is
then numbered with the lower half of a kernel pointer instead of 0.

The list is empty when the local quota file header claims the file has no
chunks.  ocfs2_local_read_info() takes dqi_chunks from that header without
validating it, so an image with dqi_chunks == 0 takes this path when the
first quota entry is allocated.

ocfs2_create_local_dquot() turns the bad number into a file offset with
ol_dqblk_off(), which shifts a 32-bit block number left by the block size
bits, so the top bits of such a large block number are lost. 
ocfs2_local_release_dquot() turns the offset back into a bit index with
ol_dqblk_chunk_off(), using the full chunk number, so the lost bits push
that index far outside the bitmap, and clearing it corrupts unrelated
memory.

Compute the chunk number before putting the chunk on the list, and use 0
when the list is empty.

In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

nvmet-fc: fix use-after-free in nvmet_fc_ls_create_connection()

nvmet_fc_ls_create_connection() looks up the association with
nvmet_fc_find_target_assoc(), which returns it with a reference held,
and drops that reference as soon as the target queue has been allocated.
iod->assoc is then dereferenced again by nvmet_fc_makeconnid() while
building the connection id.

The queue only borrows the pointer and takes no reference of its own.
Once the lookup reference is dropped the association is kept alive
solely by the reference taken when it was created, so a disconnect LS or
a remote port unregister running concurrently can free it before
nvmet_fc_makeconnid() reads it:

BUG: KASAN: slab-use-after-free in nvmet_fc_handle_ls_rqst_work (drivers/nvme/target/fc.c:193 drivers/nvme/target/fc.c:1841 drivers/nvme/target/fc.c:1995 drivers/nvme/target/fc.c:2021)
Read of size 8 at addr ffff888179f1b000 by task kworker/u9:2/1167

Hardware name: QEMU Ubuntu 24.04 PC v2 (i440FX + PIIX, arch_caps fix, 1996), BIOS 1.16.3-debian-1.16.3-2 04/01/2014
Workqueue: nvmet-wq nvmet_fc_handle_ls_rqst_work
Call Trace:
 <TASK>
 dump_stack_lvl (lib/dump_stack.c:94 lib/dump_stack.c:120)
 print_report (mm/kasan/report.c:378 mm/kasan/report.c:482)
 kasan_report (mm/kasan/report.c:595)

 process_scheduled_works (kernel/workqueue.c:3322 kernel/workqueue.c:3405)
 worker_thread (kernel/workqueue.c:3486)

 ret_from_fork_asm (arch/x86/entry/entry_64.S:245)
 </TASK>

Freed by task 1167 on cpu 0 at 405.998150s:
 kasan_save_track (mm/kasan/common.c:57 mm/kasan/common.c:78)
 kasan_save_free_info (mm/kasan/generic.c:584)
 __kasan_slab_free (mm/kasan/common.c:253 mm/kasan/common.c:285)
 kfree (include/linux/kasan.h:235 mm/slub.c:2705 mm/slub.c:6405 mm/slub.c:6720)

 ret_from_fork_asm (arch/x86/entry/entry_64.S:245)

The buggy address belongs to the object at ffff888179f1b000
 which belongs to the cache kmalloc-2k of size 2048
The buggy address is located 0 bytes inside of
 freed 2048-byte region [ffff888179f1b000, ffff888179f1b800)

Hold the lookup reference until the response has been built, and drop it
on the error path as well.

In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

ksmbd: prevent session binding in compound requests

A failed multichannel binding can retain its target session on the work
item so that the error response can be signed. Subsequent compound
commands can then use that session together with a tree connection left
over from an earlier command.

Limit binding SESSION_SETUP requests to standalone messages during
message validation, before smb2_sess_setup() can replace work->sess.
Check both NextCommand and the current request offset to cover binding
in the first, middle and last positions of a compound. The existing
validation error path returns STATUS_INVALID_PARAMETER and stops
processing the remaining commands.

This intentionally limits support for compounded binding. It is not a
protocol requirement that binding be standalone. Standalone binding and
non-binding compounds retain their existing behavior, without changing
session, tree or response encryption handling.

In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

net/sched: cls_flower: avoid stale mask references after delete

Flower releases a mask reference when a filter is removed from the
classifier. The filter object can remain alive while dump, walk, or
hardware reoffload paths hold a reference to it. Those paths can then
dereference f->mask after the mask has already been released.

Keep the mask reference until the filter reference count reaches zero.
Release the mask synchronously from the final __fl_put() while the caller
still holds the tcf_proto reference, and leave the existing RCU work to
free the mask. This keeps the mask available to every reader that still
holds the filter.

The filter is still removed from the classifier indexes immediately.
Therefore, a deleted filter can temporarily retain an otherwise empty
mask; fl_delete() uses the handle IDR, rather than the mask list, to
determine whether the classifier has become empty.

Failed mask assignment can leave fnew->mask as an error or borrowed
pointer without an owned mask reference. Clear it before the common
failure path so the final put cannot release an unowned reference.

This fix does not add fields, snapshots, or per-filter memory.

In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

KVM: x86/mmu: Bug the VM if KVM attempts to walk more levels than the MMU has

Extend the "EFER.LMA && !CR4.PAE" check, which exists largely to guard
against KVM configuring a paging32 MMU with more than 2 levels of paging,
with a very explicit check for exactly that: that KVM isn't trying to walk
more levels of paging than the MMU template provides.  I.e. harden KVM
against all bugs that would cause KVM to generates accesses beyond the
bounds of guest_walker's arrays, regardless of how KVM ended up with the
misconfigured MMU.

Note, don't use w->cpu_role.base.level directly as the paging64 template
only provides two levels of page tables for PAE paging on 32-bit hosts, and
handles the third level by manually emulating the PDPTR access.

In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

udf: don't let the extent type hide an exhausted free-space table extent

udf_table_new_block() takes the first block of the free-space table
extent closest to the goal.  It keeps that extent's type and length
together in goal_elen, subtracts one block, and deletes the extent only
if goal_elen then reaches zero.  UDF 2.60 section 2.3.7.1 requires the
free-space extents of an Unallocated Space Entry to be of type 1
(allocated but not recorded), and mkudffs writes them that way.  For
such an extent the type bits keep goal_elen non-zero, so taking its last
block leaves a type-1 extent of length zero behind, starting at the
block after the extent, which is in use.

The next allocation that picks this empty extent returns that in-use
block.  Subtracting a block from 0x40000000 then borrows from the type
bits, and the extent becomes type 0 with a length of 2^30 - blocksize:
about a gigabyte of "free" space overlapping live metadata, the other
table extents and whatever lies behind the partition.  From then on
blocks are handed out twice, or past the end of the partition.

Extents that udf_table_free_blocks() adds are type 0, where the check
works, so only tables written by mkudffs or by another implementation
are affected.  Nothing more than filling such a filesystem is needed:
on a fresh 1 MiB "mkudffs --space=unalloctable" image, creating empty
files until the partition is full writes file entries over the reserve
volume descriptor sequence and the backup anchor, and df then reports a
negative amount of used space.

On syzbot's images the same double allocation is what the two reports
below trip over.  In the first, ftruncate() extends a new file with
enough hole extents to need a chain of allocation extent descriptors;
one AED is placed on another inode's file entry, and a later one is
placed on the block of the AED currently being filled, which
udf_setup_indirect_aext() zeroes, so __udf_add_aext() finds
lengthAllocDescs out of step with its cursor.  In the second, an AED
is placed past the end of the device, sb_getblk() fails, and the error
path of udf_do_extend_file() calls udf_truncate_extents() on an extent
list that no longer covers i_size.

Keep the type separately from the length, as udf_table_prealloc_blocks()
already does.

In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

drm/amdgpu/gfx12: disallow GFXOFF while updating the SPM VMID

gfx_v12_0_update_spm_vmid() does a read-modify-write of RLC_SPM_MC_CNTL
over MMIO without keeping GFX powered, unlike gfx11. When GFX is in
GFXOFF at that point the update doesn't stick, and with the SPM VMID
programmed on submission again, the job of a process with a reserved
VMID can still run with the SPM writing through VMID 0.

On navi48, after a few other submissions and a VM fault on the same VM,
a COPY_DATA of RLC_SPM_MC_CNTL from such a job reads 0 although the
update was called for it:

  $ amd_uapi_regression --run-subtest cs-secure-ib-compute,gem-mapping-info-high-va,gpuvm-fault-high-va,reserved-vmid-spm-vmid
  amdgpu 0000:03:00.0: [gfxhub] page fault (src_id:0 ring:40 vmid:7 pasid:185)
  amdgpu 0000:03:00.0: 	 Faulty UTCL2 client ID: SDMA1 (0xe)
  RLC_SPM_MC_CNTL in the job: 0x00000000

With GFXOFF disallowed around the update it reads the reserved VMID 15.

(cherry picked from commit 907aebc5578ae09fa5c0e2f0784201295837e60b)

In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

net: atl1c: drop oversized RX frames instead of panicking

atl1c sizes its receive buffers from the netdev MTU plus a fixed set of L2
overheads, which comes to 1522 bytes at the default MTU.  A link partner
that sends a longer frame - in practice a MikroTik CCR2004-1G-2XS-PCIe,
whose RouterOS side defaults to l2mtu 1600 while the host stays at MTU 1500
- makes the length reported by the RX return descriptor exceed what the
hardware wrote, and skb_put() then either includes bytes that were never
received or trips skb_over_panic and takes the host down.

Compare the descriptor length against buffer_info->length, the length the
hardware was given, rather than against skb_tailroom(): the skb carries 64
bytes of slack for the DMA erratum, so tailroom is larger than the DMA
buffer and a frame in between would pass the check and still be delivered
with a tail the device never wrote.  The same test rejects frames shorter
than ETH_HLEN + ETH_FCS_LEN; before this change a reported length below
ETH_FCS_LEN underflowed in skb_put().

The frame is dropped with kfree_skb_reason(SKB_DROP_REASON_PKT_TOO_BIG) so
drop_monitor and the kfree_skb tracepoint see it, and counted through
dev_core_stats_rx_dropped_inc(), which survives atl1c_get_stats()
overwriting the hardware counters on every read.  It also counts as work:
atl1c_clean_rfd() has already recycled the RFD, and the refill at the end
of the poll only runs when work_done is non-zero, so sustained oversized
traffic would otherwise drain the ring and stop RX.

Tested on a MikroTik CCR2004-1G-2XS-PCIe (4x AR8151) in a Proxmox VE host,
with atl1c built from a DKMS tree carrying this change: the l2mtu-1600
traffic that panics the stock driver is dropped and counted with the patch
applied, and received normally once the host MTU is raised to match.

This complements commit 36c2009d90f2 ("net: atl1c: fix soft lockup on
out-of-range tpd_cons read"), which fixed the TX side of the same
"host dies while the card resets" problem.

In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

scsi: target: Verify the iSCSI ISID is null-terminated

iscsi_parse_pr_out_transport_id() returns the ISID of a FORMAT CODE 01b
TransportID as a pointer into the PERSISTENT RESERVE OUT parameter list,
lowercased in place and never null-terminated.  spc4r37 Table 508 requires
the field to be null-terminated, but a non-conforming initiator can omit
the NULL; when the ISID ends at the end of the received buffer, the pointer
is not a C string.

The registration code still consumes it as one: strcmp() in
__core_scsi3_locate_pr_reg() and in the REGISTER AND MOVE path, and
snprintf("%s") in __core_scsi3_do_alloc_registration(), which also reads
its first 8 bytes unconditionally with get_unaligned_be64() - a NUL check
does not bound that read.

When the parameter list spans more than one page, transport_kmap_data_sg()
maps it with vmap(), and the over-read walks off the end of the mapping
into the vmalloc() guard page and oopses.  Reproduced with a PR OUT
REGISTER + SPEC_I_PT parameter list of exactly 8192 bytes whose final
TransportID carries a 12-byte ISID without a terminating NUL:

  BUG: unable to handle page fault for address: ffffc9000138c000
  RIP: 0010:strcmp+0xc/0x30
  Call Trace:
   __core_scsi3_locate_pr_reg+0xd3/0x120 [target_core_mod]
   core_scsi3_decode_spec_i_port+0x8fc/0x13a0 [target_core_mod]
   core_scsi3_emulate_pro_register+0x73c/0x900 [target_core_mod]
   ...
   iscsi_target_rx_thread+0xef/0x1d0 [iscsi_target_mod]

With a single-page parameter list the buffer is a kmap() direct mapping, so
the over-read continues into the physically adjacent page instead of
faulting.  snprintf("%s") then copies whatever follows the ISID in memory
into pr_reg_isid, and PR IN READ FULL STATUS reports the registration back
to any initiator, turning the over-read into an info leak of kernel heap
contents.  Reproduced with a 4096-byte parameter list whose last
TransportID ends at the end of the buffer with a 4-byte ISID and no NUL,
interleaved with I/O to populate adjacent pages: the READ FULL STATUS
response returned the ISID as "0xleak" followed by raw bytes that were not
part of the parameter list.  The snprintf() into
pr_reg_isid[PR_REG_ISID_LEN] caps the echoed ISID at 15 characters, so at
most 11 bytes past the buffer are leaked per command, but the PR OUT
command is not rate limited.

Any initiator that can send PR OUT to an iSCSI-exported LUN can trigger
either variant, including a guest via vhost-scsi.

Require 8 bytes to remain after the ",i,0x" separator, and a NUL inside the
rest of the descriptor, before the ISID pointer is returned.  REGISTER AND
MOVE fails with TCM_INVALID_PARAMETER_LIST; on SPEC_I_PT no target port
claims the malformed TransportID, and the command fails the same way.

MemberPress Members before 3.3.1, with the Block Permissions add-on enabled, contains a denial of service vulnerability that allows authenticated Author-level users to crash pages by saving a non-string blockPermissionsMessage block attribute. Attackers can store a JSON array in the attribute so wpautop() in get_block_replacement_content() throws a PHP 8 TypeError, causing fatal errors on post, home, search, and REST pages for unauthorized viewers.

pgjdbc, the PostgreSQL JDBC Driver, misreads some quoted text in its query parser. A `}` inside a literal ends a JDBC escape such as `{ts}`, and the rest of the literal is translated as SQL. A dollar quote whose tag has a non-ASCII symbol or space is not recognized. An `E''` string with a doubled quote is scanned as a standard string. `{fn right}` and `{fn timestampdiff}` with a negative argument produce a `--` comment. In each case text that the application quoted correctly can run as SQL with the privileges of the application's database role. All versions before 42.7.15 are affected, and 42.7.15 fixes the problem.

pgjdbc, the PostgreSQL JDBC Driver, can quote a string parameter for the wrong value of standard_conforming_strings when preferQueryMode=simple is set. A statement, trigger or configuration reload can turn the setting off during a session. A parameter value with a backslash and a quote then ends the literal, and the rest of the value runs as SQL. Before 42.7.6 any session with the setting off was affected. The statement cache can also reuse a parse made under the other setting. With allowEncodingChanges=true and the EUC_JP or SJIS client encoding, the yen sign acts as a backslash. All versions before 42.7.15 are affected, and 42.7.15 fixes the problem.

items.title: Cisco Expressway Series Use of Hard-coded Credentials Vulnerability
items.description: Cisco Expressway Series contains a use of hard-coded credentials vulnerability that allows an unauthenticated, remote attacker with persistent cookies and network access to execute commands as root on a clustered device via the database service.

items.title: Cisco BroadWorks Improper Restriction of XML External Entity Reference Vulnerability
items.description: Cisco BroadWorks contains an improper restriction of XML external entity reference vulnerability that could allow an unauthenticated, remote attacker to read sensitive configuration information on an affected system.

The gettext family of functions in the GNU C Library version 2.0 and later accept LANGUAGE environment variable entries that contain '/' or that are equal to "..", unless the program is setuid or setgid (AT_SECURE).  An attacker who can set LANGUAGE in the environment of a program that uses gettext can make it load a message catalog (.mo file) from an arbitrary location in the file system.  A crafted .mo file can crash the program through out-of-range offsets, or supply translations whose format directives do not match the arguments passed by the program.  That causes undefined behaviour in the printf family of functions and may allow arbitrary code execution with the privileges of the program.  The safety of message catalogs relies on them being installed in trusted, read-only locations, and the directory traversal bypasses this.

The fix for CVE-2014-0475 rejects ".." path components in locale names passed to setlocale or taken from the LC_ALL, LC_* and LANG environment variables.  gettext reads LANGUAGE directly and appends each colon-separated entry to the message catalog directory, so that fix did not cover LANGUAGE.

LANGUAGE is only used when the LC_MESSAGES locale is not "C", "C.<encoding>" or "POSIX", so the attacker must also be able to select another installed locale, for example through LANG or LC_ALL.  Exploitation also requires that the attacker can place the crafted file in a location readable by the target program, and that the environment crosses a trust boundary without the program running as AT_SECURE.  An example is an SSH server that accepts LANGUAGE and LANG from clients through the AcceptEnv directive and restricts an account to a forced command; the attacker may use this to escape the restriction.

In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

net/mlx5: HWS, Handle destroying table that has a miss table

If a table has a miss table that was created by
'mlx5hws_table_set_default_miss' API function, its miss_tbl
keeps the table that points to it in a list.
If such table is deleted, we need to also remove it from the
miss_tbl list, otherwise the node in miss_tbl list will contain
garbage.

In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

Bluetooth: mgmt: fix race in read_unconf_index_list()

read_unconf_index_list() counts unconfigured controllers before allocating
its response, then checks the device flags again while filling it.

hci_dev_list_lock stabilizes list membership, but it does not serialize the
per-device flags. During asynchronous controller setup, the worker can set
HCI_UNCONFIGURED and clear HCI_SETUP between the two passes. A controller
omitted from the allocation count can then become eligible for the fill
pass, causing an out-of-bounds write to rp->index[].

Allocate space for every device on hci_dev_list. Since list membership
cannot change while hci_dev_list_lock is held, the response remains large
enough regardless of flag transitions. The reported count and response
length still include only eligible unconfigured controllers.

items.title: Copy Anything to Clipboard < 5.5.5 - Contributor+ Stored XSS via 'success-text' Shortcode Attribute
items.description: The Copy Anything to Clipboard for WordPress  WordPress plugin before 5.5.5 does not sanitize and escape a shortcode attribute before storing it and writing it back into the page through a client-side script, which could allow users with the contributor role and above to perform Stored Cross-Site Scripting attacks against higher-privileged users who view and interact with the content.
vendor_products: Unknown Copy Anything to Clipboard for WordPress

items.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

smb: client: fix heap overflow in cifs_do_set_acl()

cifs_set_acl() validates ACL size using posix_acl_xattr_size():

        4 + (count * 8)  // 4-byte header + 8 bytes per ACE

cifs_do_set_acl() then calls posix_acl_to_cifs() to write the CIFS
wire format into the same buffer:

        6 + (count * 10)  // 6-byte header + 10 bytes per ACE

An ACL that passes the xattr-based check in cifs_set_acl() can
overflow the heap when posix_acl_to_cifs() writes the larger CIFS
format.

Validate the CIFS format size against the remaining buffer space and
USHRT_MAX before converting--data_count is __u16, so sizes above
USHRT_MAX truncate the on-wire packet length, causing the server to
apply a partial ACL.  Replace MaxDataCount = 1000 with
min(CIFSMaxBufSize, USHRT_MAX).

In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

dm-crypt: fix a tiny race condition in crypt_dec_pending

crypt_dec_pending reads io->error before calling atomic_dec_and_test.
Another context, for example crypt_endio called from an interrupt, may
set io->error and drop its reference between the read and the
decrement. crypt_dec_pending then drops the last reference and completes
the bio with the stale status - so a read that failed and was never
decrypted, or a write that failed, is reported as successful.

The read was placed before the decrement by commit b35f8caa0890 ("dm
crypt: wait for endio to complete before destruction"), because that
commit freed dm_crypt_io before calling bio_endio. This is no longer the
case, dm_crypt_io lives in the per-bio data now.

Read io->error after atomic_dec_and_test instead. atomic_dec_and_test is
fully ordered, so no additional barrier is needed.

In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

drm/amdgpu: keep the eviction fence until the last handle is closed

amdgpu_gem_object_close() detaches the user queue eviction fence from
the BO before it checks bo_va->ref_count, so closing any handle of a BO
removes the fence, even when the file still has another handle to the
BO and the bo_va with its GPU mappings stays. The BO can then be evicted
without suspending the user queues of the file, which keep accessing it
through mappings that are only marked for update.

Seen on navi31 with a SDMA user queue: a BO opened twice in the same
file (GEM_FLINK + GEM_OPEN) loses its eviction fence when the second
handle is closed (traced attach/detach of the fence):

  attach bo=ffff8c78a6c84c00
  GEM_CLOSE handle=7
  detach bo=ffff8c78a6c84c00

while handle 6 and the mapping are still in use.

Only detach the fence when the last reference to the bo_va goes away,
matching amdgpu_gem_object_open(), which attaches it only when the
bo_va is created. With this the fence stays until the file is closed.

(cherry picked from commit 8387982f03d4026b7dc11b0b5e3118298eee4d6a)

In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

net/rds: don't let the rdma_cm destroy an id RDS still owns on route failure

rds_rdma_cm_event_handler_cmn() hands the return value of
rdma_resolve_route() straight back to the rdma_cm on
RDMA_CM_EVENT_ADDR_RESOLVED.  A synchronous failure there - -ENOMEM
from the route work allocation, an SA query that cannot be set up, a
RoCE route with no usable device - makes addr_handler() destroy the
id the event was delivered on.  That id is ic->i_cm_id, and nothing
clears the pointer: the connection sits in RDS_CONN_CONNECTING with a
freed id until its shutdown calls rdma_disconnect() and
rdma_destroy_id() on it.

The ROUTE_RESOLVED case already avoids this: rds_ib_cm_initiate_connect()
forces a zero return while ic->i_cm_id == cm_id, as the comment there
explains.  Do the same here - drop the connection and return 0 - so
the id stays RDS's to destroy from the shutdown, and the reconnect
gets a fresh one.

In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

coredump: hold RCU while releasing parked threads

coredump_finish() releases the parked threads by clearing ->task in
their core_thread entry and calling wake_up_process() on each of them.
It does that without holding a reference on the task and without being
inside rcu.

But calling wake_up_process(task) without rcu here isn't safe. A parked
thread doesn't need that wakeup to leave. A spurious wakeup or a
preemption after the store is enough for the task to go away.

So if the coredump client is preempted between the store and
wake_up_process() the thread can exit and be freed in the meantime and
try_to_wake_up() takes pi_lock in freed memory.

Hold rcu across the loop.

In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

keys: Protect the type name while describing a key

keyctl_describe_key() must keep the key type's name alive until
kasprintf() has consumed it. The retained key reference keeps the key
and its description alive, but does not pin the module providing its
type. The name is passed to kasprintf() without holding key->sem.

kvasprintf() uses the saved name pointer in two formatting passes, with
a GFP_KERNEL allocation between them. With AF_RXRPC=m, a task that
passes View permission before type retirement can overlap a privileged
module unload in this order:

1. KEYCTL_DESCRIBE looks up the key, saves key->type->name in the
   kasprintf() arguments and completes the first formatting pass.
2. While the formatter is delayed before its second pass,
   af_rxrpc_exit() calls unregister_key_type(), which removes the type
   from the registry and waits for key_gc_keytype().
3. The collector takes key->sem for writing, retypes the retained key
   to key_type_dead and completes retirement. Unregistration and module
   exit return, allowing free_module() to release the type and name.
4. The formatter resumes its second pass and reads the saved name from
   released module storage, which can fault in string().

Hold key->sem for reading across kasprintf(). The collector then cannot
retype the key or complete retirement until both formatting passes have
finished. If retirement wins the lock first, formatting uses the core
key_type_dead name instead. Release the semaphore immediately after
kasprintf(), including on allocation failure, before copying to
userspace.

Oops report as below:

    BUG: unable to handle page fault for address: fffffbfff8054794
    #PF: supervisor read access in kernel mode
    #PF: error_code(0x0000) - not-present page
    RIP: 0010:string+0x23f/0x470
    Call Trace:
     vsnprintf+0x330/0x1110

items.title: psqlODBC ODBC escape parser stack buffer overflow
items.description: The psqlODBC parser for ODBC escape sequences in application SQL text writes the argument offsets of a {fn} escape into a fixed 16-entry stack array without a bound and does not initialize the array. An escape with too many arguments overflows the stack, and a reference to an unsupplied argument copies arbitrary bytes into the query. The copy of a {d}, {t}, {ts}, or {escape} body also writes one byte past a 128-byte stack buffer. An application that forwards untrusted SQL text to the driver exposes its process to memory corruption. Versions before psqlODBC 18.00.0006 are affected.

items.title: psqlODBC SQL injection through SQLSpecialColumns table and schema names
items.description: SQLSpecialColumns in psqlODBC splices the table and schema names it receives into its catalog query without escaping them, while the other catalog functions escape them. An application that passes an untrusted table or schema name to SQLSpecialColumns lets the caller execute arbitrary SQL with the privileges of the connection. Versions before psqlODBC 18.00.0006 are affected.

items.title: psqlODBC does not validate column numbers and row indexes in binding and descriptor functions
items.description: Several psqlODBC entry points use an application-supplied column number or row index as an array index without validating it. SQLBindCol with a column number above 32767 wraps the binding count negative and a later copy runs off the array. A negative SQL_DESC_COUNT on an application row descriptor unbinds columns at negative indexes. SQLColAttribute with a very large column number uses a negative index. SQLSetPos(SQL_ADD) does not check the row number against the rowset size. An application that forwards untrusted column or row numbers exposes its process to out-of-bounds reads and writes. Versions before psqlODBC 18.00.0006 are affected.

items.title: BackUpWordPress < 3.15 - Subscriber+ Backup Directory File Deletion via hmbkp_dismiss_error
items.description: The BackUpWordPress plugin before 3.15 does not perform a capability or nonce check on an AJAX action that cleans up its backup directory, allowing any authenticated user (Subscriber and above) to delete the BackUpWordPress plugin before 3.15's backup protection and working files, removing download protection from stored backups and disrupting in-progress backups.

items.title: ssl.get_server_certificate(addr, ca_certs=...) verifies the chain but never the identity
items.description: When ca_certs parameter was supplied to ssl.get_server_certificate() function, the identity of the certificate is not checked.

items.title: .NET Elevation of Privilege Vulnerability
items.description: Time-of-check time-of-use (toctou) race condition in .NET allows an authorized attacker to elevate privileges locally.

items.title: Node.js is vulnerable to Permission Model file-name disclosure via recursive fs.watch
items.description: A Permission Model bypass in Node.js recursive file watching discloses the names of files and directories the process is not permitted to read. On macOS and Windows, fs.watch() and fs.promises.watch() in recursive mode are backed by the native libuv watcher: FSEventWrap::Start checks kFileSystemRead only once, on the watched root, and FSEventWrap::OnEvent then forwards every filename libuv reports (relative paths at any depth) to the JavaScript callback without checking that each path is covered by the read grant. Code running under --permission with an exact read grant on a directory can therefore learn names such as sub/secret.txt even though readdir on that subdirectory is denied. The flaw exposes names and timing metadata, not file contents, and requires macOS or Windows plus files created under the watched directory by another actor. This vulnerability affects Node.js 26.x, 24.x, and 22.x.

items.title: Trustindex Review Widget Plugins < 14.3 - Editor+ Stored XSS via Business Name
items.description: The Widgets for Google Reviews WordPress plugin before 14.3, WP Tripadvisor Review Widgets WordPress plugin before 14.3, Widgets for Booking.com Reviews WordPress plugin before 14.3, Widgets for Reviews & Recommendations WordPress plugin before 14.3, Widgets for Airbnb Reviews WordPress plugin before 14.3, Widgets for Yelp Reviews WordPress plugin before 14.3, Widgets for Amazon Reviews WordPress plugin before 14.3, Widgets for Thumbtack Reviews WordPress plugin before 14.3, Widgets for Ebay Reviews WordPress plugin before 14.3, Widgets for Zillow Reviews WordPress plugin before 14.3, Widgets for Capterra Reviews WordPress plugin before 14.3, Widgets for Expedia Reviews WordPress plugin before 14.3, Widgets for Opentable Reviews WordPress plugin before 14.3, Widgets for WordPress Reviews WordPress plugin before 14.3, Widgets for Hotels.com Reviews WordPress plugin before 14.3, Review Widgets for Szallas.hu WordPress plugin before 14.3, Widgets for AliExpress Reviews WordPress plugin before 14.3, Widgets for Árukereső Reviews WordPress plugin before 14.3, Widgets for Foursquare Reviews WordPress plugin before 14.3, Widgets for Alibaba Reviews WordPress plugin before 14.3, Widgets for SourceForge Reviews WordPress plugin before 14.3 do not sanitise and escape the connected business details before outputting them in their review widgets, which could allow users with the Editor role and above to perform Stored Cross-Site Scripting attacks even when the unfiltered_html capability is disallowed (for example in a multisite setup).

In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

ALSA: usx2y: Initialize idle URBs before submitting streams

usb_stream_start() submits the first two capture and playback URBs and
only afterwards assigns sk->idle_inurb, sk->idle_outurb,
sk->completed_inurb and sk->completed_outurb to the remaining two URBs
of each direction.

A transfer can complete as soon as usb_submit_urb() has been called, so
the completion handler i_capture_start() or i_playback_start() may run
before those pointers are set.  While the stream is still being
synchronized (state below usb_stream_sync1), stream_start() then calls
playback_prep_freqn(sk, sk->idle_outurb) with sk->idle_outurb still
NULL, and the packet descriptors are written through that NULL pointer:

  Oops: general protection fault, probably for non-canonical address
  0xdffffc0000000018: 0000 [#1] SMP KASAN
  KASAN: null-ptr-deref in range [0x00000000000000c0-0x00000000000000c7]
  RIP: 0010:playback_prep_freqn+0x11c/0x4a0 sound/usb/usx2y/usb_stream.c:33
  Call Trace:
   <IRQ>
   stream_start+0x5dc/0x8d0 sound/usb/usx2y/usb_stream.c:596
   i_capture_start+0x3da/0x710 sound/usb/usx2y/usb_stream.c:654
   __usb_hcd_giveback_urb+0x238/0x550 drivers/usb/core/hcd.c:1657
   usb_giveback_urb_bh+0x20b/0x530 drivers/usb/core/hcd.c:1691
   tasklet_hi_action+0xa/0x20 kernel/softirq.c:994
   handle_softirqs+0x16f/0x440 kernel/softirq.c:645
   </IRQ>

The four URBs referenced by these pointers are allocated long before and
do not depend on any transfer state, so assign them before the submit
loop.  Keeping the assignment inside the retry path also restores a
well-defined URB rotation when the start frame mismatch handling kills
and resubmits the streams.

In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

ipv6: raw: fix use-after-free in rawv6_send_hdrinc()

rawv6_send_hdrinc() caches the route before handing the skb to
l3mdev_ip6_out(). The VRF output path may replace skb->dst and release
the original route, leaving the cached pointer stale.

The function later dereferences that pointer for statistics accounting
and as the output device passed to NF_HOOK(). Its RCU read-side critical
section starts after l3mdev_ip6_out(), so it cannot prevent the old route
from being reclaimed in between.

Reload the route from the current skb destination after
l3mdev_ip6_out() returns.

KASAN reports a slab-use-after-free in rawv6_sendmsg(), with the route
allocated by ip6_dst_alloc(), freed by dst_destroy() from rcu_core(), and
the related RCU callback queued from vrf_l3_out().

items.title: SAP NetWeaver Improper Neutralization of Special Elements in Data Query Logic Vulnerability
items.description: SAP NetWeaver Enterprise Portal contains an improper neutralization of special elements in data query logic vulnerability that allows an unauthenticated attacker to disclose or modify server information via injected JNDI environment properties or a URL used during JNDI lookup operations.

items.title: Mapster WP Maps < 2.0.7 - Contributor+ Arbitrary Post, Page and Attachment Modification
items.description: The Mapster WP Maps — Mapbox, MapLibre & Google Maps for WordPress plugin before 2.0.7 does not perform any authorization check when saving edits made through its bundled photo-gallery library, allowing any authenticated user with at least Contributor-level access to overwrite the title and content of, and write arbitrary metadata onto, any post, page or media attachment on the site regardless of ownership.
vendor_products: Unknown Mapster WP Maps — Mapbox, MapLibre & Google Maps for WordPress

items.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

media: imx-jpeg: cancel timeout worker when streaming stops

Each per-fd context ctx owns a delayed_work (ctx->task_timer, callback
mxc_jpeg_device_run_timeout) armed via schedule_delayed_work() at the end
of mxc_jpeg_device_run() to recover a stalled encode/decode job. The only
existing cancellation is cancel_delayed_work() in the frame-done IRQ
handler, which de-queues a pending work item but does not wait for a
callback that has already started, and it only runs when a frame completes.

When the fd is closed while a job is in flight (the frame-done IRQ has not
fired yet), nothing syncs the worker before mxc_jpeg_release() frees ctx
with kfree() after v4l2_m2m_ctx_release(). A queued or executing
mxc_jpeg_device_run_timeout() can then recover ctx through
container_of(&ctx->task_timer) and dereference it (ctx->mxc_jpeg,
slot_data, dev_warn) after ctx has been freed.

Cancel the worker from mxc_jpeg_stop_streaming(). The cancel cannot live
in mxc_jpeg_release(): mxc_jpeg_device_run() arms the timer while holding
only hw_lock, not the mxc_jpeg->lock mutex that release holds, so a cancel
in release could still race a concurrent mxc_jpeg_device_run() that
re-arms the timer afterwards. mxc_jpeg_stop_streaming() instead runs inside
v4l2_m2m_ctx_release() -> vb2_queue_release(), i.e. after
v4l2_m2m_cancel_job() has set TRANS_ABORT and waited for any in-flight job
to finish (so __v4l2_m2m_try_queue() will not queue and v4l2_m2m_try_run()
will not run any further job for this context, which prevents
mxc_jpeg_device_run() from re-arming the timer) and before the m2m context
is freed. cancel_delayed_work_sync() removes a pending work item and waits
for a running callback, so the worker can no longer race with the
subsequent kfree(). The cancel is placed before the buffer-release loop so
a concurrently running timeout callback cannot race with it over the same
buffers. If the frame-done IRQ canceled a still-pending timer, this cancel
is a no-op; if the timeout callback has already started, it waits for the
callback to finish. The same mxc_jpeg_stop_streaming() call is also
reached from VIDIOC_STREAMOFF, which drains the worker early, although
STREAMOFF itself does not free ctx -- the use-after-free arises only
when the fd is later closed.

This bug was found by static analysis.

In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

KVM: guest_memfd: Gracefully handle xarray errors when binding a memslot

If inserting a memslot into a guest_memfd's bindings xarray fails,
propagate the error back to the caller, i.e. fail memslot creation as well.
Signalling success and continuing on with memslot creation results in
use-after-free, as the guest_memfd instance will remain reachable via the
memslot after the file is freed (kvm_gmem_release() won't nullify the file
pointer due to lack of a valid binding).

Opportunistically WARN and reject binding if KVM_MEMSLOT_GMEM_ONLY is
already set, partly to guard against goofs elsewhere, but mostly so that
KVM doesn't need to worry about clobbering flags when unwinding on failure.

Regarding the unwind, the slot must be fully prepared before inserting it
into the bindings, at which point the slot becomes reachable.  I.e. waiting
to update the slot in order to avoid the ugly unwind isn't an option.  And
as part of the unwind, explicitly nullify the relevant bindings, as xarray
can store a subset of entries when populating a range.

In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

fsverity: Set S_VERITY only after rollback is no longer possible

Commit f77f281b6118 ("fsverity: use a hashtable to find the
fsverity_info") changed the implementation of FS_IOC_ENABLE_VERITY to
make concurrent reads start going through fsverity verification slightly
earlier than they did before.

Instead of it happening when enable_verity() calls fsverity_set_info(),
it now happens when ->end_enable_verity() sets S_VERITY.

However, ext4 and btrfs can roll back verity after they set S_VERITY,
causing a use-after-free.

Fix that by making ext4 and btrfs set S_VERITY only after rollback is no
longer possible.  On failure, don't roll back S_VERITY, but do roll back
the filesystem-specific verity flag.

Also update enable_verity() to handle any future instances of this bug
more safely by warning and *not* freeing the fsverity_info.

Finally, tweak some comments.  Clarify one, and move information from
another to its proper place in the comment for ->end_enable_verity().

In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

accel/amdxdna: clear the mailbox channel pointer when starting it fails

aie2_create_context() allocates a mailbox channel, starts it, and on a
failed start frees it again:

	hwctx->priv->mbox_chann = xdna_mailbox_alloc_channel(ndev->mbox);
	...
	ret = xdna_mailbox_start_channel(hwctx->priv->mbox_chann, ...);
	if (ret)
		goto free_channel;
	...
free_channel:
	xdna_mailbox_free_channel(hwctx->priv->mbox_chann);

hwctx->priv->mbox_chann keeps pointing at the freed channel. That
pointer is the driver's own test for whether a hardware context has a
usable channel: aie2_destroy_context() returns early on NULL,
aie2_sched_job_run() refuses to run a job on NULL, and the message
helpers return -ENODEV on NULL. A stale pointer passes all of them.

It matters on the restart path. aie2_hwctx_restart() calls
aie2_create_context() again on a hardware context that is already live,
after aie2_hwctx_stop() has torn its channel down, and the context
survives a failure there: aie2_sched_job_timedout() discards the return
value entirely, and aie2_hwctx_resume() only propagates it. What is
left is a live hardware context holding a freed channel, and every
later user of it takes the non-NULL branch:

  - the next job submitted reaches xdna_mailbox_send_msg() on the freed
    channel, via the !mbox_chann guard in aie2_sched_job_run(),
  - a second command timeout reaches aie2_hwctx_stop() ->
    aie2_destroy_context(),
  - closing the device reaches aie2_hwctx_fini() ->
    aie2_release_resource() -> xrs_release_resource() ->
    aie2_xrs_unload() -> aie2_destroy_context(),

and aie2_destroy_context() then calls xdna_mailbox_stop_channel()
followed by xdna_mailbox_free_channel() on memory that was already
freed: a use-after-free, and a second free of the same channel.

The AIE4 management channel already does this correctly -
aie4_mailbox_start() clears ndev->aie.mgmt_chann right after freeing
it. Do the same here.

The create path itself is not affected: when aie2_xrs_load() fails,
xrs_allocate_resource() removes the solver node without calling
->unload, and aie2_hwctx_init() frees hwctx->priv, so the stale pointer
never outlives the structure holding it.

Starting a channel can fail today without this patch: the ring buffer
sizes firmware reports are rejected unless both are powers of two, and
request_irq() can fail.

In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

media: hackrf: fix use-after-free in hackrf_alloc_urbs() error path

hackrf_alloc_urbs() frees the URBs it allocated so far when one
allocation fails, but leaves the entries in dev->urb_list[] and
dev->urbs_initialized untouched. The caller, hackrf_start_streaming(),
then calls hackrf_free_urbs() on the error path, which walks
dev->urbs_initialized entries and calls usb_free_urb() a second time on
the already-freed URBs, causing a use-after-free (slab-use-after-free
Write in usb_free_urb()).

Drop the redundant cleanup loop inside hackrf_alloc_urbs() and let
hackrf_free_urbs(), which the caller already invokes on error, own the
cleanup of the successfully allocated URBs.

In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

rtnetlink: wait for RCU readers in rtnl_link_unregister()

rtnl_link_ops_get() finds ops on link_ops under rcu_read_lock() and only
then takes ops->srcu. rtnl_link_unregister() unlinks ops, then calls
synchronize_srcu() and cleanup_srcu_struct() without first waiting for
RCU readers. A reader that found ops before list_del_rcu() and has not yet
taken ops->srcu is not waited for.

Such a reader then locks a cleaned-up srcu_struct and keeps using ops
after the module that owns it is gone. rtnl_newlink() and
rtnl_dump_ifinfo() both look up ops without RTNL, the latter for any
user that dumps links filtered by kind.

With delays added between the lookup and srcu_read_lock() in
rtnl_link_ops_get(), and before rtnl_link_ops_put() in
rtnl_dump_ifinfo(), running "ip link show type dummy" alongside
"rmmod dummy" on a KASAN kernel gives:

  BUG: KASAN: vmalloc-out-of-bounds in __srcu_read_unlock+0x57/0x70
  Read of size 8 at addr ffffffffc02ff318 by task ip/147
  Call Trace:
   __srcu_read_unlock+0x57/0x70
   rtnl_dump_ifinfo.cold+0x30/0x3b
   rtnl_dumpit+0x7a/0x1b0
   netlink_dump+0x486/0x11b0
   __netlink_dump_start+0x661/0x910
   rtnetlink_rcv_msg+0x611/0x9e0
   netlink_rcv_skb+0x126/0x380
   netlink_unicast+0x605/0x830
   netlink_sendmsg+0x6d0/0xbb0
   __sys_sendto+0x335/0x3a0

Call synchronize_rcu() before synchronize_srcu(), as
rtnl_af_unregister() already does. This should be enough because
rtnl_link_ops_get() is the only RCU walker of link_ops, and it takes
ops->srcu before rcu_read_unlock(), so every reader that found ops is
covered by synchronize_srcu() once the RCU grace period ends. The extra
grace period only costs time at module unload.

Readers and the writer were serialized by RTNL until link_ops got its
own mutex, which is why the missing RCU wait did not matter before.

In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

KVM: guest_memfd: take the invalidate lock when unbinding a dying file

kvm_gmem_unbind() takes mapping->invalidate_lock only if the
get_file_active() succeeds. When the guest_memfd file is dying, its
reference count is already zero so get_file_active fails and the binding
is removed without holding the invalidate lock.

kvm_gmem_invalidate_{start,end}() checks f->bindings independently to
decide whether to begin or end KVM MMU invalidation. So, the bindings
must therefore remain stable between the two calls. Otherwise, unbind
can remove a binding after start increments mmu_invalidate_in_progress,
but before end finds the binding and decrements it.
Example, unbind race with memory failure:

  CPU 0: memory failure               CPU 1: memslot delete
  ----------------------------------  ---------------------------
                                      (guest_memfd file is dying)
  kvm_gmem_error_folio()
    kvm_gmem_invalidate_start()
      finds binding
      mmu_invalidate_in_progress++
                                      kvm_gmem_unbind()
                                        get_file_active() fails
                                        removes binding
    kvm_gmem_invalidate_end()
      no binding found
      counter stays elevated

mmu_invalidate_retry() then returns 1 forever, so guest page faults
retry without ever installing a mapping and the guest hangs.

Remove the distinction between live and dying files in the unbind path.
Always use slot->gmem.file and take the invalidate lock when it's non-NULL.
Normal unbind callers hold slots_lock, which prevents release from clearing
the pointer or freeing the file state until unbind completes. Final VM
teardown can only see a NULL pointer because guest_memfd pins the KVM until
release has cleared all bindings.

In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

drm/amdgpu: Fix duplicate dependency fence releases

drm_sched_job_add_dependency() consumes its fence reference on success
and failure. Do not release the fence again if
drm_sched_job_add_dependency() fails.

(cherry picked from commit e04f3dfb2071451633e6440a3911a9bb65df9144)

In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

drm/amdgpu/userq: validate the moved individual BOs on restore

An individual BO of a user queue VM, i.e. one which doesn't share the
root reservation, goes to the individual needs_update list when it is
evicted. The user queue restore looked at vm->invalidated for them, which
the VM state machine rework turned into the always_valid evicted list and
commit 18decfc9e8cc ("drm/amdgpu/userq: actually validate userq BOs")
into the individual evicted one. That list only holds imported DMA-bufs of
compute VMs though, so for a user queue VM nothing is validated.

The restore then neither locks such a BO nor moves it back. Its PTEs are
updated to wherever it is now, cleared if it went to system memory, and
it doesn't get the new eviction fence, so it can move again under the
running queue.

On navi48, once the BOs of an SDMA user queue are evicted from GTT
(debugfs amdgpu_evict_gtt) the queue faults on its ring and rptr:

  amdgpu 0000:03:00.0:   in page starting at address 0x0000000100000000 from client 10
  amdgpu 0000:03:00.0: 	 Faulty UTCL2 client ID: SDMA0 (0xd)
  amdgpu 0000:03:00.0:   in page starting at address 0x0000000100101000 from client 10

Validate the BOs on the individual needs_update list like before.

(cherry picked from commit eb0d94765d4be18d41e93ad09947dd9cc06ed31a)

In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

mm/cma: don't release CMA pages still in use

When a driver calls dma_free_contiguous() before quiescing DMA, the
page might still have a reference from the device.
put_page_testzero() there returns false, WARN fires, but the code proceeds
to free_contig_frozen_range() putting a live page onto buddy and clearing
the bitmap. A subsequent allocation can hand the same PFN to a new
owner while the original holder still references it.

A concurrent put_page() that drops the last reference between the
testzero loop and free_contig_frozen_range() can double-queue the page
via page->lru, corrupting buddy lists.

Avoid the corruption by not freeing a CMA region if any of the
pages inside are still in use.

Make it explicit in the warning that the driver allowed a leak.

While at it, use page_ref_freeze() to make the semantics clearer and
switch to pr_warn_ratelimited().

[ david: use page_ref_freeze() + pr_warn_ratelimited() ]

In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

mm/mmu_gather: fix flushing ranges with 4 GiB or larger

__tlb_adjust_range() takes the size of the range which has to be flushed
as an unsigned int. Its callers, tlb_flush_{pte,pmd,pud,p4d}_range(), get
and pass an unsigned long. Consequently, a range that is 4 GiB or larger
gets truncated, possibly to 0.

On arm64 with hugetlb, a 64k kernel can have 16 GiB hugetlb folios
mapped contiguously at the PMD level and flush them when unmapping, and a
16k kernel can flush 64 GiB PUDs through tlb_unshare_pmd_ptdesc(). So
at least these two scenarios are affected.

Fix it by flushing the proper range instead of the truncated one by
properly using "unsigned long" for range_size.

Fix generated by an LLM and sent by Josef Bacik in private.

[ david: use two-tab indent, simplify description ]

In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

mm/khugepaged: always recheck the pmd in try_collapse_pte_mapped_thp()

try_collapse_pte_mapped_thp() drops the PTE lock after it has cleared the
page table, and takes the PMD lock and the PTE lock to remove it.

In between, MADV_DONTNEED with CONFIG_PT_RECLAIM can reclaim the
page table. The pmd_same() check is supposed to handle this, but it is
only done with CONFIG_SPLIT_PTE_PTLOCKS.

Fix it by performing the check unconditionally.

Fix generated by an LLM and sent by Josef Bacik in private.

[ david: adjust description ]

In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

cipso: fix optlen corruption in cipso_v4_delopt()

cipso_v4_delopt() recomputes the option length by walking the option
buffer after the CIPSO option has been moved out.  The walk then reads
the stale bytes at the tail of the buffer as option data, and a crafted
setsockopt(IP_OPTIONS) buffer can make it treat one of them as an option
length, increasing opt->opt.optlen beyond the valid option data.

The corrupted length stays on the socket and is later used as the copy
length by getsockopt(IP_OPTIONS) and by the udp/raw/ping sendmsg paths,
where it exceeds the size of the buffers they copy into.

Compute the new length from the intact options before the move and
subtract the CIPSO length, and fill the padding with IPOPT_END.

In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

ASoC: SOF: Intel: hda-sdw-bpt: Stop active DMA before closing BPT streams

When sdw_enable_stream() fails in intel_ace2x_bpt_send_async() after
hda_sdw_bpt_send_async() has already started the TX and RX DMA streams,
intel_ace2x_bpt_close_stream() invokes hda_sdw_bpt_close() directly
without calling hda_sdw_bpt_wait().  As a result,
hda_sdw_bpt_dma_deprepare() tears down the DMA buffers and BDL while
the DMA hardware is still running.

Disable any running TX or RX BPT DMA stream at the start of
hda_sdw_bpt_close() before unmapping channels and depreparing DMA
resources.

k8s-mcp-server manages Kubernetes clusters through the Model Context Protocol. Prior to 1.1.0, SERVER_MODE defaults to SSE, with the listener on 0.0.0.0:8080, but main.go creates the SSE server without an authentication option or context function. The GET /sse handler creates a sessionId that is only a correlation value, and the POST /message handler accepts a loadable sessionId without an authorization or Origin check before dispatching tools/call; consequently, any client able to reach the port can enumerate and invoke registered Kubernetes tools without credentials. Read-only mode is disabled by default, leaving write-capable Kubernetes tools available to run with the server's configured cluster privileges. This issue is fixed in version 1.1.0.
Sensitive authentication material written to a log file in Citrix NetScaler ADC and Citrix NetScaler Gateway.
Memory overflow in Application Firewall data decompression/inspection can lead to unpredictable or erroneous behavior or Denial of Service in Citrix NetScaler ADC and Citrix NetScaler Gateway.
Improper request handling can lead to a denial-of-service / reboot-loop condition in Citrix NetScaler ADC and Citrix NetScaler Gateway.
Memory overflow in an authentication request can lead to unpredictable or erroneous behavior or Denial of Service in Citrix NetScaler ADC and Citrix NetScaler Gateway.

items.title: mcp-ffmpeg through 1.0.5 OS Command Injection via videoPath and outputDir
items.description: mcp-ffmpeg through 1.0.5 contains an OS command injection vulnerability that allows attackers to run shell commands by supplying crafted videoPath or outputDir values to the resize-video, extract-audio and get-video-info tools. Attackers can embed $(), backticks or a closing double quote in an existing file or directory name to break out of the child_process.exec command string and execute commands as the MCP server user.

items.title: Adobe Commerce and Magento Unrestricted Upload of File with Dangerous Type Vulnerability
items.description: Adobe Commerce and Magento contain an unrestricted upload of file with dangerous type vulnerability that could result in arbitrary code execution in the context of the current user, potentially gaining elevated access or control over the victim's account or session.

items.title: Bake filesystem entitlement consent is skipped under --progress=rawjson in Docker Buildx
items.description: Buildx bake requires the user to grant entitlements with --allow or an interactive prompt before a build reaches outside the working directory. Under --progress=rawjson that consent step is skipped.

LXC is a userspace interface for the Linux kernel containment features used to create and manage system containers. In LXC 7.0.0 and earlier, lxc-copy and the public liblxc clone() API can follow attacker-controlled symbolic links while updating /etc/hostname in a copied container root filesystem. The affected surfaces are lxc-copy and liblxc's public lxc_container::clone() API. The privileged cloning process must run as root. The source rootfs must be attacker-controlled or less trusted. A symlink can be placed at etc/hostname or in an intermediate component. The clone operation preserves the symlink before updating the hostname. The vulnerable write truncates and overwrites an existing file outside the destination rootfs. When root clones an untrusted container without LXC_CLONE_KEEPNAME, the copied symlink can resolve outside the destination rootfs and cause the privileged process to overwrite an existing host file with the destination container name. Unprivileged use and managers with independent cloning implementations are not affected. LXC_CLONE_KEEPNAME avoids the hostname update and therefore the affected write.

items.title: FFmpeg through 9.0.2 Heap Buffer Overflow via RISC-V Vector diff_bytes Routine
items.description: FFmpeg through 9.0.2 contains a heap buffer overflow vulnerability in ff_llvidenc_diff_bytes_rvv() that allows attackers to corrupt heap memory by triggering negative length values in the Huffyuv encoder. Attackers can supply RGB video narrower than 8 or 16 pixels for huffyuv transcoding on RVV-enabled RISC-V builds, causing writes past the encoder's temp buffer.

items.title: FFmpeg through 9.0.2 Heap Overflow via Nellymoser Encoder Trellis Search
items.description: FFmpeg through 9.0.2 contains an off-by-one heap overflow vulnerability in get_exponent_dynamic() in libavcodec/nellymoserenc.c that allows writing one element past the opt and path allocations. Attackers can supply crafted audio to applications encoding Nellymoser with trellis enabled, causing idx to equal OPT_SIZE and overwrite adjacent heap memory.

items.title: FFmpeg through 9.0.2 Heap Buffer Overflow in EXR Encoder RLE Path
items.description: FFmpeg through 9.0.2 contains a heap buffer overflow vulnerability in libavcodec/exrenc.c that allows attackers to corrupt heap memory when encode_scanline_rle() processes frames taller than the encoder height. Attackers can supply crafted input whose resolution grows mid-stream, transcoded to OpenEXR with RLE compression, to write pointers past the scanline array and crash the application.

items.title: FFmpeg through 9.0.2 Double Free via cbs_sei_delete_message in cbs_sei.c
items.description: FFmpeg through 9.0.2 contains a double free vulnerability in libavcodec/cbs_sei.c where cbs_sei_delete_message() leaves a stale extension_data reference that ff_cbs_sei_add_message() reuses. Attackers can supply a crafted H.264 stream with a display orientation SEI message followed by payload extension data, processed by h264_metadata with display_orientation=insert, to corrupt heap memory.

items.title: FFmpeg through 9.0.2 FLIC Decoder Out-of-Bounds Write via FLI_BRUN Byte Swap
items.description: FFmpeg through 9.0.2 contains an out-of-bounds write vulnerability in flic_decode_frame_15_16BPP() in libavcodec/flicvideo.c that allows attackers to corrupt heap memory on big-endian builds. Attackers can supply a crafted 15/16 bpp FLIC/FLX file with an FLI_BRUN chunk whose non-terminating byte-swap loop writes packet-derived data past the frame buffer, crashing the process.

items.title: FFmpeg through 9.0.2 Heap Buffer Overflow via liboapv APV Encoder Wrapper
items.description: FFmpeg through 9.0.2 contains a heap buffer overflow vulnerability in liboapve_encode() in libavcodec/liboapvenc.c that allows attackers to corrupt heap memory by supplying frames larger than the configured encoder dimensions. Attackers can craft videos whose resolution changes mid-stream so that transcoding to APV without rescaling writes attacker-controlled pixel data past the imgb plane buffers.

items.title: FFmpeg through 9.0.2 Heap Buffer Overflow via HEVC VAAPI Tile Arrays
items.description: FFmpeg through 9.0.2 contains a heap buffer overflow vulnerability in vaapi_hevc_start_frame() in libavcodec/vaapi_hevc.c that copies unbounded PPS tile counts into fixed-size arrays. Attackers can supply a crafted HEVC bitstream with a large picture and many tiles to write controlled 16-bit values past heap-allocated hwaccel data, corrupting memory in applications decoding with VAAPI.

items.title: FFmpeg through 9.0.2 Heap Buffer Overflow in libwebp Encoder Conditional Replenishment
items.description: FFmpeg through 9.0.2 contains a heap buffer overflow in ff_libwebp_get_frame() in libwebpenc_common.c that lets attackers corrupt memory when cr_threshold is set. Attackers can supply crafted media that increases resolution mid-stream, causing memcpy() to write pixel data past the stale reference frame and crash applications.

items.title: FFmpeg through 9.0.2 V4L2 M2M Encoder Out-of-Bounds Write in v4l2_buffers.c
items.description: FFmpeg through 9.0.2 contains an out-of-bounds write vulnerability in v4l2_buffer_swframe_to_buf() in libavcodec/v4l2_buffers.c because cumulative plane offsets are not checked against the V4L2 buffer length. Attackers can supply crafted video whose dimensions or padding cause unsigned wraparound in v4l2_bufref_to_buf(), making memcpy() write past the mmaped driver buffer during V4L2 M2M encoding.

items.title: FFmpeg through 9.0.2 Heap Overflow in libaribcaption Text Subtitle Decoding
items.description: FFmpeg through 9.0.2 contains a heap buffer overflow vulnerability in aribcaption_trans_text_subtitle() in libavcodec/libaribcaption.c when decoding with sub_type text. Attackers can supply a crafted ARIB STD-B24 caption stream with zero regions, causing a pointer write past a zero-sized sub->rects allocation and corrupting heap memory.

items.title: FFmpeg through 9.0.2 Heap Corruption via libaribcaption ASS Error Cleanup
items.description: FFmpeg through 9.0.2 contains an out-of-bounds read and invalid free vulnerability in aribcaption_trans_ass_subtitle() in libavcodec/libaribcaption.c that frees subtitle rectangles using region_count instead of num_rects. Attackers can supply crafted ARIB captions whose later region exceeds the 8 KiB AVBPrint limit, triggering cleanup that frees out-of-bounds pointers and corrupts the heap.

items.title: FFmpeg through 9.0.2 Heap Buffer Overflow via VideoToolbox Encoder
items.description: FFmpeg through 9.0.2 contains a heap buffer overflow vulnerability in libavcodec/videotoolboxenc.c that copies frames larger than encoder dimensions into undersized CVPixelBuffers. Attackers can supply crafted input whose resolution grows mid-stream, transcoded with VideoToolbox encoders without rescaling, to crash the application or corrupt memory.

items.title: FFmpeg through 9.0.2 Heap Buffer Overflow via PSD Decoder RLE Path
items.description: FFmpeg through 9.0.2 contains a heap buffer overflow vulnerability in the PSD decoder in libavcodec/psd.c that allows attackers to corrupt heap memory on 32-bit builds by supplying a crafted PSD image. Attackers can choose dimensions and channel counts whose product exceeds 4 GB, truncating the av_malloc allocation size so decode_rle() writes attacker-controlled data past the buffer, causing crashes or possible code execution.

items.title: FFmpeg through 9.0.2 Heap Buffer Overflow in Blu-ray PCM Decoder
items.description: FFmpeg through 9.0.2 contains a heap buffer overflow vulnerability in pcm_bluray_decode_frame() in libavcodec/pcm-bluray.c on big-endian hosts. Attackers can supply a crafted Blu-ray (M2TS) LPCM stream whose payload length is not a multiple of the sample size, writing attacker-controlled bytes past the audio frame buffer.

items.title: FFmpeg through 9.0.2 APNG Encoder Heap Buffer Overflow via encode_apng()
items.description: FFmpeg through 9.0.2 contains a heap buffer overflow vulnerability in the APNG encoder's encode_apng() function in libavcodec/pngenc.c when frame size changes mid-stream. Attackers can supply crafted media whose resolution grows mid-stream, causing APNG_DISPOSE_OP_BACKGROUND memset writes past prev_frame and crashing or corrupting heap memory in transcoding applications.

items.title: FFmpeg through 9.0.2 Heap Buffer Overflow via HEVC VDPAU Tile Arrays
items.description: FFmpeg through 9.0.2 contains a heap buffer overflow vulnerability in vdpau_hevc_start_frame() in libavcodec/vdpau_hevc.c that copies unbounded PPS tile counts into fixed-size VDPAU arrays. Attackers can supply crafted HEVC bitstreams with excessive tile columns or rows to write controlled 16-bit values past heap-allocated hwaccel data, corrupting memory in applications using VDPAU decoding.

items.title: FFmpeg through 9.0.2 Heap Buffer Overflow via hap_parse_frame_header()
items.description: FFmpeg through 9.0.2 contains an integer overflow vulnerability in hap_parse_frame_header() in libavcodec/hapdec.c that allows attackers to trigger a heap buffer overflow on 32-bit builds. Attackers can craft Hap video frames with Snappy length prefixes that wrap tex_size, causing decompress_chunks_thread() to write outside tex_buf and crash the application or potentially execute code.

items.title: FFmpeg through 9.0.2 Heap Buffer Overflow via cbs_jpeg_write_scan Integer Overflow
items.description: FFmpeg through 9.0.2 contains an integer overflow in cbs_jpeg_write_scan() in libavcodec/cbs_jpeg.c that causes a heap buffer overflow on 32-bit builds. Attackers can supply a crafted MJPEG/JPEG stream with a scan of 512 MiB or more, processed by CBS bitstream filters like filter_units, to corrupt the heap or crash the application.

items.title: FFmpeg through 9.0.2 Heap Overflow via QSV Encoder submit_frame()
items.description: FFmpeg through 9.0.2 contains a heap overflow vulnerability in libavcodec/qsvenc.c that allows attackers to corrupt memory by reusing an undersized pooled QSVFrame buffer when input dimensions increase. Attackers can supply crafted input whose resolution grows mid-stream, transcoded with Intel Quick Sync encoders without rescaling, to crash the application or corrupt heap memory.

items.title: FFmpeg through 9.0.2 Heap Buffer Overflow via HEVC DXVA Tile Parameters
items.description: FFmpeg through 9.0.2 contains a heap buffer overflow vulnerability in ff_dxva2_hevc_fill_picture_parameters() that allows attackers to corrupt memory via unbounded non-uniform tile counts. Attackers can supply crafted HEVC bitstreams with many non-uniformly spaced tiles to write controlled 16-bit values past fixed-size DXVA arrays during DXVA2, D3D11VA, or D3D12VA decoding on Windows.

items.title: FFmpeg through 9.0.2 Heap Buffer Overflow via FLIC Decoder check_pixel_ptr
items.description: FFmpeg through 9.0.2 contains a heap buffer overflow vulnerability in libavcodec/flicvideo.c that allows attackers to write out of bounds because check_pixel_ptr() checks only one bound with negative-stride frames. Attackers can supply a crafted FLIC file whose RLE and delta chunks write pixel data past frame storage, corrupting heap memory to crash applications or possibly execute code.

items.title: FFmpeg through 9.0.2 VVC Decoder Heap Out-of-Bounds Write via refs.c
items.description: FFmpeg through 9.0.2 contains an integer overflow vulnerability in the VVC decoder alloc_frame() function in libavcodec/vvc/refs.c that undersizes the reference picture list allocation on 32-bit builds. Attackers can supply a crafted VVC (H.266) file with a very large number of NAL units per access unit to trigger heap out-of-bounds writes and corrupt memory.

items.title: Action Pack: Possible cache poisoning in Action Pack content negotiation
items.description: Action Pack is a framework for handling and responding to web requests. Prior to 8.1.4.1 and 8.0.5.2, Action Pack negotiates the format of a rendered response from the Accept, X-Requested-With and, for XHR requests without Accept, Content-Type request headers, but ActionController::Rendering#_set_vary_header adds Vary: Accept only when the request carries a usable Accept header and the response has no Vary header yet. A response to a request without Accept, or to an XHR request, therefore omits the headers that selected its representation, and a response whose Vary the application set before rendering (for example Vary: Accept-Language) never gains Accept. A shared cache that honours Vary could store such a response and serve it to later clients that request a different representation, possibly leading to cache poisoning in which visitors receive, until the entry expires, a page without its layout or HTML in place of JSON. The attacker cannot choose the content of the response. Applications that render negotiated responses from actions marked public (for example with expires_in ..., public: true) behind a shared cache that honours Vary, such as Thruster or Rack::Cache, are affected. This issue is fixed in versions 8.1.4.1 and 8.0.5.2.

items.title: Docker Sandboxes privilege escalation through untrusted state directories
items.description: Docker Sandboxes reuses existing state and configuration directories without verifying their ownership. If sbx or sandboxd is run as root with HOME or, on Linux, XDG_STATE_HOME pointing to an attacker-controlled location, a local unprivileged user can substitute control-plane sockets and configuration trusted by the root process, potentially executing commands as root. Exploitation requires a privileged invocation with an attacker-influenced environment. The issue affects Linux and macOS and is fixed in version 0.53.0.

The Model Context Protocol TypeScript SDK provides TypeScript client and server implementations of the Model Context Protocol. From 2.0.0 until 2.3.0 in @modelcontextprotocol/server, applications that shared one stateless HTTP transport or one McpServer or Server instance among multiple clients could deliver responses and notifications to the wrong client. The affected surface is an MCP server reached over HTTP by multiple clients. The trigger is reuse of one stateless transport or server instance. Messages were associated with a connection using only the JSON-RPC request identifier. SDK clients start request identifiers at zero, so collisions occur in normal operation. Cross-client delivery exposes one client's responses and notifications to another client. The issue requires an HTTP endpoint reachable by more than one client and an application that constructs the server or transport once at startup instead of once per request or session. stdio servers and factory-created per-call servers are not affected. Upgrading causes reused instances to fail and therefore requires an application code change. This issue is fixed in @modelcontextprotocol/server 2.3.0.

A flaw in Node.js TLS hostname verification allows a certificate with only a DNS SAN to authenticate an IP endpoint when the client connects using a non-canonical IPv4 spelling, such as `0177.0.0.1`, `0x7f.0.0.1`, `2130706433` or `127.1`.

`tls.checkServerIdentity()` did not classify these hosts as IP addresses, but normalized them to their canonical form and matched the result against the certificate DNS names. A certificate containing `DNS:127.0.0.1` and no `IP Address:127.0.0.1` SAN was therefore accepted, while the same certificate is correctly rejected for `127.0.0.1`. Exploitation requires a certificate with a numeric DNS SAN issued by a CA trusted by the client, and a platform resolver that accepts these spellings, such as glibc.

This vulnerability affects Node.js **26.x**, **24.x**, and **22.x**.

ImageMagick before 6.9.13-58 and 7.x before 7.1.2-33 contains a stack-based buffer overflow in the handling of bzip2 compressed images. Attackers can supply a crafted image using bzip2 compression to overwrite stack memory during decoding, causing crashes or memory corruption.

Improper input validation in Ivanti EPMM before version 12.11.0.0, 12.10.0.1, and 12.9.0.3 allows a remote authenticated attacker with admin privileges to set arbitrary Linux kernel parameters as root.

items.title: AWS-advanced-jdbc-wrapper: Java Deserialization RCE via Cache Poisoning
items.description:
### Impact
The AWS Advanced JDBC Wrapper is an open-source JDBC driver wrapper that extends a JDBC driver to enable Amazon Aurora and AWS Cloud features such as failover handling and caching. We identified CVE-2026-14265, an issue in the RemoteQueryCachePlugin of the AWS Advanced JDBC Wrapper. When this plugin is enabled, query results read from the shared Redis/Valkey cache are deserialized without class filtering. An actor with write access to the shared cache infrastructure could insert a crafted serialized Java object that, when read by an application, results in execution of arbitrary code on the application server.

### Workarounds
The RemoteQueryCachePlugin is not enabled by default. Customers who cannot immediately upgrade can mitigate this issue by disabling the RemoteQueryCachePlugin, and by restricting write access to the Redis/Valkey cache infrastructure to trusted principals.

AdminNeo before 5.9.1 contains an sql injection vulnerability that allows remote attackers to inject SQL by supplying crafted IN and NOT IN search values that process_length() passes unescaped. Attackers can send a logged-in user a cross-site GET link using a backslash-escaped apostrophe to run blind SQL with that user's database rights on PostgreSQL, SQLite, MS SQL, Oracle, or MySQL in NO_BACKSLASH_ESCAPES mode.

rConfig Core 8.2.19 before 8.2.22 contains a server-side request forgery vulnerability that allows authenticated users to bypass the DeviceIpIsValid loopback guard by supplying unresolved hostnames. Attackers can create a device with a hostname resolving to loopback and device_port_override 6379, causing configuration downloads to send Redis inline commands for remote code execution.

items.title: LiteLLM: Privilege Escalation to Proxy Admin via Cross-Domain Reuse of the Salt Key
items.description:
### Summary

An authenticated user with `internal_user` privileges can escalate to `proxy_admin` and achieve remote code execution. The proxy uses one encryption key for two purposes: sealing secrets at rest and minting session tokens. An attacker exploits this by requesting a new API key with a crafted metadata field containing a forged admin credential as the "secret" value. The proxy encrypts and returns this payload. When this value is then presented as a bearer token, the proxy decrypts it, trusts the forged admin identity, and grants full administrative access, including the ability to execute arbitrary commands via the MCP stdio endpoint.

### Affected versions

Versions later than 1.91.0 are exploitable in the default configuration. Versions 1.87.0 through 1.90.x are exploitable only if `EXPERIMENTAL_UI_LOGIN=true` was explicitly set.

### Mitigation

Upgrade to a patched version as soon as possible.

If you cannot upgrade immediately, set `EXPERIMENTAL_UI_LOGIN=false`. This disables the vulnerable authentication path but also breaks CLI SSO and Claude Code gateway login.

### Impact

An internal user can escalate to proxy admin and execute arbitrary commands on the host.

**Discovery Credit:** Hoa X. Nguyen (OPSWAT Unit 515)

A improper authentication vulnerability in Fortinet FortiOS 7.6.0 through 7.6.6 may allow a remote authenticated attacker to gain improper access control via an invalid token after entering a valid username and password

items.title: psqlODBC does not escape a server-supplied column name in its updatable-cursor queries
items.description: For an updatable cursor over a table without OIDs that has an auto-increment int4 column, psqlODBC uses that column to identify rows.
