items.description: Kiwi TCMS before 17.1 contains a hard-coded cryptographic key vulnerability that allows remote attackers to forge signed data by using the publicly known Django SECRET_KEY in tcms/settings/common.py. Attackers can forge or tamper with signed cookie-based messages and django.core.signing payloads, weakening password-reset and session-authentication HMACs on deployments keeping the default.

thirdweb Dashboard through commit 940b3745 contains a missing authorization vulnerability in the fetchClientSecret Next.js server action that allows unauthenticated attackers to create Stripe checkout sessions for other teams. Attackers can invoke the action with a forged Team object containing a victim's stripeCustomerId to obtain Growth plan Checkout session client secrets with attacker-influenced return URLs.

FFmpeg before 9.1 contains a heap out-of-bounds read vulnerability in libavfilter/vf_lut2.c because the second input's pixel format is unrestricted when the output depth option is set. Attackers can supply crafted media such as monoblack BMP or PBM images to index beyond lookup tables, crashing applications or leaking heap contents into output video.

items.title: FFmpeg before 9.1 Out-of-Bounds Read via lut1d Filter Interpolation
items.description: FFmpeg before 9.1 contains an out-of-bounds read vulnerability in the lut1d filter in libavfilter/vf_lut3d.c that allows attackers to read heap memory by supplying planar high bit depth samples above the nominal depth. Attackers can craft 9, 10, 12 or 14 bit planar RGB video processed with a large 1D LUT to crash applications or disclose heap contents in output pixels.

Authentication bypass vulnerabilities in the GlobalProtect™ portal and gateway of Palo Alto Networks PAN-OS® software enables an unauthenticated user to bypass security restrictions and establish an unauthorized VPN connection. 



Panorama, Cloud NGFW, and Prisma® Access are not affected by this vulnerability.

youlai-boot through 2.21.1 contains a missing authorization vulnerability that allows authenticated users to assign arbitrary menu and button permissions to roles via PUT /api/v1/roles/{roleId}/menus. Low-privileged users such as the GUEST test account can grant all permissions to their own role, refreshing the Redis permission cache to gain administrator-equivalent access.

vLLM from 0.22.0 before 0.24.0 contains an improper input validation vulnerability in the Rust gRPC converter that allows remote attackers to bypass max_logprobs limits via CandidateTokens.top_n. Attackers can send Generate or GenerateStream requests with oversized or integer-wrapping top_n values to trigger torch.topk failures that terminate EngineCore.

vLLM from 0.22.0 before 0.24.0 contains a denial of service vulnerability that allows remote attackers to terminate EngineCore by bypassing logprob_token_ids limits in the Rust gRPC frontend. Attackers can send Generate or GenerateStream requests with output_logprobs enabled and more than 128 output_candidates.token_ids, triggering a fatal sampler exception that crashes the engine.

Temporal Server compiles a Worker Controller Instance module, go.temporal.io/auto-scaled-workers, into its Worker Service, and that module registers a compute provider named k8s whose function is to manage workers running in a Kubernetes cluster. The k8s provider built its Kubernetes client from the client configuration supplied in the caller's request rather than from operator configuration, and building and using that client could run a command of the caller's choosing on the Worker Service host, under the account the server process runs as. Two frontend operations reach the provider. CreateWorkerDeploymentVersion requires a namespace write role. ValidateWorkerDeploymentVersionComputeConfig is registered as a read-only namespace operation, so an authenticated caller holding only a read role in a single namespace can reach the provider through it, and that route does not require a worker deployment to already exist. Execution happens while the submitted configuration is validated, so no scaling decision, task arrival, or unusual request sequence is required. Because the Worker Service process holds the persistence credentials for every namespace in the cluster and the cluster's TLS material, the consequence reaches beyond the caller's namespace to the cluster as a whole. The provider is present in the official temporal-server binaries and container images for the affected releases. The control that keeps it unreachable is the compute provider allowlist, the dynamic configuration setting workercontroller.compute_providers.enabled. On Temporal Server 1.31.0 through 1.31.2 that allowlist does not deny by default: when the setting is unset the check is skipped and every registered compute provider is permitted, k8s included, so a stock deployment of those releases is exposed. On 1.31.3 and later 1.31 releases, and on 1.32.0 and later 1.32 releases, the allowlist denies by default, and a deployment is exposed only where k8s has been added to it. The 1.30 release line does not include the Worker Controller Instance module and is unaffected. To determine whether a deployment is affected, check the following together. The deployed Temporal Server version is in an affected range. The Worker Service is running, which it is in the default service set and therefore in a stock deployment. The effective value of workercontroller.compute_providers.enabled contains k8s, or, on 1.31.0 through 1.31.2 only, is unset; check both the global value and every namespace-constrained override, because an override can add k8s for a single namespace. And authorization is configured, meaning a real authorizer and claim mapper are in place; a deployment running with no authorizer already grants every caller unrestricted access to every namespace, so it has no namespace boundary for this to cross. Deployments that use a custom authorizer should also check whether it permits ValidateWorkerDeploymentVersionComputeConfig to callers without namespace write access. The separate per-namespace dynamic configuration setting workercontroller.enabled does not gate the affected path on any affected release.

Improper access control in the Babelfish for PostgreSQL extension versions 1.2-1.5, 2.1-2.15, 3.1-3.12, 4.0-4.8, 5.1-5.4 and in Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL with Babelfish may allow remote authenticated users to elevate their privileges. To remediate this issue, we recommend users upgrade to Babelfish for PostgreSQL extension versions 4.10, 5.6, 6.1 or later. Customers using Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL with Babelfish should upgrade their cluster to Aurora PostgreSQL 13.9.16 (1.5.5), 13.23.3 (1.17.2), 14.6.16 (2.3.5), 14.17.8 (2.12.4), 14.18.6 (2.13.3), 14.19.5 (2.14.2), 14.20.5 (2.15.2), 14.22.3 (2.16.1), 14.23.1 (2.17.0), 15.10.8 (3.8.4), 15.12.8 (3.9.4), 15.13.6 (3.10.3), 15.14.5 (3.11.2), 15.15.5 (3.12.2), 15.17.3 (3.13.1), 15.18.1 (3.14.0), 16.8.8 (4.5.5), 16.9.6 (4.6.3), 16.10.5 (4.7.2), 16.11.5 (4.8.2), 16.13.3 (4.9.1), 16.14.1 (4.10.0), 17.4.8 (5.1.4), 17.5.6 (5.2.3), 17.6.5 (5.3.2), 17.7.5 (5.4.2), 17.9.3 (5.5.1), 17.10.1 (5.6.0), 18.3.4 (6.0.2), 18.4.1 (6.1.0) or later, and apply any pending maintenance to ensure they are on the latest patch.

items.title: Docker Desktop logs can expose stored third-party credentials
items.description: Docker Desktop before version 4.97.0 could write third-party API keys and OAuth access tokens in cleartext to local application logs and diagnostics bundles due to insufficient IPC payload redaction. An attacker with read access to these files could obtain the credentials. These OAuth tokens are not Docker account tokens. Docker Desktop 4.94.0 and 4.95.0 addressed the known logging paths, but logs containing credentials can remain after upgrading. Docker Desktop 4.97.0 fixes the issue and includes cleanup of existing host logs and crash dumps.

vLLM from 0.22.0 before 0.24.0 contains an improper input validation vulnerability in the Rust gRPC Generate and GenerateStream service that forwards unchecked prompt token IDs to EngineCore. Attackers can submit requests with out-of-vocabulary prompt.token_ids values to trigger a fatal embedding lookup failure that terminates EngineCore and leaves the server unhealthy.

vLLM from 0.20.0 before 0.30.0 contains a denial of service vulnerability that allows remote attackers to crash the engine by sending inconsistent multimodal metadata to the disaggregated /inference/v1/generate endpoint. Attackers can replay a valid multimodal item with repeated or overlapping mm_placeholders ranges or mismatched kwargs_data and mm_hashes lists, producing a negative text span in Qwen2.5-VL position construction that terminates the engine.

items.title: FFmpeg through 9.0.2 VAAPI Memory Leak via Abandoned Picture Buffers
items.description: FFmpeg through 9.0.2 contains a memory leak vulnerability in libavcodec/vaapi_decode.c that allows attackers to exhaust memory by supplying streams with slice parse errors. Attackers can craft H.264 or other VAAPI-decoded video where later slices fail to parse on every frame, continuously leaking VA parameter and slice buffers plus driver and heap memory.

items.title: FFmpeg through 9.0.2 Division by Zero via dovi_configure_ext() in dovi_rpuenc.c
items.description: FFmpeg through 9.0.2 contains a division by zero vulnerability in dovi_configure_ext() in libavcodec/dovi_rpuenc.c that allows attackers to crash the process via an unvalidated frame rate denominator. Attackers can supply a crafted HEVC or AV1 input with a nonzero frame rate numerator and zero denominator to the dovi_rpu bitstream filter or libx265, libaom, or libsvtav1 encoders, causing denial of service.

FFmpeg through 9.0.2 contains a NULL pointer dereference vulnerability in the Motion Pixels decoder because mp_decode_frame() ignores init_get_bits() failure. Attackers supplying a roughly 2^28-byte packet through the libavcodec API overflow the bit count, causing reads from a NULL buffer that crash the process.

FFmpeg through 9.0.2 contains a NULL pointer dereference vulnerability in libavcodec/jvdec.c that allows attackers to crash applications by supplying oversized JV video packets. Attackers can pass a roughly 268435460-byte packet through the libavcodec API, overflowing the bit count so decode_frame() reads from a NULL buffer and causes denial of service.

FFmpeg through 9.0.2 contains a NULL pointer dereference vulnerability in mp_decode_frame() in libavcodec/mpegaudiodec_template.c because init_get_bits() failure is ignored after a signed integer overflow. Attackers can pass an oversized packet to the mp3adu decoder through the libavcodec API, causing reads through a NULL buffer that crash the process.

items.title: FFmpeg through 9.0.2 CPU Exhaustion via dts2pts Bitstream Filter
items.description: FFmpeg through 9.0.2 contains an uncontrolled resource consumption vulnerability in the dts2pts bitstream filter that allows attackers to exhaust CPU through unbounded per-packet POC node allocation. Attackers can supply a crafted H.264 packet with many slices of alternating picture order counts, forcing h264_queue_frame() to allocate tree nodes per slice and deny service.

items.title: FFmpeg through 9.0.2 V4L2 M2M Decoder Deadlock via Reference Count Leak
items.description: FFmpeg through 9.0.2 contains a reference count leak in libavcodec/v4l2_buffers.c that allows attackers to deadlock the V4L2 mem2mem decoder on multi-plane capture formats. Attackers can supply crafted H.264, HEVC, or VP9 streams with resolution changes, making ff_v4l2_m2m_codec_reinit() wait forever and hang the decoding application.

items.title: FFmpeg through 9.0.2 Memory Leak via VDPAU Hwaccel Bitstream Buffer Table
items.description: FFmpeg through 9.0.2 contains a memory leak vulnerability in libavcodec/vdpau.c that allows attackers to exhaust heap memory by aborting pictures before end_frame. Attackers can supply crafted H.264 streams with malformed NAL units that repeatedly abandon pictures, leaking the bitstream_buffers table continuously and causing denial of service.

items.title: FFmpeg through 9.0.2 Memory Leak in MJPEG Hwaccel SOF Decoding
items.description: FFmpeg through 9.0.2 contains a memory leak vulnerability in ff_mjpeg_decode_sof() in libavcodec/mjpegdec.c, which overwrites the hwaccel_picture_private pointer without freeing it. Attackers can supply crafted MJPEG streams with repeated SOF markers or failing frames to leak hwaccel private data and hardware buffers under VAAPI or NVDEC decoding.

items.title: FFmpeg through 9.0.2 Assertion Failure DoS via cbs_jpeg_assemble_fragment
items.description: FFmpeg through 9.0.2 contains a denial of service vulnerability in cbs_jpeg_assemble_fragment() that miscounts 0xff stuffing bytes in JPEG scan headers. Attackers can supply a crafted JPEG/MJPEG stream with 0xff in the scan header, triggering an av_assert0 abort when CBS-based bitstream filters process it.

django-tenants 3.4.8 before 4.0.1 contains an SQL injection vulnerability in its PostgreSQL backend that allows attackers to inject SQL through unescaped tenant schema names. Attackers who can choose or influence a schema name can supply quote characters that are interpolated into SET search_path and CREATE, DROP or ALTER SCHEMA statements, letting them read other tenants' data or run SQL as the application's database user.

OpenCTI is an open source platform for managing cyber threat intelligence knowledge and observables. Prior to 7.260706.0, the logsWorkerConfig GraphQL query is authorized with the broad CONNECTORAPI capability and returns Elasticsearch connection details including elasticsearch_username, elasticsearch_password, elasticsearch_api_key, the URL, index, proxy, and TLS-verification setting. A holder of any connector API bearer token can retrieve this credential material. If the returned credentials are valid and Elasticsearch is reachable, the caller can directly read, modify, or delete OpenCTI indices and audit history outside application-layer role, marking, organization, and audit controls, with the practical impact bounded by the credentials' privileges and network reachability. This issue is fixed in version 7.260706.0.

Treeio through 2.0 contains an insecure deserialization vulnerability in UpdateRecord.get_format_strings and ModuleSetting.loads that allows staff users to execute code via unverified pickle data. Attackers can store a crafted base64 pickle payload in an UpdateRecord format_strings field through the Django admin, executing Python code as the web server user when news feeds render.

DBHub is a database MCP server for Postgres, MySQL, SQL Server, Oracle, MariaDB, SQLite. Prior to 0.22.6, read-only SQL validation can be bypassed on the MySQL and MariaDB connectors. In `src/utils/sql-parser.ts`, `scanSingleLineComment` treats every double dash as a comment start, whereas MySQL and MariaDB require following whitespace, a control character, or the end of the line. The read-only check in `src/tools/execute-sql.ts` validates split statements with `isReadOnlySQL`, but `src/connectors/mysql/index.ts` and `src/connectors/mariadb/index.ts` execute the original string with `multipleStatements` enabled. A double dash followed by a non-whitespace character can therefore hide a subsequent write or destructive DDL statement from the validator while the database interprets the dashes as minus operators and executes both statements. Anyone able to influence the assistant's SQL, including through prompt injection in content the assistant reads, can bypass read-only mode to modify or drop database data, subject to the database account's privileges. PostgreSQL is not affected by this path because its double-dash parsing agrees with the checker and its connector executes individual split statements. This issue is fixed in version 0.22.6.

Execution After Redirect (EAR) vulnerability in Apache Tomcat.



This issue affects Apache Tomcat: from 11.0.0-M1 through 11.0.26, from 10.1.0-M1 through 10.1.60, from 9.0.0.M1 through 9.0.122.



The following versions were EOL at the time the CVE was created but are 
known to be affected: from 8.5.0 through 8.5.100, from 7.0.0 through 7.0.109. Other unsupported versions may also be affected.




Users are recommended to upgrade to version 11.0.27, 10.1.61, 9.0.123, which fixes the issue.

items.title: DBHub: MySQL and MariaDB comment interpretation bypasses read-only SQL validation
items.description:
The read-only mode can be bypassed on the MySQL and MariaDB connectors. In read-only mode a caller can still execute arbitrary write and DDL statements (for example DROP TABLE), which defeats the protection that read-only mode is meant to provide when a database is exposed to an AI agent.

Root cause

The problem is a mismatch between how DBHub's SQL parser handles single-line comments and how MySQL and MariaDB actually parse them.

In src/utils/sql-parser.ts, scanSingleLineComment treats "--" as the start of a comment no matter what character follows it. MySQL and MariaDB only begin a "--" comment when the two dashes are followed by whitespace, a control character, or the end of the line. Otherwise the dashes are read as two minus signs and the rest of the line is ordinary SQL.

The read-only check in src/tools/execute-sql.ts splits the input and validates each statement with isReadOnlySQL, but the connector then executes the original, unmodified string. The MySQL and MariaDB connectors open their connection pool with multipleStatements: true (src/connectors/mysql/index.ts:54 and src/connectors/mariadb/index.ts:53) and run the whole string in a single call.

Because of this, the following payload:

    SELECT 1--1;DROP TABLE victim

is seen by DBHub as a single SELECT statement, since everything after "--" is treated as a comment and the read-only check passes. MySQL and MariaDB instead parse it as "SELECT 1 - -1" followed by "DROP TABLE victim" and execute both statements.

Proof of concept

1) DBHub's own parser. Running splitSQLStatements and isReadOnlySQL from this repository on the payload returns a single statement and readOnly = true, so the query is allowed in read-only mode. The same code correctly rejects "SELECT 1; DROP TABLE victim", which confirms that the "--1" is what gets through.

2) Execution. Connecting to MariaDB 11.4 with mysql2 and multipleStatements: true (the same option the connector uses) and sending the payload returns 2 for the first statement, which confirms "--" was not treated as a comment, and then drops the table. The table exists before the call and is gone afterwards.

Impact

Read-only mode is the control operators rely on to let an assistant read from a database without being able to change it. With this bypass, anyone who can influence the SQL the assistant sends, most realistically through prompt injection in content the assistant reads, can perform writes and destructive DDL against MySQL and MariaDB. PostgreSQL is not affected by this path, because it treats "--" as a comment regardless and executes each split statement individually.

Affected code (current main, commit e99c3aa9, package version 0.22.3)

- src/utils/sql-parser.ts — scanSingleLineComment does not require whitespace after "--"
- src/tools/execute-sql.ts — validates the split statements but executes the original string
- src/connectors/mysql/index.ts and src/connectors/mariadb/index.ts — multipleStatements: true

Suggested fix

The most reliable fix is to stop executing the original string: run only the statements that were validated, and disable multipleStatements on the MySQL and MariaDB connections unless it is genuinely required. As defense in depth, make the comment scanner dialect-aware so that for MySQL and MariaDB "--" only starts a comment when it is followed by whitespace, a control character, or the end of the line, similar to the handling already in place for MySQL conditional comments.

A race condition was addressed with improved locking. This issue is fixed in Safari 27.2, iOS 26.7.2 and iPadOS 26.7.2, iOS 27.2 and iPadOS 27.2, macOS Golden Gate 27.2, tvOS 27.2, visionOS 27.2, watchOS 27.2. Processing maliciously crafted web content may lead to an unexpected process termination.

items.title: Bake filesystem path entitlements approval can be skipped in some multi-target builds
items.description: In Docker Buildx versions v0.19.0 through v0.38.0, an untrusted Bake definition that builds multiple targets together may expose files accessible to the Buildx client without the expected fs.read approval. Under certain conditions, filesystem paths from some targets are not verified against the approved entitlements. Users who run untrusted Bake definitions may be affected. The issue is fixed in v0.38.1.

items.title: Kubeflow Pipelines: Reflected XSS in the frontend pod information and events error responses
items.description:
## Summary

The Kubeflow Pipelines frontend reflected untrusted pod names and namespaces into HTML error responses from the pod-information and pod-events routes. An attacker could craft a link that causes JavaScript to execute in the frontend's origin when a user follows it and reaches an affected error response.

Affected routes include `/pipeline/k8s/pod` and `/pipeline/k8s/pod/events` (the deployment's configured base path may differ).

## Impact and prerequisites

Successful exploitation requires a victim to open an attacker-supplied link and reach the vulnerable response. JavaScript execution may expose information accessible to the victim's browser or perform actions in the application's origin.

The attacker does not need an account merely to construct and deliver the link. The victim must satisfy the deployment's authentication and route-access requirements. Cookie theft depends on cookie attributes and deployment protections; it is not guaranteed. The submitted evidence does not establish an availability impact or server-side code execution.

## Technical details

The pod handlers pass `podname` and `podnamespace` query values to `getPod` and `listPodEvents` in `frontend/server/k8s-helper.ts`. Before remediation, failure messages incorporated those values, along with backend error details, and were returned as HTML-capable string responses.

Kubernetes rejecting an invalid resource name did not prevent the issue: the rejected name could still be included in the frontend's error response.

[PR #12295](https://github.com/kubeflow/pipelines/pull/12295) changed the error construction to validate pod names and namespaces with `isAllowedResourceName`. Invalid values produce a constant error message instead of reflecting the supplied value, and backend error details are no longer included in these responses. The change includes invalid-resource-name tests.

## Affected versions and remediation

Affected product: the Kubeflow Pipelines frontend server, identified as `ghcr.io/kubeflow/kfp-frontend`. Historical releases may use earlier image registry names.

Upgrade to **KFP 2.15.0 or later**.

The fix merged on October 10, 2025, in commit [fedc25e3f7251933d4a37b964bc3e8176beea28e](https://github.com/kubeflow/pipelines/commit/fedc25e3f7251933d4a37b964bc3e8176beea28e). It is first present in the **2.15.0** release, published November 25, 2025.

The affected range is recorded as `< 2.15.0`. The original introduction version and separate maintenance-branch backports have not been established. These are KFP component versions, not Kubeflow platform or Python SDK versions.

## Distinction from existing artifact XSS

[CVE-2023-6571](https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-7rvc-xw75-43jf), tracked in the repository as [GHSA-j9xw-rrjg-2p9r](https://github.com/kubeflow/pipelines/security/advisories/GHSA-j9xw-rrjg-2p9r), documents reflection of the artifact `source` parameter in an unknown-storage-source error.

This report concerns different handlers and error construction: pod information and pod events. The artifact-source fix in [PR #9844](https://github.com/kubeflow/pipelines/pull/9844), released in 2.0.2, did not repair these pod responses. They required the later change in #12295.

This independently fixable pod-route defect is tracked as CVE-2026-88986. It does not broaden CVE-2023-6571 or absorb artifact-content rendering and other XSS reports.

## Attribution

**@pwny0** submitted this report on September 23, 2023, and retains the reporter credit.

**@JerT33** authored the remediation in PR #12295. Fix attribution is separate from vulnerability-report attribution.

items.title: Kiwi TCMS account confirmation open redirect through protocol-relative URLs
items.description:
## Summary

In Kiwi TCMS version 16.1, the fix for CVE-2026-54724 (open redirect via unvalidated `next` parameter) in the account confirmation endpoint is incomplete. The validation uses `startswith("/")` to check if the redirect URL is local, but this is bypassed by protocol-relative URLs like `//evil.com` which start with `/` but redirect the browser to an external attacker-controlled domain. 16.1’s incomplete mitigation still allows protocol-relative destinations and earlier releases lack the mitigation.

## Vulnerable Code

In `tcms/kiwi_auth/views.py`, the `Confirm` view (line ~113):

    def get_redirect_url(self, *args, **kwargs):
        self.url = self.request.GET.get("next", reverse("core-views-index"))
        if not self.url.startswith("/"):
            self.url = reverse("core-views-index")

The check `startswith("/")` passes for `//evil.com` because it begins with `/`, but browsers interpret `//evil.com` as a protocol-relative URL that redirects to `https://evil.com` (or `http://evil.com` depending on the current page's protocol).

## Proof of Concept

    GET /confirm/<activation_key>/?next=//evil.com/phishing HTTP/1.1
    Host: kiwi.example.com

Response:

    HTTP/1.1 302 Found
    Location: //evil.com/phishing

The browser follows the redirect to `https://evil.com/phishing`.

Verification:

    >>> url = "//evil.com/phishing"
    >>> url.startswith("/")
    True  # passes the check!

## Impact

An attacker can craft a confirmation link that, after the user confirms their account, redirects them to a phishing page. This is useful for:

- Credential phishing (fake login page on attacker domain)
- Malware delivery after trusted action
- Social engineering (user trusts the link because it's from the legitimate Kiwi TCMS instance)

The attack requires sending a crafted activation link to a user who is registering, or intercepting/predicting the activation key.

## Suggested Fix

Use Django's `url_has_allowed_host_and_scheme()` utility instead of a simple `startswith` check:

    from django.utils.http import url_has_allowed_host_and_scheme

    def get_redirect_url(self, *args, **kwargs):
        self.url = self.request.GET.get("next", reverse("core-views-index"))
        if not url_has_allowed_host_and_scheme(
            self.url,
            allowed_hosts={self.request.get_host()},
            require_https=self.request.is_secure(),
        ):
            self.url = reverse("core-views-index")

This properly rejects protocol-relative URLs, absolute URLs to other hosts, and other bypass patterns.

Fixed in Version 16.2

items.title: Microsoft Security Advisory CVE-2026-109476 - ASP.NET Core Information Disclosure Vulnerability
items.description: Improper encoding or escaping of output in ASP.NET Core allows an unauthorized attacker to disclose information over a network.

Winter CMS is a content management system built on the Laravel PHP framework. From 1.0.319 until 1.2.14, Backend\Classes\Controller::actionExists() accepts public handler-shaped methods as page actions, so a top-level GET request can invoke state-changing backend AJAX handlers without a CSRF token. Because backend routes use Route::any, CSRF validation skips GET, and the default SameSite=Lax session cookie is sent on cross-site navigation, an unauthenticated attacker can induce an authorized backend user to follow a link such as /backend/system/eventlogs/index_onEmptyLog. Affected handlers in the backend, CMS, and system modules can truncate logs, reset settings, alter backend user state, or delete CMS templates, while URL path segments can select a target record. This issue is fixed in version 1.2.14.

items.title: Action Pack: Missing SameSite attribute on session cookies from Action Pack session stores
items.description: Action Pack is a framework for handling and responding to web requests. Prior to 8.1.4.1 and 8.0.5.2, Action Pack session stores other than ActionDispatch::Session::CookieStore (CacheStore, MemCacheStore, and third-party stores built on AbstractStore, AbstractSecureStore or the session mixins) write the session cookie without a SameSite attribute, regardless of config.action_dispatch.cookies_same_site_protection, which defaults to :lax. Only CookieStore applies the configured policy. In browsers that do not treat a cookie without the attribute as SameSite=Lax, a cross-site request could carry the session cookie, possibly leading to cross-site request forgery against actions that do not verify an authenticity token, such as those of API-only applications. Applications are affected when they use a session store other than CookieStore and do not pass same_site: to config.session_store. This issue is fixed in versions 8.1.4.1 and 8.0.5.2.

An untrusted search path issue in Aurora PostgreSQL dialect detection in the AWS Advanced Go Wrapper from release 2026-04-06 (awssql/v2.0.0) and before release 2026-07-29 (awssql/v2.0.3) could allow a remote authenticated user to escalate privileges to those of another database user, including a member of the rds_superuser role, via a crafted function that runs when that user connects to an Aurora PostgreSQL cluster through an affected version of the wrapper.



To remediate this issue, users should upgrade to the AWS Advanced Go Wrapper release 2026-07-29 (awssql/v2.0.3) or later.

The pREST database REST API in Zenitel Connect firmware before 1.11.0 signs and verifies JWTs with the platform CA private key, which is stored on a data volume shared between containers, and sets the PostgreSQL session role from the unvalidated sub claim of each request while connected to the database as the "postgres" superuser, which allows local attackers who can read the platform CA private key from the container filesystem to execute database operations as the PostgreSQL superuser, including reading the master encryption key and password hashes, via a forged JWT with sub=postgres sent to the pREST API.

Contentlayer @contentlayer/core through 0.3.4 contains a code injection vulnerability that allows attackers to inject JavaScript by embedding single quotes in content file names. Attackers can add a content file whose name breaks out of the import specifier in makeDataExportFile(), executing injected code when contentlayer dev or a Next.js dev server imports the generated module.

A cross-site scripting vulnerability exists in Win Bird JYUGYO SHIEN browser extensions for Google Chrome and Microsoft Edge, which allows an attacker to execute arbitrary script in the user's web browser.
In JetBrains TeamCity before 2026.2 reflected XSS in Kubernetes cloud profile namespace and deployment choosers was possible

ATXP Gemini CLI extension through 1.0.0 contains an OS command injection vulnerability in runAtxp() that allows attackers to execute shell commands through unsanitized MCP tool parameters. Attackers can plant instructions in email or SMS content to inject $() or backtick substitutions into parameters like message_id, subject, or query, running commands as the user.

A flaw was found in Ansible Operator Plugins. A low-privileged Kubernetes user can exploit a Jinja2 template injection vulnerability by crafting malicious custom resource (CR) specification values. These values are processed by Ansible without proper sanitization, allowing embedded Jinja2 expressions to be executed within the operator pod. This can lead to arbitrary code execution and privilege escalation, granting the attacker control over the operator's service account with cluster-wide permissions.

Vulnerability in the MySQL Server, MySQL Cluster product of Oracle MySQL (component: Server: Security: Encryption).  Supported versions that are affected are MySQL Server: 9.7.0-9.7.3, 26.7.0-26.7.1; MySQL Cluster: 9.7.0-9.7.3 and  26.7.0-26.7.1. Easily exploitable vulnerability allows high privileged attacker with network access via multiple protocols to compromise MySQL Server, MySQL Cluster.  Successful attacks of this vulnerability can result in unauthorized ability to cause a hang or frequently repeatable crash (complete DOS) of MySQL Server, MySQL Cluster and  unauthorized read access to a subset of MySQL Server, MySQL Cluster accessible data. CVSS 3.1 Base Score 5.5 (Confidentiality and Availability impacts).  CVSS Vector: (CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:H/UI:N/S:U/C:L/I:N/A:H).

FFmpeg before 9.1 contains a stack-based buffer overflow vulnerability in ff_rtmp_packet_write() in libavformat/rtmppkt.c that allows malicious RTMP servers to overflow a 16-byte header buffer. Attackers can send a Set Chunk Size packet on a high channel id with an extended timestamp, which handle_chunk_size() echoes back, corrupting the publishing client's stack.

FFmpeg before 9.1 contains a heap out-of-bounds write vulnerability in the deflicker filter that lets attackers corrupt heap memory via unclamped high bit depth luma samples. Attackers can supply crafted video whose luma values exceed the nominal depth, making calc_avgy16() increment counters past the histogram allocation, causing crashes or possibly code execution.

FFmpeg before 8.1.3 and 9.x before 9.0.2 contains a heap buffer overflow vulnerability in the Cook multichannel decoder in libavcodec/cook.c that fails to verify subpacket channel masks are disjoint. Attackers can supply a crafted RealMedia Cook stream with overlapping subpacket masks, causing cook_decode_frame() to write decoded samples beyond allocated output planes in any application decoding the file.

FFmpeg before 8.1.3 and 9.x before 9.0.2 contains a heap buffer overflow vulnerability in the DVD subtitle encoder that underestimates RLE output size for odd-width rectangles. Attackers can supply files with crafted bitmap subtitles that, when transcoded to the dvdsub encoder, write past the output buffer and corrupt heap memory.

FFmpeg before 8.1.3 and 9.x before 9.0.2 contains an out-of-bounds write vulnerability in the VVC decoder's sh_entry_points() function in libavcodec/vvc/ps.c. Attackers can supply a crafted VVC (H.266) bitstream whose SPS/PPS tile and WPP layout produces excess entry points, overflowing entry_point_start_ctu and corrupting decoder memory.

FFmpeg before 8.1.3 and 9.x before 9.0.2 contains a heap out-of-bounds write vulnerability in the APAC decoder in libavcodec/apac.c caused by an unreset bitstream index. Attackers can supply a crafted APAC file whose growing bitstream_index triggers an integer overflow, bypassing the reallocation check so memcpy() corrupts heap memory or crashes the application.

items.title: identrail: Cross-tenant GitHub installation binding without ownership verification
items.description: identrail is a machine identity security platform for AWS, GitHub/OIDC, and Kubernetes. Prior to 1.0.2, the default-on `POST /v1/workspaces/:workspace_id/projects/:project_id/github/connect/complete` endpoint in `internal/api/router.go` accepts `installation_id` from the request body or `X-GitHub-Installation-ID` header without verifying the installation belongs to the caller's workspace. `CompleteGitHubConnection` in `internal/api/github_connect.go` rigorously binds `state` to the caller's tenant, workspace, and project, but checks only that the installation ID is positive before persisting it as the caller's connection. `ListInstallationRepositories` in `internal/connectors/github/repositories.go` invokes token creation through `internal/connectors/github/app.go` and `POST /app/installations/{installationId}/access_tokens`, using the application's JWT. An authenticated tenant who starts a legitimate connection can supply another customer's non-secret installation ID to read the victim organization's private repository inventory, content, and metadata or drive posture scans, provided identrail's GitHub App is installed there. The default-off V2 `CompleteGitHubConnector` path shares the installation-ownership gap and additionally matches pending `state` without rechecking caller scope. This issue is fixed in version 1.0.2.

The Model Context Protocol Python SDK is the official Python SDK for Model Context Protocol servers and clients. From 1.8.0 until 1.30.0 and 2.2.0, streamable_http_client, streamablehttp_client, sse_client, ClientSessionGroup, OAuth, and create_mcp_http_client client paths enable follow_redirects and follow redirects to a different origin, forwarding caller-supplied custom credential headers and, for 307 or 308 responses, the request body. An attacker who can influence a trusted endpoint's redirect destination can receive that material. This issue is fixed in versions 1.30.0 and 2.2.0.

Autobahn Python is a WebSocket and WAMP implementation for Python that supports Twisted and asyncio. From 26.7.1 until 26.10.1, PerMessageBrotli.decompress_message_data in compress_brotli.py calls the Brotli decompressor without an output limit and checks maxMessagePayloadSize only after a complete frame has been inflated. An unauthenticated WebSocket client can send a small, highly compressed frame that allocates hundreds of MiB before rejection, causing memory-exhaustion denial of service on servers that enable the opt-in permessage-brotli feature through the compress extra. Deflate and bzip2 already enforce the remaining output budget and are outside this residual vulnerability. This issue is fixed in version 26.10.1.

A double free in the X.509 name constraints enforcement of GnuTLS 3.8.13 on all platforms allows a remote attacker to cause a denial of service (application crash) via a certificate chain containing a NameConstraints extension processed while the application is under memory pressure. When an already populated name constraints object is reinitialized, previously freed list pointers are not cleared, so a memory allocation failure precisely at reinitialization leaves a dangling pointer that is freed again during a later cleanup.
Uncontrolled resource consumption in Windows Internet Information Services allows an unauthorized attacker to deny service over a network.
Integer underflow (wrap or wraparound) in Windows Internet Information Services allows an unauthorized attacker to deny service over a network.

undici is an HTTP client for Node.js. In versions 7.0.0 through 7.30.1 and 8.0.0 through 8.12.3, when the cache interceptor is composed with a downstream handler that throws during response processing (such as the built-in dump interceptor exceeding its maxSize, or the decompress interceptor rejecting more than five Content-Encoding values), a throw raised asynchronously while a cached response is replayed escapes as an uncaught exception or unhandled promise rejection and terminates the Node.js process. A malicious or compromised HTTP server can crash any such client by serving a cacheable response that triggers the throw on replay, including on a 304 revalidation of a stale entry, so the impact is availability only. The issue is fixed in undici 7.30.2 and 8.12.4, and users should upgrade to one of those versions or later. As a workaround, avoid composing the cache interceptor with a response handler that throws during response processing until upgrading.

undici is an HTTP client for Node.js. In versions 7.0.0 through 7.30.1 and 8.0.0 through 8.12.3, the redirect interceptor strips sensitive headers such as Authorization, Cookie, Proxy-Authorization, and Host when a request is redirected to a different origin, but when request headers are supplied as an array of name and value tuples (a valid documented input, for example from Object.entries), the redirect handler misreads them as a flat list so the header names never match and the sensitive headers are not removed. If a header-normalizing interceptor such as cache or deduplicate is composed outside the redirect interceptor, it then serializes the retained headers onto the cross-origin request, disclosing the caller's origin-bound credentials to the unrelated redirect destination. This is a representation-dependent bypass of the cross-origin header stripping added in CVE-2024-30260. The issue is fixed in undici 7.30.2 and 8.12.4, and users should upgrade to one of those versions or later. As a workaround, supply request headers as a plain object or a flat name and value array rather than an array of tuples, or compose the redirect interceptor outside the normalizing interceptor.

undici is an HTTP client for Node.js. In versions 7.15.0 through 7.30.1 and 8.0.0 through 8.12.3, fetch verifies Subresource Integrity metadata by splitting the integrity string on a single space, but the SRI grammar separates metadata by ASCII whitespace, which also includes the horizontal tab. An integrity value whose digest is preceded by a tab or other ASCII whitespace is parsed as a single unrecognized token and skipped, and when no recognized algorithm remains undici treats the integrity list as empty and accepts the response, so a server returning a body different from the pinned digest passes the check. An application that pins a response with a valid but whitespace-surrounded SRI value receives attacker-controlled bytes with no integrity error, and the attacker needs only to control the response body, not the integrity metadata. The issue is fixed in undici 7.30.2 and 8.12.4, and users should upgrade to one of those versions or later. As a workaround, supply SRI integrity metadata without surrounding whitespace, using a single space to separate multiple digests.

undici is an HTTP client for Node.js. In versions 7.0.0 through 7.30.1 and 8.0.0 through 8.12.3, when an Agent composes the redirect and shared cache interceptors, a cached response that is revalidated with a conditional request can be validated by a 304 Not Modified from a different origin. When the origin that stored the response redirects the conditional revalidation request to another origin, the redirect handler strips origin-bound credential headers but not the cache-generated If-None-Match or If-Modified-Since validators, so the redirect destination receives the original origin's validator and undici treats its 304 as successful revalidation of the stored representation. As a result, a shared cache can serve the original origin's stored authenticated response, including one gated by Authorization, to a later unauthenticated caller. The issue is fixed in undici 7.30.2 and 8.12.4, and users should upgrade to one of those versions or later. As a workaround, compose the interceptors as cache then redirect, use per-origin dispatchers and cache stores, or disable shared caching on redirect-capable requests.

Incorrect authorization in the issuer resolution logic in AWS Private CA Connector for Kubernetes (aws-privateca-issuer) before v1.10.1 might allow an authenticated remote user to obtain certificates, including subordinate CA certificates, signed by a cluster-scoped AWS Private CA issuer that their approval policy does not authorize.



To remediate this issue, users should upgrade aws-privateca-issuer to version v1.10.1 or the AWS Private CA Connector for Kubernetes EKS add-on to version v1.10.1-eksbuild.1, and update any certificate requests, Certificate resources, or Ingress annotations whose issuerRef.kind is missing, incorrect, or does not match the referenced issuer, since v1.10.1 requires issuerRef.kind to be exactly AWSPCAIssuer or AWSPCAClusterIssuer and to match the issuer it references.

GnuTLS v3.8.13 does not properly enforce name constraints, as demonstrated by a permitted subtree violation for "EE O=Evil accepted although outside permitted O=Good." NOTE: the Supplier does not consider this an actionable security vulnerability because of its "threat model doesn't consider attacks only possible by modifying anything within the trust boundary (private keys, trusted certificate authorities and their issued certificates including intermediate CAs, etc.)" policy.

An improper input handling vulnerability in the GlobalProtect™ gateway of Palo Alto Networks PAN-OS software enables an authenticated user to establish a GlobalProtect session using the identity of another user. 

Cloud NGFW and Panorama are not affected by this vulnerability.

pgEdge RAG Server is an API server for retrieval-augmented generation over PostgreSQL content using pgvector. Prior to 2.0.0, the BM25 keyword index is a single per-pipeline object shared by the unauthenticated query endpoint, and concurrent requests lock its clear, refill, and search operations separately. This allows one request to search a corpus populated through another request's search filter, which can return documents belonging to a different tenant or customer without malformed input. The affected responses cannot be identified retrospectively from the server logs. This issue is fixed in version 2.0.0.

ImageMagick before 7.1.2-35 contains a code injection vulnerability in the MAGICK, XBM, XPM and UIL encoders that allows local attackers to inject content via crafted filenames. Attackers with access to the output directory and control over the filename can inject additional headers or code into the generated image source output.

items.title: pmo-platform: eval-viewer (pmo-skill-refiner): symlink-following arbitrary file read, verbatim secret/PII embedding, and CSRF write on the local review server
items.description: pmo-platform is a modular PMO and release-management platform for Claude Code. Prior to 3.73, release/skills/pmo-skill-refiner/eval-viewer/generate_review.py and viewer.html contain three security weaknesses in the local evaluation viewer. During workspace scanning and generation, _find_runs_recursive and build_run follow symlinks and embed_file reads their targets without confining resolved paths to the workspace, although the server do_GET path is not a traversal surface. embed_file also reads output files without a size cap or redaction, allowing secrets or personally identifiable information to be embedded in a no-auth locally served page or shareable static file. Separately, do_POST /api/feedback writes caller-supplied JSON without authentication, an Origin check, or a cross-site request forgery token, allowing a malicious page or DNS-rebound localhost target to modify feedback while the server runs. This issue is fixed in version 3.73.

items.title: compose-lint: A pull request can make compose-lint quote a secret from a CI-generated `.env` into its findings
items.description:
### Impact

Since 0.22.0, compose-lint fills in `${VAR}` references from the `.env` beside the Compose file, as Compose does. The documentation says values under `environment:` are never resolved from a `.env`, "that is where secrets live". But `image:` values are resolved, and CL-0004 and CL-0019 quote the resolved image in their message and fix text.

Some CI workflows write secrets into that `.env` before linting or building. In such a workflow, a pull request that changes one line to `image: "${DB_PASSWORD}"`, or `image: "nginx:${DB_PASSWORD}"`, gets the secret's value quoted in a finding. The finding reaches the job log, JSON output, and the SARIF uploaded to Code Scanning. GitHub masks registered secrets in the job log, but not in uploaded JSON or SARIF artifacts or in Code Scanning alert text. The pass/fail result is not affected.

This needs a workflow that writes secrets into the `.env` beside the Compose file *and* runs on pull requests from authors who should not see them. Pull requests from forks normally run without secrets, so the common setup is not exposed, which is why this is scored as low confidentiality impact. Where the conditions hold, such as a `pull_request_target` workflow, pull requests from branches in the same repository, or a self-hosted runner that keeps a populated `.env` in the checkout, the whole value is disclosed.

Found during an internal pre-1.0 security review.

**GitHub Action.** Action tags v0.22.0 through v0.31.0 install their own compose-lint version and are affected. Earlier tags install the newest release unless `version:` is set, and so currently install an affected one.

**Docker image.** `composelint/compose-lint` tags 0.22.0 through 0.31.0, the matching minor tags, and `latest` are affected when the `.env` is mounted with the project.

### Patches

Fixed in 0.32.0. Rules still grade the value the sibling `.env` substituted, but findings, fix guidance and notes quote the `${NAME}` reference in its place, in text, JSON and SARIF. A value shorter than 8 characters is shown as written, because short values are also words the guidance itself uses; `docs/what-a-run-reads.md` states this limit.

### Workarounds

- Upgrade to 0.32.0 or later.
- Run with `--no-env`, which skips the sibling `.env`.
- Don't write secrets into the `.env` beside the Compose file in a job that lints untrusted pull requests.

### Reproduction

```
project/.env          DB_PASSWORD=example-secret      (written by CI, not committed)
project/compose.yml   services: {web: {image: "${DB_PASSWORD}"}}
```

`compose-lint --format sarif compose.yml` reports CL-0004 with the message `Image 'example-secret' has no tag, ...`.

items.title: compose-lint: A `.compose-lint.yml` symlinked outside the project is read, and a parse error quotes part of the target
items.description:
### Impact

compose-lint automatically reads a `.compose-lint.yml` policy file beside the Compose file. It is meant to read nothing outside the project directory, but it follows that file if it is a symlink, wherever it points.

A pull request can commit `.compose-lint.yml` as a symlink to a file on the CI runner. If the target is not valid YAML, the error compose-lint reports quotes part of the line the parser failed on. That quote reaches the job log (standard error), JSON `errors[]`, and the SARIF `toolExecutionNotifications`, which the Action uploads to Code Scanning. The run exits 2.

What can be read is small. The quote is cut to about 30 characters around the error position, and the attacker cannot choose which line of the target the parser fails on. For an INI-style credentials file, this was the start of the second line (`aws_access_key_id = ` followed by the first characters of the value). Targets in `KEY=value` form, and YAML files that parse, disclosed no values in testing. The pass/fail result is not affected. On a public repository, the job log is visible to the pull request's author.

The Compose file loader stopped quoting source lines in parse errors in 0.25.0 (GHSA-whr6-fgpq-fpv9). The policy loader did not.

Found during an internal pre-1.0 security review.

**GitHub Action.** Action tags v0.18.0 through v0.31.0 install their own compose-lint version and are affected. Earlier tags install the newest release unless `version:` is set, and so currently install an affected one.

**Docker image.** `composelint/compose-lint` tags 0.3.3 through 0.31.0, the matching minor tags, and `latest` are affected. Inside the container, a symlink resolves within the container, so what can be read is the container's own files and anything mounted into it.

### Patches

Fixed in 0.32.0. A `.compose-lint.yml` discovered in the working directory that resolves outside it is refused with exit 2 rather than read, and a policy parse error no longer quotes the line it failed on, matching the Compose loader. `--config` is read as given. 0.32.0 also stops following a Compose file that is a symlink to a target outside the checkout.

### Workarounds

- Upgrade to 0.32.0 or later.
- Run with an explicit `--config` pointing at a policy file inside the project; the automatic lookup is then skipped.
- Don't run compose-lint on untrusted pull requests on a machine whose files outside the checkout hold credentials.

### Reproduction

```
project/.compose-lint.yml -> /path/outside/project/credentials   (symlink)
project/compose.yml          services: {web: {image: nginx:1.27}}
```

`compose-lint --format sarif compose.yml` exits 2, and the notification text quotes the start of the target's second line.

pgEdge RAG Server is an API server for retrieval-augmented generation over PostgreSQL content using pgvector. Prior to 2.0.0, the unauthenticated query API in internal/server/handlers.go returns err.Error() from failed LLM provider calls, preserving provider-controlled error text that can quote a partially masked submitted API key. A remote caller can cause an authentication failure and obtain part of the operator's credential for the third-party provider account through the query API error response. This issue is fixed in version 2.0.0.

Winter CMS is a content management system built on the Laravel PHP framework. Prior to 1.2.14, the ImportExportController behavior applies userHasAccess() only to the import() and export() page actions, while Backend\Classes\Controller::execAjaxHandlers() dispatches onImport(), onImportLoadForm(), onImportLoadColumnSampleForm(), onExport(), and onExportLoadForm() before those gated actions run, and the separately reachable download() action also lacks the granular export check. An authenticated backend user with a valid session and coarse access through $requiredPermissions, but without the configured import[permissions] or export[permissions], can use the import handlers to write or overwrite records and can use onExport() followed by download() to retrieve the complete dataset exposed by the export model. Controllers without granular permission keys are unaffected because userHasAccess() is intentionally default-permissive. This issue is fixed in version 1.2.14.

CAST Imaging has multiple path traversal vulnerabilities in various endpoints. The application does not properly validate the path parameters, allowing an authenticated attacker to use "../" sequences to escape the intended directory and read arbitrary files.


Critically, by reading "/proc/self/environ", the attacker can obtain environment variables containing sensitive credentials such as Keycloak and PostgreSQL passwords, leading to full server compromise and administrative access.


The vulnerability has only been confirmed in version 3.6.2 but may also affect other versions. The vendor did not provide the affected version range, but assured that the vulnerability is fixed "in newer versions".

items.title: sanitize_message() address regex is lowercase-only and does not match PIL's uppercase __repr__, leaking live heap addresses to unauthenticated clients
items.description:
### Summary

`sanitize_message()` scrubs heap addresses from error messages with the regex `r" at 0x[0-9a-f]+>"` - lowercase only, no `IGNORECASE`. `PIL.Image.Image.__repr__` formats its address as `0x{id(self):X}` - uppercase. The scrubber structurally cannot match the one object class both parent advisories are about.

A 564-byte PNG sent to an unauthenticated endpoint returns a live heap address of the running server process.

This is not a new hardening proposal. The CVE-2026-54236 advisory explicitly recommended widening this exact regex to `[0-9a-fA-F]`; three months on it is byte-identical.

### Details

#### The mismatch

```python
# the scrubber
r" at 0x[0-9a-f]+>"

# what PIL actually emits
# PIL/Image.py — Image.__repr__
"<%s.%s image mode=%s size=%dx%d at 0x%X>" % (..., id(self))
```

The parent CVE's own lowercase `BytesIO` shape is scrubbed correctly today. PIL's uppercase form is not.

#### The sink

`vllm/multimodal/processing/context.py:347` f-strings the PIL objects into any HF-processor failure message, which is returned to the client.

#### Why the recommendation was dropped - the in-tree answer

`test_error_sanitization.py` already contains a case with the id `pil-image-repr`, asserting that the PIL form is scrubbed. Its input is a hand-written **lowercase** literal that PIL never emits. I ran both halves against the same object class: the test passes, and a real `repr()` leaks.

That is why a documented, accepted recommendation looked already-covered and was never implemented. Any fix must include a test built from a real `repr()`, not from a literal.

#### Related PRs inspected at diff level (neither closes this)

* **PR #35492** adds `sanitize_message` to a new Responses-API WebSocket path, continuing the CVE-2026-54236 remediation - but does not widen the regex, and its new test also uses a lowercase literal.
* **PR #52120** patches a stale path (`serve/utils/api_utils.py`) and only touches the path regex's backtracking.

### Reachability - default configuration, no authentication

* `api_key` defaults to `None`, and `AuthenticationMiddleware` is installed only when a key is configured - a default `vllm serve` is entirely unauthenticated.
* Even with `--api-key` set, `GUARDED_PREFIX = ("/v1", "/v2", "/inference", "/cohere")`, so `/tokenize` remains unauthenticated.
* Default-on for any multimodal deployment.

### Impact

Information disclosure: a live heap address of the API-server process, to an unauthenticated remote client. CWE-532.

**Scope, stated plainly.** This is information disclosure, not memory corruption. It is Stage 1 of the chain CVE-2026-22778 was rated 9.8 for - an ASLR defeat that made the second stage reliable. **Stage 2 is patched at the current OpenCV floor, so I am not claiming RCE.** The value of the fix is that the disclosure primitive the chain depended on is still live, and the advisory that recommended closing it was never acted on.

**Proposed CVSS v3.1:** `AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:L/I:N/A:N` (5.3, Medium). Severity is proposed, not insisted on.

### Suggested fix

1. Widen the regex to `[0-9a-fA-F]` and add `re.IGNORECASE`, as CVE-2026-54236's advisory recommended.
2. Replace the `pil-image-repr` test case's hand-written literal with a string produced by calling `repr()` on a real `PIL.Image.Image`, so the case cannot pass while the production path leaks. Apply the same to PR #35492's new test.

Item 2 matters as much as item 1 here: the test is the reason the first recommendation was lost.

### Weaknesses of this report, stated upfront

* No GPU was used. Results come from the in-tree GPU-less render server (`vllm launch render`), which runs the real frontend, the real request model and the real `/tokenize` route. Media processing happens entirely in the frontend, so I do not believe the engine's presence changes the result - but I have not confirmed it under a full `vllm serve`.
* The disclosed value is an address, not memory contents. No read primitive is claimed.
* I did not attempt to chain this to anything.

---

*Prepared with AI assistance (Claude), per the repository's contributing guidance on disclosing AI-assisted contributions. All findings were verified by executing vLLM's own code at the commits cited; the analysis and the claims are my own.*

*Reported by Eva Crystal / 0xiviel (XSource Security).*

## Affected versions

- Package: `vllm` (PyPI).
- Affected versions: `>= 0.14.0rc1, < 0.31.0`.
- First stable patched version: `0.31.0`.

Advisory fixed in [#58832](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/58832).

Roundcube Webmail before 1.6.20 and 1.7.x before 1.7.5 passes potentially unsafe content into ImageMagick when resizing images. SVG and EPS were accepted as valid image types for contact photo upload and conversion, and both formats can reference external resources and invoke ImageMagick delegates when processed. Upstream fixed this in the commit “Fix passing potentally unsafe attachment content into ImageMagick on image resize”, which removes svg and eps from the accepted types.

items.title: Field Collection for Drupal 7 access bypass via missing parent entity access check
items.description:
Improper Authorization vulnerability in Drupal Field Collection for Drupal 7 allows a user with the "edit field collections" permission to bypass access control on the parent (host) entity.

The access check for field collection items (field_collection_item_access()) granted edit and delete access to any user holding the "edit field collections" permission without verifying the user's access to the host entity. As a result, a user with "edit field collections" but without edit/update access to the host entity (for example a node they cannot edit) could edit or delete field collection items attached to that entity, bypassing the intended entity/node access restrictions. The fix requires access to the parent entity in addition to the field collection permission.



This issue affects Field Collection for Drupal 7: version 7.x-1.0 up to and including 7.x-1.2.

items.title: psqlODBC log files are created with default permissions at a predictable path and follow symbolic links
items.description: On Unix-like systems, when logging is enabled, psqlODBC creates its log files in /tmp by default, named from the program name, user name, and process ID, with the default permissions, typically world-readable, and follows symbolic links when opening them. A local user can read query text and data from another user's logs, and can place a symbolic link at the predictable path so that the driver appends log data to a file of the attacker's choosing with the victim's privileges. Versions before psqlODBC 18.00.0006 are affected.

draw.io is a configurable diagramming and whiteboarding application. Prior to 30.3.8, the optional /proxy endpoint contains an incomplete server-side request forgery blocklist. When the endpoint is enabled, the URL validator does not reject the RFC 6598 shared address range 100.64.0.0/10. An unauthenticated remote attacker can cause the draw.io server to request internal services that are reachable in this range, potentially disclosing data from Carrier-Grade NAT, Kubernetes, cloud, or overlay-network addresses. This vulnerability is fixed in 30.3.8.

NocoDB before 2026.08.0 contains an sql injection vulnerability that allows authenticated users with read access to run arbitrary read queries via the legacy where parameter on PostgreSQL. Attackers, including Viewer-role users, can inject single quotes into filter values concatenated by CustomKnex.ts to read other tables, schemas, view-filtered rows, and hidden columns.

items.title: OpenAirInterface CN5G SMF through 2.2.2 Orphaned N7 SM Policy Associations via PDU Release
items.description: OpenAirInterface CN5G SMF through 2.2.2 contains a missing resource release vulnerability in handle_pdu_session_release_sm_context_request() that fails to delete N7 SM policy associations at the PCF. Authenticated UEs can repeatedly establish and release PDU sessions through the AMF-initiated Release SM Context path to accumulate stale associations and exhaust PCF memory.

items.title: OpenAirInterface CN5G PCF through 2.2.2 Memory Leak via SM Policy Deletion
items.description: OpenAirInterface CN5G PCF through 2.2.2 contains a memory leak vulnerability in pcf_smpc::delete_sm_policy_handler() that leaves stale UE IPv4, SUPI and DNN index entries after association deletion. Attackers can trigger repeated SM policy create and delete cycles over N7 via PDU session establishment and release to grow PCF memory without bound and break association lookups.

items.title: Cross-user Data Disclosure in Elasticsearch ES|QL Arrow Responses
items.description: A pooled-buffer lifetime error in Elasticsearch ES|QL Arrow response formatting can disclose data from other users' concurrent requests. An authenticated user with read access to an index who requests Arrow output containing an affected column type can receive data from indices they are not authorized to access. A temporary block can be released to a shared memory pool before deferred response writers finish using it, allowing concurrent requests to reuse the same memory. The attacker cannot select which concurrent data is disclosed.

node-fontnik is a library that delivers a range of glyphs rendered as SDFs (signed distance fields) in a protocol buffer. Prior to version 0.7.7, a crafted font could trigger a heap out-of-bounds write in RenderSDF (include/mapbox/glyph_foundry_impl.hpp). RenderSDF computed the SDF bitmap allocation size as buffered_width * buffered_height in 32-bit unsigned int. Glyph dimensions are derived from the uploaded font's outline bounding box with no upper bound, so a glyph large enough to make that product exceed 2³² wrapped to a small value. The buffer was then under-allocated while the render loop still wrote one byte per pixel, corrupting the heap (CWE-190 → CWE-787) and crashing the process. A 680-byte font is enough to drive FreeType to a 65536×65536 buffered glyph, wrapping the size to 0. This issue has been patched in version 0.7.7.

External control of file name in PostgreSQL dblink and CREATE/ALTER SUBSCRIPTION allows a user to achieve persistent denial of service, via appending invalid data to a chosen file.  Specifically, the "sslkeylogfile" connection parameter appends data, in NSS keylog format, to a file of the user's choosing.  This "sslkeylogfile" mechanism cannot add arbitrary bytes.  Within major version 18, minor versions before PostgreSQL 18.7 are affected.  Versions before PostgreSQL 18 are also affected if libpq version 18 or later is installed and in use by the server.

items.title: pgEdge Postgres MCP Server read-only mode can be bypassed by SQL statement smuggling through query_database
items.description: pgEdge Postgres MCP Server enables SQL queries against PostgreSQL databases through Model Context Protocol compatible clients. Prior to 1.1.0, query_database on a read_only connection could send unrecognized statements through pgx Exec without bind parameters, selecting PostgreSQL's simple query protocol and allowing multiple semicolon-separated statements in one request. A caller could combine transaction or session state changes with database writes, and pooled session state could leave later calls writable, when the connecting role held write privileges. The flaw affected deployments relying on read_only as a safety boundary, could compromise integrity and availability, and did not add confidentiality impact beyond the reads already permitted by the connection. This issue is fixed in 1.1.0.

items.title: Drupal Icon API (Icon API: Menu) Stored XSS via unsanitized Title Wrapper Class
items.description:
A stored cross-site scripting (XSS) vulnerability exists in the Icon API: Menu submodule of the Drupal 7 Icon API module. When a menu item is configured with the Title Wrapper option enabled, the value of the Title Wrapper Class field is output directly into an HTML attribute without sanitization or escaping. A user with the "administer menu icons" permission can inject a payload such as `title" onmouseover="alert(document.cookie)` that is rendered verbatim on every page displaying the affected menu item, executing arbitrary JavaScript in the browser of any user who interacts with the menu link. This can lead to session theft, account hijacking, and further attacks against site users.

This issue affects Icon API 7.1.0.

ImageMagick before 7.1.2-35 contains a data tampering vulnerability in the Distributed Pixel Cache that allows adjacent attackers to modify pixel data in transit between client and server. Attackers who can observe or modify the network path between a configured DPC client and server can tamper with pixel data to alter the resulting image.

SQL injection in PostgreSQL reindexdb allows an object creator to execute arbitrary SQL as the database user running reindexdb, via a crafted index name embedded in the parallel catalog query for --jobs with --index.  Within major versions 17-18, minor versions before PostgreSQL 18.7 and 17.12 are affected.  Versions before PostgreSQL 17 are unaffected.

items.title: Broadcom VMWare ESX Insufficient Logging Vulnerability
items.description: Broadcom VMWare ESX contains an insufficient logging vulnerability that could allow a malicious actor with admin access to perform certain operations without being logged.

items.title: Unauthenticated EngineCore crash via out-of-range prompt token id under skip_tokenizer_init (incomplete fix of GHSA-25q3-v2hm-8vpf)
items.description:
### Summary

A single unauthenticated request with an out-of-range prompt token id crashes
the shared EngineCore (and the API-server process) when vLLM is served with
`--skip-tokenizer-init`, denying service to all tenants until the process is
restarted.

The vocab-range validation added for GHSA-25q3-v2hm-8vpf lives in
`InputProcessor._validate_model_input` but is gated on `tokenizer is not None`.
`--skip-tokenizer-init` is the mode where the client is expected to send raw
token ids (pre-tokenized / token-in-token-out / RL serving), and there is no
tokenizer, so the check is skipped entirely. The OpenAI `/v1/completions`
`prompt` field only constrains integer ids from below (`Field(ge=0)`), so a
large positive id passes all validation, reaches the embedding as an index, and
raises out of the model forward. EngineCore treats that as fatal and shuts down.
The same gap reopens the `/v1/embeddings` and `/pooling` paths that GHSA-25q3
originally covered, whenever the tokenizer is disabled.

Verified against `main` at HEAD `dc89fdfb0e` (2026-09-15).

### Details

`vllm/v1/engine/input_processor.py`, `_validate_model_input`:

```python
if prompt_ids and tokenizer is not None:   # <- skipped when tokenizer is None
    ...
    if min_input_id < 0: raise VLLMValidationError("... out of vocabulary")
    if max_input_id > max(tokenizer.max_token_id, model_vocab_size - 1):
        raise VLLMValidationError("... out of vocabulary")
```

Reachability (unauthenticated; the OpenAI server has no auth by default):

```
/v1/completions (prompt = list[int], Field(ge=0) only, no upper bound)
  -> InputProcessor.process_inputs -> _validate_model_inputs
  -> _validate_model_input  # tokenizer is None -> vocab check skipped
  -> model forward -> embedding index out of range -> exception
EngineCore._process_engine_step -> run_busy_loop (no per-step guard)
  -> run_engine_core: "EngineCore encountered a fatal error" -> _send_engine_dead
```

The busy loop has no per-request guard around the model step, so the exception
is fatal for the whole engine, not scoped to the offending request.

### Impact

Unauthenticated remote denial of service (availability): one request
permanently takes down the shared engine for all tenants, on any deployment run
with `--skip-tokenizer-init` (pre-tokenized / token-in-token-out / RL serving).
Same class as GHSA-25q3-v2hm-8vpf (High), whose remediation did not cover the
tokenizer-disabled path. CWE-20 / CWE-1284 / CWE-248.

### Suggested fix

Run the vocab-range check whenever prompt ids are present, not only when a
tokenizer exists. When the tokenizer is disabled, use `model_config
.get_vocab_size() - 1` as the upper bound; otherwise keep the existing
`max(tokenizer.max_token_id, model_vocab_size - 1)` bound. This validation is implemented by the merged fix.

Reported by Matteo Atkinson (matteoatkinson@gmail.com), with AI assistance.

A fix for this was introduced in https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/62911.

items.title: Missing request-wide media budget allows single-request frontend resource exhaustion
items.description:
### Summary

  A remote inference client can submit one request containing many individually valid remote images. vLLM validates only
  the image count and per-item limits before scheduling every image for download and decoding. It does not enforce a
  request-wide encoded-byte, decoded-byte, or memory budget.

  For models permitting multiple images, one compact request can therefore consume outbound connections, decoder CPU,
  and API-frontend memory before prompt-length admission. API authentication is optional by default; when enabled,
  ordinary inference access is sufficient.

  Affected entry points include /v1/messages, non-Harmony /v1/responses, and equivalent chat-rendering paths.

  ### Details

  The verified flow is:

  1. parse_image() registers a deferred fetch after count validation.
  2. AsyncMultiModalItemTracker.resolve_items() starts all registered media operations in one asyncio.gather() and
     materializes every result.

  3. MediaConnector.load_from_url_async() downloads and decodes each response independently.
  4. The HTTP size limit is per response, not per request.
  5. ImageMediaIO.load_bytes() eagerly decodes each image into a MediaWithBytes, retaining both the decoded raster and
     original bytes.

  6. _resolve_items() retains the complete result list.
  7. Fetching precedes downstream template/token-length admission in the HF renderer and Responses renderer.

  MultiModalConfig defaults an unspecified modality count to 999. Representative LLaVA processing information supplies
  no lower model-specific limit.

  The aiohttp connection-pool limit of 100 and vLLM’s eight-worker decode pool constrain instantaneous concurrency, but
  do not constrain aggregate request memory. Completed images accumulate until gathering and later preprocessing finish.

  A complete fix should enforce a request-wide media resource budget, including aggregate encoded/decoded-byte
  accounting, bounded request/process concurrency, and cancellation/release after validation failure or budget
  exhaustion.

  ### Impact

  A remote client can cause disproportionate frontend memory, CPU, network, and connection-pool consumption with one
  syntactically small request containing many compressed-image URLs. This work occurs before prompt-length rejection, so
  even an over-context request can incur the full media cost.

  Possible consequences include API-process termination, decoder saturation, outbound-connection occupation, and
  degraded availability for other clients.

  The bounded PoC demonstrates the resource-allocation and retention primitive, not an actual out-of-memory crash.

A fix for this was introduced in https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/61226.

items.title: Unbounded Out-of-Order Fragment Reassembly in QUIC Streams
items.description:
Issue summary: A QUIC peer that sends many small out-of-order STREAM fragments
while withholding the first byte of the stream may cause OpenSSL to buffer
a large number of reassembly nodes occupying much larger memory than
the actual data sent.

Impact summary: A remote peer can pin large amounts of memory on a server that
accepts incoming QUIC streams, potentially exhausting memory and causing
Denial of Service.

CWE: CWE-770: Allocation of Resources Without Limits or Throttling

Description: QUIC receive flow control limits the highest byte offset a peer
may reach on a stream. It does not limit how many out-of-order fragments the
receiver buffers. OpenSSL allocates a reassembly node for each non-adjacent
STREAM fragment and never caps the count. A peer that opens a stream and sends
many one-byte fragments at increasing offsets, while withholding the first
byte, makes the receiver retain one node per fragment without delivering any
data.

Only applications that accept incoming streams are exposed. With the default
policy, which rejects peer-initiated streams, the stream is torn down before
state accumulates. Because the read side never advances past the missing
prefix, the flow control window never slides and the nodes stay pinned for the
life of the connection.

The per-stream window bounds the highest offset, so the memory one stream can
pin is finite, but it can reach tens of megabytes and, across many streams and
connections, drive memory pressure and Denial of Service. The severity is
limited because the exhaustion is bounded by flow control and requires a
non-default configuration.

FIPS impact: no
The affected code is outside the FIPS module boundary.
