in cxlctl_get_supported_features() but missed this one.

[ dj: Fixed up title typo per Jonathan. ]

items.title: Path Rules Enforced in Front of PHP Can Be Bypassed by Appending the Path to the Script Name
items.description:
Since the fix for CVE-2025-64500, Request::getPathInfo() strips the script name from the start of the URL. It does so even when the script name is only the start of a longer path segment. With SCRIPT_NAME set to /index.php, a request to /index.phpadmin gets the path info /admin and is routed like /admin. Encoded spellings such as /index%2Ephpadmin or /%69ndex.phpadmin work too. Before that fix, the path info was admin, which no route matched.

Rules enforced by Symfony are not affected: access_control and firewalls read the same path info as the router. Rules enforced in front of PHP are. The nginx configuration of the Symfony documentation and the .htaccess file of symfony/apache-pack make /index.php/admin unreachable, but they pass /index.phpadmin to the front controller. So a location /admin block in nginx, a <Location /admin> section in Apache, or a CDN or WAF rule on /admin can be bypassed.

The script name is now stripped only when it is followed by /, ? or the end of the URL. A request to /index.phpadmin gets the path info /index.phpadmin.

items.title: Generated URLs Can Point to a Host Chosen by the Client
items.description:
When Request::getBaseUrl() does not find the script name at the start of the request URI, it looks for it further into the path. This supports web servers that rewrite every URL to a front controller in a subdirectory. The base URL then kept everything before the script name, and the client chooses that part. A request URI starting with // or /\ made the base URL start with a host.

With SCRIPT_NAME=/public/index.php, a request for //evil.example/public/index.php/login is routed to /login, with the base URL //evil.example/public/index.php and the base path //evil.example/public. The URLs generated for that page then point to evil.example:
- links built with path() and the actions of forms, so a login form sends the credentials of the user to evil.example;
- redirects to generated URLs, such as the ones of redirectToRoute();
- assets referenced with a relative path through asset(), so the page can load scripts from evil.example.

The attacker has to make a user follow a crafted link, such as https://app.example//evil.example/public/index.php/login. framework.trusted_hosts does not help, since the host of the request is the real one.

Applications are affected when their front controller is in a subdirectory and the web server sends it URIs that do not start with that directory. A .htaccess file at the root of the project that rewrites every URL to public/ does that, for instance.

Applications are also affected when the web server sets SCRIPT_NAME to the path of the request. Some nginx configurations do that when they send every request to the front controller without fastcgi_split_path_info. php -S does it too, with a router script outside the document root. A request for /\evil.example/index.php then gets the base URL /\evil.example/index.php, which browsers read as a link to evil.example.

The configurations recommended in the Symfony documentation are not affected.

Request::getBaseUrl() now returns an empty base URL when the request URI starts with // or /\.

Talos Linux is a Linux distribution built for Kubernetes deployments. Prior to 1.12.9 and 1.13.3, talosctl support includes the auth field from resources/registryconfigs.cri.talos.dev.yaml and sensitive content from etcfilespecs.files.talos.dev.yaml in generated support bundles instead of marking or redacting those resources. An operator who shares a bundle with an unintended party can therefore disclose private registry authentication parameters, with impact depending on the registry's network exposure and credential privileges. Talos 1.14 and later encrypt support bundles by default, which reduces but does not replace the need for redaction. This issue is fixed in versions 1.12.9 and 1.13.3.

djust provides Phoenix LiveView-style reactive server-side rendering for Django with Rust-powered performance. From 0.9.0 until 1.0.10, 1.1.7, 1.2.4, and 1.3.0rc8, the find_handlers_for_template MCP tool in python/djust/mcp/server.py accepts an existing absolute template_path and reads it without restricting the resolved path to the project or configured template directories. A local MCP client can use the tool as a file existence and readability oracle and can obtain substrings that match the tool's dj-click, dj-submit, dj-change, dj-input, dj-keydown, or dj-keyup attribute pattern from files readable by the djust process. The maintainer assessment states that the MCP server communicates over local stdio as the same operating-system user and has no network listener, and the tool does not return arbitrary raw file contents. This issue is fixed in versions 1.0.10, 1.1.7, 1.2.4, and 1.3.0rc8.

items.title: Thinking-budget sparse state aliases onto a co-batched request during a mixed `SWAP`, forcing the reasoning-end token into another request's output
items.description:
## Weakness

CWE-488 (Exposure of Data Element to Wrong Session)

## Affected

- **Ecosystem / package:** pip / `vllm`
- **Affected versions:** vLLM v0.21.0 through v0.27.1 when using the V1 model runner.
- **Patched version:** v0.28.0.

## Summary

`thinking_token_budget` is a public sampling parameter on the OpenAI-compatible completion route. When the budget is reached, vLLM forces the configured reasoning-end token sequence (e.g. `</think>`) into the request's output. On the legacy V1 model runner this state is tracked in `ThinkingBudgetStateHolder`, a sparse dictionary keyed by mutable batch-row index.

`ThinkingBudgetStateHolder.sync_batch()` implements its own row-move logic. Its `SWAP` branch reads both endpoints with `get()` and reassigns them, but never removes the source entries. When an attention backend reorders a mixed batch and only **one** side of a `SWAP` owns thinking-budget state, that state is copied to the destination row while the original row entry is left intact — so a single mutable state object is now aliased under two batch rows. The next sampling step treats both rows as owned by the budgeted request, and the forced-token sink drives the reasoning-end token into both.

In practice, one ordinary request can force the configured reasoning-end token sequence into another concurrent request's output when the two share a batch and a mixed reorder occurs. This is a cross-request integrity break visible to the victim. It is not code execution and no confidentiality impact is demonstrated.

## Affected code

Links pinned to the confirmed commit [`752a3a504485`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/tree/752a3a504485790a2e8491cacbb35c137339ad34) (v0.25.1):

- [`vllm/v1/sample/thinking_budget_state.py` — `ThinkingBudgetStateHolder.sync_batch()` (L82-L115)](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/752a3a504485790a2e8491cacbb35c137339ad34/vllm/v1/sample/thinking_budget_state.py#L82-L115). The buggy `SWAP` branch reads both endpoints with `get()` instead of popping them ([L101-L107](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/752a3a504485790a2e8491cacbb35c137339ad34/vllm/v1/sample/thinking_budget_state.py#L101-L107)):

```python
# vllm/v1/sample/thinking_budget_state.py Lines 100-111
        for i1, i2, direction in batch_update.moved:
            if direction == MoveDirectionality.SWAP:
                state1 = self._state.get(i1)
                state2 = self._state.get(i2)
                if state1 is not None:
                    self._state[i2] = state1
                if state2 is not None:
                    self._state[i1] = state2
            else:
                state = self._state.pop(i1, None)
                if state is not None:
                    self._state[i2] = state
```

The `SWAP` branch reads each endpoint with `get()` and reassigns, but never removes the source key. When only one endpoint owns state, that single mutable object ends up aliased under both `i1` and `i2`.

- The forced-token sink iterates every sparse row whose state is in the reasoning-end phase ([`thinking_budget_state.py` — `_apply_forcing_to_logits()` force loop, L515-L556](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/752a3a504485790a2e8491cacbb35c137339ad34/vllm/v1/sample/thinking_budget_state.py#L515-L556), writing at [L585](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/752a3a504485790a2e8491cacbb35c137339ad34/vllm/v1/sample/thinking_budget_state.py#L585)); aliased state makes both rows receive the forced end token:

```python
# vllm/v1/sample/thinking_budget_state.py Lines 515-519
        for seq_idx in sorted(self._state.keys()):
            if seq_idx not in self.cu_num_tokens:
                continue
            state = self._state[seq_idx]
            if state.get("in_end", False):
```

```python
# vllm/v1/sample/thinking_budget_state.py Lines 583-585
                # Avoid CPU->GPU sync.
                fill = logits.new_full((len(active_indices_cpu),), 1e9)
                logits.index_put_((active_indices, force_tokens), fill)
```

Because the loop keys on `self._state`, an aliased row is indistinguishable from a genuinely budgeted one: both are forced with `think_end_token_ids`.
- [`vllm/v1/worker/gpu_input_batch.py` — `InputBatch.swap_states()` (L567-L642)](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/752a3a504485790a2e8491cacbb35c137339ad34/vllm/v1/worker/gpu_input_batch.py#L567-L642) records the two-way `SWAP` move for row-indexed sampler state.
- [`vllm/v1/attention/backends/utils.py` reorder loop (L729-L738)](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/752a3a504485790a2e8491cacbb35c137339ad34/vllm/v1/attention/backends/utils.py#L729-L738) is the mixed-batch reorder that emits the `SWAP` (it cycle-walks `src_dest_map`, calling `input_batch.swap_states(src, dst)` at [L734](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/752a3a504485790a2e8491cacbb35c137339ad34/vllm/v1/attention/backends/utils.py#L734)).
- The correct shape already exists in the generic sparse-state helper: [`vllm/v1/sample/logits_processor/builtin.py` — `process_dict_updates()` SWAP branch (L315-L327)](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/752a3a504485790a2e8491cacbb35c137339ad34/vllm/v1/sample/logits_processor/builtin.py#L315-L327), which pops both endpoints before reassigning.
- The parameter enters through [`vllm/entrypoints/openai/completion/protocol.py#L207`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/752a3a504485790a2e8491cacbb35c137339ad34/vllm/entrypoints/openai/completion/protocol.py#L207) and is gated in [`vllm/v1/engine/input_processor.py#L102-L116`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/752a3a504485790a2e8491cacbb35c137339ad34/vllm/v1/engine/input_processor.py#L102-L116) (reasoning must be enabled; only the legacy runner is supported).

## Impact

**Preconditions:**

- reasoning support is enabled and `reasoning_end_str` is configured;
- the server runs Model Runner V1;
- the attention backend takes a reorder path that emits a `SWAP`;
- the attacker grooms the queue so a budgeted row and an unbudgeted victim row land on opposite sides of that swap.

Once the feature is enabled, a mixed batch swap can alias a budgeted request's state onto an unbudgeted request, forcing the configured reasoning-end sequence into the other request's output.

The primitive is precise but constrained: it forces the operator-configured `reasoning_end_str` (e.g. `</think>`) into the victim's output, not arbitrary tokens, and it requires the reorder path plus queue grooming. It is not backend-specific — any backend that produces the same mixed sparse swap is a candidate.

## Credit

**Reported by:** Patch the Planet (Trail of Bits + OpenAI collaboration)

This vulnerability was discovered using GPT-5.5-Cyber as part of the Patch the Planet security initiative.

A fix for this was introduced in https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/49613.

Missing authorization in PostgreSQL type conversion allows a database user to invoke a cast function despite lacking EXECUTE privilege on that function, via foreign keys, to_json(), and others.  A successful attack requires the attacker to search each database for access-restricted cast functions and identify confidentiality impact specific to each function implementation found.  There are few or no practical examples of an access-restricted cast function or of a cast function having confidentiality impact.  Versions before PostgreSQL 18.7, 17.12, 16.16, 15.20, and 14.25 are affected.

An uncatchable exception in the Node.js zlib streaming API lets a peer crash a process by disconnecting while data is being compressed. zlib.params() queues a flush and completes its work in that write's callback; if the stream is destroyed first, as pipeline() does when the peer goes away, Writable still invokes the callback with an error, but the callback ignores its arguments and asserts that the native handle still exists. The handle is gone, so an ERR_INTERNAL_ASSERTION is thrown from inside stream internals and bypasses the stream's error event, the params() callback, and the pipeline() callback, terminating the process. An application is affected only if it calls deflate.params() while streaming to a peer, which is uncommon. This vulnerability affects Node.js 26.x, 24.x, and 22.x.

items.title: Password hash disclosure to "view only" admin users with custom user models
items.description:
An issue was discovered in Django 6.1 before 6.1.3 and 6.0 before 6.0.10.
The `django.contrib.admin.utils.display_for_field()` function did not obfuscate the password field of user models other than `AUTH_USER_MODEL`, or of an `AUTH_USER_MODEL` inheriting its password field from a concrete parent model through multi-table inheritance, which allows authenticated staff users with only the view permission on such a model to obtain full password hashes via the read-only change form.
Earlier, unsupported Django series (such as 5.1.x, 5.0.x, and 4.2.x) were not evaluated and may also be affected.
Django would like to thank Aaron chen for reporting this issue.

AdminNeo before 5.9.1 contains a stored HTML injection vulnerability that allows database users to inject markup into another user's session via column type names rendered with innerHTML. Attackers can create a PostgreSQL type or table with markup in its name to render live elements in the help popup, enabling content spoofing and requests to attacker servers.

FFmpeg before 9.1 contains an uninitialized memory disclosure vulnerability in dxa_read_packet() in libavformat/dxa.c that ignores short avio_read() results for CMAP palette data. Attackers can supply a crafted DXA stream over a stalling network source so uninitialized stack bytes are copied into returned video packets and decoded frames.

Winter CMS is a content management system built on the Laravel PHP framework. From 1.1.0 until 1.2.14, Backend\Widgets\Lists::evalImageTypeValue() interpolates the result of ImageResizer::filterGetUrl() into a single-quoted image source attribute without escaping it. In a third-party plugin that renders an attacker-influenced value through an image list column, an unsupported image value is returned verbatim, can break out of the attribute, and can inject event handlers that execute when a backend user views the list. Winter core ships no image list column, so a default installation is unaffected. This issue is fixed in version 1.2.14.

items.title: pmo-platform: Warn-mode security hooks fail open (skip their check) when a co-shipped awk primitive is absent
items.description: pmo-platform is a modular PMO and release-management platform for Claude Code. Prior to 3.73, core/hooks/block-fragile-refs.sh and core/hooks/block-gh-path-leak.sh source co-shipped awk primitives from core/hooks/lib/ and degrade when a required primitive is absent. In a partial or corrupted deployment, block-gh-path-leak.sh skips its entire path-leak check, while block-fragile-refs.sh skips only the positional-issue-reference detector and continues running its other detectors. Both hooks operate in a warning posture, so the impact is a skipped warning rather than bypass of an enforcing control, with no established exfiltration or code-execution primitive. This issue is fixed in version 3.73.

An information disclosure vulnerability in Zstandard versions 1.5.1 through 1.5.7 allows specially crafted compressed data to expose the contents of an internal buffer through decompressed output. The buffer is 64 KiB in the default configuration and may contain uninitialized memory or literals from earlier decompressions performed using the same decompression context. An attacker who can submit compressed data and observe the resulting output can recover the buffer's contents.

Use of cache containing sensitive information vulnerability in Apache Tomcat's ExpiresFilter caused by the filter removing cache-control header fields set by the authentication layer.



This issue affects Apache Tomcat: from 11.0.0-M1 through 11.0.27, from 10.1.0-M1 through 10.1.61, from 9.0.0.M1 through 9.0.123.



The following versions were EOL at the time the CVE was created but are known to be affected: from 8.5.0 through 8.5.100, from 7.0.1 through 7.0.109. Older unsupported versions may also be affected.



Users are recommended to upgrade to version 11.0.29, 10.1.62 or 9.0.124, which fix the issue.
Note: Tomcat 11.0.28 was not released

items.title: Apache Texera: Missing authorization on the computing unit workflow websocket
items.description:
Missing Authorization vulnerability in the computing unit workflow websocket of Apache Texera (incubating) allows an authenticated user to view workflow results, control workflow executions, and run code in a computing unit they have not been granted. In local JVM and single-node Docker Compose deployments this is possible directly; in Kubernetes deployments it is possible from code running inside another computing unit in the cluster.



This issue affects Apache Texera : from 1.1.0 through 1.2.0.



Users are recommended to upgrade to version 1.3.0, which fixes the issue. Local JVM and Docker Compose deployments do not provide the full security model and should only be used by trusted users.

Missing Authentication for Critical Function in Apache Texera (incubating).



The Python virtual environment (PVE) management endpoints of a computing unit are not authenticated by the application itself. In the local JVM and single-node Docker Compose deployments, which place no authenticating gateway in front of the services, these endpoints are reachable without credentials. The Kubernetes deployment gates them at the gateway, so only the Kubernetes deployment provides the full security model described in SECURITY.md.



This issue affects Apache Texera (incubating): from 1.1.0 through 1.2.0.



Users are recommended to use the Kubernetes deployment, which enforces the full security model, and to upgrade to 1.3.0-incubating, which documents that the local JVM and single-node Docker Compose deployments do not provide the full security model and should only be used by trusted users.

items.title: Quadratic Cohere2 Vision preprocessing DoS via request-controlled max_patches
items.description:
## Summary

The Python OpenAI-compatible server accepts a request-controlled
`mm_processor_kwargs.max_patches` value when serving Cohere2 Vision models.
vLLM forwards the value to the Hugging Face processor without applying a
server-side upper bound. The processor enumerates candidate tile aspect ratios
with two loops whose bounds are both controlled by `max_patches`, causing
quadratic CPU work before normal inference limits can protect the service.

A client that can access the chat-completions endpoint can submit a small,
valid image together with a large `max_patches` value. Varying the value across
requests also avoids reuse of the helper's small LRU cache. This can occupy
multimodal preprocessing workers, substantially increase request latency, and
deny service to other clients.

No code execution, confidentiality impact, or integrity impact was
demonstrated.

## Confirmed Affected Revision

The issue was rechecked on 2026-09-08 against the then-current upstream
`main` commit:

```text
f6326f53bda46898a331c2d24500332c285d9a2b
```

Commit permalink:
https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/commit/f6326f53bda46898a331c2d24500332c285d9a2b

The original audited revision was:

```text
7ca49fbe4bab019e55d57cdc4b7fd3d55c67c1a6
```

The vulnerable data flow was present at the revision assessed in this report.

## Why This Is a Security Issue

`max_patches` is a computational budget, but the Python serving path lets a
remote request choose it. The expensive enumeration occurs during request
preprocessing, before the request reaches normal model execution. A small
request body can therefore trigger work disproportionate to its size.

The default server does not require an API key. If an operator configures API
authentication, exploitation instead requires a client authorized to call the
affected endpoint.

## Pre-requisites

- vLLM is serving a Cohere2 Vision model through the Python OpenAI-compatible
  frontend.
- The caller can submit an image chat request.
- The request supplies a large positive integer as
  `mm_processor_kwargs.max_patches`.

No special build flag, remote model code, malformed image, or unsafe runtime
option is required. The issue is model-specific and is not a claim that every
vLLM deployment is affected.

## Technical Details

The request-to-sink chain at the confirmed revision is:

1. `ChatCompletionRequest.mm_processor_kwargs` is an unrestricted
   `dict[str, Any]`:
   https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/f6326f53bda46898a331c2d24500332c285d9a2b/vllm/entrypoints/openai/chat_completion/protocol.py#L372-L375
2. `OnlineRenderer.preprocess_chat` copies the request value into both the chat
   parameters and prompt extras:
   https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/f6326f53bda46898a331c2d24500332c285d9a2b/vllm/renderers/online_renderer.py#L675-L704
3. `BaseRenderer` applies the extras and constructs `MMProcessorInputs` with
   the same processor kwargs:
   https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/f6326f53bda46898a331c2d24500332c285d9a2b/vllm/renderers/base.py#L769-L779
   https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/f6326f53bda46898a331c2d24500332c285d9a2b/vllm/renderers/base.py#L846-L880
4. `Cohere2VisionProcessingInfo.get_num_patches` passes the merged mapping to
   `get_number_of_image_patches` without bounding `max_patches`:
   https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/f6326f53bda46898a331c2d24500332c285d9a2b/vllm/model_executor/models/cohere2_vision.py#L170-L188
5. In Transformers 5.16.1, `get_number_of_image_patches` reads
   `max_patches` from that mapping and calls `get_optimal_tiled_canvas`:
   https://github.com/huggingface/transformers/blob/v5.16.1/src/transformers/models/cohere2_vision/image_processing_cohere2_vision.py#L257-L285
6. The aspect-ratio helper loops from 1 through the attacker-selected value in
   both dimensions:
   https://github.com/huggingface/transformers/blob/v5.16.1/src/transformers/models/cohere2_vision/image_processing_cohere2_vision.py#L53-L80

The relevant operation is equivalent to:

```python
for width in range(1, max_image_tiles + 1):
    for height in range(1, max_image_tiles + 1):
        if width * height <= max_image_tiles:
            aspect_ratios.append((width, height))
```

The nested loops perform Theta(`max_patches` squared) iterations. The helper
has an LRU cache of only ten argument values, so requests using distinct large
values continue to force cold computations.

## Expected Result

Request-level processor overrides must not be able to raise a server-owned
preprocessing budget beyond a safe configured limit. An excessive value should
be rejected before invoking the Hugging Face processor.

## Security Impact

A remote or API-authorized caller can consume disproportionate CPU time in the
multimodal preprocessing path. Repeated cold computations can delay image
requests and reduce or deny availability for other clients. The demonstrated
impact is limited to availability.

## Severity Assessment

- Severity: Moderate
- CWE-407: Inefficient Algorithmic Complexity
- CWE-400: Uncontrolled Resource Consumption
- CVSS v3.1: 5.3
- Vector: `CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:N/I:N/A:L`

`PR:N` reflects the default server configuration without an API key. An
authenticated deployment changes the required access conditions, and the vLLM
team should assign the final severity and version range.

## Duplicate Search

On 2026-09-08, public vLLM issues, pull requests, and published GitHub Security
Advisories were searched using combinations of `max_patches`, `Cohere2
Vision`, `get_all_supported_aspect_ratios`, `mm_processor_kwargs`, `quadratic`,
and `denial of service`. No public report with this specific model, request
parameter, and root cause was found.

Private vulnerability reports are not searchable, so this does not rule out a
private duplicate.

## Suggested Remediation

- Treat the server/model configuration as the authority for the maximum
  permitted patch count.
- Reject request-level `max_patches` values that are not strict positive
  integers or that exceed that server-owned limit.
- Apply the validation to both flat and modality-scoped processor kwargs where
  supported.
- Add tests proving that an oversized value is rejected before Cohere2 Vision
  preprocessing and that safe values continue to work.
- Consider improving the upstream Transformers enumeration independently, but
  do not rely on that optimization as the request-boundary security control.

## Disclosure Coordination

Please handle this report through vLLM's private vulnerability-reporting
workflow. No public issue or pull request has been created for this finding.
The reporter can provide additional source traces or help validate a proposed
fix. Public disclosure and any public remediation pull request should follow
the maintainers' triage and coordination guidance.

## Affected versions

- Package: `vllm` (PyPI).
- Affected versions: `>= 0.10.1, < 0.31.0`.
- First stable patched version: `0.31.0`.

PR #58830 blocks untrusted per-request `mm_processor_kwargs` and `media_io_kwargs` by default before preprocessing. Keep `--trust-request-mm-kwargs` disabled for untrusted clients. Explicitly enabling it restores trusted override behavior; the underlying processor/sampler is not independently bounded by this fix.

Advisory fixed in [#58830](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/58830).
